# PROJECT AUDIT: AnnualStatement_oldv1 (project A)

A complete "Project Archaeology" of one of the author's two GST programs: what it does, how it is built, every rule it applies, what goes wrong, and how it came to be. It is written for the author (a CA/GST consultant, not a programmer) and for whoever later compares it with project B and rebuilds a merged program.

## SECTION 1: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

Project A is a desktop program that takes **one folder holding many clients' GST Excel files**, recognises each file **only from its name** as one of six kinds - GSTR-2B Reco, IMS Reco, GSTR-3B Export, Sales, Sales Reco and Annual Report [GST RULE] ⚠ (`utils/constants.py:13-75`; apart from an 8-byte check that the file really is an Excel file, nothing inside a client file is ever read, Section 4.1) - copies (never moves) the files into a dated folder tree per client and state (`core/file_organizer.py:71-300`), and builds for every client an **ITC report and a Sales report** from the author's own Excel templates (pre-built workbooks the program fills in) by writing folder paths and file names into each template's "Links" sheet, the sheet the template's queries read (`core/excel_handler.py:66-322, 603-713`) [Corrected during verification - originally `603-708`; the function that prepares those Links values, `prepare_template_data`, runs to its `return data` at `:713`]. In its fourth step it opens each report in Microsoft Excel, refreshes its **Power Query** (Excel's built-in data-import tool, which re-reads the client files the Links sheet points to), reads 22 configured cells [GST RULE] ⚠ (`power_query_extractor/config/cell_mappings.py:33-228`) and writes them, for all clients, into one consolidated workbook `PQ_Extraction_Report_<YYYYMMDD_HHMM>.xlsx` (`power_query_extractor/core/data_consolidator.py:20-186`).

It is built for the author's own CA/GST practice (HIGH: the author's audit method says so, `Project_Audit_FINAL.md:7`, and the code's file names and templates are those of an annual-statement job), where an annual-statement batch means sorting several downloads per client for many clients, pointing each client's report at the right files, refreshing every report and copying the key figures into one summary - work it replaces with one window of four steps, "Setup", "Validation", "Processing" and "Extract" (the tabs are created at `gui/main_window.py:131-149`; their labels "📁 Step 1: Setup", "✅ Step 2: Validation", "🚀 Step 3: Processing" and "🔄 Step 4: Extract" are set at `gui/tabs/setup_tab.py:161`, `gui/tabs/validation_tab.py:21`, `gui/tabs/processing_tab.py:20` and `gui/tabs/extract_tab.py:50`, added during verification); that office staff use it on a shared network folder is MEDIUM (the code assumes a share, and the July 2026 commit messages of `4f84ba9` and `7347383`, A only (after the split), describe runs of 2,508 and 3,030 files on the office share).

It is built with Python and uses **Tkinter** for the window, **openpyxl** (a Python library that reads and writes `.xlsx` files without Excel, but drops Power Query when it saves) for the summary and consolidated workbooks and as a fallback, and **Microsoft Excel through COM** via the **pywin32** package for writing into and refreshing the Power Query reports (`gui/main_window.py:9-10`; `core/excel_handler.py:19-33`; `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:20-36`; `requirements.txt:5, 9`), so its real job needs a Windows PC with Excel and pywin32; `requirements.txt:2` says "Python 3.7 or higher required" ⚠, but the package versions that ran here need at least Python 3.8 (openpyxl 3.1.5) and 3.10 (pytest 9.1.1), and the July 2026 commit messages name a Python 3.14 on the author's PC (Section 9.4).

The program reached git (the tool that records every saved change) already large and modular on 31-08-2025, after about 2½ months of unrecorded work (Section 12B.1); it then changed only in ten modest shared commits of 29-30-10-2025 (import and threading fixes in `6237597`, clean-ups that took a run log, a shebang line (a first line that tells Linux or macOS which program runs the file) and the compiled `__pycache__` files (Python's automatically made, compiled copies of the code) out of git, a README rewrite, `.gitignore`, mouse-wheel scrolling, Step 4's wait-time, file-suffix and per-report selection options in `bd176bf` - 412 lines added, 162 removed - and six more extraction sheets in `47a1492`; all shared - before the split on 30-10-2025; RAN during verification: `git log --shortstat`) [Corrected during verification - originally "it barely changed until A's own commits of July 2026", which understated `bd176bf`], and its program code was not touched again (the two March 2026 commits changed only a document) until A's own commits of July 2026, which sped it up on the network share, added a test suite, rebuilt the Setup screen and dark mode, added a start-up package check, and turned the formerly separate "Power Query Extractor" into the fourth tab of the main window (`gui/tabs/extract_tab.py`, `bfcb24a`, A only (after the split)) while keeping it startable on its own (`launch_extractor.py`).

**Current state: complete and in real use, not abandoned, but carrying many defects** (MEDIUM-HIGH): all 31 features exist and do their main job, yet every one "works with defects" (Section 3); five July commits fix problems their messages call "Reported" from use (`2acffed`, `2aaa2b1`, `725fbaf`, `169c7b5`, `bf2f1dd`, all A only (after the split)); the 288 automated tests pass except one Windows-path test that can pass only on Windows (RAN (me): "1 failed, 287 passed"), but no test exercises organising the files, building the reports, the Power Query refresh or the consolidated workbook (Appendix X3.5); nothing has been committed since 27-07-2026, and GitHub still showed `bf2f1dd` on 21-10-2026 (RAN, Section 12A) and again on 22-10-2026 (RAN during verification: `git ls-remote` (lists the branches a GitHub repository holds) of `goyal-sidhant/AnnualStatement_oldv1` and of the old name `goyal-sidhant/AnnualStatement` - only `HEAD` and `refs/heads/main`, both `bf2f1dd`). Section 6 rates the defensive coding **MODERATE** overall and **FRAGILE** exactly where the program touches Excel or produces the figures - 68 of its 147 error handlers leave no trace at all and 124 never show anything to the user (Section 6.8.1) - and Section 7 lists **79 gaps, 13 of them HIGH**; most of the HIGH ones (for example `A-G1`, `A-G3`, `A-G4`, `A-G8`, `A-G10`, `A-G22`, `A-G33`, `A-G54`) lie in code written before the split (`edac6a3` … `47a1492`, shared - before the split on 30-10-2025; RAN (me): the same code lines exist at `edac6a3`; re-run during verification with `git show edac6a3:<file>` for each of the eight - for `A-G1` only the lookup itself is that old, `power_query_extractor/core/data_consolidator.py:142-143@edac6a3`, while the configuration whose one-word column titles trigger it arrived in `47a1492`), so project B very probably inherits them (to be checked in the comparison).

### Headline findings

The most important findings of Sections 3, 5 and 7 and of Appendix X1. The first three are the ones to read first. Each item names its IDs, the code (`file:line` at `bf2f1dd`), how it was established and where the full entry is.

**Read these three first**

1. **Nine figures in the consolidated workbook come from a different cell than the configuration names** [GST RULE] ⚠ - `A-G1` (HIGH; `A-F24`, `A-R80` to `A-R82`, `A-R88`). In `PQ_Extraction_Report_*.xlsx` the IGST, CGST and SGST columns of the sheets "IMS Reco", "Extra In Purchase" and "Extra In GSTR2B" show the values read from `Diff GSTR-3B!J15/K15/L15`, not their configured cells `IMS_Reco!AA1/AD1/AG1`, `ExtraInPurchase!O1/P1/Q1` and `ExtraInGSTR2B!S1/T1/U1`. Cause: for each column the code first takes the first stored field whose name merely *contains* the column title (`power_query_extractor/core/data_consolidator.py:141-145`) and only then the exact field (`:147-150`); the one-word titles "IGST", "CGST", "SGST" match the "GSTR-3B Difference" fields first. The workbook looks complete and nothing warns. RAN (me, `/root/merge-scratch/run/A-S1/check_consolidator.py`, one made-up marker per configured cell: "columns OK 13, mismatched 9", the nine listed above; re-run during verification on a fresh copy, `/root/merge-scratch/run/VERIFY-A-S1/check_consolidator.py`: the same 13 / 9 and the same nine columns, each receiving J15, K15 or L15); the same 13 / 9 result was RAN in Sections 3, 7, 12C and Appendices X1, X4. It began with `47a1492` (shared - before the split on 30-10-2025), which added those sheets to an unchanged lookup, so project B very probably has it too; no test covers it. This is a technical mismatch between the configuration and the code - **which cell each column should show is the author's call**. See Section 7 `A-G1`, Appendix X1.1 finding 7.

2. **A Power Query refresh cannot be trusted as done** - `A-G3`, `A-G2`, `A-G44` (all HIGH; `A-F21`, `A-F22`, `A-R69`, `A-R71` to `A-R73`; Appendix X1.1 findings 2, 4 and 5). Step 4 does not ask Excel to refresh: it presses the keys Alt+A, R, A ⚠ (Excel's English ribbon shortcut for Data → Refresh All; other Excel versions or languages may differ) into whichever window has the keyboard focus (`power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:282-292`), waits fixed times (about 39 seconds of fixed waiting per report at the default 10-second setting, Section 3 `A-F21`), and then saves the workbook whether or not an error dialog appeared or the check failed (`:349`). Apart from no error dialog having been spotted (`:304-342`), the only proof of success is that cell `BB2` of the sheet `Info` (name matched ignoring letter case, `:646`) is not empty, not 0 and not an Excel error text [GST RULE] ⚠ (`:638-685`, cell read at `:656`), which a value already in the file also passes. A refresh that fails leaves its copy under the "_Refreshed_" name (copy made at `:164`), and the next run with "Skip Refresh" ticked reuses that copy and marks it a success, "Skipped - Using existing refreshed file" (`:137-155`). The key presses are READ (they cannot run here); the reuse of a failed copy RAN with Excel replaced by stand-ins (Sections 7, X1.5.3). Excel's own refresh commands (`RefreshAll` with `CalculateUntilAsyncQueriesDone`, the method of Standard 12) appear in no `.py` file at any of A's 46 commits (RAN, Section 12E.6; RAN (me) at the snapshot; re-run during verification: `git grep` (a text search inside a saved commit) of every one of the 46 commits finds no `RefreshAll`, `CalculateUntilAsyncQueriesDone` or `DispatchEx` in any `.py` file, tests included; the only related text at the snapshot is the log line "Refresh All command executed", `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:293`) [Corrected during verification - originally "no hit outside the tests", which implied hits inside the tests; there are none]. HIGH for the code; what a real Excel does: MEDIUM.

3. **The program takes over the user's own Excel and acts on other programs' windows** - `A-G54`, `A-G55` (both HIGH; `A-F14`, `A-F15`, `A-F21`, `A-F26`, `A-R97`, `A-R103`, `A-R105`; Appendix X1.1 findings 1, 3 and 8). Step 3 first grabs the Excel the user already has open (`core/excel_handler.py:124`, `GetActiveObject` = "attach to the running Excel"), hides it (`:131`; never shown again), switches its "save changes?" prompts back on just before the end (`:240`) and then **always** quits it (`:244`), because the "Don't quit if Excel was already open" test (`:241-242`) reads `self.excel_app`, which is set only once, to "nothing" (`:56`). Step 4 asks Windows for "an Excel" with `Dispatch` (`power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:218, 536`), which may also hand back the user's running Excel, and its dialog scan looks at every window on the desktop (`:450`) and, on any visible dialog (window classes `#32770`, `NUIDialog` or `bosa_sdm_msword`, `:441`) whose title contains "microsoft excel" or an error word such as "error", "cannot", "failed" or "missing" (`:425-438`), clicks the first button whose text merely contains "ok", "close", "yes" or "continue" (`:506-508`) [Wording made exact during verification - originally "a button reading … on any dialog whose title contains an error word"]. Nothing stops Step 3 and Step 4 from driving Excel at the same time (`A-G71`). The call order RAN with recording stand-ins (the user's unsaved workbook was still open at `Quit()`; another program's "Replace existing file?" dialog had its "Yes" clicked, Appendix X1.3.2-X1.3.3); the real effect on unsaved work is READ, MEDIUM-HIGH. Standard 12 asks for a separate, private Excel (`DispatchEx`), which A never uses (Appendix X1.3.6).

**Further headline findings**

4. **Reports can be "successful" while useless** - `A-G4` (HIGH), `A-G5` [GST RULE] (MEDIUM-HIGH), `A-G7` (HIGH consequence, LOW-MEDIUM likelihood on Windows) (`A-F14`, `A-F15`, `A-R56`, `A-R58`, `A-R60`, `A-R96`). A template without a "Links" sheet produces no error: the Excel path first takes any sheet whose name merely contains "link" (for example "Hyperlinks", `core/excel_handler.py:172-178`) and, if there is none, adds a new, empty "Links" sheet and fills that one (`:180-183`), the openpyxl path writes nothing (`:289-303`), and both report success (RAN, Section 7; the "link" case RAN with stand-ins, Appendix X1.3.2) [Detail added during verification]. Cells for file types a client does not have are skipped (`if value:` at `:192` and `:300`), so they keep whatever the template holds; a client with no Sales, Sales Reco or Annual Report file therefore gets an unfilled copy of the Sales template, logged "✅ Success" (`gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:386`), counted in "Sales Reports Created" (the summary workbook's count, `core/excel_handler.py:450`) and offered pre-ticked in Step 4 (RAN, Section 3 `A-F15`). Whether such a client should get a Sales report at all is a GST matter for the author (`A-R60`). When COM cannot be used - off Windows, or on Windows with a pywin32 that is installed but cannot load, which the start-up check misses because it only asks whether the module file exists (`utils/requirements_check.py:64-70`, `find_spec`) - the openpyxl fallback saves the report without its Power Query parts (`core/excel_handler.py:306`) and still says success, with only two warnings in the log file (`:98`, `:267`) (RAN, Appendix X1.4).

5. **Two different clients can land in one folder and overwrite each other's files** [GST RULE] - `A-G8` (HIGH; `A-F13`, `A-R17`, `A-R19`, `A-R35`). Clients are told apart by the name exactly as written in the file names, together with the state code (`core/file_parser.py:229-230`), but the client folder is named from an abbreviated form ("Private" → "Pvt", "Limited" → "Ltd") cut to 35 characters by default (`utils/helpers.py:620-644`). So "<Client A> Private Limited" and "<Client A> Pvt Ltd" in the same state become two clients sharing one folder, and because the copied file names and report names are cleaned with the same abbreviations (`utils/helpers.py:91-93`; report names `gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:291, 297, 355`) the second client's copies and reports replace the first's (in a Fresh run the first client's copied files survive only as `…_backup_<time>` copies, `core/file_organizer.py:277-282`; its reports are simply replaced). Long names in the same state that agree in their first 32 characters (35 minus the "-" and a two-letter state code) also share one folder; their files keep their different full names there, but Step 4 then sees one client and refreshes only one report of each kind, possibly the ITC report of one company and the Sales report of the other (RAN TRACE T9, Section 7 `A-G8`). The log shows ✅ for both (RAN, Sections 4.7 item 5 and 7; re-run during verification, `/root/merge-scratch/run/VERIFY-A-S1/check_rules.py`: both abbreviation spellings → folder `ClientA Pvt Ltd-GJ` and the same file name; two invented 38-character names → the same 35-character folder, different file names) [Corrected during verification - originally said that in both cases "the second client's copies and reports replace the first's"; that holds for the abbreviation case only].

6. **A hyphen inside a client or state name misfiles or drops the file** [GST RULE] ⚠ - `A-G33` (HIGH), `A-G34` (MEDIUM) (`A-R1` to `A-R7`). The six name patterns take the client and the state as "everything up to the next hyphen" (`[^-]+`, `utils/constants.py:15-55`). For a hyphenated client, GSTR-2B Reco, Sales Reco and Annual Report files are filed under a different client and state, while GSTR-3B, Sales and IMS Reco files are not recognised at all; a name written `Sales-Reco-…` instead of `SalesReco-…` is read as a Sales file of a client called "Reco" (RAN, Section 7; re-run during verification on invented names, `/root/merge-scratch/run/VERIFY-A-S1/check_rules.py`: all six outcomes as stated).

7. **"Resume" does not resume** - `A-G10` (HIGH; `A-F13`, `A-R38`, `A-R43`). Every run creates a new `Version-<DDMMYY HHMM>` folder named after the current minute (`core/file_organizer.py:102-108`), so a Resume started a minute or more after an interruption copies everything again into a new folder; the hover help promises "Continue a run that was interrupted, skipping files that are already in place" (`gui/tabs/setup_tab.py:108-109`) (RAN, Section 7). Related: any second run in the same minute silently overwrites earlier output (`A-G9`; in a Fresh run each copied client file is first backed up next to itself, `core/file_organizer.py:277-282`, while the reports, the summary workbook and the consolidated workbook are replaced without a backup - detail added during verification from Section 7 `A-G9`).

8. **No period, financial-year, GSTIN or PAN logic exists, and the choice of file is silent** [GST RULE] ⚠ - `A-R24`, `A-R25`, `A-G39`, `A-R57`, `A-G6` (Section 5). Client, state, type and period come only from the file NAME; the period, month, date and year parts are stored (`core/file_parser.py:97-106`) and never read, so files of different periods or years of one client are grouped together and an impossible date such as `99999999` is accepted (RAN, Section 5 `A-R2`, `A-R25`); nothing in A reads, checks or derives a GSTIN or PAN, and no tax rate, threshold, rounding of a tax figure or due date exists (RAN: search of every non-test `.py` file, Appendix X4.8). When a client has several files of one type, only the first in alphabetical full-path order is linked into the report (`utils/helpers.py:361`; `core/excel_handler.py:628-700`) and nothing tells the user which - a Windows duplicate "x (1).xlsx" sorts before "x.xlsx" (RAN, Section 5 `A-R57`). The sort is that of Python's path objects: on Windows it ignores letter case, on Linux capital letters sort before small ones (RAN during verification with `PureWindowsPath` and `PurePosixPath` on invented names; MEDIUM that a real Windows run gives the same order, as it uses the same Python code). These are described only; whether any of them is right is the author's call.

9. **Where the GST rules live, and how stable they are** [GST RULE] ⚠ - Section 5 (5.22), Section 12C.2. The six file-name patterns and the six expected file types (`utils/constants.py:13-75`), the 39-name state → two-letter-code table (`utils/constants.py:251-292`) with its fallback that invents codes for unknown names - "Unknown Place" becomes "UP", the same code as Uttar Pradesh's entry (`utils/helpers.py:608-618`, `A-R22`; re-run during verification: both give "UP") - the Links-sheet cell positions (`utils/constants.py:102-126`), the `Info!BB2` success test and the 22 extraction cells are all listed, with every ⚠ value, in Section 5.22 (44 rules tagged [GST RULE], 29 ⚠ values) so the author can check them in one pass. Almost all of them are textually unchanged since the first commit `edac6a3`. The only changes ever made to [GST RULE]-tagged rules are (Section 12C.2, READ of every diff, HIGH): the six extraction sheets added in `47a1492` (which also started the nine cross-wired columns of headline 1) and "Missing" for unticked reports in `bd176bf` (both shared - before the split on 30-10-2025); and, A only (after the split), the optional "(N)" marker after the IMS Reco date (`5c8ce95`), the per-client folder-name flag keyed by state code (`33d0baf`), the Step 3 start guard and the hand-over to Step 4 (`33d0baf`, `510f7b4`), report recognition by name prefix in Step 4 (`275d9a4`), the folder text written into the Links cells after the category folders were renamed (`7347383`; cell positions unchanged) and the pattern descriptions shown on the Setup screen (`322717f`, display only).

10. **Starting without a console window, or closing the window during a run, loses the work silently** - `A-G22`, `A-G27` (both HIGH; `A-F1`, `A-F2`, `A-F17`, `A-F21`, `A-R127`). `main.py:17` re-wraps the console output as soon as the file is loaded and fails when there is no console (a console = the black text window; there is none under `pythonw.exe` (the Windows Python that runs a program without a console window), which the author's Standard 13 launcher uses (`rebuild_pipeline_FINAL.md:957, 969`), or under a shortcut without one): the program stops before any log file or window exists (RAN (me): `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'buffer'`, no log file created; re-run during verification from an empty scratch folder with the same result; the line is unchanged since `edac6a3`, where it is `main.py:18@edac6a3`). Closing the window asks a question only while Step 3 runs and, on "Yes", destroys the window one second later; during a Step 4 run it closes at once without asking (`gui/main_window.py:344-355`); both workers are daemon threads (background workers that are killed instantly, without clean-up, when the program ends), so a Step 3 or Step 4 run stops mid-client, in Step 4 possibly with a visible Excel left mid-refresh (RAN, Section 3 `A-F2`; READ for Step 4).

11. **Every feature works, but help texts and labels promise more than the code does** - Section 3, `A-G66` (MEDIUM), `A-F5`, `A-F31`. None of the 31 features is missing or wholly broken; every one carries defects. The workflow choice "🔄 Full pipeline" - "Also refresh Power Query and extract the data (slower)." (`utils/constants.py:169-170`) only switches to Step 4, fills its folder and lists the clients; the refresh still needs the user's press on "🚀 Start Processing" (`gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:136-175`, RAN). "Fast - no Excel automation involved" for organise-only (`gui/tabs/setup_tab.py:96-97`) is untrue on Windows with a working pywin32, where every report is built through Excel (`core/excel_handler.py:19-28, 90-95`) [Precision added during verification - originally "on Windows"; without a loadable pywin32 the reports are built by openpyxl, headline 4]. The "Power Query refresh is unavailable" card of Step 4 says it needs pywin32 but cannot appear for a missing pywin32 (`gui/tabs/extract_tab.py:84-105`, RAN, `A-R129`).

12. **Originals are never changed** (a reassurance) - Appendix X1.1 finding 9 (`A-R47`). Client input files are only read (their first 8 bytes) and copied with their dates (`utils/helpers.py:282-283, 199`); templates are only copied (`core/excel_handler.py:154, 279`); Step 3's reports are copied before Step 4 touches them (`power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:164`). RAN (checksums - fingerprints of each file's content - and dates unchanged, Sections 3 and X1); HIGH. No code anywhere kills an Excel process (RAN, search; re-run during verification: no `taskkill`, `os.kill`, `terminate(`, `psutil`, `TerminateProcess` or `EXCEL.EXE` in any `.py` file).

## SECTION 2: PROJECT STRUCTURE MAP

This section maps every file of project A (`goyal-sidhant/AnnualStatement_oldv1`, branch `main`, snapshot `bf2f1dd`, 27-07-2026), says which file starts the program, and lists the dead code (code that nothing in the program ever uses) at every level: files, classes, functions and methods, constants and variables, dictionary keys, stored values, parameters and imports.

### 2.0 How to read this section

- **Paths** are repository-relative (`core/file_parser.py:136` = line 136 of that file at `bf2f1dd`). An old version is written `path:line@commit`.
- **Line counts** are the real number of lines. 37 of the 70 files have no newline character after their last line, so the file list `/root/merge-scratch/audit/A_files.txt` (made with `wc -l`, which counts newline characters) shows one line fewer for those 37 files (for example it shows `.gitignore` as 79 and `core/__init__.py` as 12; the real counts are 80 and 13). RAN: a Python count of every tracked file.
- **READ** = established by reading the code. **RAN** = established by running something, always on a copy under `/root/merge-scratch/run/A-S2/` (copies `A/`, `A2/`), with `python -B` and `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1` (no compiled files written), `pytest -p no:cacheprovider`, a redirected home folder (`HOME=/root/merge-scratch/run/A-S2/home2`, `home3`) and a redirected temporary folder (`TMPDIR=/root/merge-scratch/run/A-S2/tmp2`). Nothing was written into `/root/merge-scratch/A-copy` or `/home/user` (RAN: the copy check below, and `find … -name __pycache__` = 0 after every run).
- **A-copy is identical to the repository.** RAN: for all 70 files, `git hash-object` of the file in `/root/merge-scratch/A-copy` equals the blob hash in `git -C /root/merge-scratch/combined ls-tree -r A/main`.
- **Confidence** on inferences: **HIGH** (clear from the code or reproduced), **MEDIUM** (a reasonable inference), **LOW** (a guess; how to check is given).
- **Commit labels.** The 12 commits shared by A and B (`edac6a3`, `cbfa4a5`, `6237597`, `9c56a1c`, `d674386`, `5ea77c2`, `1cb878b`, `01862a0`, `1c48722`, `4c42758`, `bd176bf`, `47a1492`) are marked "shared - before the split on 30-10-2025". A's own 34 commits (`fc279af` … `bf2f1dd`) are marked "A only (after the split)".
- **[GST RULE]** marks anything that decides a tax figure, a return/table/sheet/cell, a state code, a period and so on. For these this section only says what the code does; it never says whether it is right. **⚠** marks values that change over time (return and table names, template cell positions, state lists, package versions) so the author can check them.
- **Registry IDs** (`A-F…` features, `A-R…` rules) are those of `/root/merge-scratch/audit/A_registry.md`. See Section 3 for features and Section 5 for rules.
- **Verification.** This section was checked afterwards, citation by citation, by an independent verifier (task VERIFY-A-S2): every `file:line` was opened, the important RAN claims were re-run on a fresh copy under `/root/merge-scratch/run/VERIFY-A-S2/` (`python -B`, `pytest -p no:cacheprovider`, redirected home and temp folders; `find … -name __pycache__` = 0 afterwards). Where the first version was wrong it was corrected in place and marked `[Corrected during verification - originally stated …]`; additions found by the verifier are marked `(added during verification)`.

**Tags used on every file** (from the author's audit method):

| Tag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| [CORE] | essential program logic |
| [UI] | the window and what the user sees and clicks |
| [CONFIG] | settings files and configuration tables |
| [DATA] | templates, samples or input/output data |
| [UTIL] | helper code used by several parts |
| [TEST] | the automated tests |
| [DOCS] | documentation |
| [TOOLING] | files for development tools (here: the AI coding assistant) |
| [GENERATED] | created automatically when the program runs; "safe to delete" is stated per file, because some generated files are the user's real output |

**Plain-English terms used in this section** (explained once here):
- *module* (one `.py` file of Python code); *package* (a folder of modules that contains an `__init__.py` file; Python runs that file whenever anything inside the folder is first used).
- *import* (one file asking to use code from another file); *re-export* (a package's `__init__.py` importing names from its own modules so that other code could write `from package import Name`); `__all__` (an optional list in a module naming what it "officially" offers).
- *class* (a blueprint for objects, for example the main window); *instantiate* (create an object from a class); *method* (a function that belongs to a class); *attribute* (a value stored on an object, written `self.name`).
- *parameter* (an input a function accepts); *default* (the value used when the caller gives none).
- *entry point* (the file a person runs to start a program).
- *dead code* (code that exists but is never used by the running program; it may still be used by the tests); *unreachable* (code that can never run because of how the code around it is written); *dormant* (code that could run, but the shipped configuration never makes it run).
- *AST* (abstract syntax tree: Python's own parsed form of a source file; my scripts read it to list every definition and every use without running the program).
- *callback* (a function handed to the window or to another function, to be called later, for example on a click, a timer `after(…)`, a variable `trace_add(…)`, or as the starting function of a *thread*, which is a second line of work running beside the window).
- *COM* (Windows' way for Python to drive Microsoft Excel; needs the `pywin32` package); *openpyxl* (a Python library that reads and writes `.xlsx` files without Excel); *Tk / Tkinter* (Python's built-in window toolkit, which A uses).
- *current folder* (the folder a program was started from; a file name with no folder part is created there); *home folder* (`%USERPROFILE%` on Windows, for example `C:\Users\<user>`); *system temp folder* (`%TEMP%` on Windows).
- *Power Query* (Excel's data-import tool; its queries live inside the report workbook and are re-run by "refresh"); *Links sheet* (the sheet of the ITC/Sales templates into which the program writes folder paths and file names that the template's queries then read); *staging copy* (a temporary local copy that is worked on and then copied to its final place).
- *pip* (Python's package installer); *pytest* (the tool that runs the automated tests); *virtual screen* (Xvfb, a screen that exists only in memory, so windows can be built on this Linux machine, which has no monitor); *ttk* (the newer, themable set of Tk widgets; a *ttk style* sets the colours of all widgets of one kind at once); *Tcl* (the scripting language underneath Tk); *Tk variable* (`StringVar`, `IntVar`, `BooleanVar`: a value the window shows and that the program reads with `.get()`).
- *daemon thread* (a worker thread that is killed at once, without clean-up, when the program ends); *lambda* (a small one-line function written in place, often used as a callback); *delegator* (a one-line method that only passes the call on to another object); *named record* (a `NamedTuple`: a small fixed set of named values, such as one checklist row).
- *glob* (a wildcard file search such as `Version-*`); *mtime* (a file's or folder's "date modified"); *stat* (the size, dates and type of a file as the operating system reports them; a *cached stat* is the copy that came with the folder listing, so the file need not be asked again); *file signature* (the first bytes of a file, which show whether it really is an Excel file); *8.3 short path* (an old DOS-style short alias of a long Windows path).
- *git* terms: *commit* (one saved change in the history); *blob hash* (git's fingerprint of a file's exact content; two files with the same hash are byte-identical); *trailer* (a `Key: value` line at the end of a commit message, such as `Co-Authored-By:`); *md5* (an older fingerprint method for file contents).

Two structural facts (both READ, HIGH):
- **The two halves meet in two places only.** The main program reaches the extractor through `gui/tabs/extract_tab.py:25`, and the extractor reaches the main program's helpers through `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:39` (`utils.excel_com`). Otherwise the extractor keeps its own configuration (`cell_mappings.py`) and never imports `utils/constants.py`, so folder patterns such as `"Annual Statement-*"` and `"Version-*"` are typed again at `power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:623, 641` instead of read from `utils/constants.py:82, 84`.
- **The package `__init__.py` files are run but their contents are not used.** Every importer names the module it wants directly (for example `from .tabs.setup_tab import SetupTab`, `gui/main_window.py:26`). The only package-level imports anywhere are of sub-modules: `from ..utils import setup_validation as sv` (`gui/tabs/setup_tab.py:21`) and, in tests, `from utils import dependency_installer`, `from gui.tabs import extract_tab` and similar (RAN: grep for `from utils import`, `from core import`, `from gui import`, `from gui.tabs import`, `from gui.utils import`, `from gui.widgets import`, `from gui.handlers import`). Because `gui/__init__.py:7` imports the whole main window, importing any small `gui` module loads most of the program (2.3.3).

### 2.7 Entry points (which file starts what, and how)

#### 2.7.1 `main.py` - the main program

How the user starts it: from a console window, `python main.py` (or `py main.py`) in the program folder, or by double-clicking `main.py` (Windows then runs it with the console Python - MEDIUM: this depends on which program that PC associates with `.py` files; to check, double-click `main.py` on the user's PC and see whether a console window opens). There is no `.bat` launcher, no desktop shortcut and no use of `pythonw.exe` in A (READ: no such file in `git ls-tree`).

What happens, in order (READ; RAN with the install dialog answered "No" and the window's event loop replaced by a recorder, script `/root/merge-scratch/run/A-S2/harness_main.py`, run from `cwd2` with `HOME=home2`, `TMPDIR=tmp2`):

1. **At load time, before `main()`:** the console output is re-wrapped as UTF-8 so emoji can print (`main.py:17`); logging is set to INFO with a file `gst_organizer.log` in the current folder and the console (`:20-27`). RAN: `cwd2/gst_organizer.log` was created.
2. `main()` (`:57`) calls `setup_environment()` (`:29-43`): puts the program folder first on Python's search path (`:32`) and creates `core`, `utils`, `gui`, `logs`, `temp` in the program folder (`:35-37`), writing a placeholder `__init__.py` into the first three if missing (`:39-43`). RAN: `logs/` and `temp/` appeared in the copy.
3. Prints a banner "🚀 GST File Organizer v3.0 - Production Ready" (`:62-64`) and the requirements report (`:68-73`; checks in `utils/requirements_check.py`, A-R124). RAN: the report showed openpyxl "OK" and pywin32 "not found" (optional off Windows).
4. If anything is missing, offers to install (`:78-95`, `utils/dependency_installer.offer_install`, A-R125). RAN: the box "Install missing packages?" appeared; answering "No" continued.
5. If an essential package is still missing: error log, wait for Enter, exit code 1 (`:97-102`). Optional ones are logged as warnings (`:104-106`).
6. Imports and builds the window (`:109-111`, `gui/main_window.GSTOrganizerApp`) and enters its event loop (`:112` → `gui/main_window.py:391-398`). RAN: the recorder saw the event loop start with window title "GST File Organizer v3.0"; `TMPDIR/gst_excel_temp/` had been created by `core/excel_handler.py:53-54` while the window was built.
7. Errors: an `ImportError` prints advice and waits for Enter (`:114-127`); any other error prints "💥 Critical error" (`:130-134`); `sys.exit()` passes through both.

> **Warning (RAN, HIGH):** with no console (what `pythonw.exe` or a shortcut without a console gives: `sys.stdout` is `None`), `main.py` stops at line 17 with `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'buffer'`, before any log file exists; no window and no message appear. RAN in `cwd4`: the error was raised and no `gst_organizer.log` was created. A therefore needs a console window to start.

#### 2.7.2 `launch_extractor.py` - the extractor on its own

How the user starts it: `python launch_extractor.py` from a console (`README.md:164-169`; the file's own docstring says "Run this file separately after GST Organizer processing", `launch_extractor.py:2-3`). It does **not** run `main.py`'s package check or install offer.

What happens (READ; RAN with the event loop replaced by a recorder, script `/root/merge-scratch/run/A-S2/harness_le.py`, run from `cwd3` with `HOME=home3`): its own folder is **appended** (searched last) to Python's search path (`:10`); `power_query_extractor/extractor_main.py` is imported, which at load time sets up logging to `pq_extractor.log` in the current folder (`extractor_main.py:12-19`); `PowerQueryExtractor()` looks for the target folder in `~/.gst_organizer_cache.json` and three legacy files (`:36-63`, A-R118); `run()` opens `PowerQueryExtractorApp` (`extractor_window.py:1032-1049`) and its event loop. RAN: the log said "No cached folder found" and "Initializing Power Query Extractor with folder: " (empty, because the test home folder had no settings file); the window title was "Power Query Extractor"; `cwd3/pq_extractor.log` was created. With a remembered folder the panel scans it at once (`extractor_window.py:135-137`).

#### 2.7.3 `power_query_extractor/extractor_main.py` - a third start-up file that works only one way

It has its own `main()` (`:75-78`) and `if __name__ == "__main__": main()` (`:81-82`), but it imports its window with a relative import (`:9`, `from .gui.extractor_window import …`), so:
- `python power_query_extractor/extractor_main.py` fails. RAN: `ImportError: attempted relative import with no known parent package`.
- `python -m power_query_extractor.extractor_main` (from the program folder) works. RAN (event loop replaced): window "Power Query Extractor" opened and `pq_extractor.log` was written in the current folder.
Nothing in A or its documents tells the user to run it this way, so `main()` and the `__main__` block are reachable only by a developer (HIGH). `launch_extractor.py` imports the class and does not use this `main()`.

#### 2.7.4 Step 4 inside the main window (not an entry point)

The same extractor panel is also built inside the main window as "🔄 Step 4: Extract" (`gui/main_window.py:144-146` → `gui/tabs/extract_tab.py:74-80`) without banner, status bar or start-up scan. It is deliberately imported from `extractor_window.py`, not from `extractor_main.py`, so that `extractor_main.py`'s logging set-up does not run inside the main program (`gui/tabs/extract_tab.py:8-10`). Step 4's log lines therefore go to `gst_organizer.log` (A-R121).

#### 2.7.5 The tests

`pytest` (or `python -m pytest`) from the repository root, using `pytest.ini` and `tests/conftest.py:9` (which puts the project folder on the search path). RAN in `/root/merge-scratch/run/A-S2/A2` under a virtual screen: 288 collected, 287 passed, 1 failed (`tests/test_setup_validation.py:66`, which expects a Windows path to be split at `\`; it fails only off Windows). No test imports or runs `main.py`, `launch_extractor.py` or `extractor_main.py` directly (READ: grep), although `test_extractor_standalone.py` and `test_main_window_tabs.py` build the windows in separate processes.

#### 2.7.6 Start-up compared with the author's Standard 13 (facts only)

Standard 13 (`rebuild_pipeline_FINAL.md:900-1061`) describes a `Run [App Name].bat` launcher starting `pythonw.exe -B -s main.py` from a shared `_runtime` folder, no console, `sys.excepthook` / `threading.excepthook` writing error files to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\[App Name]\`, settings and logs in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\[App Name]\`, files found from `APP_DIR`, nothing installed on users' PCs, and a `pytest.ini` with `pythonpath = .`.

| Standard 13 point | What A does | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Launcher `.bat` + `pythonw.exe`, no console | No launcher; needs a console; crashes silently under `pythonw.exe` | 2.7.1 (RAN) |
| `-B` (no compiled files written into the shared folder) and `-s` (no packages from the user's own Python folder) | Neither is used (no launcher passes any flag); `main.py` itself writes `logs/`, `temp/` and possibly `__init__.py` files into the program folder | `main.py:35-43` (RAN) |
| No console, so `print()` shows nothing; problems are reported in the window and logged to files in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\[App Name]\` (row added during verification) | Start-up reports everything with `print()` to the console (banner, requirements report, "Could not start", "Critical error": `main.py:62-73, 90, 93, 116-125, 132`); the console is also one of the two logging outputs (`main.py:25`) | READ |
| Each app's `requirements.txt` lists the packages it imports with exact versions (not pytest); packages go into the shared `_runtime` (row added during verification) | Minimum versions only (`>=`), and `pytest>=7.0.0` is listed with the program's own packages (`requirements.txt:5, 9, 12, 15`) ⚠ (versions); the install offer installs the whole file, pytest included (`utils/dependency_installer.py:133-134`, `main.py:84-88`) | READ |
| Errors reported by `sys.excepthook` / `threading.excepthook` | Neither is set; start-up errors go to the console; errors in button clicks and worker threads go to the console or the in-window log | READ: grep finds no `excepthook` |
| Settings and logs in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\[App Name]\` | Settings in the home folder (`gui/utils/cache_manager.py:15`); logs in the current folder (`main.py:24`, `extractor_main.py:16`) | READ; RAN for the logs |
| Find own files from `APP_DIR`, never the current folder | Search path and `requirements.txt` from `Path(__file__).parent` (`main.py:31-32, 84`); log files and the legacy settings fall-backs from the current folder (`main.py:24`, `extractor_main.py:16, 42-44`) | READ |

Which approach the merged program should follow is the author's decision; this table only records the differences.

### 2.8 Dead code at every level

#### 2.8.0 How the dead code was found

Every item below was found by a script and then confirmed by reading the code at the cited lines.

| Script (all in `/root/merge-scratch/run/A-S2/`) | What it does | Output |
|---|---|---|
| `dead_scan.py` | Parses all 62 Python files (43 program, 19 test) into their AST; lists every module, class, function, method, nested function, module variable, class variable and stored attribute; counts every use of each name (plain names, `x.name` attribute uses, identifier-like strings such as those used by `getattr`/`hasattr`, and `from … import name`), split program / tests; lists parameters never read inside their own function; writes the import map | `scan_defs.tsv`, `scan_params.tsv`, `scan_imports.tsv` |
| `dead_scan2.py` | Same count, but ignores imports inside package `__init__.py` files and names inside `__all__` lists, so a name that is only re-exported counts as unused | `scan2.txt` |
| `receivers.py` | For every function/method name, every use with its *receiver* (`self.app.x`, `self.client_handler.x`, `UIHelpers.x` …) and the function it sits in. 36 function or method names are defined in more than one place (for example `toggle_client_selection` in `ClientHandler` and in `GSTOrganizerApp`, `scan_folder` in `FileParser` and in `ExtractorPanel`), so a plain name count cannot tell which one is used; all 36 were checked here | `receivers.txt` |
| `perfile_names.py` | Module-level names never used in their own file and not imported elsewhere; imports never used; local variables assigned but never read | `perfile.txt` |
| `attrs.py` | Attributes stored with `obj.x = …` that are never read as `.x` anywhere, plus `getattr`/`hasattr`/`setattr` string uses | console output |
| `defaults.py` (left by an earlier run of this task, re-run now with identical output) | For every parameter with a default, whether any program call supplies it | `defaults_now.txt` |

**At a glance.** No dead program file and no dead class. 16 methods and functions are never called (2.8.3); 17 pieces of code run but can never do anything, cannot be reached, or never run with the shipped configuration (2.8.4); 22 constants and module-level names (2.8.5) and 13 dictionary entries (2.8.6) are never used; 20 kinds of stored values are never read (2.8.7); 5 rows of parameters are accepted but never used (one row groups the Tk event parameters), 12 optional parameters (in 11 rows) are never supplied by any program call, and 5 optional parameters are always supplied so that their default branch never runs (2.8.8); 26 import lines bring in a name that nothing uses, or that only dead code uses (2.8.9); 8 items are used only by the tests (2.8.11). [Corrected during verification - originally stated "19 kinds of stored values" (a 20th, the never-read size fields, was found during verification, 2.8.7 #20) and "5 parameters are never used and 16 optional parameters only ever take one value" (the 16 were the 11 rows of 2.8.8 B plus the 5 rows of 2.8.8 C; the parameters of 2.8.8 C do take varying values, only their default is never used).]

Hand checks (READ), so that nothing reached only in an indirect way was called dead: button `command=` targets, `.bind(…)`, `.bind_all(…)`, `after(…)`, `trace_add(…)`, `protocol('WM_DELETE_WINDOW', …)` (`gui/main_window.py:153`), lambdas, thread targets (`gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:130`, `power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:879`, the signature-reading thread pool `utils/helpers.py:346-357`), Windows window-enumeration callbacks (`power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:450, 475, 515`), the `getattr(self, 'setup_tab', None)` / `hasattr(setup_tab, 'refresh_status')` lookup (`gui/main_window.py:188-189`), the attribute forwarder `PowerQueryExtractorApp.__getattr__` (`power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:1051-1063`) and the methods Python calls by itself (`__init__`, `__del__`, `__getattr__`). The dead-code reader's notes (`/root/merge-scratch/notes2/A_dead_code_patterns.md`) and the four code readers' notes were compared item by item; disagreements are in 2.10.

### 2.10 Corrections to the working notes

The code was followed wherever a note disagreed. Each point was checked in the code (READ) or by a run (RAN).

1. `/root/merge-scratch/audit/A_files.txt` gives `wc -l` counts, which are one lower than the real line count for the 37 files that have no newline after their last line (for example `.gitignore` 79 → 80, `core/__init__.py` 12 → 13, `power_query_extractor/config/__init__.py` 0 → 1). RAN.

## SECTION 3: FEATURE INVENTORY

This section lists every feature of project A (`goyal-sidhant/AnnualStatement_oldv1`, branch `main`, snapshot `bf2f1dd` of 27-07-2026, the Tkinter program that calls itself "GST File Organizer v3.0") and, for each one, says what it does, where it lives, what goes in and what comes out, how the user starts it, and what really happens when one realistic example is pushed through it. **This is the first part of Section 3: features A-F1 to A-F15** (start-up, Step 1 Setup, Step 2 Validation and Step 3 Processing up to the two reports). Features A-F16 to A-F31 (summary workbook, progress and log, Step 4 extraction, settings, dark mode, logging, help texts) follow in the second part, which begins at "### A-F16" below. [Wording adjusted during self-review - originally "This file is the first part"; the section files have been joined into this one document]

The feature IDs are those of the project registry (`/root/merge-scratch/audit/A_registry.md`); rule IDs (A-R1 ...) refer to the same registry and are explained in full in Section 5. Gaps found here are listed for Section 7 (they will get A-G numbers there).

### How to read this section

- **READ** = established by reading the code. **RAN** = the code was executed on made-up inputs in a scratch copy of the project (`/root/merge-scratch/run/A-S3a/proj`, identical to the snapshot; checksums of the original copy were taken before and after all runs and are identical). "RAN (me)" = run for this section; scripts are in `/root/merge-scratch/run/A-S3a/scripts/`, the long outputs in `/root/merge-scratch/run/A-S3a/out/`. "RAN (TRACE)", "RAN (CORE)", "RAN (GUI)", "RAN (START)", "RAN (XL)", "RAN (EXT)" = run earlier by the reader whose working notes carry that short name (list in the registry); I re-checked each such claim against the code.
- **Verification pass (VERIFY-A-S3a).** Every file:line citation in this part was re-opened in the code, and the main scripts (`t_f1_startup.py` scenarios 1-3, the no-console start, `t_f2_window.py`, `t_f2b_window.py`, `t_f3_paths.py`, `t_f4_checklist.py`, `t_pipeline.py`, `t_edges_f6_f8_f10.py`, `t_f13_originals.py`, `t_f14_fakecom.py` all four scenarios) were re-run on a fresh copy in `/root/merge-scratch/run/VERIFY-A-S3a/` (output `out/pipeline.txt` there). The results were the same except file sizes, which differ by a few bytes because the scratch path is longer. Two extra checks were run there: `scripts/v_parse.py` (hyphenated and edge file names) and `scripts/v_sales_midrun.py` (the Sales template changed during a run). Statements corrected by that pass say so where they stand.
- **Confidence** of every inference: **HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW**. Where I am not sure I say so and give a way to check.
- **[GST RULE]** marks anything that decides which return, table, sheet or cell a file or figure belongs to, a state code, a period, and the like. For these I only say what the code does; I never say whether it is right. The symbol **⚠** marks values that can change over time (return names, file-naming conventions, template cell positions, state lists) so the author can check them.
- **Excel through COM** (Windows' way for one program to drive another; here Python drives Microsoft Excel through the **pywin32** package) cannot run on this Linux machine. Those parts are traced **by reading**. For report creation I additionally drove the Python code with **fake COM objects** (stand-ins that only record which calls are made); that proves the order of the Python calls, not what real Excel would do.
- Window tests ran under **Xvfb** (a virtual screen, so Tk windows can be built without a monitor). Message boxes, file dialogs and `os.system` were replaced by recorders so the runs need no clicks.
- All client names are invented. In the runs, **`<Client A>` = the made-up name "ClientA Traders", state Maharashtra** and **`<Client B>` = the made-up name "ClientB Exports Private Limited", state Gujarat**. They appear inside made-up file names because the code reads the client from the file name; they are not real clients.

### Plain-English terms used in this section (first use)

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Tk / Tkinter | Python's built-in toolkit for windows, buttons and boxes. **widget** = any one on-screen element. |
| ttk | Tk's "themed" widgets, whose colours come from a shared style table. |
| Treeview | Tk's table widget; it shows the Step 2 client list. |
| Tk variable (`StringVar`, `IntVar`, `BooleanVar`) | a value holder that a widget shows and edits; an `IntVar` must hold a whole number. |
| trace (on a Tk variable) | an automatic call made every time the variable is written. |
| debounce | wait until typing pauses before re-checking. |
| thread / worker thread | a second line of work running beside the window, so the window does not freeze. **daemon thread** = a worker that is killed instantly, without clean-up, when the program exits. |
| main loop | Tk's endless "wait for a click, handle it" loop; a worker thread can only talk to Tk while it runs. |
| regex / pattern | a text-matching rule used to recognise file names; `[^-]+` means "one or more characters that are not a hyphen". |
| openpyxl | a Python library that reads and writes `.xlsx` files without Excel. When it saves a workbook it drops Power Query. |
| Power Query | Excel's data-import tool; its queries live in a hidden part of the workbook (DataMashup); "refresh" re-runs them. |
| Links sheet | the sheet in the ITC/Sales templates into which the program writes folder paths and file names that the template's queries read. |
| staging file | a temporary local copy that is worked on and then copied to its final place. |
| stem | a file name without its extension (`Sales-X.xlsx` → `Sales-X`). |
| mtime | a file's or folder's "date modified". |
| JSON / settings cache | a plain-text settings format; the program keeps its remembered settings in `~/.gst_organizer_cache.json` (the user's home folder). |
| CWD (current folder) | the folder a program was started from; a file name with no folder part is created there. |
| `find_spec` | a Python check that a module file exists, without loading it. |
| pip | Python's package installer (downloads packages from the internet). |
| UNC path | a network path `\\server\share\...`. |
| Python error names (`KeyError`, `TypeError`, `AttributeError`, `TclError`, `FileNotFoundError`, `IndexError`) | the kind of error Python reports when it stops: `KeyError` = a key (here a client key) was looked up in a dictionary that does not hold it; `TypeError` = a value of the wrong kind (text where a number is needed); `AttributeError` = something that does not exist was asked for (e.g. `os.startfile` on Linux); `TclError` = an error reported by Tk itself; `FileNotFoundError` = a file is missing; `IndexError` = a position past the end of a list. |
| exit code | the number a program hands back when it ends: 0 = normal end, 1 = stopped because of a problem. |
| `sys.argv` / `Popen` | the words the program was started with / Python's way of starting another program. |
| shebang | a first line `#!...` that tells Unix which program runs a script. |
| GetActiveObject / Dispatch / DispatchEx | three ways of getting an Excel through COM: take the one already running; start one (which may attach to a running one); always start a separate one. |
| CoInitialize / CoUninitialize | the calls that switch COM on and off for one line of work (thread). |
| 8.3 short path | an old DOS-style short alias of a long Windows path (e.g. `C:\PROGRA~1\...`). |
| content type (`[Content_Types].xml`) | the label inside an Excel file that says whether it is a normal workbook or a template. |
| sha256 | a fingerprint of a file's bytes; two files with the same sha256 have the same content. |
| in place / by reference (live) | "emptied in place" = the very list or dictionary that other parts of the program are holding is emptied, so all of them see it empty; "passed by reference (live)" = the receiver keeps using the very same object, so later changes reach it. |
| callback | a function handed to another function so that it can be called back later (e.g. to report progress). |
| dictionary | a lookup table of key → value pairs (e.g. client key → that client's record). |
| `%TEMP%` / `TMPDIR` | the operating system's folder for temporary files (Windows / Linux name). |
| ETA | "estimated time of arrival" — the program's guess of the time still needed. |
| `[DEBUG]` lines | messages meant for the programmer while hunting a fault, not for the user. |

### A-F1: Start-up and dependency checks (incl. offer to install missing packages)

#### What it does

When the user runs `python main.py`, the program first re-wraps the console output as UTF-8 (so emoji print), sets up the log file, makes sure its own folder is on Python's search path, creates a few folders, prints a banner and a short report of which required packages are installed, and — if anything is missing — offers in a Yes/No box to install the missing packages with pip (when `requirements.txt` is present it actually installs everything listed there, see the trace) and restart itself. If an essential package is still missing it stops with exit code 1; otherwise it opens the main window (A-F2).

#### Where it lives

| What | File and lines (READ) |
|---|---|
| Console re-wrap to UTF-8 (runs the moment `main.py` is loaded) | `main.py:17` |
| Log set-up: `logging.basicConfig(level=INFO, ...)` with `FileHandler('gst_organizer.log')` + console | `main.py:20-27` (see A-F30) |
| `setup_environment()`: program folder first on the search path; creates `core`, `utils`, `gui`, `logs`, `temp` in the program folder; writes a placeholder `__init__.py` into core/utils/gui if missing | `main.py:29-43` |
| `_pause()`: waits for Enter, ignores end-of-input / Ctrl+C / OS errors | `main.py:45-54` |
| `main()`: banner, check, report, offer, block or warn, open the window, two error handlers | `main.py:57-134` |
| Which packages are checked: `REQUIREMENTS` (openpyxl essential; module `pythoncom` = package pywin32, essential only when `sys.platform == 'win32'`) | `utils/requirements_check.py:17, 37-61` (essential flag `:57`) |
| Presence test without importing (`find_spec`) | `utils/requirements_check.py:64-70` |
| Split into essential / optional missing; interpreter hint; console report | `utils/requirements_check.py:73-133` |
| pip command, install with 600 s time limit, restart, offer dialog | `utils/dependency_installer.py:23, 26-38, 41-60, 63-74, 88-158` |
| Package list the installer uses | `requirements.txt:1-19` (`openpyxl>=3.1.2`, `pywin32>=305; sys_platform == 'win32'`, `lxml>=4.9.0`, `pytest>=7.0.0`) |

#### Input → Output

The Python that runs the program and the packages installed in it → console banner and report; possibly a Yes/No box "Install missing packages?"; possibly a pip run and a restart; exit code 1 when an essential package is missing; otherwise the main window. Side effects on the PC: `logs\` and `temp\` folders (and possibly `__init__.py` files) in the program folder; `gst_organizer.log` in the current folder; with the user's consent, packages downloaded from the internet into that Python.

#### User interaction

Automatic when the user starts `python main.py` (or double-clicks it, which opens a console). The only choices are "Yes/No" in the install box and pressing Enter at "Press Enter to exit...". There is no launcher file and no `pythonw` (no-console) start in A (READ; START notes).

#### Concrete trace

Script `scripts/t_f1_startup.py` (RAN, me). The main window was replaced by a recorder so no window opened; `offer_install` was replaced by a recorder that answers "No" in scenarios 1-2; in scenario 3 only the Yes/No box, `subprocess.run` and `subprocess.Popen` were replaced, so the real offer code ran. Each run started from an empty work folder (the current folder).

**Scenario 1 — a Linux PC with openpyxl but without pywin32; the user answers "No" (RAN).**

1. `main.py:17` re-wraps `sys.stdout`; `main.py:20-27` creates `gst_organizer.log` **in the current folder** (RAN: it appeared in `work/f1_linux_decline`, not in the program folder).

#### What the trace shows against what the feature claims

> **BUG (for Section 7): without a console the program dies silently.** `main.py:17` assumes a console; under a no-console start nothing is shown and nothing is logged (RAN). HIGH.

> **BUG (for Section 7): the box names one package, the command installs the whole `requirements.txt`.** The box lists only pywin32, but the command is `pip install -r requirements.txt` (RAN), which also installs or upgrades openpyxl, lxml and **pytest** (a test tool) on the user's PC (`requirements.txt:5-15`). Installing the whole file is deliberate according to the commit message of `a5ad487` ("Installs from requirements.txt when present, so a fresh machine is set up in one go"), but the user is not told. The manual command shown after a failure combines `-r requirements.txt` **and** the package names, with paths not quoted (`utils/dependency_installer.py:142`; READ), so a path with spaces breaks when pasted. HIGH.

- **Off Windows the offer comes back at every start** (READ + RAN START): pip skips pywin32 because of its marker `sys_platform == 'win32'` (`requirements.txt:9`), reports success, the program restarts, pywin32 is still missing, and the offer appears again. HIGH.
- **"Found" is not "importable"** (RAN XL E2, simulated): `find_spec` (`utils/requirements_check.py:68`) only checks that a `pythoncom` file exists. A pywin32 that is present but cannot load passes the check on Windows, and report creation then falls back silently to openpyxl, losing Power Query (`core/excel_handler.py:21-28, 96-102`; see A-F14) — "silently" for the user: the only traces are WARNING lines in the console/log file (`core/excel_handler.py:28, 98, 267`), while the Step 3 log says "✅ Success". The check also never looks at `win32com`, `win32gui`, `win32api` or `lxml` (`:37-61`), nor whether Excel itself is installed. MEDIUM likelihood, HIGH for the mechanism.
- **The banner may appear late** (RAN START in a pseudo-console): the UTF-8 wrapper made at `main.py:17` is not line-buffered, so text printed before the Yes/No box can stay invisible until a later flush. MEDIUM for the Windows console.
- **Exit code 0 although the app did not start** when the automatic restart fails (`main.py:93-95`; READ).
- The restart drops interpreter options such as `-B` because `sys.argv` does not contain them (`utils/dependency_installer.py:70`; READ, HIGH).
- pip runs on the window's own thread (`:47-50` called from `:133`), so the "Installing…" window cannot repaint for up to 600 s; its output appears only after pip ends (`:57-59`; READ). The commit message of `a5ad487` says the window "streams pip's output" — the code shows it only at the end. (Added during self-review, from Section 10.4:) the window itself is a plain 760×380 text area with no button, no progress bar and no "please wait" text (`utils/dependency_installer.py:121-125`, READ during self-review); until pip ends it shows only "Installing into: …" and "Running: …" (RAN in Section 10, shot 37, pip replaced by a stand-in). When only an OPTIONAL package is missing, the "Installation failed" box ends after the manual command, without the sentence "The app cannot start without them." (RAN Section 10, tour 5; `:141-148`).
- The `ImportError` advice `pip install -r requirements.txt` (`main.py:124`) uses a relative path, which works only when the console is in the program folder (READ).
- `logs/` and `temp/` are created at every start (`main.py:35-37`) and never used (READ, grep). They are not in the repository (`.gitignore:46-47` excludes them), so on the first start from a read-only program folder `mkdir` fails → "💥 Critical error" and exit 1 (`main.py:130-134`; READ, HIGH). Once the two folders exist, `mkdir(exist_ok=True)` passes even in a read-only folder (READ, MEDIUM; not run, because this machine runs as the administrator user, for whom folder permissions do not apply — how to check: on Windows, copy the program to a folder the user cannot write to, delete `logs`/`temp`, start it).
- Errors in button clicks and in worker threads after the window opens are **not** caught by `main()` (there is no `sys.excepthook` / `threading.excepthook`; READ): they go to the console only.

Rules involved: A-R124 (which packages, essential vs optional), A-R125 (offer to install), A-R126 (requirements.txt ⚠ package versions), A-R127 (a console is assumed), A-R128 (program folder preparation), A-R120 (log file). None is a [GST RULE].

It owns all shared state (the Tk variables for the paths and options, the scan results, the "processing" flags), creates the three handlers that do the work, restores the remembered settings, and asks for confirmation before closing — but only while Step 3 is running.

### A-F4: Live setup checklist

#### What it does

At the top of Step 1, a four-row checklist shows for each input a ✓ (set and found), ○ (not chosen yet) or ✕ (chosen but not found / wrong kind) with a short message. A "pill" in the header reads "N of 4 items set" or "Ready - all 4 items set", and a coloured strip under the Scan buttons says what is still needed. The rows are re-checked 350 ms after the user stops typing. "🔍 Scan Files" and "🔄 Re-scan" are enabled only when the source folder exists.

#### Where it lives

| What | File and lines (READ) |
|---|---|

| Repaint rows, problem labels, accent bars, tooltips, pill | `gui/tabs/setup_tab.py:531-583` |
| Enable/disable Scan and Re-scan; strip text | `gui/tabs/setup_tab.py:585-608` |
| Tk-free decision logic: states, folder and template checks, template suffixes `{'.xlsx', '.xltx', '.xltm', '.xlsm'}`, `can_scan`, `can_process`, labels, summary line | `gui/utils/setup_validation.py:13-115` (suffixes `:21`; folder check `:47-53`; template check `:56-64`; shortening `:67-72`) |

#### Input → Output

The four path texts → row icons and messages, a red message under a wrong entry, the pill text, the strip text, and the enabled/disabled state of Scan and Re-scan.

Automatic: whenever a path changes (typed, browsed or restored from settings), and forced at start-up and after a dark-mode switch.

#### Concrete trace

Script `scripts/t_f4_checklist.py` (RAN, me, real window under Xvfb). Scenario: the user picks a real source folder and a real ITC template (`ITC_Template.xlsx`), but points the Sales template at a file named `Sales_Template.xls` and types a target folder that does not exist yet.

1. At start-up (`gui/tabs/setup_tab.py:156`, forced): all four rows `○ Not selected yet`; pill `0 of 4 items set`; strip `Select a valid source folder to scan`; Scan and Re-scan **disabled** (`:586-591`, `can_scan` false).
2. The four variables are set. Each write fires the trace (`:506-510`), which cancels and re-schedules the check (`:512-519`). **100 ms later** the pill still read `0 of 4 items set` (debounce working).
3. After the 350 ms pause `refresh_status()` (`:531-583`) called `evaluate_setup` (`gui/utils/setup_validation.py:75-85`) with the remembered-existence checker (`gui/tabs/setup_tab.py:521-529`):
   - source → exists → `✓ <base>/source` (`:47-53`; shown whole because it is ≤ 46 characters);
   - ITC → exists, suffix `.xlsx` in the list → `✓ ITC_Template.xlsx` (`:56-64`);
   - Sales → exists, suffix `.xls` not in `{'.xlsx', '.xltx', '.xltm', '.xlsm'}` → `✕ Not an Excel template`, and the same text in red under the entry (`gui/tabs/setup_tab.py:557-559`);
   - target → not on disk → `✕ Folder not found`.
   Pill `2 of 4 items set`; strip `Ready to scan · still needed for Step 3: Sales template, Target folder` (`:601-604`); Scan and Re-scan **enabled** (only the source matters, `gui/utils/setup_validation.py:88-91`).
4. The target folder was then **created on disk** and the Sales box corrected to `Sales_Template.xlsx`. After the pause: Sales `✓`, but target **still `✕ Folder not found`** — its text had not changed, so the remembered "does not exist" answer was reused (`gui/tabs/setup_tab.py:524-529`). Pill `3 of 4 items set`.
5. A forced refresh (`refresh_status(force=True)`, what start-up and a dark-mode switch do) cleared the memory (`:534-535`): target `✓ ...e-scratch/run/A-S3a/work/f4/target_not_yet` (the start of the path cut off, `gui/utils/setup_validation.py:67-72`), pill `Ready - all 4 items set`, strip `Ready to scan, and to process afterwards`.
6. The source box pointed at a **file** (`.../source/ClientB notes.xlsx`): row `✓`, pill still `Ready - all 4 items set`, Scan enabled. Pressing Scan with a file as the source ends in the error box "Scan Error: Not a directory: …" (`core/file_parser.py:154-155`; RAN TRACE T7).

#### What the trace shows against what the feature claims

> **BUG (for Section 7): the checklist can show a stale ✕ (or ✓) for a path whose state changed on disk.** The yes/no answer is remembered per exact text and forgotten only at start-up and on a dark-mode switch (RAN, step 4). A network share that comes back, or a folder created after the first check, stays ✕ until the text changes or the program restarts. HIGH.

> **BUG (for Section 7): "set and present" only means "exists".** A file passes as the source or target folder, and a folder named `x.xlsx` passes as a template (RAN step 6 and TRACE T7); the checklist then says "Ready". HIGH.

- "Ready - all 4 items set" only colours the pill and the strip. Nothing disables Step 3's Start buttons; Step 3's own gate (`gui/handlers/file_handler.py:132-151`, A-R51) is weaker: it does not check the target exists or the template type (READ; RAN TRACE T7: a `.txt` "template" and a missing target pass that gate).
- Three different template-type lists exist: the Browse filter `*.xltx *.xlsx` (`gui/handlers/file_handler.py:31, 42`), this checklist `{.xlsx, .xltx, .xltm, .xlsm}` (`gui/utils/setup_validation.py:21`), and the unused `TEMPLATE_EXTENSIONS = {'.xlsx', '.xltx', '.xltm'}` (`utils/constants.py:197`) (READ).
- The existence checks run on the window's own thread (`gui/tabs/setup_tab.py:521-529`), so on an unreachable network path each new text can freeze the window for the network time-out (READ, MEDIUM).
- `_short` keeps the **end** of a long path ("..." + last 42 characters) although its docstring says "Trim the middle" (`gui/utils/setup_validation.py:67-72`; RAN step 5) — cosmetic.

Rules involved: A-R113 (350 ms delay, remembered answers), A-R133 (row states, pill, strip texts), A-R52 (accepted template types). None is a [GST RULE].

### A-F5: Workflow mode (organise-only vs full pipeline)

#### What it does

A card on Step 1, "WHAT SHOULD THIS RUN DO?", has two radio buttons: "📁 Organise files & create reports" (value `organize`, the default) and "🔄 Full pipeline" (value `full`). The choice is saved at once. It only matters at the very end of a Step 3 run: in `organize` mode Step 3 writes one hint line into its log; in `full` mode Step 3 switches to Step 4, puts the target folder into Step 4's folder box and scans it, so the client list is ready — but the Power Query refresh itself still has to be started by the user.

#### What it does

"🔍 Scan Files" reads the **top level only** of the source folder, keeps genuine Excel files, matches each file name against six name patterns (one per document type) ⚠ [GST RULE], groups recognised files by "client + state code" [GST RULE], works out per client which of the six expected types ⚠ are missing or duplicated, fills Step 2 (A-F8) and switches to it when at least one client was found. "🔄 Re-scan" empties the previous results first and then scans again.

The GSTR-3B, Sales **and IMS Reco** patterns reject such names instead (they become variations) [Corrected during verification: originally only GSTR-3B and Sales were named; the IMS pattern `-([^-]+)-([^-]+)-(\d{8})` also fails on `ImsReco-Alpha-Test-Traders-Maharashtra-31032026.xlsx`, RAN]. [GST RULE] (which client a file belongs to): whether hyphenated client names must be supported, and how, is the author's call. HIGH.

> **BUG (for Section 7): a scan cannot be told apart from an empty folder when the share fails.** Any listing error makes `scan_excel_files` return an empty list (`utils/helpers.py:363-365`), and the screen says "No valid GST files found" (`gui/handlers/file_handler.py:89-91`; READ, RAN TRACE T8 §6 for a missing folder). HIGH.

> **BUG (for Section 7): Re-scan stays usable during Step 3 and pulls the data from under the running job.** `rescan_files` empties `client_data` and `variations` in place (`gui/handlers/file_handler.py:102-105`) and then scans again on the window's thread (`:118`); `app.client_data` and `app.variations` are replaced by new objects only when that scan ends (`:71-72`). If the worker moves on to its next client while the re-scan is still running (the dictionary is empty during that time), or if the re-scan does not find that client again, the worker's next `self.app.client_data[client_key]` (`gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:232`) sits **outside** the per-client error handling, so the KeyError ends the whole run with "Fatal error" (READ, HIGH for the mechanism, MEDIUM that the timing occurs). If the re-scan ends first and finds the same clients, the run carries on with the new records (READ). Whenever the run reaches the summary, the workbook's Variations sheet comes out empty, because the run holds the old list that was emptied (`gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:224`; RAN GUI exp8). MEDIUM likelihood. [Corrected during verification: originally the KeyError was stated without the timing condition.]

- The scan runs on the window's own thread (`gui/handlers/file_handler.py:71-72`): the window does not repaint or respond until the scan ends; the progress texts are set but never painted (READ, HIGH; commit `4f84ba9` measured about 41 s for 2508 files on the office share).
- "Found 2 clients" is replaced by "Step 2: Validation" in the status bar the moment Step 2 opens (RAN, step 6); the "✅ Found 2 clients" log line is on Step 3, not visible on Step 2.
- Spelling decides identity: `<Client A> Private Limited`, `<Client A> Pvt Ltd` and a lower-case spelling become three clients; two state spellings with the same code merge, and the client then shows the state text of the last file read (RAN TRACE T6, T8; A-R17).
- The parts after client and state (period, IMS date, month, start/end month, year) are kept in `metadata` and never read (`core/file_parser.py:106`; READ, grep) — files of different periods are grouped together [GST RULE] ⚠ (A-R25). The IMS date only has to be 8 digits (`99999999` accepted; RAN TRACE T1).
- An unknown state text gets an invented code: first letters of the first two words (`Unknown Place` → `UP`, the same as Uttar Pradesh) or the first three characters (`TamilNadu` → `TAM`, `27` → `27`) [GST RULE] ⚠ (RAN TRACE T2; A-R22).
- `validate_client_name` results are stored as `warnings` and never shown (`core/file_parser.py:108-119`; READ); errors collected in `self.errors` are never read outside the parser (READ).
- File names of unparsed files go into the log file at WARNING level (`core/file_parser.py:131`) — confidentiality note, see A-F30.

Rules involved (all [GST RULE] where marked): A-R1 to A-R7 (the six patterns ⚠ and how matching works) [GST RULE]; A-R8 to A-R10 (scope, size, signature); A-R11, A-R12 (variations, suggestions ⚠) — A-R12 [GST RULE]; A-R17 (client key) [GST RULE]; A-R18 (client and state text checks, result never read); A-R21, A-R22 (state table ⚠ and fallback) [GST RULE]; A-R23 (where the state code and where the state text are used) [GST RULE]; A-R24 (no GSTIN or PAN handling: the state comes only from the file name) [GST RULE]; A-R25 (periods ignored ⚠) [GST RULE]; A-R26 to A-R31 (expected types ⚠, duplicates ⚠, completeness, status, the dead "critical" types list ⚠, statistics) — A-R26 to A-R30 [GST RULE]; A-R109, A-R110 (one listing, parallel reads); A-R132 (automatic switch to Step 2); A-R134 (scan gate); A-R152 (the "no_source" message). Dead constants of this feature: A-R13 (`EXCEL_EXTENSIONS`), A-R14 (`MAX_FILE_SIZE_MB`), A-R15 (`EXCEL_SIGNATURES`), A-R16 (pattern `category`/`folder` labels, [GST RULE]).

### A-F8: Client list with completeness status (Validation)

#### What it does

Step 2 shows, on the left, collapsible instructions, the scan summary text (A-F7) and three action buttons (Dry Run, Export List, Start); on the right, a table with one row per client — tick box, client name, state, status ("✅ Complete" / "⚠️ Missing N files" / "⚠️ Has duplicates"), number of files, missing types, number of duplicated types, and the per-client folder-name toggle "📁 Name" (A-F10). The user ticks clients by clicking the first column, with Space and the arrow keys, or with "☑️ Select All", "☐ Clear All", "✅ Complete Only". The ticked rows become the list of client keys that Dry Run, Start and Export use.

- The instructions say "⚠️ = missing files" (also used for duplicates) and "Click 'Start Processing' when ready" (the button reads "🚀 START") (`gui/tabs/validation_tab.py:52-58`; READ). The folder-name toggle (7th column) is not mentioned anywhere on screen.
- Fixed widths (450 px left column, 200 px summary) on a window whose minimum width is 1000 px (READ).

Rules involved: A-R26 (six expected types ⚠) [GST RULE], A-R27 (duplicates; GSTR-3B may repeat ⚠) [GST RULE], A-R28 (completeness %, rounded to 1 decimal) [GST RULE], A-R29 (status) [GST RULE], A-R31 (summary text), A-R17 (client key) [GST RULE], A-R21/A-R22 (state code ⚠) [GST RULE], A-R138 (table and selection behaviour). ### A-F9: Unrecognised files / variations list

#### What it does

Excel files that pass the scan's checks but whose names match no pattern — or match with an empty client or state — are collected as "variations", each with an issue text and a suggested file-name pattern. The window shows only how many there are (Step 2 summary); the list itself appears only later, as the "Variations" sheet of the Step 3 summary workbook.

#### Where it lives

| What | File and lines (READ) |
|---|---|
| No match → error "No matching pattern found" (and a WARNING log line with the file name) | `core/file_parser.py:130-132` |
| A file becomes a variation when not parsed or when client/state is empty: `{filename, path, issue, size, pattern_expected}` | `core/file_parser.py:209-220` |
| Suggested pattern by keyword (first hit wins) | `core/file_parser.py:288-306` |
| Count in the Step 2 summary ("❌ Unparsed/Variations", "🔍 FILE VARIATIONS") | `gui/main_window.py:306, 320-321`; `core/file_parser.py:311, 325, 329` |
| Passed by reference into the Step 3 summary data | `gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:224` |
| Written as the "Variations" sheet (Filename, Issue, Expected Pattern, Size, Action "Rename file") | `core/excel_handler.py:554-585` |

#### Input → Output

Unrecognised files → variation records → a count on Step 2 and, after processing, rows in the "Variations" sheet of `GST_Processing_Summary_<DDMMYY_HHMM>.xlsx`. Variations are never copied.

#### User interaction

None directly: produced by the scan, visible after processing.

   Sales Reco-ClientA Traders-Maharashtra-Q1.xlsx   | No matching pattern found | SalesReco-ClientName-State-Period.xlsx | 5260

   (the second name contains "sales" and "reco", `:299-300`; the first contains no keyword, `:306`).

### A-F13: Organise files into client and category folders (fresh / re-run / resume, backups)

#### What it does

When the user presses Start, a background worker (a daemon thread) handles the ticked clients one after another. For each client it creates the folder tree under the target folder — `Annual Statement-<DDMMYY HHMM>` / `<client>-<STATE CODE>` / `Version-<DDMMYY HHMM>` / `GSTR3B`, `ITC`, `Sales` — and **copies** (never moves) each of the client's source files into the folder the code assigns to its type (⚠ [GST RULE], A-R41) under a cleaned name. What happens when a file of that name is already there depends on the processing mode (Fresh / Re-Run / Resume). The reports (A-F14, A-F15), the text report and the summary workbook (A-F16) follow in the same run.

| Worker: organiser created, per-client loop, folders, copies, log lines | `gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:182-284` (organiser `:189-195`, client lookup `:232`, per-client `try` from `:243`, folders `:253`, copies `:271-284`) |
| Organiser set-up (default length 35, run time stamp, mode check, target created) | `core/file_organizer.py:26-69` (`:42, 43, 62-63, 66-69`) |
