#### A-R7 — How a name is matched · [GST RULE]
- **What the code does.**
  1. The six patterns are tried in the order of A-R1 to A-R6; the first match wins (`break`).
  2. All ignore letter case; all accept only `.xlsx` or `.xls` (so `.xlsm` is listed by the scan, A-R8, but can never match).
  3. Each captured part is trimmed of surrounding spaces; an empty part is skipped (so an all-space client becomes `''`).
  4. Because client and state are `[^-]+`, a hyphen inside either shifts the parts: A-R1, A-R5 and A-R6 then accept the file with client and state taken from the first hyphen-separated pieces (e.g. `Alpha-Test-Traders` gives client `Alpha`, state `Test`, RAN VERIFY-A-S45 `v_patterns.py`), not the text the person meant; A-R2, A-R3 and A-R4 reject it (technical splitting behaviour; which naming the author expects is the author's call).
  5. The six fixed beginnings (`GSTR-2B-Reco-`, `ImsReco-`, optional `(N)` + `GSTR3B-`, `Sales-`, `SalesReco-`, `AnnualReport-`) cannot both match one name, so the order does not change any result today.
  6. A match fills `type`, `category`, `folder`, `pattern`, `client`, `state`, `metadata` (the remaining parts); no match → `error = 'No matching pattern found'` and a WARNING log line `Could not parse filename: <name>` (client file names reach the log).
- **Where.** `core/file_parser.py:82-128` (first match, `break` at `:128`), `:98-106` (trim at `:102, :104, :106`; skip empty at `:100`), `:130-132` (no match).
- **Evidence.** READ; RAN (TRACE T1: at most one pattern matched each of 60 names).
- **History.** Since `edac6a3` (shared - before the split on 30-10-2025).

#### A-R8 — Which files are looked at
- **What the code does.** Only the top level of the source folder is listed (one `os.scandir`, no sub-folders). A name is kept if, lower-cased, it ends in `.xlsx`, `.xls` or `.xlsm`. It must then be a regular file (a folder named `x.xlsx` is skipped) and have a suffix in a second list `.xlsx`, `.xls`, `.xlsm`, `.xltx`, `.xltm` (which adds nothing after the first filter). Anything else (`.xlsb`, `.xltx`, `.csv`, files in sub-folders) is dropped with no message, no count and no variation entry. If an entry cannot be read between listing and checking it is skipped (`OSError`).
- **Exact values.** First filter `('.xlsx', '.xls', '.xlsm')`; second filter `{'.xlsx', '.xls', '.xlsm', '.xltx', '.xltm'}`.
- **Where.** `utils/helpers.py:327` (first list), `:328` (one listing), `:330` (test), `:332-338` (vanished entry), `:296` (regular file), `:299` (second list). Used by `core/file_parser.py:158`. The test-only twins `utils/helpers.py:240-260, 368-373` repeat the same checks.
- **Evidence.** READ; RAN (me s1: the `.csv` and the sub-folder file never appeared; TRACE T6).
- **History.** One listing since `a603c02` / `56aaad9` (A only (after the split)); at the split three globs (`utils/helpers.py:249-257@47a1492`).
- **Not a GST rule.**

#### A-R9 — Minimum file size
- **What the code does.** A candidate must be at least **1024 bytes**; smaller files (including Excel's own `~$` lock files of about 165 bytes) are dropped silently.
- **Where.** `utils/helpers.py:302-303`.
- **Evidence.** READ; RAN (TRACE T8: 1023 bytes rejected, 1024 accepted; me s1: a 104-byte file dropped).
- **History.** Since `edac6a3` (shared - before the split on 30-10-2025).
- **Not a GST rule.**

#### A-R10 — Excel signature
- **What the code does.** The first 8 bytes are read; the file is kept only if they start with `PK\x03\x04` (ZIP-based `.xlsx/.xlsm/.xltx/.xltm`) or `\xd0\xcf\x11\xe0` (old `.xls`). A wrong signature is dropped with no log line; an unreadable file is dropped with an ERROR log line. Any ZIP file renamed `.xlsx` passes.
- **Where.** `utils/helpers.py:264` (`_XLSX_SIG`), `:265` (`_XLS_SIG`), `:275-287` (`_has_excel_signature`, read `:282-283`, test `:284`).
- **Evidence.** READ; RAN (TRACE T8: a plain `.zip` renamed `.xlsx` accepted).
- **Not a GST rule.**

#### A-R11 — Unrecognised files become "variations"
- **What the code does.** A file that passed A-R8 to A-R10 but matches no pattern becomes a variation record `{filename, path, issue: 'No matching pattern found', size (bytes), pattern_expected (A-R12)}`. A file that matched but has an empty client or state becomes a variation with issue `'Could not parse filename'`, while the scan statistics still count it as parsed. Variations are never copied; Step 2 shows only their number; the list appears as the "Variations" sheet of the Step 3 summary workbook (A-R61).
- **Where.** `core/file_parser.py:130-132` (issue text), `:209-220` (variation record), counted `:311` (parsed) and `:329` (variations); shown `gui/main_window.py:320-321`; written `core/excel_handler.py:554-585`.
- **Evidence.** READ; RAN (TRACE T11: 3 files → parsed 2, unparsed 1, variations 2; me s1: `Random notes.xlsx`).
- **Not a GST rule.**

### 5.3 Category 2 — Client identity and name cleaning (A-R17 to A-R20)

#### A-R17 — Client key · [GST RULE]
- **What the code does.** Recognised files are grouped under the key `"<client text exactly as written in the file name>-<state code>"` (state code from A-R21 / A-R22). The key is case- and space-sensitive, so `<Client A> Private Limited`, `<Client A> Pvt Ltd` and a lower-case spelling are three clients. Two state spellings that give the same code merge into one client, and the client's stored `client` and `state` are those of the LAST file read for that key (e.g. `Orissa` and `Odisha` merge, shown as whichever came last). The GUI rebuilds the key from the table's displayed text; Tk returns number-looking text as numbers (`0042` → 42), giving keys that do not exist.
- **Where.** Built `core/file_parser.py:229-236`; rebuilt `gui/handlers/client_handler.py:169-170, 181, 218`; `core/file_organizer.py:122`; looked up `gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:56, 101, 232`.
- **Evidence.** READ; RAN (TRACE T6/T8: spelling variants → separate clients; T7/T12: `0042` → `42-MH`, a state `27` crashes `get_state_code`).
- **History.** Key by state code since `edac6a3` (shared - before the split on 30-10-2025); the GUI's per-client-flag key was by state NAME until `33d0baf` (A only (after the split)).

#### A-R18 — Client and state text checks · DEAD (output never read)
- **What the code does.** `validate_client_name` returns (False, message) for text that is empty or blank (`"Client name cannot be empty"`), shorter than **2** (`"Client name too short"`), longer than **100** (`"Client name too long"`) or containing any of `< > : " / \ | ? *` (`"Client name contains invalid characters"`); otherwise (True, ""). It is applied to the client AND to the state (the state message reuses the client wording: `"State name issue: Client name too short"`). The result goes into the parse result's `warnings`, which nothing reads — so it changes nothing.
- **Where.** `utils/helpers.py:428-449` (2 at `:438`, 100 at `:441`, characters `:445`); applied `core/file_parser.py:108-119`.
- **Evidence.** READ; RAN (me s2: all five branches; TRACE T1 rows 30-31, 51).

#### A-R19 — Business abbreviations
- **What the code does.** Whole words `Private` → `Pvt` and `Limited` → `Ltd`, any letter case; words that merely contain them (`Privateer`, `Unlimited`) are untouched. There are TWO routines:
  - in file names and the Level-4 suffix (`sanitize_filename`) runs of spaces/underscores are first turned into single spaces, so `X_Private_Limited` is abbreviated (`X_Pvt_Ltd`);
  - in the Level-2 folder name (`create_client_state_key`) this step is missing, so `X_Private_Limited` keeps the full words.
- **Where.** `utils/helpers.py:91-93` (file names), `:624-625` (Level-2 key).
- **Evidence.** READ; RAN (me s2: `Zeta_Private_Limited` → `Zeta_Pvt_Ltd` in file names, `Zeta_Private_Limited-DL` as the folder; `Privateer Unlimited` unchanged).
- **History.** The key version has used whole-word, case-insensitive matching since `edac6a3` (shared - before the split on 30-10-2025) (`utils/helpers.py:517-518@47a1492`). The file-name version was a case-sensitive substring replace (`base_name.replace('Private', 'Pvt')`, `utils/helpers.py:78-79@47a1492`, which turned `Privateer` into `Pvter`) until `33d0baf`; the underscore step was added in `4219ffb` (both A only (after the split)).
- **Older documents.** `PROJECT_AUDIT_ANNUALSTATEMENT.md:500-507` describes the old case-sensitive replace (DOCS R-SAN); `tests/README.md:27-31` names the `Privateer` quirk, which the same day's change removed (DOCS T9).
- **Not a GST rule.**

#### A-R20 — Name cleaning (`sanitize_filename`)
- **What the code does**, in this order:
  1. empty text → `unnamed`;
  2. the "extension" = the text after the LAST dot (`Path.suffix`), put back unchanged at the end; the rest is the stem;
  3. abbreviations as A-R19;
  4. control characters (codes 0-31 and 127-159) → `_`;
  5. each of `` < > : " / \ | ? * [ ] { } + = ! @ # $ % ^ , ; ' " ` ~ `` (one character each; the backtick is one of them) → `_` (hyphen, dot, `&`, `(`, `)` are kept; `"` is listed twice);
  6. runs of spaces/underscores → one `_`;
  7. `_`, `.` and spaces stripped at both ends; empty → `unnamed`;
  8. the stem cut to `max_length − len(extension) − 10` characters (default `max_length` 200 → 185 characters + `.xlsx` = 190 in total).
  Because the extension is the text after the last dot, client names with a dot are only partly cleaned (`Omega Co. Private Limited` → `Omega_Co. Private Limited`), and a trailing dot behaves differently on Python 3.12/3.13 and 3.14 (RAN CORE exp3b). (Added during self-review, from Sections 7 `A-G40` and 9.4: the older behaviour holds for 3.11 as well; RAN during self-review on the snapshot's `utils/helpers.py`: `sanitize_filename('ClientA Co.')` → `'ClientA_Co'` on Python 3.11.17, 3.12.3 and 3.13.16, `'ClientA_Co.'` on 3.14.6. So the same client gets different report, folder-suffix and copy names on PCs with different Python versions.)
- **Where.** `utils/helpers.py:68-126` (default 200 `:68`, `unnamed` `:72-73, 115-116`, stem/suffix `:76-77`, characters `:96`, control `:99-102`, collapse `:109`, strip `:112`, length `:119-120`, extension back `:123-124`). Used for copied file names `core/file_organizer.py:271`, the Level-4 client suffix `core/file_organizer.py:90`, report names `gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:292`.
- **Evidence.** READ; RAN (me s2: `Alpha's #1, Shop!.xlsx` → `Alpha_s_1_Shop.xlsx`; `___` → `unnamed`; a 250-character name → 190 characters; `Omega Co. Private Limited` → `Omega_Co. Private Limited`).
- **Not a GST rule.**

### 5.5 Category 4 — Financial year and tax period (A-R25)

#### A-R25 — Period parts are captured but never used; no financial-year or tax-period logic · [GST RULE] · ⚠ · DEAD (metadata never read)

#### A-R32 — Level-1 (run) folder name
- **What the code does.** The run folder is named `Annual Statement-{timestamp}`, with the run time stamp of A-R33 (for example `Annual Statement-211026 1030`, 28 characters). In Fresh mode it is created with "exist is fine" (`mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)`), so a second Fresh run started in the SAME minute silently reuses the same folder (and the same Version folders, A-R38). In Re-run / Resume mode the same name is used only when no earlier `Annual Statement-*` folder exists (A-R43).

#### A-R33 — Run time stamps (clock time, minute resolution)
- **What the code does.** Every name the program builds carries the LOCAL clock time at minute resolution, in these formats:

| Used for | Format (Python `strftime`) | Example (21-10-2026 10:30) | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| Level-1 and Version folder names | `%d%m%y %H%M` (day-month-year, space, hour-minute) | `211026 1030` | `utils/helpers.py:25-27`; taken `core/file_organizer.py:43` |
| ITC/Sales report and summary file names | the same, taken AGAIN at `gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:186`, with the space replaced by `_` | `211026_1030` | `gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:186, 294, 462` |
| Backup copies | `%d%m%y_%H%M`, taken at the moment of the backup | `211026_1031` | `utils/helpers.py:33-35, 224` |
| Refreshed copies (Step 4) | `%d%m%y_%H%M`, taken per report | `211026_1100` | `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:128` |
| Consolidated workbook | `%Y%m%d_%H%M` (year first) | `20261021_1100` | `power_query_extractor/core/data_consolidator.py:175` |
| Exported client list (suggested name) | `%Y%m%d_%H%M%S` | `20261021_103015` | `gui/handlers/client_handler.py:236` |
| Text inside reports ("Generated: …") | `%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S` | `2026-10-21 10:30:15` | `core/file_organizer.py:336`; `power_query_extractor/core/data_consolidator.py:231`; `gui/handlers/client_handler.py:243` |
| "Last Refresh Status" column | `%Y-%m-%d %H:%M` of the file's date modified | `2026-10-21 11:00` | `power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:80` |
| Log lines on screen; Errors sheet "Time" | `%H:%M:%S` | `10:30:15` | `gui/utils/ui_helpers.py:19`; `power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:1024`; `gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:447` |
| Summary sheet "Processing Date" | the folder stamp TEXT `%d%m%y %H%M` (not a date value) | `211026 1030` | `gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:210` → `core/excel_handler.py:443` |

  Two separate clock reads name one run (`core/file_organizer.py:43` for folders, `gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:186` for report and summary names); if a minute boundary falls between them, the report names carry a different minute from their Version folder (READ; LOW likelihood — the two lines run microseconds apart). Day-first text does not sort by date (`Version-311225 2359` sorts after `Version-020726 0900`, RAN TRACE T3c), which is why "newest" is decided by date modified (A-R42, A-R43). `get_date_only()` (`%d%m%y`) is dead (A-R34).
- **Evidence.** READ; RAN (me s3: `211026 1344` / `211026_1344`; TRACE T3 (c)).

#### A-R35 — Level-2 client folder name · [GST RULE]
- **What the code does** (`create_client_state_key(client, state, max_length)`):
  1. whole words `Private` → `Pvt`, `Limited` → `Ltd`, any letter case, on the client text AS WRITTEN (spaces kept; underscores are NOT turned into spaces first, so `ClientA_Private_Limited` keeps its full words — A-R19);
  2. state code from A-R21 / A-R22;
  3. key = `"<client>-<state code>"`;
  4. if the key is longer than `max_length` (default **35**, A-R36): `available = max_length − len(code) − 1`; if `available > 5` the client part is cut to `available` characters (it may end with a space, e.g. `ClientA Pvt -DL`), otherwise the WHOLE key is cut to `max_length` characters and the state code is lost.
  No character cleaning is done here (the name comes from a valid file name, so only characters Windows allows in file names can arrive; `&`, `,`, `(`, `)`, `.`, `'`, `{`, `}`, `[`, `]`, `!`, `@`, `#`, `$`, `%`, `^`, `~`, `` ` ``, `+`, `=` and Unicode pass into the folder name — TRACE T2 obs 6). A client text starting with `_` gives a folder that Step 4 skips (A-R42).
- **Exact examples** (RAN me s2, s3):

| Client text | State text | Max | Folder name |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Beta Demo Industries Private Limited` | `Maharashtra` | 35 | `Beta Demo Industries Pvt Ltd-MH` |
| `Zeta_Private_Limited` | `Delhi` | 35 | `Zeta_Private_Limited-DL` |
| `Gamma Sample Manufacturing Company of India One` | `Maharashtra` | 35 | `Gamma Sample Manufacturing Compa-MH` (the "… Two" client gets the SAME folder) |
| `ClientA Private Limited` | `Delhi` | 15 | `ClientA Pvt -DL` (ends with a space before the hyphen) |
| `Beta Demo Industries` | `Maharashtra` | 9 | `Beta D-MH` |
| `Beta Demo Industries` | `Maharashtra` | 8 | `Beta Dem` (state code gone) |
| `_Alpha` | `Delhi` | 35 | `_Alpha-DL` (skipped by Step 4) |
| `ClientA` | `` (empty) | 35 | `ClientA-` |

  Consequences (RAN TRACE T6 §7, T8 §1; Windows part READ, MEDIUM): two different client keys share one Level-2 folder (and one Version folder) when they are abbreviation variants (`… Private Limited` / `… Pvt Ltd`), when their first `max − code − 1` characters agree (32 characters with a two-letter code at the default 35), or — on Windows, whose file names ignore letter case — when they differ only in capitals. For abbreviation variants the cleaned report names are identical too, so inside the shared Version folder the second client's reports replace the first's (A-R59; RAN VERIFY-A-S45 `v_abbrev_merge.py`). [GST RULE] because the state code is part of the name; nothing here is judged.
- **Where.** `utils/helpers.py:620-644` (abbreviations `:624-625`, code `:628`, key `:631`, limit `:634-642`, the "> 5" test `:637`); used `core/file_organizer.py:83-87, 97-100`. The redundant `import re` inside the function is at `:623`.

#### A-R38 — Version folder

#### A-R42 — Step 4: which run and which version are used
- **What the code does.**
  1. Inside the folder in Step 4's box, every entry matching `Annual Statement-*` is collected — FILES included (no folder test). None → log "No Annual Statement folders found" (warning), status "No processed folders found", and the PREVIOUS client list and run folder stay as they were.
  2. The entry with the newest date modified is the run folder; it is stored as `self.level1_folder` and later receives the consolidated workbook (A-R86). If that newest entry is a FILE, listing it fails and the scan ends with "Error scanning folder" (RAN PQ).
  3. Every sub-folder of it whose name does not start with `_` is a client; inside it every `Version-*` entry is collected (files too) and the newest by date modified is used. Client folders with no `Version-*` are left out without a message.
  4. For that Version folder, `has_itc` / `has_sales` = some file name (any letter case) starts with `itc_report_` / `sales_report_` and ends with `.xlsx` (refreshed copies count, A-R59).
  5. Clients appear in the order the file system lists the folders (no sorting; see UNREGISTERED U3 in 5.18).
  6. Pointing the box AT an `Annual Statement-…` folder finds nothing (it looks for `Annual Statement-*` INSIDE the chosen folder).
  Writing any file into an older run folder or Version folder (for example Excel's `~$` lock file when someone opens a report there) makes that older folder "newest" (RAN PQ scan probe, TRACE T3c on Linux; that Windows updates folder dates the same way is MEDIUM).
- **Where.** `power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:611-668` (empty box `:613-615`; glob `:622-623`; none found `:625-628`; newest `:631`; stored `:632`; clients `:638-639`; versions `:641-648`; classify `:651` → `:20-42`; record `:653-659`; error `:665-668`).
- **Evidence.** READ; RAN (PQ scan probes; TRACE T3c, T6 §8; EXT t14).
- **History.** Version by date modified since `c1583d6` (A only (after the split)); before it by NAME (`power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:529@47a1492`, shared - before the split on 30-10-2025), which picked the wrong folder across month boundaries.
- **Older documents.** The design note (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-25-merge-extractor-design.md:85-89`) and the `bfcb24a` commit message say pointing at an older `Annual Statement-…` folder "still works"; the code does not support that (RAN EXT t14, PQ).
- **Not a GST rule** (it decides WHICH data set is reported; technical).

#### A-R46 — Backup name
- **What the code does.** `<stem>_backup_<DDMMYY_HHMM><suffix>` in the SAME folder as the file being replaced, with the clock time of the backup (not the run stamp). A second backup of the same file in the same minute overwrites the first (RAN TRACE T8 §4: "v1 lost"). Backups therefore sit inside the category folders that the reports link to (the GSTR-3B folder is linked as a whole folder, A-R54 B2) — whether a template query reads them depends on the template (MEDIUM; not visible in the repository).

- **Not a GST rule.**

#### A-R47 — Copy method
- **What the code does.**
  1. The source must exist and be a file, else the copy fails (`Source file not found: …` in the log).
  2. The destination folder is created if needed.
  3. `shutil.copy2` copies the content AND the dates (the copy keeps the original's date modified).
  4. With `verify=True` (always, from the organiser) the two sizes are compared; on a mismatch the copy is DELETED and the copy fails (in Re-run mode the previous good copy at that path was already overwritten).
  5. Any error → failure; a half-written destination (e.g. after a network drop) is NOT removed.
  6. Copying a file onto itself fails (the `SameFileError` is caught).
  7. Success logs `Successfully copied <name> to <full destination>` at INFO.
  Source files are only read: never moved, renamed or deleted (RAN TRACE T6: names, checksums, sizes and dates to the nanosecond unchanged after nine runs).
- **Where.** `utils/helpers.py:172-215` (source check `:191-193`, folder `:196`, copy `:199`, size check `:202-208`, log `:210`, error `:213-215`); caller `core/file_organizer.py:290`.
- **Evidence.** READ; RAN (TRACE T6; CORE exp4).
- **Not a GST rule.**

#### A-R48 — Names of the copies and the in-memory rename
- **What the code does.** Each copy is named `sanitize_filename(original file name)` (A-R20), e.g. `GSTR3B-Alpha Test Traders-Maharashtra-Apr.xlsx` → `GSTR3B-Alpha_Test_Traders-Maharashtra-Apr.xlsx`, `… 31032025 (1).xlsx` → `…31032025_(1).xlsx`, `(1) GSTR3B-…` → `(1)_GSTR3B-…` (RAN me s1, s3). After a SUCCESSFUL copy the client's file record gets `name` and `sanitized_name` = the copy's name; these names are what the Links cells later receive (A-R54 to A-R57). `Skipped` or `Failed` files keep the ORIGINAL name, so a same-minute Resume links names that do not exist on disk (RAN CORE exp8, EXT t12). The records are the same objects as the scan results (`app.scanned_files`, `app.client_data`), so after a run the original names are gone from memory until the next scan (Dry Run then shows cleaned names). Two originals that clean to the same name (e.g. `…-Apr-Mar.xlsx` and `…-Apr-Mar .xlsx`, or a `Private Limited` and a `Pvt Ltd` spelling of one client) overwrite or skip each other; both are reported "Success" (RAN TRACE T8 §1-2).
- **Where.** `core/file_organizer.py:271-274` (name), `:233-246` (rename after Success); organisation report uses `sanitized_name` when present `core/file_organizer.py:359`.
- **Evidence.** READ; RAN (CORE exp8; EXT t12; TRACE T8).
- **Not a GST rule.**

#### A-R56 — Form of the Links values · [GST RULE]
- **What the code does.**
  - Folder values: the full path exactly as chosen in Step 1 (a mapped drive letter or a `\\server\share` path), passed through `str(Path(...))` with every `/` turned into `\` (`clean_windows_path`; on Windows the `Path` step already gives backslashes).
  - File values: the cleaned copy name (A-R48) WITHOUT its extension (`Path(name).stem`), so the template must add the extension itself; an `.xls` input is linked by its stem exactly like an `.xlsx` (whether the template then finds it depends on the template — MEDIUM).
  - Every value is written as text (`str(value)`). Through Excel/COM, Excel may still turn a number-looking text into a number (LOW; only if a stem looks numeric; how to check: write a digits-only stem through COM and inspect the cell).
  - An EMPTY value is not written at all, so the template's existing cell content stays.
  - An unknown report type gets an empty mapping and no cells are written.
  - Each written value is logged at INFO with its first 50 characters (`  B2 = <value>...`), so folder paths and client names reach the log (A-R122).
- **Where.** `utils/helpers.py:418-422` (`clean_windows_path`), `:553-555` (`extract_filename_without_extension`); `core/excel_handler.py:191-195` (COM: get value, skip empty, write `str(value)`, log), `:299-301` (openpyxl); unknown type `core/excel_handler.py:162, 285` (empty mapping).
- **Evidence.** READ; RAN (me s2: `clean_windows_path` → `Z:\Clients\Annual Statement-211026 1030\ITC`; EXT t7: placeholders kept; on Linux the converted paths look like `\root\…`, which is meaningless there — TRACE T6).
- **Note.** The values are ABSOLUTE paths. A report built through `Z:` refreshes on another PC only if that PC reaches the share by the same letter (MEDIUM; depends on how the template's queries use the cells).

#### A-R57 — Which file of a type feeds the report: the first in sorted full-path order · [GST RULE]

#### A-R68 — Recognising a refreshed file
- **What the code does.**
  - Markers = the non-empty pieces of the LOWER-CASED suffix pattern split at `{timestamp}`; none (empty pattern, or `{timestamp}` alone) → the legacy marker `['_refreshed_']`.
  - A name is "refreshed" if, lower-cased, it ends in `.xlsx` AND (it contains ALL markers anywhere, OR it contains `_refreshed_`).
  - A "refreshed copy of" an original additionally starts with the original's stem (any case).
  RAN (me s3; TRACE T5):

| Suffix pattern | Markers | Copy recognised? | Plain original looks refreshed? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `_Refreshed_{timestamp}` | `_refreshed_` | yes | no |
| `_Done_{timestamp}` | `_done_` | yes | no |
| `_R{timestamp}` | `_r` | yes | **yes** (`_r` is inside `itc_report_`) |
| `_{timestamp}` | `_` | yes | **yes** |
| `{timestamp}` | `_refreshed_` (legacy) | **no** (the copy has no `_refreshed_`) | no |
| `_Refreshed_{TIMESTAMP}` | `_refreshed_` | yes (literal `{TIMESTAMP}` in the name) | no |

  Also: an original whose cleaned client name contains `Refreshed` looks refreshed under every pattern; with `_v{timestamp}` any client starting with V does; Excel's `~$…` lock files pass the name test but are excluded by the callers' prefix tests. The pieces are not checked in order or position.
- **Where.** `power_query_extractor/core/refresh_naming.py:14-66` (`TIMESTAMP_TOKEN` `:15`, `LEGACY_MARKER` `:20`, `refresh_markers` `:23-40`, `is_refreshed_name` `:43-55`, `is_refreshed_copy_of` `:58-66`); used `power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:64` and `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:142-146`.
- **Evidence.** READ; RAN (me s3; TRACE T5; registry check2.py).
- **History.** Added in `2aaa2b1` (A only (after the split)); before it both readers hard-coded `_Refreshed_` / `_refreshed_`.

#### A-R69 — Skip refresh

#### A-R71 — How the refresh is done: key presses · ⚠
- **What the code does** (one visible Excel session per report):
  1. `CoInitialize`; `Dispatch("Excel.Application")` (may attach to an Excel already running — MEDIUM).
  2. Up to 5 tries, 2 s apart: `Visible = True` ("Keep it visible to avoid issues"), `DisplayAlerts = False`, `WindowState = -4137` (maximised); after 5 failures it carries on.
  3. Open the refreshed COPY (A-R102), up to 3 tries 3 s apart, only when the error text contains `Call was rejected by callee`; after three such failures it carries on with no workbook and fails later at Save.
  4. Wait 5 × 1 s ("Loading... i/5 seconds").
  5. `WScript.Shell.AppActivate(excel.Caption)` up to 3 times, 1 s apart; if it never succeeds a warning is logged and it CARRIES ON — the keys then go to whatever window has the focus; then 1 s.
  6. `SendKeys("%a")` (Alt+A), 1 s, `SendKeys("r")`, 1 s, `SendKeys("a")` — in English Excel this is Data → Refresh All ⚠.
  7. Wait `wait_time` × 1 s; error-dialog checks (A-R105); extended wait `max(10, wait_time)` × 1 s; final dialog check.
  8. `Info!BB2` check (A-R73); `Save()` ALWAYS (even after an error dialog or a failed check); 2 s; `Close(SaveChanges=True)`; 1 s.
  9. `finally`: `Close(SaveChanges=False)` (usually already closed — error swallowed), `Quit()`, `CoUninitialize()` (each error swallowed).
  There is no `RefreshAll`, no `BackgroundQuery = False`, no `CalculateUntilAsyncQueriesDone`, no "still refreshing" test anywhere (READ, search). A `return {'success': True, 'error': None}` at `:383-386` can never be reached.
- **Where.** `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:209-415` (Dispatch `:218`; properties `:221-234`; open `:236-249`; load wait `:251-255`; activation `:258-276`; keys `:278-293`; wait `:297-302`; dialogs `:305-322`; extended `:324-330`; final `:332-342`; check `:345`; save `:348-351`; status `:354-357`; close `:360-363`; result `:365-374`; inner error `:376-381`; unreachable `:383-386`; outer error `:388-393`; clean-up `:394-415`).
- **Evidence.** READ only (COM and key presses cannot run on Linux).
- **History.** Since `edac6a3` (shared - before the split on 30-10-2025); the "Increased from 0.5" / "Increased from 3 to 5" comments (`:253, 283, 288`) record earlier, shorter waits.
- **⚠** Ribbon key tips depend on the Excel version and the UI language; the window title used for activation depends on Excel.
- **Not a GST rule.**

| Third open attempt | 2 s | `:758` |

  Fixed waiting per refreshed report when nothing fails = 5 + 1 + 2 + W + 5 + max(10, W) + 2 + 1 = **16 + W + max(10, W)** seconds, plus 3 s before extraction: W = 5 → 31 + 3 s; W = 10 → **36 + 3 s**; W = 60 → 136 + 3 s (RAN me s2, arithmetic over the code's own constants), plus Excel start/open times, twice per client with both reports.

- **History.** Configurable wait since `bd176bf` (shared - before the split on 30-10-2025).
- **Not a GST rule.**

#### A-R73 — When a refresh counts as successful · [GST RULE] · ⚠
- **What the code does.** A refreshed report's status is `success: True` only if ALL hold:
  1. no error dialog was found (A-R105) during the 5 checks or the final check;
  2. a sheet named `info` (any letter case) exists — else "Info sheet not found";
  3. its cell `BB2` is not `None` ("Cell BB2 is empty"), not blank after trimming ("Cell BB2 is blank"), not `0` / `0.0` ("Cell BB2 contains 0"), and its upper-cased text is not one of `#REF!`, `#VALUE!`, `#NAME?`, `#NULL!`, `#DIV/0!`, `#N/A`, `#NUM!`, `#ERROR!` ("Cell BB2 contains error: …");
  4. no error was raised on the way.
  Success message: `Validated - Client Name: <BB2>` (the code comment says BB2 holds the client name). A failed check sets the error text `Refresh validation failed: <reason>`, which REPLACES a dialog's text if both happened. The check cannot tell a value freshly loaded by the refresh from one already in the file (READ, HIGH). A COM error cell probably arrives as a large negative number such as `-2146826246`, which passes the check (RAN with fake sheets; that COM returns that number is MEDIUM). Whatever the status, the cells are read afterwards (A-R83), and a non-success status later turns every figure of that report into "Missing" (A-R89).
- **Where.** `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:638-685` (sheet `:645-648`, cell `:656`, checks `:659-678`, list `:675`, message `:681`); combined `:344-374`; extraction regardless `:187-188`.
- **Evidence.** READ; RAN (PQ: `_validate_refresh` with fake sheets — `None`, `''`, `'   '`, `0`, `0.0`, `'0'`, `'#N/A'`, `'#n/a'` fail; `'SomeName'`, `12.5`, `-2146826246` pass). RAN VERIFY-A-S45 (`v_validate.py`): the same results, and also `True` and `False` (a TRUE/FALSE cell) PASS (`Validated - Client Name: False`), and a workbook whose only sheet is not `info` gives "Info sheet not found".
- **History.** Since `edac6a3` (shared - before the split on 30-10-2025).
- **⚠** The sheet name and cell position follow the template layout. [GST RULE] conservatively: it decides whether a report's figures appear.

#### A-R83 — How the mappings are read · [GST RULE]
- **What the code does.**
  1. **At load time** (when the module is imported): for each output sheet and each mapping that has BOTH an input sheet and an input cell, the field name `"<output sheet>_<output column>"` with every space turned into `_` is filed as `CELL_MAPPINGS[report type][input sheet][input cell] = field name`. A second mapping of the same cell for the same report type and sheet would replace the first, so the first output column would always show "Missing" (RAN TRACE T4b; not the case today). A missing key in any entry stops the module (and Step 4) from loading. "Backward compatibility" in the comment is misleading: this IS the structure the extractor uses.
  2. **At extraction** (A-F23): for each input sheet of the report type, the sheet is looked for by EXACT name, capitals and spaces included (`diff - gstr-1` is not `Diff - GSTR-1`, RAN TRACE T4); missing → each of its fields is stored as `None` (the bare cell keys are not added) and a warning is logged; found → each cell's `Range(cell).Value` is stored TWICE, under the field name and under the bare cell reference (e.g. `IMS_Reco_IGST` and `AA1`); a cell that cannot be read → both `None`; any other error with the sheet → its fields `None`. Every value is logged (`✓ <field> (<cell>) = <value>`) and listed again in an "Extraction summary" (A-R122). The count "Total values extracted: n" counts both keys, so it is about twice the number of cells. Any error outside the sheet loop → an empty result `{}` (the report's status from the refresh is unchanged, so a ✓ row can show only "Missing", A-R89).
  3. The extraction opens the copy in a second, HIDDEN Excel (`Dispatch`, `Visible = False`, `DisplayAlerts = False`); the log says "Opening file in read-only mode" / "✓ File opened in read-only mode" but the file is opened normally, not read-only (READ, HIGH); it is closed without saving.
- **Where.** Builder `power_query_extractor/config/cell_mappings.py:260-278` (condition `:270`, field name `:276`, filing `:277`); extraction `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:527-636` (hidden Excel `:533-539`, "read-only" texts `:541-543`, mappings `:546`, exact sheet `:564-568`, missing sheet `:570-576`, two keys `:584-588`, cell error `:591-594`, sheet error `:596-601`, summary log `:603-611`, `{}` on error `:615-617`, clean-up `:618-636`).
- **Evidence.** READ; RAN (TRACE T4 Part B2 through an openpyxl-backed stand-in for COM — it can only show values cached in the file, so a never-calculated formula reads as empty there while real Excel would compute it; TRACE T4b).
- **Note.** Excel error cells (`#N/A` …) probably arrive through COM as large negative whole numbers and would be written as numbers (MEDIUM, cannot be tested here; how to check: put `=NA()` in a mapped cell and run Step 4).

#### A-R88 — Which extracted value goes into a column · [GST RULE]
- **What the code does.** For each configured column of a report whose status is success and that has no calculation:
  1. walk the stored values in the order they were stored (sheets in `CELL_MAPPINGS` order, inside a sheet the field name then the cell reference) and take the FIRST key that CONTAINS the column title as a piece of text;
  2. only if that gave nothing (`None`) look up the exact key `"<sheet name>_<column title>"` with spaces → `_`.
  Column titles with a space (`Diff IGST`, `IGST Diff`, `Table 6J Match`, …) can never be contained in the underscore field names, so they always fall through to step 2 and show the configured cell. The one-word titles `IGST`, `CGST`, `SGST` of `IMS Reco`, `Extra In Purchase` and `Extra In GSTR2B` are contained in `GSTR-3B_Difference_Diff_IGST` etc., which are stored first — so those nine columns show J15/K15/L15 (RAN: 13 of 22 columns as configured, 9 cross-wired). This is a technical mismatch between configuration and code; which cell is right is the author's call (see the warning box in 5.11).
- **Where.** `power_query_extractor/core/data_consolidator.py:137-150` (substring loop `:142-145`, exact key `:147-150`).
- **Evidence.** READ; RAN (me s1; TRACE T4 Part E; XL E3; registry check2.py).
- **History.** The lookup is unchanged since `edac6a3`; the affected one-word columns arrived with `47a1492` (both shared - before the split on 30-10-2025), so the cross-wiring exists in A and B alike.

#### A-R90 — Number display · [GST RULE]
- **What the code does.** A value that is a whole or decimal number and is not 0 gets the cell format `#,##0.00` (two decimals, thousands separators); the stored value keeps full precision (no rounding). `True` counts as a number (Python treats it as 1) and gets the format; 0 and `False` keep the general format; a number stored as TEXT in the report (e.g. `'1,234.00'`) is copied as text with no format, so Excel will not add it up (RAN TRACE T4 obs 4).
- **Where.** `power_query_extractor/core/data_consolidator.py:160-162`.
- **Evidence.** READ; RAN (TRACE T4 Part D).
- **Note.** Tagged [GST RULE] because it is display rounding of figures; nothing is judged.

#### A-R96 — Excel or openpyxl for Step 3 reports
- **What the code does.** When `core/excel_handler.py` is loaded: if `platform.system() == 'Windows'` AND both `import win32com.client` and `import pythoncom` succeed → `USE_WIN32COM = True` (INFO `Using win32com for Excel operations (Power Query support)`), else a WARNING `win32com not available. Install with: pip install pywin32` (Windows only). Reports are then built through Excel (A-R97) or, otherwise, with openpyxl, logging WARNING `Not on Windows - Power Query may not be preserved!` (also printed on Windows without pywin32) and `Using openpyxl - Power Query content may be lost!`. openpyxl saving drops the Power Query part (`customXml/item*.xml` with `DataMashup`) and macros, and the run still reports success (RAN XL E1, CORE exp5, EXT t6). No check for a DataMashup part exists. On Windows, start-up refuses to run without pywin32 (A-R124), so in normal office use the COM path runs (MEDIUM — it depends on how the app is started).
- **Where.** `core/excel_handler.py:19-28` (switch), `:89-102` (choice; warning `:98`), `:267` (warning).

#### A-R97 — Step 3 Excel session (per report)
- **What the code does.**
  1. `pythoncom.CoInitialize()`;
  2. `GetActiveObject("Excel.Application")` FIRST — i.e. the user's own running Excel (INFO `Using existing Excel instance`) — else `Dispatch("Excel.Application")` (INFO `Created new Excel instance`; `Dispatch` itself may attach to a running Excel — MEDIUM);
  3. `Visible = False`, `DisplayAlerts = False`, `ScreenUpdating = False` (applied to the user's Excel too, hiding it);
  4. staging copy (A-R98), open (A-R101), find the sheet (A-R58), write (A-R56), `Save()`, `Close(SaveChanges=True)`, 0.5 s, copy to the Version folder;
  5. `finally`: if a workbook is still open, `Close(SaveChanges=False)` (errors ignored); then `ScreenUpdating = True` and `DisplayAlerts = True` OUTSIDE any protection (if Excel has died these raise and the rest of the clean-up is skipped — RAN with fake objects, CORE exp6); then `Quit()` ALWAYS, because the "Don't quit if Excel was already open" test looks at `self.excel_app`, which is never set (so the user's own Excel is quit too, with alerts switched back on just before); `CoUninitialize()` (errors ignored) while local variables still hold Excel objects; delete the staging file.
  `Visible` is never restored. One Excel start/attach and quit per report, two per client.
- **Where.** `core/excel_handler.py:56` (`excel_app = None`, never changed), `:104-260` (CoInitialize `:120`; attach `:123-128`; settings `:131-133`; save/close `:201-210`; copy `:215`; finally `:230-260`; the unprotected lines `:239-240`; the test `:242`; Quit `:244`; CoUninitialize `:249-252`); `__del__` `:58-64` never acts.
- **Evidence.** READ (cannot run COM here); control flow RAN with fake COM objects (CORE exp6: the fake "user" Excel was quit; with a dead Excel the finally block raised and the staging file stayed).
- **History.** Since `edac6a3` (shared - before the split on 30-10-2025).
- **Not a GST rule.** (Section 9 compares this with the author's Standard 12.)

#### A-R98 — Local staging of Step 3 reports
- **What the code does.** When the main window starts, the folder `%TEMP%\gst_excel_temp` (`tempfile.gettempdir()` + `gst_excel_temp`) is created; it is never removed. For each report: a stale file of the report's name there is deleted (errors ignored); the template is copied there under the REPORT's file name with `shutil.copy2`; Excel (or openpyxl) works on that local copy; the result is copied with `shutil.copy2` to the final path in the Version folder (an existing file there is overwritten without warning; a copy broken half-way leaves a partial file and returns failure); the staging file is deleted (best effort; it is left behind when the COM clean-up raises, A-R97). If `%TEMP%` is unusable, the folder creation raises and the window cannot start. Two copies of the program building the same report name in the same minute would share a staging file (LOW).

#### A-R100 — "Already open" detection
- **What the code does.** Before opening a file, both Excel users ask the Excel they hold for its open workbooks and reuse the first whose `FullName`, made absolute, equals the file's absolute path (`Path` equality — case-insensitive on Windows). A drive-letter path and a UNC path to the same file do not match; a workbook open in ANOTHER Excel process is not seen; a OneDrive/SharePoint workbook (web address) never matches. Errors while looping are not caught here. Step 3's staging file is normally never open, so the branch matters mainly for Step 4 (MEDIUM).

#### A-R101 — Step 3 open with one fallback
- **What the code does.** Missing file → `FileNotFoundError`. "Already open" → reuse (A-R100). Then `Workbooks.Open(<path>)` with no options. If that fails and the error text contains `-2147352567` (a general "exception occurred" code — MEDIUM on the meaning) or the word `path` (any case), or the path is longer than 218 characters, the 8.3 short path is tried (Windows `GetShortPathName`; skipped if it equals the long path, as it does where short names are switched off); otherwise — or if that also fails — the FIRST error is raised again. No `IgnoreReadOnlyRecommended`, no `UpdateLinks`, no read-only check.
- **Where.** `core/excel_handler.py:324-369` (conditions `:355-356`, short path `:359-366`, re-raise `:369`); `utils/helpers.py:580-590` (`get_short_path`).

- **Not a GST rule.**

#### A-R102 — Step 4 open with several fallbacks
- **What the code does.**
  1. Missing file → log `❌ File does not exist` and `FileNotFoundError`.
  2. Read 1 byte as an access test (failure → log and raise).
  3. Already open in this Excel → reuse (`📌 File already open, using existing workbook`).
  4. If the path is longer than **218** characters ("Excel's typical limit"): `/` → `\`, then prefix `\\?\` (local) or `\\?\UNC\` (network) — Windows' extended-length form; whether Excel accepts it is not sure (LOW).
  5. Attempt 1: `Workbooks.Open(<path>)`.
  6. Attempt 2: close WITHOUT SAVING every workbook in that Excel whose file NAME (not full path) equals this file's name, wait 3 s, open again (in a borrowed user Excel a different workbook with the same name would lose its unsaved changes — MEDIUM).
  7. Attempt 3: wait 2 s; try the 8.3 short path if different (any error there, even a failed open, is reported only as `Could not get short path`); then, if the extended prefix was added, open the plain path; otherwise `Open(Filename=<path>, UpdateLinks=0, ReadOnly=False, IgnoreReadOnlyRecommended=True, Notify=False)`.
  8. All failed → `❌ All attempts failed. Final error: …`; for `-2147352567` a list of likely causes (file open in another program, corrupted, path too long, OneDrive/SharePoint sync) and, over 218 characters, `📋 Path length is definitely an issue!` / `Consider enabling long path support in Windows`; the error is raised.
  `workbook.ReadOnly` is never checked after opening.
- **Where.** `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:687-799` (missing `:692-694`; access `:697-703`; reuse `:709-712`; prefix `:720-732`; attempt 1 `:735-741`; attempt 2 `:744-753`; attempt 3 `:756-783`; failure `:784-799`).
- **Evidence.** READ; RAN with a fake Excel (PQ: a 232-character path → two `\\?\` opens, then the plain path, then the error re-raised).
- **History.** Since `edac6a3` (shared - before the split on 30-10-2025).
- **Not a GST rule.**

#### A-R103 — Step 4 Excel sessions
- **What the code does.** Two separate sessions per report, both with `Dispatch` (not a private `DispatchEx`): the refresh session is visible and maximised (A-R71) and saves; the extraction session is hidden, alerts off, closes without saving and quits. Each starts with `CoInitialize` and ends in `finally` with `Close`, `Quit` and `CoUninitialize`, every error swallowed; `CoUninitialize` runs while the local variables still hold the Excel objects. Four Excel starts/attaches per client with both reports. If `Dispatch` attaches to the user's own Excel, that Excel is maximised, typed into and then quit with alerts off (unsaved user work may be closed without saving — MEDIUM, not testable here). Step 3 (`GetActiveObject`/`Dispatch`) and Step 4 (`Dispatch`) can end up driving the same Excel when run at the same time (MEDIUM).

- **History.** Since `edac6a3` (shared - before the split on 30-10-2025).

#### A-R105 — Error-dialog handling · ⚠
- **What the code does.**

#### A-R109 — One directory listing per scan, reusing its file details
- **What the code does.** The source folder is listed ONCE with `os.scandir`; each entry's cached details (size, type, dates) are reused for the checks of A-R8/A-R9 and for the file record (`get_file_info(path, stat)`), so the only per-file network read left is the 8-byte signature (A-R10). The code comments give the motivation: on the office share each extra existence check or `stat` was a separate round-trip (~45 ms for a Setup check, ~270 ms per file open over the VPN). A listing error throws away everything already listed and returns an empty list, which the screen then reports as "No valid GST files found".

#### A-R141 — Progress and ETA
- **What the code does.** The bar (0-100) = client index ÷ number of clients × 100; within a client, copying fills the first half of its share (`+ files done ÷ files × 50 ÷ clients`) and report creation starts at the second half (`+ 50 ÷ clients`); the summary step shows 95 and the end 100. Labels: `📊 Progress: X.X%` and the current operation, e.g. `Client i of n: <client> | ETA: <eta>`, `Client i/n: Creating folders | ETA: …`, `Client i/n: Copying <file> | ETA: …`, `Client i/n: Creating Excel reports | ETA: …`, `Creating summary report | ETA: …`, `Processing complete | Total time: Mm Ss`. ETA: `Calculating...` for the first client, then remaining ÷ (done ÷ elapsed) shown as `Ns`, `Mm Ss` or `Hh Mm`; the tracker advances by 0 for the first client and 1 for each later one, so while client i is being worked on it counts the i − 1 clients already finished (right for an even workload), but the last client is never counted: it ends at total − 1 (RAN me s3: 3 clients → final count 2 of 3), and the summary step therefore shows a non-zero ETA; with one client it shows `Unknown`. [Corrected during self-review - originally stated "so it is always one client behind", but Section 3 `A-F17` (RAN t16 with a fake clock: "ETA: 3m 0s" at client 2 and "1m 30s" at client 3, both right, then "2m 15s" at the summary step) revealed that the count is one behind only at the end; READ `gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:235-236, 457`, `utils/helpers.py:485-510`]
- **Where.** `gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:203, 235-241, 251-252, 266-269, 287-289, 457-459, 478-482`; `utils/helpers.py:476-523`; `gui/utils/ui_helpers.py:35-40`.
- **Evidence.** READ; RAN (me s3: `format_duration` 59.9 → `59s`, 61 → `1m 1s`, 3661 → `1h 1m`, 90061 → `25h 1m`).

#### A-R157 — Shortened paths in the status bar
- **What the code does.** `truncate_path(path, 60)`: paths of 60 characters or fewer unchanged; a path of two parts or fewer → `...` + the last 57 characters; otherwise `<first part><sep>...<sep><last part>` when `60 − len(first) − len(last) − 8 > 0`, else `...<sep><last part>` — which can be LONGER than 60 when the last part is long, and doubles the separator when the first part is a root such as `C:\` (RAN TRACE T8 §7: `//.../long.xlsx`). The separator is the running system's; on Linux a Windows-style path counts as one part (RAN me s3: both 85-character examples became `...` + last 57). Used for `Source: …` and `Target: …` after a Browse.
- **Where.** `utils/helpers.py:394-416`; used `gui/handlers/file_handler.py:24, 54`.
- **Evidence.** READ; RAN (me s3; CORE exp3; TRACE T8 §7).

### 5.18 UNREGISTERED rules found while checking

The registry lists every rule above. While checking the code for this section, three further decisions turned up that the registry does not name as rules. They are described here under the label the audit conventions require; none is a GST rule.

#### U1 — UNREGISTERED: Step 3 per-file log line names the file TYPE, not the folder
- **What the code does.** After each client's copies, one line per SUCCESSFUL copy is logged: `📁 <ORIGINAL file name> → <file type> folder`, e.g. `📁 GSTR3B-Alpha Test Traders-Maharashtra-Apr.xlsx → GSTR-3B Export folder`, `… → IMS Reco folder`, `… → Annual Report folder`. The words are the TYPE text (A-R26), not the real destination (`GSTR3B`, `ITC`, the Version folder itself, A-R41), and the name is the original, not the cleaned copy name (A-R48). Failed and skipped copies get no line.
- **Where.** `gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:281-284`.
- **Evidence.** READ; RAN (TRACE T6 run 1 GUI log: `AnnualReport-… → Annual Report folder` while the file went into `Version-211026 1030`).
- **Why it matters.** A reader of the log would look for folders that do not exist; technical only.

#### U2 — UNREGISTERED: Step 4 run log and progress format
- **What the code does.** At Start the Step 4 log is CLEARED, then: a line of 60 `=`, `PROCESSING STARTED`, `Wait Time: <N> seconds`, `File Suffix: <text>`, 60 `=`; per client `📋 Processing <client> - Reports: ITC, Sales` (only the ticked ones), the processor's own lines (indented by two spaces, A-R122), then per report `✅ <ITC|Sales> Report - Refreshed successfully` (also shown when Skip Refresh merely reused a file), or `⚠️ <ITC|Sales> Report - <error>` plus `(Data extracted despite error)` when values came back, or `⏭️ <ITC|Sales> Report - Skipped` when not ticked; then `📊 Creating consolidated report...`, `✅ Processing complete!`, `📄 Report saved: <name>`, `📂 Location: <folder>`, or `❌ Error: <e>`. Each line is `[HH:MM:SS] <message>` (time taken when the event happened), coloured by tag: info `#000000`, success `#28a745`, warning `#ffc107`, error `#dc3545` (the box is Consolas 9 on `#f8f9fa`, 20 lines high, stays editable, never trimmed). Progress: client index ÷ number of clients × 100 with `Processing <client>`; 95 with `Creating consolidated report`; 100 with `Processing complete`; after the run 0 with `Ready`. (Compare the Step 3 log, A-R140, which uses different colours.)
- **Where.** `power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:875` (clear), `:888-892` (header; the two Tk values are read from the worker thread here), `:907-911`, `:918-938`, `:941-950`, `:958`, `:985`, `:1012-1029`; colours `:568-571`; box `:543-556`.
- **Evidence.** READ; RAN (PQ gui_probe with a stub processor).

#### U3 — UNREGISTERED: Order of clients in each step
- **What the code does.**
  - **Step 2 table:** clients appear in the order their FIRST recognised file appears in the scan's path-sorted list (the client dictionary keeps insertion order; A-R57 sorting).
  - **Step 3:** ticked clients are processed in table order (the selection dictionary is filled in table order).
  - **Step 4 list:** client folders appear in the order the file system lists them — no sorting (alphabetical on a Windows NTFS disk as a rule, arbitrary elsewhere: RAN me s1 and PQ on Linux showed `Beta…` before `Alpha…`).
  - **Consolidated workbook rows:** the Step 4 processing order, i.e. the Step 4 list order of the ticked clients.
- **Where.** `core/file_parser.py:233` (client created on first file), `utils/helpers.py:361` (sort); `gui/handlers/client_handler.py:30, 46, 165`; `power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:638, 688, 849`; `power_query_extractor/core/data_consolidator.py:104`.
- **Evidence.** READ; RAN (me s1; PQ scan probe).
- **Why it matters.** A rebuild that sorts clients would change the visible order of the Step 4 list and of the consolidated workbook; technical only.

The remaining Setup help texts, exactly (`gui/tabs/setup_tab.py:73-133`), because several of them describe rules and some disagree with the code:

| Key | Text | Agrees with the code? |
|---|---|---|
| `CHECKLIST_HELP['source']` | "The folder holding the GST files you received. They are read from here and copied into the target folder - nothing here is moved, renamed or deleted." | yes (A-R47, RAN TRACE T6) |
| `CHECKLIST_HELP['itc']` | "Your ITC report template (.xlsx / .xltx). A copy is made per client and its Links sheet is filled in, so the template itself is never modified." | yes for "never modified" (copies only); the checklist also accepts `.xltm`/`.xlsm` (A-R52) |
| `CHECKLIST_HELP['sales']` | "Your Sales report template (.xlsx / .xltx). Used the same way as the ITC template - copied per client, never modified." | as above |
| `CHECKLIST_HELP['target']` | "Where the organised folders and generated reports are created. Each run adds a new timestamped folder, so previous runs are left untouched." | only for Fresh runs in a new minute (A-R43) |
| `BROWSE_HELP` | "Pick the folder containing the GST files to organise" / "Pick your ITC report template file" / "Pick your Sales report template file" / "Pick where the organised output should be created" | yes |
| `WORKFLOW_HELP` | see A-R154 | "Fast - no Excel automation involved" disagrees on Windows with pywin32 |
| `PROCESSING_HELP` | see A-R43 | Resume "skipping files that are already in place" holds only within the same minute |
| `CLIENT_NAME_HELP` | "Adds the client's name to the folders inside each version folder, e.g. 'ITC (ABC Pvt Ltd)' instead of just 'ITC'. Leave off if paths are getting long - Excel stops opening files beyond about 218 characters." | real names use underscores (A-R39); 218 ⚠ (A-R104) |
| `LENGTH_HELP` | "Longest client name allowed in a folder name before it is shortened. Lower values keep paths shorter, which matters on a network share: Excel cannot open files whose full path exceeds roughly 218 characters." | applies to the Level-2 folder only (A-R36) |
| `SCAN_HELP` | "Read the source folder and work out which client each file belongs to. Read-only - nothing is copied or changed. Results appear on Step 2." | yes (the scan only reads) |
| `RESCAN_HELP` | "Clear the current results and read the source folder again. Use after adding or renaming files." | yes; it also clears the data a running Step 3 is using (A-R60) |

### 5.20 Rules that exist in several places with different values

| Concern | Place → value | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Which Excel file extensions count | `utils/helpers.py:327` scan `.xlsx .xls .xlsm`; `utils/helpers.py:299` check `.xlsx .xls .xlsm .xltx .xltm`; patterns `utils/constants.py:15-55` `.xlsx .xls` only; `utils/constants.py:196` (dead) `.xlsx .xls .xlsm` | `.xlsm` is listed but never recognised; `.xltx`/`.xltm` pass the second check but never reach it (A-R8) |
| Which template extensions count | dialogs `gui/handlers/file_handler.py:31, 42` `*.xltx *.xlsx`; checklist `gui/utils/setup_validation.py:21` `.xlsx .xltx .xltm .xlsm`; gate `gui/handlers/file_handler.py:143-149` any; help `gui/tabs/setup_tab.py:77, 80` ".xlsx / .xltx"; dead `utils/constants.py:197` `.xlsx .xltx .xltm` | five different answers (A-R52, A-R53) |
| Excel file signatures | `utils/helpers.py:264-265` (used); `utils/constants.py:199-202` (dead) | same bytes typed twice (A-R10, A-R15) |
| Private → Pvt, Limited → Ltd | `utils/helpers.py:91-93` (underscores turned into spaces first); `utils/helpers.py:624-625` (no such step) | `X_Private_Limited` is abbreviated in file names but not in the Level-2 folder (A-R19) |
| The client name | as written (key, text report, table); abbreviated and cut to the length setting (Level-2 folder, Step 4 and consolidated "Client Name"); cleaned with underscores, full length (copies, Level-4 suffix, report names) | three forms of one name (A-R17, A-R35, A-R20) |
| State: code or text | code in the key, Level-2 folder, report names; text in the text report, table, summary, copied file names | (A-R23) |
| Type texts (`GSTR-2B Reco` …) | `utils/constants.py:68-75` and literals at `core/file_parser.py:267, 359`, `core/file_organizer.py:306-311`, `core/excel_handler.py:625, 636, 647, 661, 677, 693` | consistent today; a rename needs about 15 edits (A-R26) |
| Run folder patterns | `utils/constants.py:82, 84` (`Annual Statement-{timestamp}`, `Version-{timestamp}`); literals `power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:623, 641`; literal prefix `core/file_organizer.py:179` | same text typed three times (A-R32, A-R38, A-R42) |
| "Newest" run folder | Re-run/Resume: newest FOLDER by date modified (`core/file_organizer.py:177-184`); Step 4: newest ENTRY (files too) by date modified (`power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:623-631`) | a newer FILE named `Annual Statement-…` breaks only Step 4 (A-R42, A-R43) |
| Maximum client name length | 35 at `gui/main_window.py:93`, `core/file_organizer.py:30, 42`, `utils/helpers.py:620`, `gui/tabs/setup_tab.py:436, 614-615`, `gui/main_window.py:386-387`; arrows 15-100 (`gui/tabs/setup_tab.py:440`) | same default in seven places (A-R36) |
| Long-name warning limit | per-client toggle: fixed 10 (`gui/handlers/client_handler.py:191`); Start: the length setting, fallback 10 (`gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:92-97`) | two different thresholds for one concern (A-R136) |
| Default refreshed-file suffix | `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:51`; `power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:297`; `power_query_extractor/core/refresh_naming.py:14` | same text typed three times (A-R67) |
| `{timestamp}` token | writer replaces only the exact lower-case token (`power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:129`); reader lower-cases the pattern first (`power_query_extractor/core/refresh_naming.py:39`) | `{TIMESTAMP}` is understood when reading but not when writing (A-R67, A-R68) |
| Settings file path | `gui/utils/cache_manager.py:15`; `power_query_extractor/extractor_main.py:41`; `power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:118` | same path typed three times; the extractor also reads three current-folder files and three extra keys nobody writes (A-R114, A-R118) |
| Wait time | default 10 at `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:50` and `power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:270`; range 5-60 only on the box's arrows | a typed 0 is accepted (A-R72) |
| "Missing" text | option `power_query_extractor/config/cell_mappings.py:252`; fallback literal `'Missing'` at `power_query_extractor/core/data_consolidator.py:129, 154` | consistent today (A-R89) |
| Sheet-name matching | Links: any case, COM also "contains link" or creates one (`core/excel_handler.py:167-183`), openpyxl any case only (`:289-293`); `Info`: any case (`power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:646`); extraction sheets: EXACT, case-sensitive (`power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:565`) | three matching rules (A-R58, A-R73, A-R83) |
| Getting an Excel | Step 3: `GetActiveObject`, then `Dispatch` (`core/excel_handler.py:123-128`); Step 4: `Dispatch` twice (`power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:218, 536`) | different acquisition rules; neither is a private `DispatchEx` (A-R97, A-R103) |
| Opening a workbook | Step 3: one 8.3 fallback (`core/excel_handler.py:324-369`); Step 4: extended paths, close-by-name, 8.3, "all parameters" (`power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:687-799`); both use the 218 threshold | deliberately different (comment `utils/excel_com.py:1-15`) (A-R101, A-R102, A-R104) |
| Excel visibility | Step 3 hidden (`core/excel_handler.py:131`); Step 4 refresh visible and maximised (`power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:225-227`); Step 4 extraction hidden (`:537`) | (A-R97, A-R71, A-R103) |
| Time-stamp formats | `DDMMYY HHMM`, `DDMMYY_HHMM`, `YYYYMMDD_HHMM`, `YYYYmmdd_HHMMSS`, `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`, `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM`, `HH:MM:SS` | seven formats (A-R33) |

### 5.23 Questions for the author

These are questions only the author can answer. The GST questions ask what is intended; they do not suggest an answer.

1. **[GST RULE] Which file feeds a report** when a client has two files of one type (two years, two IMS dates, or a Windows "(1)" copy)? Today the alphabetically first full path is used and the screen does not say which (A-R57).
2. **[GST RULE] Consolidated workbook, nine columns:** for "IMS Reco", "Extra In Purchase" and "Extra In GSTR2B", are the configured cells (`IMS_Reco` AA1/AD1/AG1, `ExtraInPurchase` O1/P1/Q1, `ExtraInGSTR2B` S1/T1/U1) the ones you want to see? Today those columns show `Diff GSTR-3B` J15/K15/L15 whenever those are filled (A-R80 to A-R82, A-R88).
3. **[GST RULE] After a failed refresh**, should the figures that were still read appear (perhaps flagged), or be replaced by "Missing" as now (A-R89)? Should the copy left by a failed refresh be kept, given that Skip Refresh later reuses it as a success (A-R69)?
4. **[GST RULE] `Info!BB2`:** is it filled by Power Query during the refresh in BOTH templates (so it is empty in an unrefreshed report)? If it already holds a value before the refresh, the check cannot detect a failed refresh (A-R73).
5. **[GST RULE] Periods:** should files of different periods or financial years ever sit in one source folder for one client? The code never looks at the period part of a name (A-R25).
6. **[GST RULE] State part of file names:** what do real names contain there — full names, short forms (`MH`, `J&K`), two-digit numbers? A number crashes client selection; unknown names get invented codes that can equal a real state's code (`Unknown Place` → `UP`) (A-R17, A-R22).
7. **[GST RULE] Expected types and GSTR-3B:** are the six expected types and the "any number of GSTR-3B files" rule still current (A-R26, A-R27)? Should "Clients with Missing Files" include clients that only have duplicates (A-R31)?
8. **Templates:** which format do you use (`.xltx`, `.xlsx`, `.xltm`, `.xlsm`)? What do the Links cells contain before the program writes (empty values leave them unchanged)? Do the queries read the whole GSTR3B folder (backups and a second client's files can land there)? Which extension do the queries add to the file stems (A-R52, A-R54 to A-R57, A-R46)? (Added during self-review, from Section 12C:) Do the queries read the folder paths only from the Links cells, or does any of them name the old folder names "GSTR-3B Exports", "Other ITC related files" or "Sales related files", which `7347383` replaced by `GSTR3B`, `ITC` and `Sales` (A-R39, A-R54, A-R55)?
9. **Resume:** is Resume meant to continue the interrupted run's own Version folder? Today it makes a new one every minute (A-R43).
10. **Folder-name length:** should the length setting also shorten the Level-4 suffix and the report names? Values of 8 or 9 and below drop the state code (A-R35, A-R36).
11. **Client names:** do real client names contain hyphens, dots ("Co.", "Pvt. Ltd."), leading digits, or two spellings ("Private Limited" / "Pvt Ltd")? Each behaves differently today (A-R7, A-R17, A-R20, A-R35).
12. **Excel on the office PCs:** which Excel version and UI language? Does anyone keep their own Excel open while Step 3 or Step 4 runs (both may borrow and quit it)? Is the 218-character limit still the figure you see (A-R71, A-R97, A-R103, A-R104, A-R105)?
13. **Step 4 batch:** do you ever need to refresh an OLDER `Annual Statement-…` batch? Today the newest by date modified is always used (A-R42).
14. **Step 4 settings:** should the wait time, the refreshed-file suffix and Skip Refresh be remembered between sessions? Have you ever changed the suffix (A-R67, A-R119)?
15. **Share and drive letters:** do all PCs reach the output share by the same drive letter, or by `\\server\…`? The reports store absolute paths (A-R56).
16. **Logs:** where should the log live, given that it receives client names and every extracted figure and is written into whatever folder the program was started from (A-R120 to A-R122)?

## SECTION 6: EDGE CASES AND DEFENSIVE CODE

### 6.0 How to read Sections 6 and 7

**What these two sections cover.** Project A (`goyal-sidhant/AnnualStatement_oldv1`, branch `main`, snapshot `bf2f1dd`, 27-07-2026; the Tkinter program that calls itself "GST File Organizer v3.0"). Section 6 lists every unusual situation the code deliberately handles ("edge case" = an input or situation at the edge of what is normal: an empty folder, a missing sheet, a blank value, a duplicate file) and lists every `try/except` block (a `try/except` block is the place where the program catches an error so that it does not stop). Section 7 lists what the code does NOT handle, numbered A-G1 onwards.

**Evidence markers.** Every statement about the code cites `file:line` at `bf2f1dd` (repository-relative; the scratch copy `/root/merge-scratch/A-copy` has the same line numbers). Older code is written `path:line@commit`.
- **READ** = established by reading the code.
- **RAN** = the code was executed on made-up inputs in a scratch copy. "RAN (me)" = re-run for this section on 21-10-2026 in `/root/merge-scratch/run/A-S67/` (scripts `scripts/r1_core.py` … `r7_extractor_scan.py`, outputs `out_r1.txt` … `out_r7.txt`; list in 7.12). "RAN (TRACE)", "RAN (XL)", "RAN (GUI)", "RAN (START)", "RAN (EXT)", "RAN (TEST)", "RAN (CORE)", "RAN (PQ)", "RAN (DCP)", "RAN (DOCS)" = run by the earlier readers; the short names map to note files in the registry's table "Notes referred to" (`/root/merge-scratch/audit/A_registry.md`, e.g. TRACE = `A_live_traces.md`, XL = `A_excel_pq_safety.md`, DCP = `A_dead_code_patterns.md`, DOCS = `A_older_docs.md`). "RAN (VERIFY)" = re-run by the verifier of this section on 21-10-2026 in `/root/merge-scratch/run/VERIFY-A-S67/` (see 7.12). Nothing that needs Excel through COM or Windows could run here (Linux, no Excel, no pywin32): those parts are READ only.
- Inferences carry **HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW** confidence. "NOT SURE" always comes with a way to check.

**IDs.** Features `A-F1` … `A-F31` and rules `A-R1` … `A-R157` are the registry's (`/root/merge-scratch/audit/A_registry.md`). Gaps are `A-G1` … `A-G79`, numbered in Section 7 in the order they appear; 7.10 lists them all in one table.

**[GST RULE] and ⚠.** Anything that decides a tax figure, which return / table / sheet / cell a figure or file belongs to, a state code, a period or a rounding is tagged **[GST RULE]**. For these, Sections 6 and 7 only say what the code does; they never say whether it is right. Values that can change over time (table numbers, template sheet names and cell positions, state lists, file-naming conventions of the portal, period texts and financial years used as examples, Excel's keyboard shortcuts, package and Python versions) carry **⚠** so the author can check them.

**Confidentiality.** No client name, GSTIN, PAN, real file name or figure appears here. Made-up names such as "Alpha Test Traders" and `<Client A>` are used; file-name PATTERNS the code recognises are quoted exactly because they are code.

**All commits after the split are "A only (after the split)"; the 12 commits `edac6a3` … `47a1492` are "shared - before the split on 30-10-2025".** Project A has one branch, `main`.

**Plain-English words used in Sections 6 and 7**

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `try/except` block, handler | The place where the program catches an error. "Handler" = one `except` part. A **bare `except:`** catches everything, including the Ctrl+C key. |
| logged | Written to the log file (`gst_organizer.log`, see A-F30); the user does not see it unless they open that file. |
| swallowed | Caught and ignored: nothing on screen, nothing in the log file. |
| re-raised | Caught, then passed on to the code that called it. |
| fallback | Instead of failing, the code continues with a substitute value or a second method. |
| worker thread | A second line of work running next to the window so the window does not freeze (Step 3 and Step 4 each start one). Tk (the window toolkit) should only be touched from the window's own thread. |
| daemon thread | A worker thread that is killed instantly, without any tidy-up, when the program ends. |
| COM / pywin32 | Windows' way for Python to drive Microsoft Excel; pywin32 is the Python package that provides it. |
| openpyxl | A Python library that reads and writes `.xlsx` files without Excel. When it saves a workbook it drops the Power Query part. |
| Power Query | Excel's data-import tool inside the ITC and Sales templates; "refresh" re-runs it. |
| staging file | A temporary local copy that is worked on and then copied to its final place. |
| mtime | A file's or folder's "date modified". |
| glob | A wildcard file search such as `ITC_Report_*.xlsx`. |
| Treeview | The client table on Step 2. |
| SendKeys | Pressing keyboard keys by program, into whatever window has the keyboard focus. |
| UNC path / mapped drive | A network path written `\\server\share\...` / the same share shown as a drive letter such as `Z:`. |
| 8.3 short path | The old DOS-style short form of a Windows path (for example `PROGRA~1` for `Program Files`); shorter, so it can get under a path-length limit. |
| `\\?\` prefix | A prefix Windows accepts in front of a path to switch off the usual 260-character limit ("extended-length path"). |
| CoInitialize / CoUninitialize | The two calls that switch COM on and off for one thread; every thread that talks to Excel must call them. |
| DataMashup | The hidden part inside an `.xlsx` file (`customXml/item1.xml`) where Excel keeps the Power Query queries. |
| pip | Python's own tool for downloading and installing packages such as openpyxl. |
| Tk variable (`IntVar`, `StringVar`) | The object behind a box or tick on screen that holds its current value; `IntVar` must hold a whole number. |
| KeyError / TypeError / AttributeError / TclError | Python's (and Tk's) names for kinds of failure: a key that is not in a table, a value of the wrong type, a missing property, an error inside Tk. They appear in the error text the user sees. |
| key tips | The letters Excel shows on the ribbon when Alt is pressed (Alt, A = Data tab; R, A = Refresh All in English Excel). |
| shell | The command-line interpreter that runs a typed command (on macOS/Linux `os.system` hands the text to it). |
| SMB / NAS / NTFS | SMB = Windows' file-sharing method for network folders; NAS = a network storage box; NTFS = Windows' own disk format. |
| coverage recorder | A tool that records which lines of the program the tests actually ran. |

### 6.8 Inventory of every `try/except` block

**Method (RAN, me).** An AST listing (AST = Python's own parse tree of a file) of the 43 non-test `.py` files (`/root/merge-scratch/run/A-S67/try_inventory.py`, output `inv2.tsv`), identical to the listing an earlier run of this task left in the same folder. Then every handler was read and its effect written down by hand (`scripts/gen_inventory.py`). Result: **143 `try` statements with 147 `except` handlers; 7 `try` statements also have a `finally` block** (`core/excel_handler.py:118` and `:270`; `gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:184`; `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:214` and `:532`; `power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:887`; `utils/dependency_installer.py:105`). There is no `try/finally` without an `except`. Tests are not counted. RAN (VERIFY): an independent AST count (`/root/merge-scratch/run/VERIFY-A-S67/inv.py`, `pairs.py`) gives the same 143 / 147 / 7 / 23 figures, the same 22 files and per-file counts, and the same 147 "try line → except line" pairs and function names as the tables in 6.8.2.

**Tags used in the tables.** **L** = logged to the log file; **S** = shown to the user (on-screen log or message box); **W** = swallowed (nothing anywhere); **F** = falls back (substitute value or second method) without stopping; **R** = re-raised or turned into another error. A handler can have several tags.

#### 6.8.1 Counts

| What the handler does | Handlers | Share |
|---|---|---|
| Swallowed: nothing on screen, nothing in the log (W) | 42 | 29 % |
| Falls back silently: substitute value, no log, no screen (F only) | 26 | 18 % |
| Logged only (L) | 16 | 11 % |
| Logged and falls back (L,F) | 29 | 20 % |
| Shown to the user (S, L+S, S+R, S+F) | 23 | 16 % |
| Re-raised / converted (L+R, R, S+R) | 15 | 10 % (4 of them also shown) |
| **Total** | **147** | |

So 68 of 147 handlers (46 %) leave no trace at all, and 124 (84 %) never show anything to the user. **23 handlers are bare `except:`** (they also swallow Ctrl+C): `core/excel_handler.py:63, 126, 235, 245, 251, 302, 597`; `gui/main_window.py:76, 173`; `power_query_extractor/core/data_consolidator.py:201, 427`; `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:269, 401, 408, 414, 444, 452, 471, 511, 624, 630, 635, 767`. 102 handlers catch `Exception`; the rest catch specific errors (`ImportError` ×3, `OSError` ×3, `TypeError` ×3, `tk.TclError` ×5, and single cases of `KeyError`, `ValueError`, `subprocess.TimeoutExpired`, `(OSError, ValueError)` ×2, `(ImportError, ValueError)`, `(EOFError, KeyboardInterrupt, OSError)`, `(tk.TclError, RuntimeError)`).

**Patterns (READ).**
- The core modules never show dialogs; only the GUI layer does (`gui/handlers/*`, `gui/main_window.py` (the close question), `power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py`, `launch_extractor.py`, `utils/dependency_installer.py`; READ, grep of `messagebox.`). `main.py` itself shows no dialog: its start-up errors go to the console only (`main.py:114-134`). Good separation. [Corrected during verification — originally listed `main.py` among the files that show dialogs and left out `gui/main_window.py`.]
- Five error styles coexist (DCP §2.1): status dictionaries `{'success': …, 'error': …}` (the whole extractor; `FileOrganizer._organize_single_file`), True/False returns (`safe_copy_file`, the report builders), None returns (`create_backup`, `create_organization_report`), raising (`scan_folder`, `FileOrganizer` set-up, both `_safe_open_workbook`s, `DataConsolidator.create_report`), and swallow-and-continue (the 42 W handlers).
- The Step 3 worker writes almost every problem only to the on-screen log (`gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:304-475`); the log FILE gets only exceptions (`:406, :524`). Step 4's `_log` always writes INFO to the file, even for "❌" lines (`power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:53-60`).
- No `sys.excepthook` or `threading.excepthook` exists anywhere (READ, grep): errors raised inside button callbacks after the window is up are printed by Tk on the console only (A-G30).

### 6.11 Rating of the defensive coding

**Overall rating: MODERATE** — the common cases are handled and the program rarely stops, but its error handling mostly hides problems instead of reporting them, and several realistic inputs produce wrong output without any warning. Confidence HIGH (147 handlers read one by one; the main failure paths re-run).

| Area | Rating | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Step 1-2: scanning and recognising files (A-F7 to A-F9) | MODERATE | Missing/empty/wrong-kind folders, tiny and fake files, odd letter case, duplicate markers and empty parts are all handled (6.1-6.6). But anything not recognised is dropped silently, hyphens and spelling variants split or misfile clients (A-G33 to A-G37), and number-looking names crash later steps (A-G25). |
| Step 3: organising files (A-F13) | MODERATE | Originals are never touched (RAN TRACE T6), copies are size-checked, existing files are handled per mode, one client's failure does not stop the others. But Resume does not resume (A-G10), name collisions merge or overwrite clients (A-G8), interrupted copies leave partial files (A-G11). |
| Step 3: building reports through Excel (A-F14, A-F15) | FRAGILE | A template without a Links sheet "succeeds" (A-G4); stale template cells stay (A-G5); the user's own Excel is attached to, hidden and quit (A-G54); the clean-up can fail before `Quit()` (A-G28); the openpyxl fallback silently strips Power Query (A-G7). |
| Step 4: refresh and extraction (A-F21 to A-F23, A-F26) | FRAGILE | Refresh by key presses and fixed waits; success judged by one cell; the workbook is saved even after an error; a failed copy is later trusted as refreshed (A-G2, A-G3); keys and dialog clicks reach other programs (A-G55). |
| Step 4: consolidated workbook (A-F24) | FRAGILE | 9 of 22 columns are filled from a cell other than the one their own configuration names (A-G1; a technical mismatch — which cell is meant is the author's call); one bad value or folder loses the whole run's results (A-G29). |
| Window, settings and start-up (A-F1 to A-F6, A-F27 to A-F31) | MODERATE | Tooltips, dark mode, wheel handlers and the settings loader are defensive; the start-up check explains missing packages. But no console → silent death (A-G22); odd settings files crash start-up (A-G24); text in number boxes stops saves and runs (A-G26); worker threads touch the window (A-G70). |

The March 2026 audit also said MODERATE (6.10). Since then the July 2026 commits (A only (after the split)) added real defences — the pywin32 guards (c463256), the start-up check and install offer (f363946, be6418c, a5ad487), local staging (12d505f), the re-entry guard and key fix (33d0baf), worker-message capture (0890022, c1f425e), the defensive tab lookup (bfcb24a) — but did not touch the silent-wrong-output paths listed above, most of which date from the shared code (edac6a3 … 47a1492, shared - before the split on 30-10-2025).
