## SECTION 7: EDGE CASES NOT HANDLED (GAPS AND VULNERABILITIES)

### 7.0 How to read this section

Each gap has an ID (A-G1 … A-G79), the place in the code, what happens, how the user notices (or does not), a severity, and the evidence. 7.10 lists all IDs in one table; 7.8 runs the "what would break if…" scenarios for every major feature and points back to these IDs.

**Severity scale used here.**
- **HIGH** — can silently produce wrong figures or wrong files, lose the user's work, damage a workbook, or stop normal use, in situations that happen in ordinary office work.
- **MEDIUM** — wrong, misleading or failed output in plausible but less common situations, or a significant obstacle the user can work around.
- **LOW** — cosmetic, rare, latent (needs a configuration change to bite) or only a maintenance trap.

Severity describes the technical consequence. For anything tagged **[GST RULE]**, only the mechanism is described: whether the rule itself is right is the author's decision. "Which cell is right" in A-G1 and similar items is likewise the author's call.

### 7.1 Missing validations that could silently corrupt data

#### A-G1 — The consolidated Step 4 workbook fills 9 columns from a cell other than the one its configuration names [GST RULE] ⚠

- **Where:** `power_query_extractor/core/data_consolidator.py:137-150` (lookup), fed by `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:581-588` (how values are stored), `power_query_extractor/config/cell_mappings.py:264-278` (field names built as `"<output sheet>_<column>"` with spaces turned into `_`) and `power_query_extractor/config/cell_mappings.py:156-228` (the three affected output sheets).
- **What happens:** for each output column the consolidator first takes the FIRST extracted value whose field name merely CONTAINS the column title (`power_query_extractor/core/data_consolidator.py:141-145`), and uses the exact field name only if that found nothing (`:147-150`). Titles with spaces ("Diff IGST", "IGST Diff", "Table 6J Match" ⚠) never match the underscore field names and fall through to the exact name as configured. The one-word titles "IGST", "CGST", "SGST" of the output sheets "IMS Reco", "Extra In Purchase" and "Extra In GSTR2B" match `GSTR-3B_Difference_Diff_IGST/CGST/SGST` first (the "GSTR-3B Difference" group is the first in the configuration). Result: those 9 cells show the values read from `Diff GSTR-3B!J15/K15/L15` instead of their configured cells `IMS_Reco!AA1/AD1/AG1`, `ExtraInPurchase!O1/P1/Q1`, `ExtraInGSTR2B!S1/T1/U1` ⚠. Only when the Diff GSTR-3B cell is empty does the configured value appear.
- **How the user sees it:** not at all — the workbook looks complete; the three sheets repeat the GSTR-3B difference figures client by client.
- **Severity:** HIGH (silent figures taken from cells other than the configured ones, in a delivered workbook).
- **Evidence:** RAN (me r2, made-up marker numbers: "columns OK 13 mismatched 9", each mismatch listed in `out_r2.txt`; RAN VERIFY: same 13 / 9 result on a fresh copy); also RAN (TRACE T4 Part E; XL E3; DOCS exp-3; registry check2.py). No test covers the consolidator (RAN TEST coverage). One more detail (READ): if the Diff GSTR-3B cell holds an empty TEXT ('') rather than nothing, the fallback at `:148` is skipped too and the column shows "Missing".
- **Related:** A-F24, A-R80, A-R81, A-R82, A-R88. The lookup dates from edac6a3; the three affected sheets were added in 47a1492 (both shared - before the split on 30-10-2025), so project B very probably carries the same defect (comparison later). Which cell should feed each column is the author's call; the code simply does not do what its own configuration says.

#### A-G2 — A failed refresh is saved under the "refreshed" name and later trusted as a good refresh

- **Where:** copy made before Excel opens it: `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:164`; workbook saved whatever the result: `:349`; failures returned as a status but the file kept: `:354-357, 376-393`; "last refreshed" read from that file's name and date: `power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:45-82, 759-808`; Skip Refresh reuses the newest such copy and marks it success: `report_processor.py:137-155`.
- **What happens:** every refresh first copies the report to `<stem>_Refreshed_<DDMMYY_HHMM>.xlsx`. If Excel then fails (cannot open, dialog error, BB2 check fails, Excel busy), that copy stays — either never refreshed (it still carries the ORIGINAL's date, because `shutil.copy2` keeps it) or refreshed with errors and saved anyway. The client list then shows its date as "Last Refresh", and the next run with "Skip Refresh" ticked reuses it with status success and "Skipped - Using existing refreshed file".
- **How the user sees it:** the first run shows ✗ for that report; on the next Skip-Refresh run the same report shows ✓ with the stale or partial figures.
- **Severity:** HIGH.
- **Evidence:** RAN (me r4, Excel stubbed: run 1 failure leaves `…_Refreshed_211026_0640.xlsx` dated 3 days earlier; "last refreshed" shows that old date; run 2 with Skip Refresh → `{'success': True, … 'Skipped - Using existing refreshed file'}`); RAN (TRACE T10). The Excel part is READ.
- **Related:** A-F20, A-F21, A-F22, A-R67, A-R69, A-R145.

#### A-G3 — The refresh cannot be confirmed: key presses, fixed waits, one test cell, save regardless

- **Where:** `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:258-293` (activate Excel, press Alt+A, R, A), `:297-330` (fixed waits), `:345-357` (BB2 check, save first), `:638-685` (`_validate_refresh`).
- **What happens:** no `RefreshAll`, no `BackgroundQuery = False`, no `CalculateUntilAsyncQueriesDone`, no "still refreshing" check exists (READ, grep). The time from the last key to the save is fixed: wait time + up to 5 s of dialog checks + max(10, wait time) s — 25 s at the default 10 s. The only proof of success is that `Info!BB2` is not empty, "0" or an error text ⚠ [GST RULE] (A-R73; described only); a value already in the file (from the template or an earlier refresh) passes. The workbook is saved before the check result is used.
- **How the user sees it:** a slow query or a refresh that never started (keys landed elsewhere, non-English key tips) is reported ✅ with old figures.
- **Severity:** HIGH.
- **Evidence:** READ (cannot run COM here). The author's Standard 12 (`rebuild_pipeline_FINAL.md:860-867`) records, as tested, that a save during an unfinished refresh stored the old data; this is a technical comparison, not a recommendation. The design note keeps the key-press method on purpose (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-25-merge-extractor-design.md:125-126`).
- **Related:** A-F21, A-R71 ⚠ (Excel key tips depend on version and UI language), A-R72, A-R73 [GST RULE ⚠ template cell position].

#### A-G4 — A template without a `Links` sheet produces no error

- **Where:** COM path `core/excel_handler.py:172-183` (falls back to any sheet containing "link", else ADDS a new `Links` sheet), success decided by `:218-221`; openpyxl path `:295-310` (writes nothing, returns True).
- **What happens:** the report is saved and counted as created. On the COM path the paths are written into a new, empty sheet the template's queries never read; on the openpyxl path nothing is written at all. A sheet called e.g. "Hyperlinks" would be filled instead of the real one.
- **How the user sees it:** "✅ Success: ITC_Report_….xlsx". The hint "Check if template has 'Links' sheet" (`gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:322-323, 396-397`) appears only when the function returns False, which never happens for this cause. Nothing checks the template before processing (`gui/handlers/file_handler.py:132-151`, `gui/utils/setup_validation.py:56-64`).
- **Severity:** HIGH (every report of the run is useless, reported as success).
- **Evidence:** RAN (openpyxl path: CORE exp5, EXT t6, DOCS exp-2 — `True`, nothing written); READ (COM path).
- **Related:** A-F14, A-F15, A-R51, A-R58, A-R99. The March audit said the error "surfaces during report creation" (doc line 667) — never true (7.9).

#### A-G5 — Links cells for file types a client does not have keep whatever the template holds [GST RULE]

- **What happens:** for a client without, say, an IMS Reco file, cells B10/B11 ⚠ of the ITC report are not touched, so the paths saved in the template (for example those of the client used to build the template) remain, and the template's queries read THAT file.

#### A-G6 — When a client has several files of one type, only the first in name order feeds the report, silently [GST RULE]

- **Where:** `core/excel_handler.py:628-630, 639-641, 650-652, 666-668, 682-684, 698-700` (`[0]`); order from `utils/helpers.py:361` (sorted by full path).
- **What happens:** the "first" file is decided by alphabetical order of the names: a Windows duplicate `x (1).xlsx` sorts before `x.xlsx` (space before dot), `01042025` before `31032025` (day first), `2023-24` before `2024-25` ⚠ (made-up examples of period text). The other files are copied but not linked. GSTR-3B is linked as a whole folder, so it is not affected.
- **How the user sees it:** the client shows "Has duplicates" / "Multiple … (2 files)" but no message says which file went into the report.
- **Severity:** MEDIUM (which file should feed the report is the author's rule; the gap is that the choice is silent and depends on spelling).
- **Evidence:** RAN (TRACE T3b, T6: the "(1)" copies were linked).
- **Related:** A-R27, A-R57.

#### A-G7 — Reports can lose their Power Query without anyone noticing (openpyxl fallback; start-up guard gap)

- **Where:** fallback choice `core/excel_handler.py:19-28, 90-102`; save that drops the query parts `:306`; start-up check `utils/requirements_check.py:44-60, 64-70` (only `find_spec('pythoncom')`, i.e. "a file of that name exists").
- **What happens:** on Windows, if pywin32 is present but cannot be imported (broken install, DLL problem), the start-up check passes, `USE_WIN32COM` becomes False and every report is built with openpyxl, which drops `customXml/item1.xml` (DataMashup), its rels and `xl/connections.xml`. Off Windows this is the normal path. No check for a DataMashup part exists anywhere.
- **How the user sees it:** only two WARNING lines in the log file ("Not on Windows - Power Query may not be preserved!", "Using openpyxl - Power Query content may be lost!"); the screen says "✅ Success". Step 4 can then not refresh those reports.
- **Severity:** HIGH consequence; likelihood on Windows LOW-MEDIUM.
- **Evidence:** RAN (XL E1: function returned True and the four parts were gone; XL E2: simulated broken `pythoncom` → check passes, fallback taken).
- **Related:** A-F1, A-F14, A-F15, A-R96, A-R124. Standard 12 (`rebuild_pipeline_FINAL.md:846-850`) describes the DataMashup check the code lacks (technical comparison).

#### A-G8 — Two different clients can end up in one folder and overwrite each other's files [GST RULE]

- **Where:** Level-2 folder name `utils/helpers.py:620-644` via `core/file_organizer.py:83-100`; copied file names `utils/helpers.py:68-126` via `core/file_organizer.py:271-290`; client key `core/file_parser.py:229-230`.
- **What happens:** the parser keys clients by the text as written, but folders and file names are made from cleaned text, so three things merge distinct parser clients into one folder:
  1. "Private Limited" and "Pvt Ltd" spellings of one name → two parser clients, ONE folder `… Pvt Ltd-GJ`; both Sales files clean to the same name, the second overwrites the first (in Fresh mode the first survives only as `…_backup_<time>.xlsx`; in Re-run mode it is simply gone). RAN (me r3: the file under the real name holds the "Pvt" version, the backup the "Private" version).
  2. Long names that agree in their first 32 characters (default limit 35) → the same `Gamma Sample Manufacturing Compa-MH` folder (RAN me r1, TRACE T6 §7). Step 4 then sees ONE client and refreshes one report of each kind, possibly ITC of one company and Sales of the other in the same row (RAN TRACE T9).
  3. On Windows, names that differ only in letter case → the same folder and the same report file name (READ, MEDIUM: Windows file names ignore case; reasoned, not run).
- **How the user sees it:** nothing; the per-client log says ✅ for both.
- **Severity:** HIGH (one client's data replaced by another's, silently).
- **Evidence:** RAN (me r3, me r1, TRACE T6 §7, T8 §1, T9); READ (Windows case).
- **Related:** A-F13, A-R17, A-R19, A-R35, A-R48 ([GST RULE]: the client key and the Level-2 folder name carry the state code, A-R17 and A-R35 in the registry; only the mechanism is described). The two different abbreviation routines (underscores handled in one, not the other, `utils/helpers.py:91` vs `:624-625`) add a further mismatch (RAN me r1: `Zeta_Private_Limited` → files `Zeta_Pvt_Ltd`, folder `Zeta_Private_Limited-DL`).

#### A-G9 — Repeating a run in the same minute overwrites earlier results; backups land inside linked folders

- **Where:** minute-resolution names `utils/helpers.py:25-35`; existing-file handling `core/file_organizer.py:276-287`; backups `utils/helpers.py:217-234`; report copies `core/excel_handler.py:215, 308`; summary `gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:462-469` → `core/excel_handler.py:402`; consolidated `power_query_extractor/core/data_consolidator.py:175-179`; refreshed copies `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:128-130, 164`.
- **What happens:**
  - Fresh twice in one minute → the same `Annual Statement-…` and `Version-…` folders; each copied file first backed up next to itself, then overwritten (RAN me r3 run 5). The backups `<name>_backup_<DDMMYY_HHMM>.xlsx` sit INSIDE the category folders; the GSTR-3B folder is linked as a whole (B2), so if the template reads every file of that folder the backups are read too (MEDIUM, depends on the template).
  - Re-run in the same minute → overwritten without backup.
  - Reports, the summary workbook, the consolidated workbook and refreshed copies → overwritten without backup; the summary then lists only the second run's clients (RAN TRACE T6 run 2: 5 clients → 1).
  - Two backups in one minute → the same backup name; the first backup is lost (RAN TRACE T8 §4).
- **How the user sees it:** no warning; earlier output silently replaced.
- **Severity:** MEDIUM.
- **Evidence:** RAN (me r3; me r2: second consolidated report in the same minute replaced the first — one file left; TRACE T6, T8); READ.
- **Related:** A-R32, A-R33, A-R38, A-R45, A-R46, A-R61, A-R67, A-R86.

#### A-G10 — "Resume" does not resume an interrupted run

- **Where:** new Version folder every run `core/file_organizer.py:102-108`; skip only if the destination exists `:283-287`; in-memory rename only on success `:233-246`.
- **What happens:** the Version folder is named after the CURRENT minute, so a Resume started a minute or more after the interruption creates a brand-new Version folder and copies everything again. Only a Resume in the same minute skips. In that same-minute case the skipped files keep the names they have in memory (`core/file_organizer.py:283-287` returns before the rename at `:233-246`): after a restart and a fresh scan these are the ORIGINAL names, so the reports' Links cells name files that are not on disk under that name whenever cleaning changed the name; within the same session the earlier run has usually renamed them in memory already (RAN me r3 run 3 shows cleaned names) (READ, MEDIUM).
- **How the user sees it:** the help text promises "Continue a run that was interrupted, skipping files that are already in place" (`gui/tabs/setup_tab.py:108-109`; label `utils/constants.py:187`); in reality a second full copy appears next to the first.
- **Severity:** HIGH (the mode does the opposite of its label; duplicates and misleading reports).
- **Evidence:** RAN (me r3: later-minute Resume → all files "Success" into `Version-211026 1045`; same-minute Resume → "Skipped"); RAN (TRACE T6 runs 4-5; EXT t12 for the wrong-name links).
- **Related:** A-F13, A-R38, A-R43, A-R48.

#### A-G11 — A failed copy leaves a partial file, is not shown, and the report then names a file that was never copied

- **Where:** `utils/helpers.py:199` (copy), `:213-215` (exception → False, destination not removed); `core/file_organizer.py:290-294`; `gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:282-284` (only successes are listed); `core/file_organizer.py:233-246` (rename only on success).
- **What happens:** if the share drops or the file is locked mid-copy, `shutil.copy2` raises; the half-written destination stays under the CLEANED name (the size check at `utils/helpers.py:202-208` only runs after a copy that did not raise). The file's in-memory name stays the original one, and the report's Links cell is written with that original name — which does not exist in the folder.
- **How the user sees it:** "✓ Organized N files" with N one short; no line names the failed file. Power Query may later read the truncated file.
- **Severity:** MEDIUM.
- **Evidence:** READ (a network drop cannot be simulated reliably here).
- **Related:** A-F13, A-F17, A-R47, A-R48.

#### A-G12 — An interrupted save leaves a broken workbook under the final name

- **Where:** openpyxl saves straight onto the target path: summary `core/excel_handler.py:402`, consolidated `power_query_extractor/core/data_consolidator.py:179`; report copies `core/excel_handler.py:215, 308`; Step 4 copies and Excel saves on the share `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:164, 349`; settings file rewritten in place `gui/utils/cache_manager.py:45-46`.
- **What happens:** nothing is written to a temporary name first and renamed. A failure in the middle of a save — a dropped share, a full disk (there is no free-space check anywhere, READ grep), a crash — leaves a truncated or empty file with the real name; the next run (or Step 4, which finds reports by name) uses it.
- **How the user sees it:** an error line for this run; a file that will not open later.
- **Severity:** MEDIUM.
- **Evidence:** RAN (me r2b: a consolidated save that failed half-way left `PQ_Extraction_Report_20261021_0640.xlsx` of 3010 bytes, which openpyxl cannot open: "There is no item named '[Content_Types].xml'"; RAN VERIFY: reproduced by a save that fails on a time-zone-aware value — a 3011-byte file under the final name, same error); RAN (EXT t8: a broken settings file silently loads as defaults); READ for the network cases.
- **Related:** A-F14 to A-F16, A-F21, A-F24, A-F27.

#### A-G13 — Scanning again while Step 3 runs changes the data the worker is using

- **Where:** Re-scan empties the shared objects `gui/handlers/file_handler.py:102-105` and Scan replaces them `:71-72`; the tree rebuild resets every per-client folder flag `gui/handlers/client_handler.py:49`; the worker reads `self.app.client_data[client_key]` each loop `gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:232` (outside the per-client protection), keeps the old variations list `:224`, and holds `client_folder_settings` by reference `:193`. Scan/Re-scan stay enabled during a run (`gui/tabs/setup_tab.py:585-591` enables them from the checklist only).

Correction: the older-documents notes (DOCS §1.7 G6) say such a KeyError "is caught and counted as a failed client"; the lookup at `gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:232` is before the per-client `try` at `:243`, so it ends the whole run (DCP B9 is right).

#### A-G15 — Step 4 may treat an earlier refreshed copy as the original report

- **Where:** `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:112-125` (`glob("ITC_Report_*.xlsx")`, first hit taken).
- **What happens:** the search also matches earlier `_Refreshed_` copies; the order is whatever the file system lists. If a refreshed copy comes first, the run refreshes a copy of a copy (`…_Refreshed_0900_Refreshed_1005.xlsx`), whose BB2 is already filled.
- **How the user sees it:** growing double-suffix names; possibly stale figures accepted.

#### A-G16 — The "Refreshed File Suffix" setting can make originals look refreshed, or refreshed files invisible

- **Where:** `power_query_extractor/core/refresh_naming.py:23-55`; name built `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:128-130`; box `power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:297-304` (no validation).
- **What happens:** the marker is the lower-cased text around `{timestamp}`. With `_R{timestamp}` the marker `_r` is inside every `itc_report_…` name, so every ORIGINAL counts as refreshed (RAN me r4: `True`); `_{timestamp}` likewise. A client whose name contains "Refreshed" (or starts with "V" under `_v{timestamp}`) has an original that Skip Refresh reuses unrefreshed. `{timestamp}` alone or an empty box → only the legacy marker is recognised, so the files written are never recognised; an empty box makes the copy target the original itself ("… are the same file", RAN me r4). `{TIMESTAMP}` in capitals stays literally in the name. Characters Windows forbids (`/ : * ?` …) are not checked.
- **How the user sees it:** "Last Refresh" dates that are really the original's date; Skip Refresh skipping work that was never done; a report that fails with "are the same file".
- **Severity:** MEDIUM.
- **Evidence:** RAN (me r4; TRACE T5).
- **Related:** A-F22, A-R67, A-R68, A-R69.

- **Where:** `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:584` (`Range(...).Value`); `power_query_extractor/core/data_consolidator.py:153-162`.

### 7.2 Error conditions that would crash the program or stop a whole run

#### A-G22 — Started without a console (e.g. `pythonw.exe`, a double-click association or a shortcut), the program dies silently

- **Where:** `main.py:17` — `sys.stdout = io.TextIOWrapper(sys.stdout.buffer, …)` runs when `main.py` is loaded, before logging is set up (`:20-27`) and outside every `try`.
- **What happens:** with no console `sys.stdout` is `None`; line 17 raises `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'buffer'`. No window, no message box, no log file (the log file handler is created only on line 24).
- **How the user sees it:** nothing happens when they start the program.
- **Severity:** HIGH for the author's Standard 13 launch style (`rebuild_pipeline_FINAL.md:1035`: "There is no console"); not triggered by `python main.py` in a console.
- **Evidence:** RAN (me: `main.py` loaded with `sys.stdout = None` → exactly that error; no `gst_organizer.log` created); RAN (START, EXT t11).
- **Related:** A-F1, A-F30, A-R127. `_pause` (`main.py:45-54`) would also fail under pythonw (`input()` raises `RuntimeError`, not caught) — unreachable today because line 17 fails first.

#### A-G23 — An unwritable start folder, or a read-only program folder, stops the program at start-up

- **Where:** log file in the CURRENT folder `main.py:24` (created when `main.py` is loaded, outside `main()`'s `try`); folders and placeholder files created in the PROGRAM folder at every start `main.py:29-43`.
- **What happens:** if the folder the program is started from cannot be written, `logging.FileHandler('gst_organizer.log')` raises before the program can show any message of its own — with a console, Python prints a raw traceback; without one, nothing is seen (READ; cannot reproduce here because the run is as root, MEDIUM). If the program folder is read-only (a shared, protected app folder) AND `logs`/`temp` do not exist there yet, `mkdir` of `logs`/`temp` raises inside `main()` → "💥 Critical error" on the console and exit 1 (READ). Once those folders exist, later starts pass, because `Path.mkdir(exist_ok=True)` (`main.py:37`) ignores the error for a folder that already exists; `logs` and `temp` are not in the repository (READ, `git archive` listing), so it is the first start in a new folder that fails (MEDIUM). [Corrected during verification — originally said a read-only program folder always stops the program.] Neither `logs` nor `temp` is ever used (READ, grep).
- **Severity:** MEDIUM.
- **Evidence:** READ; RAN (me: the log appears in the current folder, not in the program folder; EXT t11).
- **Related:** A-F1, A-F30, A-R120, A-R128. Standard 13 (`rebuild_pipeline_FINAL.md:1034, 1039-1040`) asks for the opposite placement (technical comparison).

- **Where:** `gui/utils/cache_manager.py:18-27` (whatever JSON is in the file is returned, not checked to be an object); `gui/main_window.py:375-389`.
- **What happens:** a file holding a JSON list (e.g. `[1, 2]`) → `AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get'` inside `GSTOrganizerApp()`; `"client_name_max_length": "35"` (text instead of a number) → `TypeError: '>' not supported between instances of 'str' and 'int'`. Both end at `main.py:130-134` "💥 Critical error". With a list, saving also fails for ever (`cache_manager.py:33-34`, START). (Added during self-review: an EMPTY list `[]` starts normally, because `if self.cache_data:` at `gui/main_window.py:375` treats it as "no settings", and then every save fails with "Error saving cache: 'list' object has no attribute 'get'" — RAN during self-review, `cache_shapes.py`. From Section 3 `A-F27`, marked "new" there:) a processing-mode value with other letter case (e.g. `"Fresh"`) is accepted at start-up, so no radio button shows as selected, and the next Step 3 run then stops with `ValueError("Invalid processing mode: …")` (`core/file_organizer.py:62-63`) — RAN (Section 3 `A-F27` step 8d), LOW.

### 7.3 Real-world input variations that are not handled

#### A-G33 — A hyphen inside a client or state name shifts the parts of the file name [GST RULE] ⚠

- **Where:** `utils/constants.py:15-55` — client and state are matched as `([^-]+)` ("anything without a hyphen"); first match wins `core/file_parser.py:82-128`.
- **What happens:** for GSTR-2B Reco, Sales Reco and Annual Report (whose last part is `(.+)`) the file is ACCEPTED under a wrong client and state: `GSTR-2B-Reco-Alpha-Test-Traders-Maharashtra-Q1.xlsx` → client "Alpha", state "Test", period "Traders-Maharashtra-Q1", key `Alpha-TES`. For IMS Reco, GSTR-3B and Sales the file is rejected as a variation. No warning in either case.
- **How the user sees it:** an extra client row (here "Alpha" in state "Test") and the real client "missing" that file.
- **Severity:** HIGH (misfiles a client's file silently).
- **Evidence:** RAN (me r1; TRACE T1 row 6, T6: `Gamma-SAM`).
- **Related:** A-R1 to A-R7.

#### A-G34 — `Sales-Reco-…` (hyphen instead of `SalesReco-`) is read as a Sales file of a client called "Reco" [GST RULE] ⚠

- **Where:** `utils/constants.py:39` (Sales pattern has four free parts).
- **What happens:** `Sales-Reco-Alpha Test Traders-Maharashtra-Q1.xlsx` → type Sales, client "Reco", state "Alpha Test Traders", start month "Maharashtra", end month "Q1".
- **Severity:** MEDIUM.
- **Evidence:** RAN (me r1; TRACE T1 row 37).
- **Related:** A-R4, A-R5.

#### A-G35 — One client spelled in several ways becomes several incomplete clients [GST RULE]

- **Where:** client key = client text exactly as written + state code, `core/file_parser.py:229-230` (case- and space-sensitive).
- **What happens:** `<Client A> Private Limited`, `<Client A> Pvt Ltd`, the same in capitals, or with a double space are separate clients, each "Missing N files"; the scan summary under-counts complete clients. Combined with A-G8 the Pvt/Private variants then share one folder and overwrite each other.
- **How the user sees it:** several rows for one company, each looking incomplete although all files were supplied.
- **Severity:** MEDIUM.
- **Evidence:** RAN (me r3: two keys for "Beta Demo Industries Private Limited" / "… Pvt Ltd"; TRACE T6: capitals → separate row "Missing 5 files").
- **Related:** A-R17, A-R19 ([GST RULE]: the client key = client text + state code, A-R17; described only).

#### A-G36 — State text written in other ways gets invented codes, which can collide with real ones [GST RULE] ⚠

- **Where:** `utils/helpers.py:592-618`; table `utils/constants.py:251-292` (39 names, 36 codes) ⚠.
- **What happens (described only):** names not in the table get the first letters of the first two words or the first three characters: "Unknown Place" → "UP" (same as Uttar Pradesh), "Jammu & Kashmir" → "J&", "J&K" → "J&K", "NCT of Delhi" → "NO", "New Delhi" → "ND", "TamilNadu" / "Tamil-Nadu" → "TAM", "Uttaranchal" → "UTT", a city such as "Mumbai" → "MUM", "27" → "27". The code goes into the client key, the folder name and the report names, so two spellings of one state make two clients, and two different unknown places with the same letters merge.
- **How the user sees it:** a WARNING line per unknown state in the log only.
- **Severity:** MEDIUM (which spellings and codes are acceptable is the author's rule).
- **Evidence:** RAN (me r1; TRACE T2).
- **Related:** A-R21, A-R22, A-R23.

#### A-G37 — Files the scan never looks at, and never reports

- **Where:** `utils/helpers.py:309-365` (one folder level, `os.scandir` at `:328`; extensions `:327`; regular file `:296`; size `:302-303`; signature `:275-287`); patterns accept only `\.xlsx?$` (`utils/constants.py:15-55`).
- **What happens:** silently dropped, with no count, no variation entry and (except read errors) no log line: files in sub-folders; `.xlsb`, `.xltx`, `.csv`, `.pdf`; files under 1024 bytes; files whose first bytes are not a ZIP/OLE signature; any ZIP renamed `.xlsx` passes. `.xlsm` files ARE listed but no pattern accepts them, so a correctly named `.xlsm` always becomes a "variation". A listing failure of the whole folder (share dropped, no permission) returns an empty list (`utils/helpers.py:363-365`) and reads exactly like an empty folder: "No valid GST files found".
- **How the user sees it:** files that "disappear"; or a scan that says there is nothing to do when the share was simply unreachable.
- **Severity:** MEDIUM.
- **Evidence:** RAN (me r1: of 10 entries only 3 listed; missing folder → `[]`); RAN (TRACE T1, T6, T8).
- **Related:** A-F7, A-F9, A-R8 to A-R10.

#### A-G38 — Near-miss file names are refused, and the hint offers only one guess [GST RULE] ⚠

- **Where:** `utils/constants.py:15-55`; hint `core/file_parser.py:288-306`.
- **What happens:** refused (RAN TRACE T1, me r1): a leading "(1) " for any type except GSTR-3B (`(1) Sales-…`); "Copy of …"; a leading space; `GSTR-3B-…`, `GSTR2B-Reco-…`, `IMS Reco-…`, `Sales Reco-…`, `Annual Report-…`; underscores instead of hyphens; an IMS date with 6 digits or written `01-01-2024`; a month with a year after a hyphen (`Apr-2024`). The hint is one guess from keywords ("claims" gets the IMS hint, A-R12), never two, although the code joins guesses with " or ".
- **Severity:** LOW-MEDIUM (the naming convention is the author's; the gap is the strictness and the silent counting).
- **Evidence:** RAN.
- **Related:** A-R1 to A-R7, A-R11, A-R12 ([GST RULE] ⚠: the file-name patterns decide which return type a file is, A-R1 to A-R7; described only — the naming convention is the author's).

#### A-G39 — No period or financial-year check: files of different periods are grouped and impossible dates accepted [GST RULE] ⚠

- **Where:** the period, month, date and year parts are stored in `metadata` (`core/file_parser.py:97-106`) and never read anywhere (READ, grep).
- **What happens (described only):** files of two years for one client are grouped together (then A-G6 decides which feeds the report); "13", "31022025", "99999999", "FY", "x" are accepted as periods or dates.
- **Severity:** MEDIUM (whether such checks belong in the tool is the author's rule).
- **Evidence:** RAN (TRACE T3; me r1: `99999999` accepted).
- **Related:** A-R25.

#### A-G40 — Client names containing dots are only partly cleaned, and the result depends on the Python version

- **Where:** `utils/helpers.py:76-77, 123-124` — everything after the LAST dot is treated as a file extension and put back unchanged; used for report names (`gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:292`) and the Level-4 suffix (`core/file_organizer.py:90`).
- **What happens:** "Omega Co. Private Limited" → `Omega_Co. Private Limited` (spaces and words after the dot untouched), so the report becomes `ITC_Report_Omega_Co. Private Limited_MH_….xlsx`. A name ending in a dot keeps the dot on Python 3.14 (`Mu_Test_Traders.`) but loses it on Python 3.11 and 3.13 (`Mu_Test_Traders`), so the same client gets different report names on PCs with different Pythons.
- **Severity:** LOW.
- **Evidence:** RAN (me: Python 3.11.17, 3.13.16 and 3.14.6 side by side; TRACE T2).
- **Related:** A-R20.

#### A-G41 — Long paths are not measured before folders and files are created ⚠

- **Where:** the 218-character figure appears only in fallbacks and help texts: `core/excel_handler.py:356`; `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:720, 795`; `utils/constants.py:85-90`; `gui/tabs/setup_tab.py:112-123`.
- **What happens:** with default settings a copied file's full path is at most `len(target) + 90 + len(file name)` characters in the `ITC` folder (EXT §3.7), `+ 92` in `Sales` and `+ 93` in `GSTR3B` (the longest category name); an Annual Report in the Version folder is `+ 86` (READ, arithmetic: separators + `Annual Statement-DDMMYY HHMM` 28 + Level-2 name up to 35 + `Version-DDMMYY HHMM` 19 + category 3/5/6). [Corrected during verification — originally "+ 90 at most" for every file.] Add the client name a third time when "include client name" is on, and ~22 characters (`_Refreshed_DDMMYY_HHMM`) for a refreshed copy. Nothing warns before the run; Excel/Power Query then fail on individual files deep inside the run. The comment at `utils/constants.py:85-90` says "Measured on a real run of 3030 files" the long category names gave a worst path of 235 characters with 27 files over the limit; the message of commit 7347383 (A only (after the split)), which shortened the names, gives the measured figures as a worst path of 270 characters with 1094 files (36 %) over ~218, and calls 235 / 27 the figures modelled with a shorter share root alone — so the code comment and the commit message disagree on what was measured (READ; which figure applies to the office is the author's to confirm). Windows' own 260-character limit applies to Python's copies unless long paths are enabled.
- **Severity:** MEDIUM.
- **Evidence:** READ (commit 7347383 message itself calls a path-length guard "the durable fix").
- **Related:** A-R39, A-R104.

#### A-G42 — Template file formats: `.xltx` saved as `.xlsx`, macro templates renamed, picker and checklist disagree

- **Where:** report always named `.xlsx` (`gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:298, 356`); template bytes copied under that name (`core/excel_handler.py:147, 154, 273, 279`); openpyxl keeps the template content type and drops macros (`:282`, no `keep_vba`); Browse filter `*.xltx *.xlsx` only (`gui/handlers/file_handler.py:31, 42`); checklist also accepts `.xltm`, `.xlsm` (`gui/utils/setup_validation.py:21`).
- **What happens:** on the openpyxl path an `.xltx` template gives an `.xlsx` file whose inside still says "template" (RAN XL E1, CORE exp5) — Excel commonly refuses such a file (MEDIUM, NOT SURE). On the COM path Excel opens the renamed template bytes; whether it complains or saves it as a template package is NOT SURE (LOW) — how to check: run Step 3 once with an `.xltx` template on Windows and open the report, or unzip it and look for `template.main` in `[Content_Types].xml`. A macro template typed into the box passes the checklist but can be neither picked in the dialog nor saved correctly under `.xlsx`.
- **Severity:** MEDIUM.
- **Evidence:** RAN (openpyxl path; RAN VERIFY: a made-up `.xltx` template gave a report whose `[Content_Types].xml` still contains `template.main`); READ (COM path).
- **Related:** A-F3, A-F14, A-F15, A-R52, A-R106.

#### A-G43 — Read-only or locked files are not detected

- **Where:** `shutil.copy2` copies the read-only attribute (`core/excel_handler.py:154, 215`; `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:164`); `Workbooks.Open` without `IgnoreReadOnlyRecommended` in the normal path (`core/excel_handler.py:349, 364`; `report_processor.py:737, 751, 766, 774`); `workbook.ReadOnly` never checked.
- **What happens:** a template marked read-only on the share gives read-only staging copies → `wb.Save()` fails → every report "Failed"; the staging file cannot be deleted either (`os.unlink` refuses read-only files on Windows). A report or refreshed copy open in someone else's Excel opens read-only and the save fails ("success: False"). README only tells users to "Close all Excel files" (`README.md:301, 314`).
- **Severity:** MEDIUM (MEDIUM-HIGH confidence on the `copy2` behaviour, documented Python behaviour; Excel's reaction untested).
- **Evidence:** READ.
- **Related:** A-R97, A-R101, A-R102. Standard 12 (`rebuild_pipeline_FINAL.md:857-859`) names the `IgnoreReadOnlyRecommended` / `ReadOnly` checks (technical comparison).

#### A-G44 — Excel set-ups the code does not expect ⚠

- **Where:** keys `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:282-292`; dialog words and button texts `:425-436, 506`; no check that Excel is installed (`utils/requirements_check.py:37-61` checks only pywin32); misleading hint `gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:322-323, 396-397`.
- **What happens:** (a) Excel in another UI language: the Alt, A, R, A key tips ⚠ and the English dialog words ("error", "cannot", "ok", "close", "yes") may not apply, so the refresh may not start and dialogs not be recognised (MEDIUM, NOT SURE — check on such a PC). (b) Excel not installed: `Dispatch` fails → every Step 3 report "Failed" with the hint "Check if template has 'Links' sheet" — the wrong cause. (c) The user's own Excel open: see A-G54. (d) A locked or busy desktop (screen saver, the user typing elsewhere): see A-G55.
- **Severity:** HIGH for (a) on such PCs; MEDIUM for (b).
- **Evidence:** READ.
- **Related:** A-F14, A-F15, A-F21, A-F26, A-R71, A-R105.

#### A-G45 — Step 4's choice of run folder and client list surprises in several real situations

- **Where:** `power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:622-668` (run folder = the `Annual Statement-*` ENTRY with the newest date modified; files count too); `core/file_organizer.py:184` (same rule for Re-run/Resume); old list kept on failure `power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:625-628, 665-668`.
- **What happens:** (a) writing anything into an older run folder (e.g. saving a summary there, which makes Excel write a temporary file) makes it the "newest", so Step 4 and Re-run/Resume silently switch to that older batch; (b) pointing the box at a run folder itself finds nothing ("No Annual Statement folders found") — the design note claims this "still works" (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-25-merge-extractor-design.md:87-89`); (c) a FILE named `Annual Statement-…` newer than the folders gives "Error scanning folder"; (d) in (b) and (c) the previous client list, the Start button and (in (c)) a changed output folder remain, so Start processes the old list. (Added during self-review, from Section 3 `A-F19`, marked "new" there, MEDIUM:) (e) inside each client folder only the NEWEST `Version-*` folder (by date modified) is looked at (`power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:641-648`), so a report that exists only in an older Version folder of the same client is not offered (its tick is disabled) — RAN (Section 3 `A-F19`, case "two Version folders"). (f) (Added during self-review, from Section 3 `A-F19`:) a run folder that has client folders but no `Version-*` folders clears the list to "No clients found" while the Start button keeps its earlier state (READ `:677-685, 756-757`).
- **How the user sees it:** the wrong batch's clients, or a list that does not match the folder in the box.
- **Severity:** MEDIUM.
- **Evidence:** RAN (me r7: all four cases; TRACE T3c; EXT t14; DOCS exp-4a).
- **Related:** A-F19, A-R42, A-R43.

#### A-G46 — Drive letters versus network paths

- **Where:** "already open" test `utils/excel_com.py:26-28` (`Path(wb.FullName).absolute() == abs_path`); Links folder values written exactly as chosen (`utils/helpers.py:418-422`; A-R56).
- **What happens:** a workbook open as `Z:\…` is not recognised when the code uses `\\server\share\…` (or the reverse), nor when it is open in another Excel process or from OneDrive (FullName is a web address) — it is opened again, possibly read-only (A-G43). Reports carry absolute paths: a report built on a PC that maps the share as `Z:` refreshes on another PC only if that PC uses the same letter.
- **Severity:** MEDIUM.
- **Evidence:** READ (MEDIUM: depends on how the office maps the share).
- **Related:** A-R56, A-R100.

#### A-G47 — Upper-case `.XLSX` reports are not found by Step 4 on case-sensitive file systems

- **Where:** `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:112-113` (`glob("ITC_Report_*.xlsx")`), while the list's tick test is case-insensitive (`power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:35-39`).
- **What happens:** on Linux (or a case-sensitive share) a hand-renamed `ITC_Report_….XLSX` makes the tick available but processing says "No ITC report found". On Windows `glob` ignores case (MEDIUM). The program itself always writes `.xlsx`.
- **Severity:** LOW.
- **Evidence:** RAN (TRACE T5).
- **Related:** A-R59, A-R66.

### 7.4 Performance bottlenecks with large or slow data

#### A-G48 — Both folder scans run on the window's own thread

- **Where:** Step 1 scan `gui/handlers/file_handler.py:71-72` → `core/file_parser.py:136-177`; Step 4 scan `power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:611-668` (glob + `stat` of every run folder and every Version folder + one listing per client).
- **What happens:** on a slow or VPN-connected share the window freezes until the scan returns (the commit message of 4f84ba9, A only (after the split), measured 2508 files in about 41 s after the parallel signature reads; the "about 11 minutes" before it is the message's own projection — "~677s cold sequential projection" — not a measurement). The progress text is set many times without a repaint (`gui/handlers/file_handler.py:67-68`), so "Scanning: … (n/N)" is not seen. A dropped share makes the window hang for the network time-out.
- **Severity:** MEDIUM.
- **Evidence:** READ; RAN (START: the label is not repainted during the scan).
- **Related:** A-F7, A-F19, A-R109, A-R110.

#### A-G49 — The Setup checklist checks network paths on the window's thread

- **Where:** `gui/tabs/setup_tab.py:521-529` (`Path(...).exists()`), forced at start-up `:156` and after every theme switch (`gui/main_window.py:188-194`), and 350 ms after typing stops (`gui/tabs/setup_tab.py:506-519`).
- **What happens:** with remembered paths on an unreachable share, each existence check can block the window for the network time-out — at start-up before the user can do anything.
- **Severity:** MEDIUM.
- **Evidence:** READ (MEDIUM: depends on the SMB time-out of the PC).
- **Related:** A-F4, A-R113.

#### A-G50 — Step 4 waits a fixed time per report and cannot be stopped

- **Where:** `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:185, 253-255, 264-276, 282-292, 297-302, 310-319, 326-330, 351, 363` (sleeps); no Stop button (`power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:328-340`, A-R143).
- **What happens:** at least about 36 s of fixed waiting per report at the default 10 s (+3 s before extraction), about 136 s (+3 s) at the 60 s maximum; four Excel starts or attachments and four quits per client (two per report); the refreshed copy is made share-to-share. 100 clients × 2 reports ≈ 2 hours of fixed waiting alone, with no way to stop except closing the window (A-G27). A typed wait of 5000 is accepted (A-G26).
- **Severity:** MEDIUM.
- **Evidence:** READ (arithmetic from the sleeps; XL §5.2).
- **Related:** A-F21, A-F23, A-R72, A-R103.

#### A-G51 — Step 3 starts or attaches to Excel twice per client and pauses 1 s per report

- **Where:** `core/excel_handler.py:104-260` (one Excel session per report), `:155, 210` (0.5 s sleeps).
- **What happens:** two Excel start/attach + quit cycles per client; with Excel taking a few seconds to start, a few hundred clients add tens of minutes. (Whether quitting is safe is A-G54.)
- **Severity:** LOW-MEDIUM.
- **Evidence:** READ.
- **Related:** A-F14, A-F15, A-R97, A-R112.

#### A-G52 — Logs grow without limit

- **Where:** Step 3 on-screen log never cleared (`gui/utils/ui_helpers.py:17-33`; `gui/tabs/processing_tab.py`); Step 4 writes a line for every second of waiting (`power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:254, 301, 311, 329`) and every extracted value (`:590, 603-611`) to both the panel and the log file; log files appended and never rotated (`main.py:20-27`; `power_query_extractor/extractor_main.py:12-19`).
- **What happens:** a long Step 4 run produces thousands of log lines per client; the Tk text widgets slow down and the log files grow for ever (and carry client data, A-G56).
- **Severity:** LOW.
- **Evidence:** READ.
- **Related:** A-F17, A-F25, A-F30, A-R122.

#### A-G53 — The install offer blocks the window while pip runs, and installs more than it says

- **Where:** `utils/dependency_installer.py:41-60` (`subprocess.run`, up to 600 s), `:121-134` (called on the window's thread; `requirements.txt` used whenever it exists).
- **What happens:** the "Installing…" window cannot repaint or respond for up to 10 minutes (Windows may show "Not Responding"); the output appears only at the end, although commit a5ad487 (A only (after the split)) says it streams. With `requirements.txt` present it installs everything in it (openpyxl, pywin32, lxml, pytest), not only the package named in the prompt. (Added during self-review, from Section 3 `A-F1`:) after a failure the manual command shown is built by joining the words with spaces (`utils/dependency_installer.py:142`), combines `-r requirements.txt` with the package names and quotes no path, so a Python or program folder whose path contains spaces breaks when the command is pasted; the failure reason itself (e.g. the 600-second time-out) is not shown (6.8.2) (READ).
- **Severity:** LOW.
- **Evidence:** READ (START).
- **Related:** A-F1, A-R125, A-R126.

### 7.5 Security concerns

No passwords, tokens or keys exist anywhere in the code (READ, grep); no client data is sent over a network (READ: no `requests`/`urllib`/`socket`/`http` in the source). The concerns are about the user's own data and programs.

#### A-G54 — The program takes over the user's own Excel, hides it and quits it

- **Where:** Step 3: `core/excel_handler.py:123-128` (`GetActiveObject` first — the user's running Excel — then `Dispatch`), `:131-133` (Visible, DisplayAlerts, ScreenUpdating set False), `:238-246` (DisplayAlerts set back to True, then `Quit()` ALWAYS: the guard `if self.excel_app is None` is always true because `excel_app` is set only once, to None, at `:56`). Step 4: `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:218, 536` (`Dispatch`, which for Excel commonly connects to an already running Excel — MEDIUM-HIGH, general pywin32 behaviour), `:225-227` (made visible and maximised), `:404-409, 626-631` (`Quit()` with DisplayAlerts False), `:743-753` (second open attempt closes, WITHOUT saving, every workbook in that Excel with the same file name).
- **What happens (on Windows; cannot be run here):** if the user has Excel open, Step 3 attaches to it, hides all of the user's Excel windows and finally asks that Excel to quit — with prompts switched back on while it is invisible, so it can hang on a hidden "Save changes?" dialog (MEDIUM) or close the user's workbooks. Step 4 may maximise the user's Excel, type into it and quit it with prompts off, which closes unsaved workbooks without saving (MEDIUM-HIGH; Microsoft's documented `Quit` behaviour as recalled, not looked up). The comment at `core/excel_handler.py:241` says "Don't quit if Excel was already open" — the code does the opposite.
- **How the user sees it:** their Excel windows vanish during a run; unsaved work lost or Excel stuck in the background.
- **Severity:** HIGH.
- **Evidence:** READ (code path HIGH; real Excel behaviour MEDIUM — how to check: open an unsaved workbook in Excel, run Step 3 for one client, watch the window). Present since edac6a3 (shared - before the split on 30-10-2025).
- **Related:** A-F14, A-F15, A-F21, A-F23, A-R97, A-R103. Standard 12 (`rebuild_pipeline_FINAL.md:851-855`) requires a separate hidden Excel and "Never take over the user's own open Excel" (technical comparison).

#### A-G55 — Key presses and dialog clicks reach whatever program is in front

- **Where:** `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:258-293` (bring Excel to the front up to 3 times, then send Alt+A, R, A anyway: "continuing anyway", `:273-274`); `:417-453` (every top-level window on the desktop examined); `:492-525` (first button whose text contains "ok", "close", "yes" or "continue" clicked).
- **What happens:** if Windows does not bring Excel to the front (it often refuses while the user is working in another program — MEDIUM, general Windows behaviour), the keys are typed into the user's current window (an e-mail, a document). Any dialog of ANY program whose title contains a word such as "error", "cannot", "invalid" or "missing" and has a standard dialog class is "closed" by clicking OK/Yes/Close/Continue — for example "Yes" in another program's "replace file?" prompt.
- **How the user sees it:** stray letters typed into another window; another program's dialog answered for them. The run needs an unlocked desktop that nobody touches for its whole duration.
- **Severity:** HIGH.
- **Evidence:** READ.
- **Related:** A-F21, A-F26, A-R71, A-R105.

#### A-G56 — Client data is written to log files in whatever folder the program was started from

- **Where:** log files in the CURRENT folder (`main.py:24`; `power_query_extractor/extractor_main.py:16`); INFO lines with client names, paths and every Links value (`core/excel_handler.py:153, 158, 195, 214, 220`), every extracted figure (`power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:56, 590, 603-611`), copied file names (`utils/helpers.py:210, 229`).
- **What happens:** started from a shared program folder (as the Standard 13 launcher does), every user appends to one log file in that shared folder, containing client names and figures; never rotated (A-G52). Log files are opened with the PC's default code page (`logging.FileHandler` without `encoding=`, `main.py:24`, `power_query_extractor/extractor_main.py:16`), so on a typical Windows PC every line containing an emoji ("✅", "❌") is lost with "--- Logging error ---" ⚠ (the default encoding depends on the Python version and Windows settings — a later Python is planned to default to UTF-8; NOT SURE from which version; how to check on the office PC: `python -c "import locale; print(locale.getpreferredencoding())"`) (RAN me: with cp1252 the "✅ Success" line is missing from the file, the plain lines are kept; EXT t15) — and those are exactly the success/failure lines.
- **Severity:** MEDIUM (confidentiality and lost diagnostics).
- **Evidence:** RAN (me: log created in the start folder; cp1252 simulation); READ.
- **Related:** A-F30, A-R120 to A-R122. Standard 13 (`rebuild_pipeline_FINAL.md:1039-1040, 1046-1047`) puts logs per user and forbids shared multi-writer files (technical comparison).

#### A-G57 — On macOS/Linux a folder path is pasted into a shell command

- **Where:** `gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:509-512` — `os.system(f'open "{level1_folder}"')` / `os.system(f'xdg-open "{level1_folder}"')`.
- **What happens:** a target path containing `"` or `$(...)` would be interpreted by the shell. Not reachable on Windows (`os.startfile` is used there).
- **Severity:** LOW.
- **Evidence:** READ.
- **Related:** A-F17.

#### A-G58 — Text that starts with "=" is written into the workbooks as a formula

- **Where:** openpyxl treats any string starting with "=" as a formula: Variations sheet file names `core/excel_handler.py:575`; File Mapping and Client Status names `:480, 509-510`; consolidated client folder names and text values `power_query_extractor/core/data_consolidator.py:106, 157`.
- **What happens:** a source file named e.g. `=1+1 notes.xlsx` (legal on Windows) becomes a formula cell in the summary's Variations sheet; a client folder whose name starts with "=" becomes a formula in every consolidated sheet. Excel then shows an error or asks to repair the file; a crafted name could make Excel compute something.
- **Severity:** LOW (needs an unusual file name).
- **Evidence:** RAN (me r2: client `=1+1 Traders-DL` stored with data type "f"; me r2b: a variation `=HYPERLINK(…).xlsx` stored as a formula — characters like `"` are not allowed in Windows file names, so a real case would be simpler).
- **Related:** A-F9, A-F16, A-F24.

#### A-G59 — The install offer changes the running Python with unpinned versions ⚠

- **Where:** `utils/dependency_installer.py:26-60, 133-134`; `requirements.txt:5-15` (`openpyxl>=3.1.2`, `pywin32>=305; sys_platform == 'win32'`, `lxml>=4.9.0`, `pytest>=7.0.0`) ⚠.
- **What happens:** "Yes" runs `<this python> -m pip install -r requirements.txt`, which installs the newest versions that satisfy `>=` — including a test tool (pytest) — into whatever Python runs the app; on a shared runtime that means one user's PC changes the shared installation. Off Windows the offer appears at every start because pywin32 never installs.
- **Severity:** LOW-MEDIUM.
- **Evidence:** READ; RAN (START: the offer and the exact command).
- **Related:** A-F1, A-R125, A-R126. Standard 13 (`rebuild_pipeline_FINAL.md:919, 937-940`) asks for exact versions and no pytest (technical comparison).

#### A-G60 — One test can change the developer's real settings file

- **Where:** `tests/test_main_window_tabs.py:36-38` builds the real main window (which reads `~/.gst_organizer_cache.json`) and replaces `save_cache` only after construction; with `"dark_mode": true` in that file, start-up switches dark mode on and saves (`gui/main_window.py:388-389, 196`).
- **What happens:** running the tests on the author's PC can rewrite his real settings file, and creates `%TEMP%\gst_excel_temp` (`core/excel_handler.py:53-54`). (Added during self-review, from Appendix X3.6 item 4:) the three probe tests also start a fresh Python without `-B` (`tests/test_extractor_standalone.py:69`, `tests/test_main_window_tabs.py:94`, `tests/test_optional_pywin32.py:73`, READ during self-review), so even a `python -B -m pytest` run writes 38 compiled files into eleven of the program's own folders — against the intent of Standard 13's `-B` rule if the tests are ever run from the shared program folder (`rebuild_pipeline_FINAL.md:969-970`).
- **Severity:** LOW.
- **Evidence:** RAN (TEST exp2: a fake home settings file with dark mode on was rewritten during the test); RAN (Appendix X3.6: 38 `.pyc` files after one run with `-B`, none with `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1`).
- **Related:** A-F27.

#### A-G61 — All Python warnings are switched off for the whole program

- **Where:** `core/excel_handler.py:17` (`warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')`, run whenever any `core` module is imported, `core/__init__.py:6-8`).
- **What happens:** warnings from openpyxl (e.g. about unsupported workbook features it is about to drop) and from Python itself never appear.
- **Severity:** LOW.
- **Evidence:** READ.
- **Related:** A-R108.

### 7.6 Accessibility and usability gaps

#### A-G62 — Step 2 and Step 3 buttons cannot be used from the keyboard, and "disabled" buttons still work

- **Where:** `gui/tabs/validation_tab.py:118, 130, 142, 190` and `gui/tabs/processing_tab.py:74, 87` — buttons wired with `.bind('<Button-1>', …)` instead of `command=`.
- **What happens:** Tab + Space/Enter does nothing on Dry Run, Export List, Start, Select All, Clear All, Complete Only, Start Processing and Stop; they act on mouse-press, not release; the greyed-out Stop still reacts (logs "🛑 Stop requested by user" while nothing runs) and Dry Run can be pressed during a run (only Start is protected, by the re-entry guard). The newer Step 1 explains exactly this reason for using `command=` (`gui/tabs/setup_tab.py:383-385`).
- **Severity:** MEDIUM.
- **Evidence:** RAN (GUI exp3 for Stop); READ.
- **Related:** A-F8, A-F11, A-F12, A-F17, A-R135.

#### A-G63 — At the smallest window size controls disappear; fixed widths and Windows-only fonts

- **Where:** Dark Mode tick placed once at `x = window width − 150` (`gui/widgets/title_bar.py:27`); status bar packed after the tabs (`gui/main_window.py:138, 149`); fixed 450-px left column on Step 2 (`gui/tabs/validation_tab.py:30`) and 400 px on Step 4 (`power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:191`); fonts 'Segoe UI', 'Consolas', 'Arial' throughout.
- **What happens:** at the 1000×700 minimum the Dark Mode tick is outside the window and the status bar is not visible (RAN START); widening the window does not move the tick. On non-Windows PCs Tk substitutes fonts and layouts shift. (Added during self-review, from Section 3 `A-F31`, marked "new" there, both LOW:) tooltips are placed 12 px right of and 6 px below their control with no check against the screen edge (`gui/widgets/tooltip.py:47-48`), so near the right or bottom edge part of the help text is off the screen (RAN Section 3 `A-F31`: a popup from x 1872 to 2402 on a 1920-pixel screen); the Step 2 collapsible instructions box colours only its outer frame, leaving grey strips around the orange lines (RAN Section 3 `A-F31`).
- **Severity:** LOW.
- **Evidence:** RAN (START on a virtual display); READ.
- **Related:** A-F2, A-R131, A-R155.

#### A-G64 — Dark mode leaves new widgets light and makes some text unreadable

- **Where:** capture-once `gui/utils/dark_mode_manager.py:199-215`; nothing themes widgets created later; the client table's row colours reset to light on every rescan while the text stays white (`gui/handlers/client_handler.py:58-59` vs `gui/utils/dark_mode_manager.py:283-287`).
- **What happens:** Step 2 rows built after a scan in dark mode show white text on pale green/amber; Step 4's client rows stay light; colours the program changes in light mode after the first switch are lost on the next restore (latent: in A today the only colours changed at run time are the Setup checklist's, which are recomputed after every switch — Section 3 `A-F28`, MEDIUM); the first switch changes the selected-tab and selected-row colours for good (`:164-172`). (Added during self-review, from Sections 10.10 and 3 `A-F28`:) almost every Step 4 log line becomes black on dark grey — every `Text` widget gets the field colour `#3b3b3b` (`gui/utils/dark_mode_manager.py:32, 233-234`) while the log's "info" tag stays `#000000` (`power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:568`) and every processor line is "info" (A-G67); the Step 3 log, dark by design (`#1E1E1E`), turns the lighter `#3b3b3b`; every coloured classic-Tk button (green START, red STOP, blue Start Processing …) becomes the same grey `#404040` (`dark_mode_manager.py:33, 76`), so the colour coding is lost (RAN in Section 10.10; READ); the standalone extractor ignores the saved `dark_mode` setting altogether (nothing in `power_query_extractor/` or `launch_extractor.py` reads it — READ grep; RAN Section 3 `A-F29` case A).
- **Severity:** LOW (readability).
- **Evidence:** RAN (START dm_test; GUI darkscan; DOCS exp-4b; Section 10.10 screenshots for the additions).
- **Related:** A-F28, A-R148.

#### A-G65 — Step 4 inside the main window: hidden messages, no Stop, a Start that can launch a second run

- **Where:** status bar suppressed when embedded (`gui/tabs/extract_tab.py:78`; `power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:573-585`); no Stop (`:328-340`); any scan that finds clients re-enables Start (`:756-757`) and `start_processing` has no "already running" check (`:845-883`); header column width 25 vs row width 30 (`:414` vs `:714`); every processor line in the plain "info" colour (`power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:53-60`); the log box can be typed into (`power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:545-551`).
- **What happens:** scan results and errors appear only on the other sub-tab's log; a scan during a run re-enables Start, and pressing it starts a SECOND worker that drives Excel at the same time and writes to the same log (RAN PQ gui_probe for the re-enabling); errors are not red; columns do not line up with their headings. After a 'full' Step 3 run the hand-over sets Step 4's folder to the target unconditionally (`gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:166-168`), overwriting a folder the user had chosen there and bypassing the bookkeeping that decides whether Step 1 changes are followed (`gui/tabs/extract_tab.py:121-131`), so later Step 1 changes may stop reaching Step 4 (READ, MEDIUM).
- **Severity:** MEDIUM.
- **Evidence:** RAN (PQ gui_probe); READ.
- **Related:** A-F18, A-F20, A-F25, A-R143.

Two greps were re-run (me): no `== None`, `!= None`, `== True`, `== False`, `is True`, `is False` in non-test code; no function with `[]`, `{}` or `set()` as a default. #### A-G70 — Step 3's worker thread touches the window directly

- **Where:** see the table above (`gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:145-530`); Step 4: `power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:890-891`.
- **What happens:** Tk is not thread-safe. The project's own rule (`power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:989-1000`, commit c1f425e, A only (after the split): "Tk is not thread-safe … Every worker-thread UI update goes through here") is followed by Step 4 but only partly by Step 3: 10 `_log_async` and 4 `_progress_async` calls are marshalled, but 45 direct `log_message` calls, the progress updates at `:459, :482`, `messagebox.showinfo` (`:498-502`) and `messagebox.showerror` (`:525`) and the button resets (`:529-530`) run on the worker. Python's Tk usually forwards such calls to the main thread when Tcl is built with threads (the usual Windows build — MEDIUM-HIGH), so it mostly works; c1f425e calls this pattern "a real cause of intermittent freezes". When the window has gone, every such call raises.
- **How the user sees it:** occasional freezes (MEDIUM), and a chain of errors when the window is closed mid-run (A-G27).
- **Severity:** MEDIUM.
- **Evidence:** READ; RAN (DCP ordering check: no ordering bug seen on Linux; GUI exp4).
- **Related:** A-F17.

#### A-G71 — Nothing stops two runs from working on the same Excel, folders or files at once

- **Where:** Step 3 uses `app.is_processing` (`gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:75, 124, 528`), Step 4 its own `ExtractorPanel.is_processing` (`power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:119, 872, 962`) — neither looks at the other; Step 4's Start has no running check and is re-enabled by any scan (`:756-757, 845-883`); no single-instance guard for `main.py` or `launch_extractor.py` (READ, grep); staging file = report name in the per-user `%TEMP%\gst_excel_temp` (`core/excel_handler.py:147, 273`); settings file rewritten by whoever saves last (`gui/utils/cache_manager.py:45-46`); Skip Refresh is a module-level dictionary (`power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:486-487`).
- **What happens:** Step 3's `GetActiveObject` can grab the Excel that Step 4 (or a second program copy) started, hide it — so Step 4's keys miss — and `Quit()` it mid-refresh (MEDIUM-LOW that the collision happens exactly so; HIGH that nothing prevents it). Two copies run in the same minute on the same target share the same `Annual Statement-…`/`Version-…` folders and the same staging names, interleaving backups and overwrites. A scan in Step 4 during its own run redirects where the consolidated workbook is saved (`:632, 945`).
- **Severity:** MEDIUM.
- **Evidence:** READ; RAN (PQ gui_probe: scan re-enables Start during a run).
- **Related:** A-F17, A-F19, A-F21, A-F24, A-F29.

#### A-G72 — The ETA is one client behind

- **Where:** `gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:235` (the tracker advances by 0 for the first client and by 1 for later ones), `:457` (final ETA); `utils/helpers.py:497-510`.
- **What happens:** after the last client the tracker stands at total − 1, so "Creating summary report | ETA: …" still shows one client's worth of time; with one client it shows "Unknown". (Clarified during self-review, from Section 3 `A-F17`: DURING the run the count equals the clients already finished, so the estimate is right for an even workload; the "one client behind" effect is only at the end.)
- **Severity:** LOW (display only).
- **Evidence:** READ (DCP §3.3); RAN (Section 3 `A-F17`, t16 with a fake clock: "ETA: 3m 0s" at client 2 and "1m 30s" at client 3, then "2m 15s" at the summary step after all three were done).
- **Related:** A-F17, A-R141.

#### A-G73 — Step 4's open retries can run out silently and produce a misleading error

- **Where:** `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:239-249`.
- **What happens:** if all three attempts fail with "Call was rejected by callee", the loop ends with `wb = None` and no error; the code then activates Excel, sends the keys, waits the full time, and only fails at `wb.Save()` with "'NoneType' object has no attribute 'Save'" (caught at `:376-381`). The `_Refreshed_` copy stays (A-G2).
- **Severity:** LOW.
- **Evidence:** READ (DCP B8).
- **Related:** A-F21, A-R72.

#### A-G74 — Code that looks like protection but never acts

- **Where:** `core/excel_handler.py:56, 58-64, 241-242` (`excel_app`, `__del__`, the "don't quit" guard); `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:801-804` (`cleanup()` is `pass`, called at `power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:966`), `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:383-386` (unreachable `return`), `:167-181` (the "Open method of Workbooks class failed" branch: `_refresh_power_query_simple` never raises); `core/file_organizer.py:381-407` (`cleanup_on_error`, never called — so a failed client's half-built folders are never removed); `core/file_parser.py:338-371` (`validate_results`, never called — the "Missing Critical Files" check [GST RULE] `:359` never runs).
- **What happens:** a reader (or a future maintainer) believes these situations are handled; they are not.
- **Severity:** LOW (maintenance trap; the real consequences are A-G54 and A-G2).
- **Evidence:** READ (DCP §1.3, §1.5; RAN grep of every caller).
- **Related:** A-R30, A-R97.

#### A-G75 — Small display helpers miscount

- **Where:** `gui/utils/setup_validation.py:67-72` (`_short`); `utils/helpers.py:394-416` (`truncate_path`).
- **What happens:** the checklist keeps the last 42 characters plus "..." (45, not the 46 it is given) and trims the START although its docstring says "Trim the middle"; the status-bar path can exceed its 60-character limit and on Windows shows `C:\\...\\<last part>` with a doubled separator.

#### A-G76 — One run is named by two separate clock reads

- **What happens:** if the minute changes between the two lines, the report names carry a different minute from their `Version-…` folder.
- **Severity:** LOW (a window of microseconds).
- **Evidence:** READ (TRACE T3 obs 6).
- **Related:** A-R33.

#### A-G77 — The state-code fallback for single words uses the untrimmed text [GST RULE]

- **Where:** `utils/helpers.py:601` (trimmed copy used for the lookup) vs `:616` (`state_name[:3]`, the ORIGINAL text).
- **What happens (described only):** " Xyz" → " XY" (a leading space kept inside the code, and so inside the client key and the folder name). From real file names the parser already trims (`core/file_parser.py:104`), so this needs other callers.
- **Severity:** LOW.
- **Evidence:** RAN (me r1; TEST probe).
- **Related:** A-R22.

#### A-G78 — The cell-mapping configuration can silently overwrite itself (latent) [GST RULE]

- **Where:** `power_query_extractor/config/cell_mappings.py:270-277`; `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:585-588`.
- **What happens:** if two output sheets read the same input cell of the same sheet, only the LAST field name is kept, so the first output column always shows "Missing"; values are also stored under the bare cell reference (`J15`), not qualified by sheet, so two sheets reading the same address would overwrite each other's value for calculations; titles that differ only by a space vs an underscore produce the same field name. None of this is triggered by the shipped configuration (RAN TRACE T4 Part A); it bites when the author adds mappings. The configuration is plain Python with no validation: a typo stops Step 4 from loading (and the notice then blames pywin32, A-G66).
- **Severity:** LOW (latent).
- **Evidence:** RAN (TRACE T4b); READ.
- **Related:** A-R83, A-R84, A-R85 ([GST RULE]: which cell feeds which output column, A-R83 and A-R85; described only).

#### A-G79 — Assumptions about Excel through COM that are not verified (NOT SURE)

- **Where:** `core/excel_handler.py:193` (`ws.Range(cell_ref).Value = str(value)`); `core/excel_handler.py:172, 180, 232` and `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:397, 620` (`if not ws:` / `if wb:` on COM objects); `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:746-749` (closing workbooks while looping over `excel.Workbooks`).
- **What happens (possible, unverified):** Excel may convert a written text that looks like a number or date (e.g. a digits-only file stem) into a number; Python's "truthiness" of a pywin32 object is normally always true, but a collection-like object could be judged by its length (LOW); closing items while iterating the same COM collection can skip some.
- **Severity:** LOW. **How to check:** on Windows, write a digits-only stem through Step 3 and look at the cell; open two same-named workbooks and run Step 4's open fallback.
- **Evidence:** READ (CORE notes items 18, 20).
- **Related:** A-F14, A-F21.

### 7.8 Scenario-based failure analysis for each major feature

The seven questions of the audit method, asked of every major feature. "OK" means nothing breaks that is not already listed; the gap IDs carry the detail and the evidence.

**Scenario key:** S1 = the program is started from a different folder than the development folder; S2 = another Windows user runs it; S3 = the network drive disconnects mid-run; S4 = it runs a second time on the same data; S5 = two copies run at once on the same target; S6 = a different operating system; S7 = a different Python or library version.

#### 7.8.1 Start-up, dependency check and log files (A-F1, A-F30)

| Scenario | What breaks | Evidence | Gaps |
|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | The program finds its own files from its own location (`main.py:31-32, 84`) — OK. But `gst_organizer.log` (and `pq_extractor.log` for the standalone extractor) are created in the START folder (`main.py:24`; `power_query_extractor/extractor_main.py:16`); an unwritable start folder stops the program before any message; `logs/` and `temp/` are created in the program folder at every start (`main.py:35-43`) and never used. | RAN (me: log in the start folder); READ | A-G23, A-G56 |
| S2 | Started from a shared folder, every user appends to the same log file (with client data); a user without write access to the program folder gets "Critical error"; a different user's Python may lack pywin32 ("py" and "python" can be different interpreters — commit c463256, A only (after the split)) → on Windows the start is blocked and the offer installs into that user's Python. | READ | A-G23, A-G56, A-G59 |
| S3 | Start-up itself touches the network only through the Setup checklist's existence checks of remembered paths, which block the window until the share times out. | READ | A-G49 |
| S4 | Log files keep growing (appended, never rotated); off Windows the install offer returns at every start. | READ; RAN (START) | A-G52, A-G59 |
| S5 | Two copies append to one log file (lines interleave); both rewrite the same settings file (last save wins). | READ | A-G71 |
| S6 | Without a console (`pythonw.exe`) the program dies silently at `main.py:17`; off Windows pywin32 is "optional", reports lose Power Query, Step 4 refuses. | RAN (me) | A-G22, A-G7 |
| S7 | `requirements.txt:2` says "Python 3.7 or higher" ⚠ but the installed openpyxl 3.1.5 needs ≥ 3.8 and pytest 9 needs ≥ 3.10 (START, package metadata); versions are minimums only (`>=`), so a future openpyxl major version would be installed by the offer; `find_spec` accepts a broken pywin32. | READ; RAN (START) | A-G7, A-G59 |

#### 7.8.2 Setup, checklist and settings (A-F3, A-F4, A-F6, A-F27)

| Scenario | What breaks | Evidence | Gaps |
|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | Settings live in the home folder (`gui/utils/cache_manager.py:15`) — OK. The standalone extractor additionally reads `gst_organizer_cache.json`, `.cache/app_state.json` and `config/last_session.json` from the START folder (`power_query_extractor/extractor_main.py:42-44`) — nothing writes them, but a stray file there would supply a folder. | RAN (EXT t8) | A-G32 (added there during self-review; originally "—") |
| S2 | A new user starts with defaults (per-user file). Paths remembered as `Z:\…` exist only where `Z:` is mapped the same way → ✕ in the checklist. | READ | A-G46 |

### 7.10 Gap register (all 79 gaps in one table)

How to use: the ID links back to the full entry above (subsection in the third column). "Evidence" says whether the gap was shown by running the code (RAN) or by reading it (READ); entries with both have a run for the main point and a reading for the rest. "Related" lists the registry's feature (A-F) and rule (A-R) IDs and other gaps.

**Added during self-review.** Findings that Section 3 (and Section 10) had shown by a trace but marked "not yet in Section 7" were added to the nearest existing gap instead of being given new numbers, so the 79 IDs and the counts below are unchanged: A-G19 (Stop and all-fail summaries, text "Complete %" and "Processing Date", the organisation report's file list, the include-name display mismatch, Dry Run's Sales promise and gate), A-G20 (settings not saved by typing, the mode radio or closing), A-G24 (an empty JSON list; an unknown mode value), A-G32 (a stray settings file in the start folder; `__getattr__`), A-G45 (e) and (f) (only the newest Version folder; an empty list that keeps Start), A-G53 (unquoted manual command), A-G63 (tooltips off-screen; the collapsible box colours), A-G64 (Step 4 log black on dark grey, coloured buttons all grey, the standalone window ignores dark mode), A-G66 (no Start warning for per-client names; the "EXPECTED FILE NAMES" card; README's "Debug Mode"), A-G67 (the BB2 message replaces a dialog's text), A-G69 ("Found N clients" overwritten; a previous run's 100 % left on screen; "Step 4 ready" after an empty scan). A-G68 and A-G72 were made more precise. Section 3 rated two of the A-G19 additions (the Stop summary and the missing workbook) HIGH on its own scale; the register keeps A-G19's LOW-MEDIUM, because neither changes a figure or a file — the reader can decide otherwise.

**Count by severity:** HIGH 13 (A-G1, A-G2, A-G3, A-G4, A-G7, A-G8, A-G10, A-G22, A-G27, A-G33, A-G44, A-G54, A-G55); MEDIUM-HIGH 1 (A-G5); MEDIUM 35; LOW-MEDIUM 6 (A-G14, A-G19, A-G20, A-G38, A-G51, A-G59); LOW 24. **The gaps that matter most, in plain words** (HIGH items, grouped):
- **Wrong or untrustworthy figures with no warning:** A-G1 (9 consolidated columns take another cell's value), A-G2 and A-G3 (a refresh that failed or cannot be confirmed is saved and later reused as good), A-G4 (a template without a `Links` sheet gives useless reports marked as success), A-G33 (a hyphen in a name misfiles a client's file).
- **Files of one client overwritten or duplicated:** A-G8 (two clients in one folder), A-G10 ("Resume" starts again).
- **Lost work or a program that will not start:** A-G22 (no console → nothing happens), A-G27 (closing the window kills a run), A-G7 (Power Query dropped by the fallback path).
- **Interference with the user's own work:** A-G54 (the user's open Excel is taken over and closed), A-G55 (key presses and clicks go to whatever window is in front), A-G44 (Excel set-ups the code does not expect).
