## SECTION 8: DESIGN DECISIONS (INFERRED)

### 8.0 How to read Sections 8 and 9

**What these two sections cover.** Project A (`goyal-sidhant/AnnualStatement_oldv1`, branch `main`, snapshot `bf2f1dd`, 27-07-2026; the Tkinter program that calls itself "GST File Organizer v3.0"). Section 8 explains WHY the program is built the way it is (inferred from the code, its comments and its history), and checks whether each design pattern is applied the same way in every file. Section 9 lists everything the program needs from the computer it runs on: libraries, Python version, Windows-only parts, folders, Excel, and how it is started, compared with the author's Standard 13.

**Evidence markers.** Every statement about the code cites `file:line` at `bf2f1dd` (repository-relative; the scratch copy `/root/merge-scratch/A-copy` has the same line numbers). Older code is written `path:line@commit`.
- **READ** = established by reading the code or a diff.
- **RAN** = executed on made-up inputs in a scratch copy. "RAN (me)" = run for these sections on 21-10-2026 in `/root/merge-scratch/run/A-S89/` (scripts `scripts/s1_syntax.py` … `scripts/s7_extractor_start.sh`, outputs `out_s1_syntax.txt` … `out_s7_extractor.txt`; list in 9.11). Other RAN marks name the earlier reader whose notes hold the run: DCP = `A_dead_code_patterns.md`, START = `A_code_startup_widgets.md`, EXT = `A_outside_files_state.md`, XL = `A_excel_pq_safety.md`, TRACE = `A_live_traces.md`, TEST = `A_tests.md`, DOCS = `A_older_docs.md`, HS / H1 / H2 / H3 = the history notes (all under `/root/merge-scratch/notes2/`). Anything that needs Excel through COM or Windows could NOT run here (Linux, no Excel, no pywin32) and is READ only.
- **Inferences** (reasons nobody wrote down) carry **HIGH** (clear from the code, a comment or a commit message), **MEDIUM** (a reasonable inference from several clues) or **LOW** (speculation from limited evidence). "NOT SURE" always comes with a way to check.

**IDs.** Features `A-F1` … `A-F31` and rules `A-R1` … `A-R157` are the registry's (`/root/merge-scratch/audit/A_registry.md`). Gaps `A-G1` … `A-G79` are Section 7's. No new feature or rule was found while writing these sections.

**[GST RULE] and ⚠.** Anything that decides a tax figure, which return / table / sheet / cell a figure or file belongs to, a state code, a period or a rounding is tagged **[GST RULE]**; for those these sections only say what the code does, never whether it is right. Values that change over time (package and Python versions, Excel's keyboard shortcuts and path limit, table numbers, template cells, folder-name conventions, measured timings) carry **⚠**.

**Commit labels.** The 12 commits `edac6a3` … `47a1492` are "shared - before the split on 30-10-2025"; A's 34 later commits are "A only (after the split)". A has one branch, `main`.

**Confidentiality.** No client name, GSTIN, PAN, real file name or figure appears here. Made-up names (`<Client A>`, `ClientA`, `ClientB Pvt. Ltd.`) are used. Commit messages 4f84ba9 and 7347383 name the office file server and share; those names are not copied.

**Plain-English words used in Sections 8 and 9**

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| framework / library / package | Ready-made code the program uses. A *package* is also a folder of program files with an `__init__.py` file in it. "Third-party" = not part of Python itself; it has to be installed with `pip`. |
| module, import | A *module* is one `.py` file. To *import* is for one file to load and use another. |
| import guard | Code that tries an import and carries on in a planned way if it fails (`try: import … except ImportError: …`), instead of crashing. |
| re-export, `__all__`, facade | A package's `__init__.py` can *re-export* names from its files so callers can write `from core import FileParser`. `__all__` is the list of names a module officially offers. A *facade* is one object that forwards calls to others so callers see a single front door. |
| Tk / Tkinter / ttk | Python's built-in window toolkit; *ttk* is its "themed" set of widgets. A *widget* is any on-screen element (button, box, table). |
| PySide6 / PyQt5 | Other window toolkits (based on Qt); Standard 12 names PySide6 for desktop windows. |
| COM, pywin32 | COM is Windows' way for one program to drive another (here Python drives Excel). *pywin32* is the Python package that provides it (`win32com`, `pythoncom`, `win32api`, `win32gui`, `win32con`). |
| GetActiveObject / Dispatch / DispatchEx | Three ways to get an Excel: grab the one already running; start one but possibly connect to a running one; always start a separate one (Standard 12 asks for `DispatchEx`). |
| openpyxl, lxml | *openpyxl* reads and writes `.xlsx` files without Excel; when it SAVES a workbook it drops Power Query. *lxml* is a fast XML library openpyxl uses when it is installed. |
| Power Query, refresh, DataMashup | Excel's data-import tool inside the ITC/Sales templates; *refresh* re-runs it. Its queries live in a hidden part of the file called *DataMashup*. |
| SendKeys, key tips | Pressing keyboard keys by program into whatever window has the keyboard focus. Excel's *key tips* are the Alt shortcuts (Alt, A = Data tab; R, A = Refresh All, in English Excel). |
| worker thread, daemon thread | A second line of work running next to the window so the window does not freeze. A *daemon* thread is killed instantly, without tidy-up, when the program ends. Tk must only be touched from the window's own thread. |
| `after(0, …)` | Tk's way to ask the window's own thread to run something "as soon as possible" — the safe way for a worker thread to update the screen. |
| round-trip, SMB share, VPN | One request to a file server and its answer; on a network folder (*SMB* share) reached over a *VPN* each one is slow, so the code tries to make fewer of them. |
| staging file | A temporary local copy that is worked on and then copied to its final place. |
| `os.scandir`, stat, mtime | *scandir* lists a folder once and hands back each entry with its details; *stat* = asking for a file's size, type and dates; *mtime* = "date modified". |
| pip, PyPI, requirements.txt | *pip* is Python's installer; it downloads from *PyPI* (the public package site). *requirements.txt* lists the packages a program needs. `>=3.1.2` means "3.1.2 or newer"; `==3.1.5` would mean exactly that version. |
| `find_spec` | A Python check that a module's file can be FOUND, without loading it (so it cannot tell that a found module is broken). |
| `pythonw.exe`, console | The Windows Python that opens no black console window (Standard 13 starts apps with it); under it the program has no `sys.stdout` / `sys.stdin`. *Console* = the black text window. |
| current folder (CWD) | The folder a program was started from. A file name with no folder part (e.g. `gst_organizer.log`) is created there. |
| `%TEMP%`, `%USERPROFILE%`, `%LOCALAPPDATA%` | The user's temporary folder; the user's home folder (`C:\Users\<name>`); the per-user, per-PC settings folder Standard 13 requires (`C:\Users\<name>\AppData\Local`). |
| embeddable Python, `_runtime` | python.org's portable Python zip; Standard 13 keeps ONE of them for all apps in a shared `_runtime` folder. |
| UNC path / mapped drive | A network path written `\\server\share\...` / the same share shown as a drive letter such as `Z:`. |
| 8.3 short path, `\\?\` prefix | The old DOS-style short form of a path (`PROGRA~1`); a prefix that lifts Windows' usual 260-character path limit. |
| code page / encoding | How text characters are stored as bytes. Windows' default *code page* (often cp1252) cannot store emoji; UTF-8 can. |
| AST, grammar parse | Python's own parse tree of a file; parsing a file "with the 3.7 grammar" checks that it uses no syntax newer than Python 3.7. |
| characterization test | A test that records what the code does today so later changes cannot silently alter it. |
| exception handler, bare `except:` | An *exception handler* is an `except` block: the code that runs when an error happens (not the same as the GUI "handler" files in `gui/handlers/`). A *bare* `except:` names no error type, so it catches every error, even Ctrl+C. |
| callback | A function handed to something else (a button, a timer) to be run later, e.g. when the button is clicked. |
| docstring | The explanatory text in triple quotes at the top of a file, class or function. |
| glob | A file-name search with wildcards, such as `ITC_Report_*.xlsx`. |
| root logger, `basicConfig` | Python's one global log channel; a *module logger* (`logging.getLogger(__name__)`) is a named channel under it. `logging.basicConfig(...)` sets up where the root logger writes (here: a log file and the console). |
| `excepthook` | A Python setting naming the function that runs when an error is not caught anywhere (Standard 13 uses it to write an error file and show a box). |
| free-threaded build (`python3.14t.exe`) | A special build of Python 3.13+ without the "global interpreter lock"; it is a separate interpreter with its own installed packages. |
| late-binding bug | A scheduled screen update that reads a loop variable when it RUNS rather than when it was scheduled, so it can show the next client's name instead of the current one. |
| environment marker | The `; sys_platform == 'win32'` part of a `requirements.txt` line: pip installs that package only where the condition is true. |
| venv | A *virtual environment*: a private copy of Python with its own installed packages (here `/root/merge-scratch/venv-A`). |
| Tcl, CPython | *Tcl* is the small scripting language underneath Tk; *CPython* is the standard Python program from python.org. |

### 8.2 Why this framework and these libraries

#### 8.2.1 Tkinter for the windows (D1)

- **What the code does (READ).** Every window, tab, dialog and pop-up is Tkinter/ttk: the main window (`gui/main_window.py:9-10, 48`), the four tabs (`gui/tabs/*.py`), the widgets (`gui/widgets/*.py`), the extractor panel and its standalone window (`power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:5-6, 98, 1032`), and even the install offer (`utils/dependency_installer.py:96-97`). The theme is ttk's built-in `'clam'` (`gui/main_window.py:57-77`; `power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:85-95`).
- **Likely reason — MEDIUM.** Tkinter ships inside the normal python.org Windows installer, so nothing has to be installed for the window itself, and it is the toolkit AI chat answers most often produce for small desktop tools. The code was written through AI chats: "Author: Advanced AI Assistant" (`main.py:5`), and paste markers such as "# ADD THIS LINE" (`utils/helpers.py:17`) and "# Rest of your code remains same..." (`power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:295`) (READ, HIGH that it was AI-assisted). Nothing in the code or history states why Tkinter was picked; the pre-git history (19-06-2025 to 31-08-2025) is lost (HS 1.16).
- **History (READ).** The first GUI was one large file `gui/app.py` (89,275 bytes, last edited 25-06-2025) that was never committed; only its compiled files were (in edac6a3, shared - before the split on 30-10-2025; HS 1.16, DCP 4.3). It was split into the modular GUI on 23-07-2025 (`gui/main_window.py:4` "Modularized version - ties all components together"). After the split A kept Tkinter through all 34 of its own commits (project B moved to PyQt5; that is for the later comparison).
- **Comparison with the author's Standard 12 (fact only).** Standard 12 names PySide6 (Qt 6) for "Desktop windows and animations" (`rebuild_pipeline_FINAL.md:833`). A uses Tkinter. Which toolkit the merged app uses is the author's decision.
- **Costs of the choice that are visible in the code (READ):** Windows-only fonts typed into each widget (`'Segoe UI'`, `'Arial'`, `'Consolas'`; 9.5.3); a hand-built dark mode with four follow-up fixes (8.4.14, A-F28); Windows-style mouse-wheel events only (A-G68); Tk is not thread-safe, which the code has to work around (8.7 P5).

#### 8.2.2 Excel through COM (pywin32) for reports and refresh (D2)

- **What the code does (READ).** Step 3 writes the template copy's `Links` sheet through Excel itself when `platform.system() == 'Windows'` and `win32com.client` + `pythoncom` import (`core/excel_handler.py:19-28, 90-95, 104-260`). Step 4 refreshes and reads the reports only through Excel (`power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:20-36, 62-77, 209-415, 527-636`).
- **Reason — HIGH.** Stated in the code: "WINDOWS VERSION - Uses Excel COM to preserve Power Query and all Excel features" (`core/excel_handler.py:2-3`, unchanged since edac6a3, shared - before the split on 30-10-2025) and "Without Excel COM, report creation silently falls back to openpyxl, which does not preserve Power Query - so the ITC and Sales reports come out stripped of the queries that make them useful … Producing damaged reports is worse than refusing to start" (`utils/requirements_check.py:49-56`, be6418c, A only (after the split)). The README of the first commit says "The Excel corruption issues from previous versions have been specifically addressed" (`README.md:254@edac6a3`), i.e. an earlier (pre-git) version damaged files — MEDIUM-HIGH that this is what pushed the switch to COM (HS 6). RAN (XL E1): A's openpyxl path really drops the DataMashup part and the connections of a template.
- **Comparison with Standard 12 (fact only).** Standard 12 says a workbook with Power Query that the app writes into or refreshes must be handled by Excel through COM (`rebuild_pipeline_FINAL.md:828`) — A agrees on the choice. How A drives Excel differs from Standard 12's "Excel through COM" rules in many points (separate Excel via `DispatchEx`, `IgnoreReadOnlyRecommended` — A passes it only in Step 4's last-resort open, `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:777-783`, and never checks `workbook.ReadOnly` (READ, grep) —, `RefreshAll` + `CalculateUntilAsyncQueriesDone`, `CoUninitialize` after the function returns); the point-by-point check is XL §3 and Section 7 (A-G3, A-G28, A-G54, A-G79). Step 4's value READING (`_extract_data`) also uses COM although Standard 12 says reading a Power Query workbook with openpyxl is fine (`rebuild_pipeline_FINAL.md:827`) — fact only.

#### 8.2.3 openpyxl for everything without Power Query (D3)

- **What the code does (READ).** openpyxl creates the five-sheet Step 3 summary workbook (`core/excel_handler.py:371-409`) and the Step 4 consolidated workbook (`power_query_extractor/core/data_consolidator.py:20-186`) from scratch, and is the fallback for the ITC/Sales reports when COM is not available (`core/excel_handler.py:96-102, 262-322`).
- **Reason — HIGH.** Those two workbooks are new files that hold no Power Query, so they do not need Excel; openpyxl also works off Windows. The fallback exists so Steps 1-3 can run on a non-Windows PC ("Fallback to openpyxl if not on Windows", `core/excel_handler.py:30`), at the price of losing Power Query, which the code only logs ("Not on Windows - Power Query may not be preserved!", `core/excel_handler.py:96-102`). Since be6418c (A only (after the split)) the start-up check blocks that fallback on Windows (`utils/requirements_check.py:57`), but not when pywin32 is present-but-broken (A-G7, RAN XL E2).
- **Standard 12 (fact only).** Standard 12 says: never let openpyxl save over a workbook with Power Query; check for a `DataMashup` part first (`rebuild_pipeline_FINAL.md:846-850`). A has no such check anywhere (READ, grep for "DataMashup"/"customXml": none in non-test code).

#### 8.2.4 lxml

- **What the code does (READ + RAN me).** No A file imports lxml (RAN me: an AST list of every import in the 43 program files, inline command listed in 9.11; table in 9.1). It is listed as "Optional but recommended for better performance" (`requirements.txt:11-12`). openpyxl uses it by itself whenever it is installed: `LXML = lxml_available() and lxml_env_set()` with `OPENPYXL_LXML` defaulting to `"True"` (`openpyxl/xml/__init__.py` of the installed openpyxl 3.1.5); RAN me: `openpyxl.xml.LXML` = True in venv-A (`out_s5_imports.txt`).
- **Reason — MEDIUM.** Faster writing of the summary/consolidated workbooks. Listed since the first commit (`requirements.txt@edac6a3`).

#### 8.2.5 Standard library for everything else

| Need | Module(s) used | Where | Likely reason (confidence) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Settings file | `json` | `gui/utils/cache_manager.py:4, 22-23, 45-46`; `power_query_extractor/extractor_main.py:7, 51-52`; `power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:10, 591` | A handful of values for one user; no database needed (HIGH; same view in the older audit's D4) |
| Recognising file names | `re` | `utils/constants.py:6, 13-62`; `utils/helpers.py:7, 92-93, 623-625` | Fixed naming patterns [GST RULE] ⚠ (MEDIUM, 8.4.10) |

| Dependency check / install / restart | `importlib.util.find_spec`, `subprocess` | `utils/requirements_check.py:12, 64-70`; `utils/dependency_installer.py:16, 41-74` | Check without importing; run pip with the same Python (HIGH, f363946, a5ad487) |

#### 8.2.6 pytest (added July 2026)

- **What the code does (READ).** `pytest>=7.0.0` was a comment in the first commit (`requirements.txt@edac6a3`) and became a real line in 6c1e1c6 ("Add pytest suite for data-integrity logic (81 tests)", A only (after the split)); 288 tests at the snapshot (TEST, RAN under a virtual display: 287 pass; the one failure is a test that expects Windows-style path splitting, `tests/test_setup_validation.py:66`, so it can pass only on Windows).
- **Reason — HIGH.** Tests were written first as a "safety net" (characterization tests) and the fixes came 50 minutes later in 33d0baf (H1 "Phase reading"); later commits add tests that run the start-up in a separate process (`tests/test_optional_pywin32.py`, `tests/test_main_window_tabs.py`) and "guard" tests that read the source code to stop a known bug pattern coming back (`tests/test_scroll_bindings.py`, bf2f1dd: "This is the second time this exact pattern has broken scrolling").

#### 8.2.7 What was deliberately NOT used

READ (grep of every non-test `.py` file): no network library (`requests`, `urllib`, `socket`, `http`), no database, no `ctypes`, no `winreg`, no Tally, no e-mail, no VBA macros. The only internet access is the optional `pip install` of the start-up offer (`utils/dependency_installer.py:41-60`). HIGH that the program is a purely local desktop tool working on files a person downloaded — which matches Standard 12's "GST portal downloads: Do not automate" (`rebuild_pipeline_FINAL.md:836`; fact only).

#### 8.2.8 The library choices against Standard 12 (facts only — decisions are the author's)

| Task (Standard 12 row) | Standard 12 says | A does | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Desktop windows | PySide6 (`PySide6-Essentials`, Qt 6), pinned 6.12.x while Windows 10 PCs exist | Tkinter / ttk | 8.2.1 |
| Writing into or refreshing a Power Query workbook | Excel through COM with pywin32 | Same choice | 8.2.2 |
| Excel processing of workbooks without Power Query | openpyxl | openpyxl for the summary and consolidated workbooks | 8.2.3 |
| Saving with openpyxl over a workbook the app did not create | Check for `DataMashup` first; never let openpyxl save over a PQ workbook | The openpyxl fallback saves the copy of a PQ template with no check (Windows: blocked at start-up unless pywin32 is broken) | `core/excel_handler.py:262-322`; A-G7 |
| Reading a Power Query workbook | openpyxl is fine for reading | COM (a second, hidden Excel) | `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:527-636` |
| Summaries and dashboards | An Excel report written with openpyxl | Same (summary and consolidated workbooks) | 8.2.3 |
| Small helper scripts | Python; no `.ps1` | No scripts outside Python | — |
| GST portal downloads | Do not automate | Not automated | 8.2.7 |

### 8.3 Why the code is structured this way

#### 8.3.1 Two programs that became one, with one extractor and two hosts (D15)

- **What the code is (READ).** A has two entry points: `main.py` (the organiser, Steps 1-4) and `launch_extractor.py` (the Power Query Extractor alone). The extractor lives in its own package `power_query_extractor/` with its own `config/`, `core/` and `gui/` sub-packages and its own log file (`power_query_extractor/extractor_main.py:12-19`). Since a677670 (A only (after the split)) its whole UI is `ExtractorPanel(ttk.Frame)` (`power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:98`), hosted either by the thin standalone window `PowerQueryExtractorApp(tk.Tk)` (`:1032-1063`) or by the Step 4 tab (`gui/tabs/extract_tab.py:74-80`, bfcb24a, A only (after the split)).
- **Reason — HIGH.** Stated in the design note: the two programs "communicate only through `~/.gst_organizer_cache.json`" and running them separately "makes the normal end-to-end job feel disjointed" (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-25-merge-extractor-design.md:8-17`); the goal was "One implementation, two homes" (`:43`) under the hard constraint "the app works today and must not break" (`:19-21`). Why it was a separate program in the first place: the older audit's D3 says "the user may want to run the extractor days later or multiple times" (`PROJECT_AUDIT_ANNUALSTATEMENT.md:683-684`) — MEDIUM (the older audit's own inference), and the design note keeps Step 4 "always accessible, with its own folder picker" for that reason (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-25-merge-extractor-design.md:29, 85-89`).
- **Consequences visible in the code (READ).** Window-level settings (title, size, global ttk styles) moved into the shell because "ttk styles are application-global" (`power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:85-95, 1032-1039`; a677670 message). The Step 4 tab imports `extractor_window`, not `extractor_main`, so the second `logging.basicConfig` does not "hijack the main app's logging" (`gui/tabs/extract_tab.py:8-10`). The design note's plan to move that `basicConfig` call out of `extractor_main.py` (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-25-merge-extractor-design.md:54-56`) was side-stepped instead of done (`power_query_extractor/extractor_main.py:12-19` still configures logging at import; RAN me `out_s7_extractor.txt`: importing it creates `pq_extractor.log` in the current folder). The extractor package is no longer self-contained: since ba2a753 (A only (after the split)) it imports the main app's `utils.excel_com` (`power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:39`), so it needs the program folder on the search path (9.5.2).

#### 8.3.2 Layers: `core/` · `utils/` · `gui/` · `power_query_extractor/`

| Layer | Holds | Talks to | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| `utils/` | All constants (`utils/constants.py`), helpers (`utils/helpers.py`), the shared COM helper (`utils/excel_com.py`), the start-up check and installer (`utils/requirements_check.py`, `utils/dependency_installer.py`) | standard library only (`utils/constants.py:6-7`, `utils/helpers.py:6-17`), apart from two imports made inside functions: pywin32's `win32api` in `get_short_path` (`utils/helpers.py:584`) and tkinter in the install offer (`utils/dependency_installer.py:96-97`) | READ; RAN (START): importing `utils.requirements_check` loads no third-party module |
| `core/` | The organiser's logic: scan and recognise (`core/file_parser.py`), create folders and copy (`core/file_organizer.py`), build reports and the summary (`core/excel_handler.py`) | `utils` (absolute imports, e.g. `core/file_parser.py:12-13`), openpyxl, pywin32 | READ |
| `gui/` | Windows and buttons: `main_window.py`, `tabs/`, `handlers/`, `utils/`, `widgets/` | `core`, `utils`, `power_query_extractor` (Step 4) | READ |
| `power_query_extractor/` | Step 4 / standalone extractor: `config/cell_mappings.py`, `core/report_processor.py`, `core/data_consolidator.py`, `core/refresh_naming.py`, `gui/extractor_window.py`, `extractor_main.py` | its own sub-packages (relative imports), plus `utils.excel_com` | READ |

- **Reason — MEDIUM.** A conventional "logic / helpers / screens" split that AI tools produce by default; the older audit calls it "separation of concerns … applied somewhat mechanically" (`PROJECT_AUDIT_ANNUALSTATEMENT.md:698-699`). One clean rule holds everywhere: `core/` (and the extractor's `core/`) never shows a dialog; only GUI-facing files do (S67 6.8.1, READ grep of `messagebox.`) — HIGH.

#### 8.3.3 The GUI split into tabs, handlers, utils and widgets

- **What the code is (READ).** `gui/main_window.py` builds the window and holds the shared state; each tab file builds one screen (`gui/tabs/setup_tab.py`, `validation_tab.py`, `processing_tab.py`, `extract_tab.py`); each handler file holds the button logic for one area (`gui/handlers/file_handler.py` browse/scan, `client_handler.py` the Step 2 table, `processing_handler.py` Dry Run / Start / Stop and the Step 3 worker); `gui/utils/` holds the settings file, dark mode, status bar and log helpers, and (since 322717f) the Tk-free Setup checks `setup_validation.py`; `gui/widgets/` three small reusable widgets (collapsible frame, title bar, tooltip).
- **Reason — HIGH that it was a split of the monolithic `gui/app.py`** (identifier strings in its compiled leftover include `create_setup_tab`, `create_validation_tab`, `create_processing_tab`, `create_title_bar`; DCP 4.3), **MEDIUM that the motive was size** (89 KB in one file). The split date (23-07-2025) and the comment "Import core modules (these imports remain the same)" (`gui/main_window.py:14`) record the refactor; the reasons are lost with the pre-git history.
- **What was not split (READ).** The Step 3 worker is still one 349-line function, `process_files_thread` (`gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:182-530`), which the design note calls "the `process_files_thread` god-method" and keeps out of scope (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-25-merge-extractor-design.md:127`). The extractor GUI is one 1,063-line file (`power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py`; the last line has no line-end character, so `wc -l` and the file list `A_files.txt` show 1,062).

#### 8.3.4 The application object as a shared "state bag", with delegator methods

- **What the code is (READ).** `GSTOrganizerApp` holds every Tk variable and every shared dictionary (`gui/main_window.py:79-110`: `source_folder`, `itc_template`, …, `client_data`, `variations`, `selected_clients`, `client_folder_settings`, `is_processing`, `stop_requested`), and even the `FileOrganizer` CLASS (`gui/main_window.py:109-110` "Core component imports (needed by handlers)"), so `ProcessingHandler` can create a new organiser per run without importing `core` itself (`gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:189`). Each handler gets the whole app object (`FileHandler(self)`, `ClientHandler(self)`, `ProcessingHandler(self)`, `gui/main_window.py:125-129`) and reads and writes its attributes; tabs also hang widgets on it (`self.app.client_tree`, `self.app.start_btn`, `self.app.stop_btn`, `self.app.log_text`, `self.app.scan_btn`, created at `gui/tabs/validation_tab.py:198`, `gui/tabs/processing_tab.py:64, 76, 103`, `gui/tabs/setup_tab.py:459`). The app then has 22 one-line "delegator" methods that just call a handler (`gui/main_window.py:209-276`; RAN me: 22 `def`s in that range, each calling `self.file_handler.` / `self.client_handler.` / `self.processing_handler.`), so tab code can call `self.app.start_processing()` without knowing which handler does it.
- **Reason — MEDIUM.** It let the monolithic `gui/app.py` (where everything was `self.…` on one object) be cut into files without rewriting every reference; the older audit's D8 says the same and notes "This avoids circular imports but creates tight coupling" (`PROJECT_AUDIT_ANNUALSTATEMENT.md:698-699`).
- **Costs (READ).** There is no declared interface: build order matters and some methods guard with `hasattr` because the attribute may not exist yet (`gui/main_window.py:165, 177, 206, 296`); three delegators have no caller at all (`toggle_client_selection` `gui/main_window.py:244-245`, `toggle_folder_name_setting` `:256-257`, `process_files_thread` `:275-276`; DCP D5-D7); the Step 3 worker reads Tk variables and the shared dictionaries straight off the app object while the window can change them (A-G13, A-G14, 8.7 P5).

#### 8.3.5 Central constants, and an extraction configuration the author can edit (D20)

- **What the code is (READ).** `utils/constants.py` holds the file-name patterns (`:13-62`), expected file types (`:68-75`), folder-name templates (`:81-96`), the `Links` cell map (`:102-126`), GUI settings (`:132-157`), workflow and processing modes (`:163-190`), file-validation constants (`:196-202`), messages (`:208-228`), `EXCEL_SAFETY` (`:234-245`) and the state-name table (`:251-292`) — [GST RULE] ⚠ for the patterns, expected types, cell map and state table (A-R1 to A-R6, A-R21, A-R26, A-R54, A-R55). The extractor keeps its own configuration (`power_query_extractor/config/cell_mappings.py`) and never imports `utils/constants.py` (READ).
- **The extraction configuration is written for the author to edit (HIGH).** It opens with "HOW TO EDIT THIS FILE" and the meaning of each field (`power_query_extractor/config/cell_mappings.py:1-27`), marks "MASTER CONFIGURATION - EDIT THIS SECTION" (`:28-31`), ends the list with a commented example "ADD MORE SHEETS HERE AS NEEDED" (`:229-241`), "OPTIONS - Edit these settings" (`:244-253`) and "DON'T EDIT BELOW THIS LINE" (`:255-257`). Which sheets and cells are read is [GST RULE] ⚠ (A-R74 to A-R82); a technical mismatch between this file and how the consolidator reads it is A-G1 / A-R88.
- **Backward-compatibility layer (READ).** Below the "DON'T EDIT" line, the file rebuilds the older `CELL_MAPPINGS` and `FIELD_DISPLAY_NAMES` dictionaries from `EXTRACTION_CONFIG` ("# Backward compatibility", `:259-278`; the file has 278 lines, the last without a line-end character), because `report_processor.py` still reads the older shape (`power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:37, 556-594`). The older format itself survived as `cell_mappings copy.py` until 47a1492 (shared - before the split on 30-10-2025; HS 1.7). So the configuration was redesigned before git (MEDIUM: the old format's compiled file is dated 21-06-2025, the new one 28-06-2025, HS 1.16) and the reader was adapted instead of rewritten.
- **How consistently constants are used** is in 8.7 P4: many values that exist in `utils/constants.py` are typed again elsewhere, and several constants are never used.

#### 8.3.6 Pure logic kept out of Tk, for testing (D19)

- **What the code is (READ).** July 2026 code puts rules into small modules with no window code: `gui/utils/setup_validation.py` ("Deliberately free of Tkinter", `:3-4`), `utils/requirements_check.py` ("no Tkinter, unit-tested", f363946 message), `power_query_extractor/core/refresh_naming.py` (one place for "is this a refreshed copy?", 2aaa2b1), `utils/excel_com.py` (one helper shared by both `_safe_open_workbook`s, ba2a753). Each has its own test file (`tests/test_setup_validation.py`, `tests/test_requirements_check.py`, `tests/test_refresh_naming.py`, `tests/test_excel_com.py`).
- **Reason — HIGH.** So rules can be tested without a display and without Excel; stated in the module docstrings and commit messages.
- **Limit (RAN, DCP 2.7; RAN me `out_s5_imports.txt`).** Because `gui/__init__.py:7` imports the whole main window, importing the "Tk-free" `gui.utils.setup_validation` through its package loads tkinter, openpyxl, `gui.main_window` and the extractor (334 modules in my run; DCP counted 222 in theirs — the number depends on what was already loaded). The file itself is Tk-free; its package is not.

#### 8.3.7 Shared helpers between the two halves, with a warning not to merge more

`utils/excel_com.py:1-15` explains why only the "is this workbook already open?" loop is shared: Step 3 opens "a freshly-copied LOCAL temp file" and needs only an 8.3 fallback, Step 4 opens "a NETWORK file that may still be locked from a just-finished Power Query refresh" and needs `\\?\` paths and close-by-name retries — "Do NOT merge those two strategies without validating BOTH flows against real Microsoft Excel" (READ, HIGH). This is a deliberate, documented duplication, not an oversight.

---

### 8.4 Why some things are done in a complex way, and the likely domain reason

#### 8.4.1 The Power Query refresh by key presses and fixed waits (D4; A-F21, A-R71, A-R72)

- **What the code does (READ; cannot run here).** For each report copy: `Dispatch("Excel.Application")` (`power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:218`); `Visible = True` "Keep it visible to avoid issues", `DisplayAlerts = False`, maximised (`:225-227`); open; wait 5 × 1 s ("Increased from 3 to 5", `:253`); bring Excel to the front with `WScript.Shell.AppActivate` up to 3 times and "continuing anyway" if that fails (`:258-276`); press `"%a"`, `"r"`, `"a"` one second apart ("Increased from 0.5", `:281-293`) = Alt+A, R, A = Data → Refresh All in English Excel ⚠; wait the configured seconds (`:297-302`); look for error dialogs (`:305-342`); wait `max(10, wait_time)` more (`:326-330`); check `Info!BB2` (`:345`); always save (`:348-351`). No `RefreshAll`, no `BackgroundQuery`, no `CalculateUntilAsyncQueriesDone` anywhere (READ, grep).
- **Evidence that it was tuned by trial and error, before git (HIGH).** The tuning comments "Increased from 0.5", "Increased from 3 to 5" are already in the first commit (`power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:189, 219, 224@edac6a3`), plus "# WAIT 7 SECONDS AS REQUESTED" above a 10-second loop (`:235@edac6a3`) — the author asked for waits in a chat and the code drifted from the comment. bd176bf (shared - before the split on 30-10-2025) then made the first wait configurable (5-60 s, default 10) instead of detecting the end of the refresh (HS bd176bf).
- **Evidence that it was kept on purpose (HIGH).** The July 2026 design note lists "Rewriting the Power Query refresh itself (the SendKeys approach and its fixed `time.sleep` waits stay as they are)" as out of scope (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-25-merge-extractor-design.md:125-126`).
- **The only refresh method A's history ever used (added during self-review, from Section 12E).** No `.py` file in any of A's 46 commits contains `RefreshAll`, `CalculateUntilAsyncQueriesDone` or `DispatchEx` (RAN during self-review: `git grep` over every commit of `A/main` → 0 files), so the key presses are not a replacement for an abandoned COM refresh inside the recorded history; anything tried earlier happened before git.
- **Why key presses instead of Excel's own `RefreshAll` command — LOW (not recorded anywhere).** Possible domain reasons, none provable here: (a) a `RefreshAll` sent through COM returned at once while Power Query kept refreshing in the background, so the saved file held old data — exactly the failure Standard 12 records as tested ("a plain `RefreshAll()` followed at once by a save stored the old 2 rows", `rebuild_pipeline_FINAL.md:860-866`); pressing the ribbon keys and waiting "worked" visibly; (b) Power Query privacy-level or credential prompts appear only in a visible Excel, hence "Keep it visible to avoid issues" (`:225`) — LOW. **NOT SURE — how to check:** ask the author whether `RefreshAll` through COM was tried and what went wrong (shared-history question 3); on Windows, refresh one report with `RefreshAll` + `CalculateUntilAsyncQueriesDone` and compare `Info!BB2` and a figure cell with the key-press result.
- **Consequences (cross-references).** The keys go to whatever window has focus (A-G55); the refresh cannot be confirmed and is saved regardless (A-G2, A-G3); about 36 s of fixed waiting per report at the default (A-R72, A-G50); English Excel key tips assumed ⚠ (A-G44).

#### 8.4.2 Step 3 attaches to a running Excel; Step 4 uses `Dispatch` (D5; A-R97, A-R103)

- **What the code does (READ).** Step 3: `GetActiveObject("Excel.Application")` first, `Dispatch` only if that fails (`core/excel_handler.py:123-128`), then `Visible = False`, `DisplayAlerts = False`, `ScreenUpdating = False` (`:131-133`); in the clean-up the comment says "Don't quit if Excel was already open" but the test is `if self.excel_app is None` (`:241-242`) and `self.excel_app` is only ever set to `None` (`:56`), so `Quit()` is always called (`:244`). Step 4: `Dispatch` for both sessions (`power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:218, 536`).
- **Likely reason — MEDIUM.** The author (or the AI) wanted to reuse an Excel that is already open, to save the start-up time of a new Excel per report and avoid many `EXCEL.EXE` processes, and to leave a user's own Excel running; the `excel_app` attribute and `__del__` (`core/excel_handler.py:56-64`) are the unfinished half of that idea (DCP 1.5, 3.6 B1; present since edac6a3, shared - before the split on 30-10-2025). The first commit's log recorded 6 × "Created new Excel instance" and 0 × "Using existing Excel instance" (HS 1.15), so in the logged runs the attach path was never taken (MEDIUM), which may be why the defect went unnoticed.
- **Standard 12 (fact only).** "Start a separate, hidden Excel … `DispatchEx` … Never take over the user's own open Excel" (`rebuild_pipeline_FINAL.md:851-855`). Gap A-G54.

#### 8.4.3 Reports built on local disk, then copied to the network once (D6; A-R98)

- **What the code does (READ).** The template is copied to `%TEMP%\gst_excel_temp\<report name>` (`core/excel_handler.py:53, 147-155`), Excel opens and saves that local copy (`:159, 203-207`), one `shutil.copy2` puts the finished file on the target (`:215`), the local file is deleted (`:254-260`); the openpyxl path does the same (`:269-279, 305-322`).
- **Reason — HIGH.** Stated in the comment (`core/excel_handler.py:135-146`) and in 12d505f (A only (after the split)): "While a workbook is open Excel performs many small random-access reads/writes; over a network share each is a slow round-trip." The comment also records the domain assumption that makes it safe: "Power Query is preserved: the report's data sources are ABSOLUTE paths written into the Links sheet" (`:143-146`) [GST RULE context: which files feed the report, A-R54 to A-R56; the `Links` cell positions are template cell positions ⚠].
- **Side effects (READ / MEDIUM).** Because Excel now opens a short local path, the 8.3 long-path fallback (`core/excel_handler.py:355-366`) is rarely needed for Step 3 (H1, MEDIUM). An Excel-saved workbook usually records the folder it was last saved in, which would now be the staging folder (H1 12d505f, MEDIUM; NOT SURE — how to check: unzip a report made on Windows and look at `xl/workbook.xml`). Step 4 does NOT stage: Excel opens and saves the refreshed copy directly on the share (`power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:164, 349`) — inconsistent with the Step 3 reasoning (XL 7.3).

#### 8.4.4 Caching folder listings, file details and existence answers (D7)

The office source and target folders are on a network share reached over a VPN (4f84ba9 message measured "on the real share"; `utils/helpers.py:267-269` "measured ~270ms/file on a VPN-backed SMB share" ⚠; `gui/tabs/setup_tab.py:135` "avoid stat'ing a UNC path on every keystroke"). HIGH that every one of the following exists to cut round-trips:

| Cache / shortcut | Where | Commit | What it saves | Trade-off (cross-reference) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| One `os.scandir` listing per scan, reusing each entry's stat | `utils/helpers.py:309-344`; passed on by `core/file_parser.py:158, 188` and `utils/helpers.py:129-166` | a603c02, 56aaad9 (A only (after the split)) | 3 glob passes per scan → 1 listing (a603c02); `get_file_info` 4 file-system calls → 2 (a603c02) → 0 with the listing's stat; measured 6.2 → 1.2 round-trips per file (56aaad9 message) ⚠; comment "Free on Windows - served from the directory listing" (`utils/helpers.py:333`) [Corrected during verification — originally "3 globs + 4 stats per file → 1 listing"] | A listing error throws away everything and reads as "no files" (A-R109) |
| Signature reads 16 at a time when there are 4 or more files | `utils/helpers.py:267-272, 346-357` | 4f84ba9 (A only (after the split)) | "11 min -> 41s on the real share" ⚠ | The scan still runs on the window's thread, so the window freezes for those seconds (A-G48) |
| No second validation in the parser | `core/file_parser.py:190-193` | a603c02 | One open + stat per file | Its comment says `scan_excel_files()` "already ran validate_excel_file()"; it calls the two halves instead (DCP 1.4) — wording only |
| Level-1 run folder worked out once per run | `core/file_organizer.py:150-161` | 275d9a4 (A only (after the split)) | In Re-run/Resume a full listing of the target per client | — (A-R111) |
| Step 4 reads each Version folder once for "has ITC / has Sales" and once for refresh times | `power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:20-82` | 275d9a4, 2aaa2b1 | Two globs per client → one listing | Runs on the window's thread (A-G48) |
| Setup checklist: re-check 350 ms after typing stops; remember each path's yes/no | `gui/tabs/setup_tab.py:135, 506-529` | 322717f (A only (after the split)) | A network check per keystroke and per repaint | A share that comes back keeps its old ✕ until a forced refresh (A-G20, A-R113) |
| The Step 4 tab never scans when the main window opens | `power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:127-139` (`auto_load=False` from `gui/tabs/extract_tab.py:74-80`) | bfcb24a (A only (after the split)) | A network scan at every start-up ("The folder is pre-filled; the user presses Scan", bfcb24a message) | Only the embedded tab: the standalone extractor (`auto_load=True`) still scans at start-up when it is given or finds a folder (`power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:135-139, 587-597`) |

Design comment (HIGH): the scan and report-building changes are described as behaviour-preserving ("behavior-preserving" in a603c02 and 275d9a4, "Behavior preserved" in 12d505f, "signature/behaviour is unchanged" in 56aaad9) and as checked against characterization snapshots by the author's AI assistant (messages of a603c02, 12d505f, 275d9a4, 56aaad9, 4f84ba9); those snapshots are not in the repository (H1, H2: unverifiable). The Setup checklist (322717f) and the Step 4 tab (bfcb24a) are new behaviour, not described that way [Corrected during verification — originally "every one of these is described as behaviour-preserving"]. RAN (H2): identical file lists before and after on a mixed made-up folder; 5 stat calls per file removed.

#### 8.4.5 Refreshing a copy, and two Excel sessions per report (D8; A-F21, A-F22, A-F23)

- **What the code does (READ).** Step 4 copies `ITC_Report_….xlsx` to `<stem><suffix>.xlsx` (`power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:127-130, 164`), refreshes and saves the copy in a visible Excel (`:209-415`), waits 3 s "for file to be released" (`:183-185`), then opens the copy again in a second, hidden Excel to read the cells (`:527-636`).
- **Reasons.** Copy: keep the Step 3 report as created, so a run can be repeated and "Skip Refresh" can reuse an earlier copy (`:132-159`) — HIGH. Two sessions: the key-press refresh needs a visible, focused window, while reading is done hidden — MEDIUM; reading only after save + reopen may also have been the only reliable way to get the refreshed values (LOW; not recorded).
- **Consequences.** Four Excel starts/attaches and four `Quit()`s per client (XL 5.2); a failed refresh still leaves a file with the "refreshed" name (A-G2); the copy may be taken from an earlier copy on some file servers (A-G15).

#### 8.4.6 Clicking away Excel error dialogs (D9; A-F26, A-R105)

- **What the code does (READ).** During each refresh wait it looks at every top-level window on the desktop for a visible dialog of class `#32770`, `NUIDialog` or `bosa_sdm_msword` whose title contains an error word, reads its text, and clicks a button labelled OK / Close / Yes / Continue or sends it a close message (`power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:305-342, 417-525`).
- **Likely reason — MEDIUM.** The refresh is a batch over many clients; a Power Query error dialog (for example a source file that cannot be found) would stop the key-press sequence and block every later client, and `DisplayAlerts = False` (`:226`) does not suppress such dialogs. The dialog text is kept as the report's error, so the user later sees why a refresh failed (`:315-317`). MEDIUM that it was tuned in real use before git (shared-history 5 lists "Excel error dialogs during refresh" among the pre-git traces and rates that list MEDIUM; the dialog code is already in the first commit, `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:240-277@edac6a3`) [Corrected during verification — originally HIGH, which the cited source does not support].
- **Consequence.** It can click another program's dialog (A-G55); the word list and class names assume an English Windows/Excel ⚠ (A-G44).

#### 8.4.7 The refresh check: `Info!BB2` (D10; A-R73) [GST RULE]

- **What the code does (READ).** [GST RULE] (the registry tags A-R73 as one). A refresh counts as good if no error dialog was seen and the sheet `info` (any case) has a non-empty, non-zero, non-error value in `BB2`; the success message calls it "Client Name" (`power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:638-685`) ⚠ (template cell position).
- **Likely reason — MEDIUM.** The templates contain a query that writes the client's name into `Info!BB2`; if that cell is filled, the queries ran. It is cheap and independent of every other sheet. It cannot tell a fresh value from one left from an earlier refresh (A-G3). Whether this is the right test is the author's call (shared-history question 6).

#### 8.4.8 Short names, state codes and path-length fallbacks (D11; A-R35, A-R39, A-R104)

- **What the code does (READ).** Level-2 folders use the two-letter state code (`core/file_organizer.py:83-91`, "Use state code instead of full name" `:91`) [GST RULE] ⚠ (the state list and codes change over time; A-R21 to A-R23); client names are shortened at 35 characters by default (A-R35, A-R36); the category folders were shortened from "GSTR-3B Exports" / "Other ITC related files" / "Sales related files" to `GSTR3B` / `ITC` / `Sales` (`utils/constants.py:85-95`, 7347383, A only (after the split)); opens fall back to 8.3 short paths (`core/excel_handler.py:355-366`) or `\\?\` long-path prefixes (`power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:720-732`) above 218 characters.
- **Reason — HIGH.** Stated: "Excel/Power Query fail above ~218 characters of full path" (`utils/constants.py:85-90`) ⚠, and 7347383's message: on "a real run (3030 output files on the network share) the worst path was 270 characters and 1094 files (36%) exceeded Excel's ~218 limit, which is why long client names have been failing" ⚠. The shortening is a quick patch (shorter labels), not a guard: the commit itself says "the margin is thin (215 vs 218)" and depends on a planned shorter share root (an `FY 2025-26` folder ⚠) (H3). Nothing measures a path before creating it (A-G41). The code comment drops the "modelled, assuming the shorter root" part of the message (H3 7347383 discrepancy (a)).

#### 8.4.9 Copy, never move; backups next to the file (D12; A-R45 to A-R47)

- **What the code does (READ).** Source files are only read and copied with `shutil.copy2` plus a size comparison (`utils/helpers.py:172-215`); a Fresh run that meets an existing destination first makes `<stem>_backup_<DDMMYY_HHMM><ext>` in the same folder (`utils/helpers.py:217-234`; `core/file_organizer.py:276-282`).
- **Reason — HIGH.** The source folder holds what the client sent; the help text promises "nothing here is moved, renamed or deleted" and "the template itself is never modified" (`gui/tabs/setup_tab.py:74-79`). RAN (TRACE T6): checksums and dates of the originals unchanged. Backups beside the file inside a linked folder are a side effect (A-G9).

#### 8.4.10 Recognition by name pattern in one flat folder, after size and signature checks (D13)

- **What the code does (READ).** Only the top level of the source folder; only `.xlsx`/`.xls`/`.xlsm` names; at least 1,024 bytes; first bytes `PK\x03\x04` or `\xd0\xcf\x11\xe0`; then six name patterns (`utils/helpers.py:262-365`; `utils/constants.py:13-62`) [GST RULE] ⚠ (A-R1 to A-R12).
- **Likely reasons.** Name patterns: the files come from portal downloads and office tools with fixed names, and the program adapts to that rather than requiring client sub-folders — MEDIUM (the older audit's D5 says the same, `PROJECT_AUDIT_ANNUALSTATEMENT.md:689-690`). The optional duplicate markers record names that really arrived with a duplicate number such as "(1)": a leading `(N)` for GSTR-3B files since the first commit (`utils/constants.py:31`, edac6a3, shared - before the split on 30-10-2025) and a trailing `(N)` for IMS Reco files since 5c8ce95 (`utils/constants.py:23`, A only (after the split); its message: IMS Reco file names "ending in a duplicate marker like " (1)" / "(2)" … were not detected") — HIGH that such names occurred (a fix was made for them); MEDIUM that the numbers come from a browser saving the same download twice (the message does not say where they come from) [Corrected during verification — originally quoted the message as saying "real downloads", which it does not]. Size and signature checks: they silently drop Excel's own `~$` lock files and broken or renamed downloads — MEDIUM; that they never appear anywhere is A-G37.

#### 8.4.11 The start-up gate and the install offer (D14; A-F1, A-R124 to A-R128)

- **What the code does (READ).** Before the GUI is imported, `main.py:66-106` checks openpyxl and pywin32 with `find_spec` (`utils/requirements_check.py:37-70`); pywin32 is essential only when `sys.platform == 'win32'` (`:17, 57`); if anything is missing it offers to run `<this Python> -m pip install -r <app folder>/requirements.txt` and restart (`utils/dependency_installer.py:26-74, 88-158`).
- **Reason — HIGH (four commits within 17 minutes on 26-07-2026, all A only (after the split)).** bfcb24a made the main window import the extractor, whose pywin32 imports were unguarded, so "on a Python without pywin32 the whole app died with "No module named 'pythoncom'" and never opened"; on the author's PC "py -> python3.14t.exe (free-threaded build, no pywin32) while python -> python.exe (has it)" (c463256 message). c463256 made pywin32 optional; f363946 added a plain-words check because the crash "blamed missing SOURCE FILES"; be6418c reversed "optional" for Windows because the openpyxl fallback strips Power Query; a5ad487 softened "refuse" into "offer, then refuse" ("This removes the typing, not the consent") (H3 safety chain).
- **Design tension (fact only).** The check is a start-up policy, not a save-time `DataMashup` check (A-G7); it uses `find_spec`, which cannot see a present-but-broken pywin32 (RAN XL E2); it installs the whole `requirements.txt`, pytest included, into whatever Python runs the app (A-G53, A-G59). Standard 13 says "Nothing is installed on users' PCs" (`rebuild_pipeline_FINAL.md:924`). See 9.9.

#### 8.4.12 "Full pipeline" never starts the refresh; the Step 4 tab never scans at start-up (D16; A-F5, A-F18)

- **What the code does (READ).** In "full" mode, after Step 3 the worker asks the window's thread (`root.after(0, …)`) to select Step 4, put the target folder into its folder box and run its folder scan (`gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:136-175`, `panel.scan_folder()` at `:169`); in "organize" mode it only logs a hint (`:145-149`). The embedded Step 4 panel is built with `auto_load=False`, so the main window's start-up does not scan (`gui/tabs/extract_tab.py:74-80`; `power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:127-139`); the standalone extractor window keeps `auto_load=True` and scans at start-up when it is given or finds a folder (`:135-139, 587-597`).
- **Reason — HIGH.** Code comment: "does NOT start the refresh: that drives Excel for many minutes per report, so it stays an explicit press" (`gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:139-142`); bfcb24a: building the panel at start-up must not scan the network. Design philosophy visible in 510f7b4: never block, "point at" the next step (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-25-merge-extractor-design.md:78-81`). The promised "Continue to extraction" button for organise-only mode was replaced by a log line (`gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:145-149`; design note `:80-81`) — DOCS P15.

#### 8.4.13 One settings file shared by two programs (D17; A-F27, A-R114 to A-R118)

- **What the code does (READ).** The main window writes `Path.home() / '.gst_organizer_cache.json'` (`gui/utils/cache_manager.py:15, 45-46`); the standalone extractor reads the same file first, then three files relative to the current folder that nothing writes, with four possible key names (`power_query_extractor/extractor_main.py:38-58`).
- **Reasons.** One small JSON file is enough for one user's last choices (HIGH; older audit D4). The extra file names and keys (`gst_organizer_cache.json`, `.cache/app_state.json`, `config/last_session.json`; `target_path`, `output_folder`, `last_target`) look like an AI's "try every likely place" guess written before the real file was known — MEDIUM; the extractor looked ONLY in those wrong places until c1583d6 (A only (after the split), HS O1), and `.gitignore:45, 64` still lists two of them.

#### 8.4.14 Dark mode by capture-and-replay (D18; A-F28)

- **Reason — HIGH.** The module docstring and aeb83cf (A only (after the split)) describe the first design's failure: it "mutated widgets and then reversed that by GUESSING", so "One toggle therefore flattened every coloured surface permanently" (`gui/utils/dark_mode_manager.py:2-14`). The rebuild records each widget's actual colours before the first change and replays them (`:199-268`), keyed by the widget object in a `WeakKeyDictionary` (`:68`). The capture-once rule is also why later colour changes are lost and new widgets stay light (A-G64), patched per screen in c89c1d4, 725fbaf and 169c7b5 (8.5).

### 8.7 Pattern consistency

For each pattern: the project's own established way, the files that follow it, the files that break it, and whether the difference matters. "Consistent" / "Inconsistent" is a technical rating, not a judgement on any GST rule.

#### P1 — Error handling: no single established style (Inconsistent)

| Style | Followed by (examples, file:line) | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Status dictionary `{'success': …, 'error': …}` | the whole extractor: `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:70-77, 90-104, 116-123, 151-155, 174-178, 199-207, 370-381`; `core/file_organizer.py:254-300` (`'status'`); `core/file_parser.py:132`; `utils/helpers.py:146, 166` | Newest-style code in the extractor uses this throughout |
| True / False | `utils/helpers.py:193-215` (`safe_copy_file`); `core/excel_handler.py:93-102, 221-228, 310-314, 405-409`; `utils/dependency_installer.py:52-60` (`(bool, text)`) | — |
| None on failure | `utils/helpers.py:222, 234` (`create_backup`); `core/file_organizer.py:379`; `utils/helpers.py:580-590` (returns the input) | — |
| Raise | `core/file_parser.py:153, 155, 177`; `core/file_organizer.py:63, 69, 148`; `core/excel_handler.py:84` (the same function otherwise returns True/False); both `_safe_open_workbook`s (`core/excel_handler.py:331, 369`; `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:694, 703, 799`); `power_query_extractor/core/data_consolidator.py:186` | — |
| Swallow | 68 of the 147 exception handlers leave no trace at all: 42 swallow the error outright and 26 silently fall back to a substitute value (S67 6.8.1). Separately, 23 handlers project-wide are bare `except:` (RAN, VERIFY AST count: 147 handlers, 23 bare) [Corrected during verification — originally "42 handlers leave no trace at all, 23 of them bare `except:`": the 23 bare handlers are a separate count, and some of them do leave a trace] | bare `except:` examples: `core/excel_handler.py:126` (falls back to `Dispatch` and logs "Created new Excel instance"), `:235, 245, 251, 302` (nothing); `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:401, 408, 414, 444, 452, 471, 511, 624, 630, 635` (nothing), `:269` and `:767` (these two DO log a line: "Could not activate window…", "Could not get short path") |

- **What IS consistent (HIGH):** only GUI-facing files show message boxes (`gui/handlers/*`, `gui/main_window.py`, `power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py`, `launch_extractor.py`, `utils/dependency_installer.py`); `core/` and the extractor's `core/` never do (S67 6.8.1, READ grep of `messagebox.`). Start-up problems in `main.py` go to the console, not to a box (`main.py:114-134`).
- **Breaks that matter (READ):** `create_report_from_template` raises for a missing template but returns `False` for everything else (`core/excel_handler.py:82-102`); the Step 3 worker reports problems only on screen and only exceptions to the log file (`gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:304-475, 406, 524`); `ReportProcessor._log` writes every line at INFO, errors included (`power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:53-60`); "Export Complete" is followed by "Export Error" off Windows (`gui/handlers/client_handler.py:251-257`; A-G31). Errors in button callbacks go to Tk's console printer because there is no `sys.excepthook` (A-G30).
- The older audit's "Error handling in COM operations … CONSISTENT" (`PROJECT_AUDIT_ANNUALSTATEMENT.md:712`) is true only for the `finally` structure; Step 3's clean-up can itself raise and skip the rest (`core/excel_handler.py:238-240`; A-G28).

#### P2 — Platform checks and import guards (Inconsistent; details in 9.5)

- **Established pattern (HIGH):** `core/excel_handler.py:19-28` — check `platform.system() == 'Windows'`, then `try: import win32com.client, pythoncom` / `except ImportError`, set a flag (`USE_WIN32COM`), and branch on it later (`:90-102`).
- **Followed by:** `utils/helpers.py:580-590` (`get_short_path`: platform check + import inside `try` + broad `except`); `gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:507-512` (platform check before `os.startfile` / `open` / `xdg-open`).
- **Broken by:**
  - `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:20-36` — `try/except ImportError` with NO platform check and a different flag name (`WIN32_AVAILABLE`); before c463256 (A only (after the split)) it had no guard at all (`:11-15@edac6a3`). Works, but a second idiom.
  - `utils/requirements_check.py:17` — `sys.platform == 'win32'` instead of `platform.system() == 'Windows'` (same answer on normal Windows Python; LOW).
  - `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:761-767` — a second local `import win32api` inside a bare `except:`, redundant with `:23`.
  - `gui/handlers/client_handler.py:255` and `power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:973` — `os.startfile` (Windows only) with no platform check, only inside `try` (A-G31).
  - `gui/tabs/extract_tab.py:24-30` — a second guard on top of the extractor's own (`except Exception`), whose "needs pywin32" notice can no longer appear for a missing pywin32 (RAN DCP 1.5; A-R129).
  - `main.py:17` — console-dependent `sys.stdout.buffer` with no guard at all (RAN me `out_s4_noconsole.txt`; A-G22).
  - tkinter is imported unguarded in every GUI file but guarded in `utils/dependency_installer.py:95-99` (deliberate: the installer must work without Tk) and imported inside the `except` block of `launch_extractor.py:20-22` (if tkinter itself is the problem, the error handler fails too; LOW).
- **Matters?** MEDIUM: three idioms for "are we on Windows / is pywin32 there", and the start-up check (`find_spec`) and the import guards can disagree (A-G7).

#### P3 — Logging (Mostly consistent, with exceptions)

- **Established pattern (HIGH):** a module logger `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` and `logger.x(...)` calls. RAN me (grep): 15 non-test modules define one — `core/excel_handler.py:43`, `core/file_organizer.py:18`, `core/file_parser.py:18`, `utils/helpers.py:19`, `utils/dependency_installer.py:20`, `gui/handlers/file_handler.py:10`, `gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:14`, `gui/main_window.py:38`, `gui/tabs/extract_tab.py:19`, `gui/utils/cache_manager.py:8`, `gui/utils/dark_mode_manager.py:22`, `power_query_extractor/extractor_main.py:21`, `power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:17`, `power_query_extractor/core/data_consolidator.py:13`, `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:41`.
- **Broken by (RAN me grep):** root-logger calls `main.py:99, 105, 115, 131` and `core/excel_handler.py:26, 28` (both at import time, before that module's own logger exists at `:43`); inline `logging.getLogger(__name__)` at `gui/main_window.py:193` (its module logger `:38` is never used) and `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:34`; an unused logger in `gui/handlers/file_handler.py:10`; `print()` only in `main.py` (14 calls, console start-up report). Two `logging.basicConfig` set-ups, each writing a log file into the current folder: `main.py:20-27` and `power_query_extractor/extractor_main.py:12-19` (8.3.1). Files that never log: `gui/handlers/client_handler.py`, the tab files except `extract_tab.py`, `gui/utils/ui_helpers.py`, `status_bar.py`, `setup_validation.py`, the widgets, `utils/requirements_check.py`, `utils/excel_com.py`, `power_query_extractor/core/refresh_naming.py` (DCP 2.2).
- **Two "sinks" that do not agree (READ):** the on-screen log and the log file get different messages (P1). A global side effect: `core/excel_handler.py:17` switches off ALL Python warnings for the whole program when it is imported (RAN me `out_s5_imports.txt`: one `('ignore', None)` filter added; A-R108, A-G61).

#### P5 — Threading and screen updates from worker threads (Inconsistent)

- **Established rule (HIGH), stated in code:** "Tk is not thread-safe … Every worker-thread UI update goes through here" (`power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:989-1010`, `_ui`, c1f425e, A only (after the split)); the design note made it "mandatory, not optional" (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-25-merge-extractor-design.md:58-69`), citing `_log_async` in the main app as "the pattern already proven".
- **Followed by:** the extractor worker (`power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:885-966`; all log, progress, dialogs and button resets go through `_ui`), except two direct reads of Tk variables from the worker (`:890-891`). The main app's `_log_async` / `_progress_async` (`gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:23-36`; 10 and 4 calls in the worker, RAN me count).
- **Broken by:** the main app's Step 3 worker `process_files_thread` (`gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:182-530`): 45 direct `self.app.log_message(...)` calls (RAN me count, lines 182-530), which end in `log_widget.after(0, …)` made FROM the worker thread (`gui/utils/ui_helpers.py:16-25`); direct `update_progress` (`gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:459, 482` → `gui/main_window.py:287-291`); Tk-variable reads (`gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:190-194, 219-225, 301, 310, 332, 501`); modal dialogs raised from the worker (`gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:498-502, 525`); direct button changes in `finally` (`gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:529-530`); `_maybe_continue_to_extraction` reads `workflow_mode` on the worker (`gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:145`). RAN (DCP): on Linux/Tcl 9 the mixed calls kept their order; on the Windows Python build NOT SURE (A-G70).
- **Other thread rules that differ:** Step 3 has a re-entry guard (`gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:71-76`), Step 4 has none (`power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:845-883`; A-G65); neither checks the other (A-G71); both workers are daemon threads (`gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:129-133`; `power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:878-883`), and the close question covers Step 3 only (`gui/main_window.py:344-355`; A-G27). Folder scans run on the window's own thread in both halves (`gui/handlers/file_handler.py:71-72`; `power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:611-668`; A-G48).
- The older audit's "Thread-safe UI updates — CONSISTENT across processing_handler" (`PROJECT_AUDIT_ANNUALSTATEMENT.md:710`) was never true (DOCS PC3).

#### P6 — File paths and where files are written (Inconsistent)

- **Established pattern (HIGH):** `pathlib.Path` for paths (18 non-test modules import it; RAN me AST list). **Broken by:** `os.path` in `launch_extractor.py:10` and `gui/handlers/client_handler.py:252`; `os.scandir` on purpose for speed (`utils/helpers.py:328`; `power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:33, 61`); text surgery on paths (`utils/helpers.py:418-422`; `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:724-731`).
- **Where the program finds and writes its own files — four different anchors (READ; DCP 2.6, EXT 4):**

| Anchor | Used for | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Program folder (`Path(__file__).parent`) | search path; `requirements.txt`; creates `logs/`, `temp/`, missing `__init__.py` | `main.py:31-43, 84`; `launch_extractor.py:10` |
| Current folder (wherever the program was started) | `gst_organizer.log`, `pq_extractor.log`, three extractor settings fallbacks | `main.py:24`; `power_query_extractor/extractor_main.py:16, 42-44` |
| Home folder | the settings file | `gui/utils/cache_manager.py:15`; `power_query_extractor/extractor_main.py:41`; `power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:118` |
| System temp | report staging | `core/excel_handler.py:53` |

- **Search path:** `main.py:32` puts the program folder FIRST (`insert(0, …)`), `launch_extractor.py:10` puts it LAST (`append`) — two ways for the same need (LOW today; matters with a portable Python, 9.5.2).
- **Text encoding when writing files:** UTF-8 is given only for the organisation report (`core/file_organizer.py:371`); every other text file uses the PC's default code page — settings (`gui/utils/cache_manager.py:22, 45`, but its JSON is pure ASCII, RAN EXT t8), the exported list (`gui/handlers/client_handler.py:241`), both log files (`main.py:24`; `power_query_extractor/extractor_main.py:16`), the placeholder `__init__.py` (`main.py:43`). RAN (EXT t15, S67 r6): with cp1252 the emoji log lines are lost (A-G56).

#### P7 — API design (Mixed)

| Aspect | Established way | Follows | Breaks / notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| How GUI parts talk | Each tab/handler receives the whole app object and reads/writes its attributes; the app exposes one-line delegators | all of `gui/handlers/*`, `gui/tabs/*` (8.3.4) | `ExtractorPanel` is the opposite: parent-agnostic, keeps its own state, needs only a parent frame (`power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:98-139`) |

| Button wiring | `command=` (honours "disabled", works from the keyboard — `gui/tabs/setup_tab.py:383-385` explains why) | `gui/tabs/setup_tab.py` (9 uses), `power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py` (12), `gui/widgets/title_bar.py:32`, `gui/widgets/collapsible_frame.py:21` | `.bind('<Button-1>')` on every Step 2 and Step 3 button: `gui/tabs/validation_tab.py:118, 130, 142, 190`; `gui/tabs/processing_tab.py:74, 87` (RAN me grep; A-G62) |
| Project imports | absolute `from utils…` / `from core…` in `core/`, `gui/handlers/`, most tabs; relative inside packages | e.g. `core/file_parser.py:12-13`; `gui/main_window.py:24-36` | mixed in one file: `gui/tabs/setup_tab.py:17-22`; the extractor's `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:37-39` uses relative imports for its own package (`..core.refresh_naming` from inside `core`) and an absolute one for the main app's `utils.excel_com` (RAN me AST list) |
| Long-running work | a daemon worker thread per step | both steps | scans and Step 4's status refresh stay on the window thread (P5) |
| Rules separated from screens | pure modules + tests (8.3.6) | July 2026 code | older code keeps rules inside handlers (e.g. long-name warnings `gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:86-113`, `gui/handlers/client_handler.py:191-199`) |
| Lessons enforced by tests | guard tests that read the source (`tests/test_scroll_bindings.py`: no `unbind_all(`, every `bind_all(` with `add='+'`) | bf2f1dd | line-based text checks; only scroll bindings are guarded |

### 8.8 Re-export and API patterns, and the maintenance they need

**`__init__.py` re-exports (READ; RAN DCP 2.7 for completeness and use).**

| Package file | Re-exports | `__all__` | Complete today? | Used by any program file? | Maintenance it needs | Side effect |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `core/__init__.py:6-13` | `FileParser`, `FileOrganizer`, `ExcelHandler`; `__version__ = '3.0.0'`, `__author__` | yes (`:10`) | yes | no (every caller imports `core.file_parser` etc. directly) | none today | importing ANY `core` module runs this file and so loads `core/excel_handler.py`, which switches off all warnings and probes pywin32 (DCP 2.7) |
| `gui/__init__.py:7-11` | `GSTOrganizerApp`; `__version__ = '3.0.0'` | yes | yes | no (`main.py:109` imports `gui.main_window`) | none | importing ANY `gui` sub-module loads the whole main window, tkinter, openpyxl and the extractor (RAN me `out_s5_imports.txt`: 334 modules for `gui.utils.setup_validation`) |
| `gui/tabs/__init__.py:4-8` | `SetupTab`, `ValidationTab`, `ProcessingTab` | yes | **no** — `ExtractTab` (bfcb24a) missing | no | add each new tab by hand | — |
| `gui/handlers/__init__.py:4-8` | `FileHandler`, `ClientHandler`, `ProcessingHandler` | yes | yes | no | — | — |
| `gui/utils/__init__.py:4-9` | `DarkModeManager`, `CacheManager`, `UIHelpers`, `StatusBar` | yes | **no** — `setup_validation` (322717f) not listed | only as a sub-module: `gui/tabs/setup_tab.py:21` (`from ..utils import setup_validation as sv`) | — | — |
| `gui/widgets/__init__.py:4-7` | `CollapsibleFrame`, `TitleBar` | yes | **no** — `Tooltip` (322717f) missing | no | — | — |
| `utils/__init__.py:6-38` | 9 constants and 22 helpers; `__version__ = '3.0.0'` | yes (`:22-36`) | **no** — missing `WORKFLOW_MODES`, `STATE_CODE_MAPPING`, `TEMPLATE_EXTENSIONS`, `MAX_FILE_SIZE_MB`, `EXCEL_SIGNATURES`, `get_short_path`, `get_state_code`, `create_client_state_key`, and the modules `excel_com`, `requirements_check`, `dependency_installer`; updated once (56aaad9 added `scan_excel_files`) | no | every new constant/helper must be added twice (import list and `__all__`); it re-exports dead helpers (`get_date_only`, `get_unique_path`, `calculate_file_hash`, `get_relative_excel_path`) | — |
| `power_query_extractor/__init__.py:1-3` and its `config/`, `core/`, `gui/` `__init__.py` files | nothing (`__version__ = "1.0.0"`; the three sub-package files hold only a one-line docstring each, e.g. `"""Core processing components"""`, and no import) [Corrected during verification — originally "the three sub-package files are empty"; READ: 45, 32 and 46 bytes] | no | n/a | n/a | none | — |

- **Established practice (HIGH):** in A, nobody imports from a package root; every import names the module directly (RAN DCP grep: only tests use `from gui.utils import …` style). So the re-export lists are dead weight, and four of them have already drifted (`gui/tabs`, `gui/utils`, `gui/widgets`, `utils` — the four "**no**" rows above) [Corrected during verification — originally "drifted three times"]; the maintenance they "require" (add new names to `__all__`) has simply not been done, without any effect on the program. Their only real effect is the eager loading in the last column.
- **`__version__` strings** (`'3.0.0'` ×3, `'1.0.0'`) are never read (A-R130); the visible version "3.0" is typed separately in the window title, status bar, console banner, welcome text, `main.py`'s docstring and `requirements.txt` (`utils/constants.py:134`; `gui/utils/status_bar.py:29`; `main.py:2, 6, 63`; `gui/main_window.py:393`; `requirements.txt:1`; A-R156) — any version bump needs all of them.

| `REQUIREMENTS` in code vs `requirements.txt` | The start-up check's own list of packages (openpyxl, pywin32 as `pythoncom`) | Two lists to keep in step; the installer installs the FILE, the check reads the CODE list (lxml and pytest only in the file) | `utils/requirements_check.py:37-61`; `requirements.txt:5-15` |

### 9.0 How to read this section

Markers, IDs, ⚠ and the terms table are those of 8.0. Versions that "work here" were RAN on this Linux computer: Python 3.14.6 with Tcl/Tk 9.0, openpyxl 3.1.5, lxml 6.1.3, et_xmlfile 2.0.0, pytest 9.1.1 (with iniconfig 2.3.1, packaging 26.3, pluggy 1.7.0, Pygments 2.21.0), NO pywin32 and no pip (RAN me: package metadata of `/root/merge-scratch/venv-A`; START). Interpreters 3.11.17, 3.12.3 and 3.13.16 also exist here, all without tkinter; 3.11 and 3.12 also lack openpyxl, while 3.13.16 has openpyxl 3.1.5 and lxml 6.1.3 in its system package folder (RAN VERIFY: `python3.13 -I -c "import openpyxl"` succeeds) [Corrected during verification — originally "without tkinter or openpyxl"]. They were used only for the syntax and name-cleaning checks in 9.4. Every package and Python version is time-varying ⚠.

| Source | What it says |
|---|---|
| `requirements.txt:2` | "Python 3.7 or higher required" ⚠ (unchanged since edac6a3) |
| `README.md:51` | "3.7 or higher (3.8+ recommended)" ⚠ [Corrected during self-review - originally cited as `README.md:50`, but Section 11.1.7 (corrected during verification) revealed that line 50 is empty; READ during self-review: the text is on line 51] |

| Commit messages | on the author's PC `py` starts `python3.14t.exe` (free-threaded Python 3.14, without pywin32) and `python` starts `python.exe` (with pywin32) (c463256, f363946, be6418c; A only (after the split)) ⚠. The messages do not state `python.exe`'s version; MEDIUM that it is also a Python 3.14 (it is the interpreter the author's AI assistant ran the tests and Excel checks with in July 2026, but no message names its version) — NOT SURE, how to check: `python -c "import sys; print(sys.version)"` on that PC [Corrected during verification — originally "runs Python 3.14 as `python.exe`"]. Compiled files of 2025 show Python 3.12 and 3.13 (HS 1.16) |
| Standard 13 | "All testing used Python 3.14" (`rebuild_pipeline_FINAL.md:931`) ⚠ |

**What the code itself needs (RAN me unless marked).**
- **Syntax:** all 62 `.py` files (43 program, 19 test) parse with the Python 3.7 grammar (`ast.parse(…, feature_version=(3, 7))`, `out_s1_syntax.txt`) and compile with Python 3.11, 3.12, 3.13 and 3.14 (`out_s2_compile.txt`). The grammar check is best-effort (it catches new syntax such as `:=`, `match` or `X | None`, not every newer library call) — MEDIUM that 3.7 syntax is enough; no 3.7 interpreter exists here, so actually running on 3.7 is NOT SURE (how to check: run the test suite under a 3.7 or 3.8 interpreter).
- **Library calls that set a floor (READ, HIGH from Python's documented history):** `subprocess.run(..., capture_output=True, text=True)` needs 3.7 (`utils/dependency_installer.py:47-50`); `typing.NamedTuple` classes with a default field need 3.6.1 (`utils/requirements_check.py:20-25`); dictionaries keep insertion order by guarantee only from 3.7, and the code relies on that order in places: the file patterns are tried in the order of `FILE_PATTERNS` (`core/file_parser.py:82-128`; the six prefixes do not overlap, so the match result does not depend on it — A_code_core_utils note, READ `utils/constants.py:15-55`), and the consolidated workbook's sheets are created in the order of `EXTRACTION_CONFIG` (`power_query_extractor/core/data_consolidator.py:45`) [Corrected during verification — the phrase "in this dict order" was quoted as if from the code; it is from the EXT notes]. So the code's own floor is 3.7, matching the stated minimum.
- **Package floors (RAN me: installed metadata):** openpyxl 3.1.5 and lxml 6.1.3 declare Python ≥3.8; pytest 9.1.1 declares ≥3.10. Because `requirements.txt` gives only minimums, pip on an older Python would pick older package versions; whether `openpyxl>=3.1.2` can be satisfied at all on 3.7 is NOT SURE (how to check: `pip download openpyxl==3.1.2 --python-version 3.7 --only-binary=:all:`). The versions actually tested (here and, by the commit messages, on the author's PC) are 3.14 ⚠.
- **Behaviour that changes with the Python version (RAN me, `out_s3_pyver.txt`):** `pathlib`'s idea of a "suffix" for a name ending in a dot changed in Python 3.14. A-R20's cleaner keeps the "suffix" aside, so the same made-up client name gives different names:

| Made-up client | Python 3.11 / 3.12 / 3.13 | Python 3.14 |
|---|---|---|
| `ClientA Co.` | `ClientA_Co` → `ITC_Report_ClientA_Co_DL_….xlsx` | `ClientA_Co.` → `ITC_Report_ClientA_Co._DL_….xlsx` |
| `ClientB Pvt. Ltd.` | `ClientB_Pvt._Ltd` | `ClientB_Pvt._Ltd.` |
| `ClientC Traders` | `ClientC_Traders` | `ClientC_Traders` |

  This decides report file names (`gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:292`), Level-4 folder suffixes (`core/file_organizer.py:90`) and copied file names (`core/file_organizer.py:271`); running the same batch on two Python versions gives differently named reports. Step 4 recognises reports by prefix, so it still finds them (READ `power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:20-42`). Technical point; A-G40.
- **Other version-sensitive points:** a603c02 (A only (after the split)) replaced three `glob` searches — case-insensitive on Windows only — with a lower-cased name test meant to "reproduce" them (`utils/helpers.py:325-330`), which made the scan case-insensitive on Linux too, a behaviour change off Windows only (RAN H1); the free-threaded 3.14t build was the interpreter WITHOUT pywin32 on the author's PC (c463256) — whether pywin32 offers a build for it is NOT SURE (how to check: `py -m pip install pywin32` on that interpreter; H3 a5ad487 item 6). Python's default text encoding is planned to become UTF-8 in a later version (PEP 686, Python 3.15 ⚠ — from memory, not checked here; how to check: the PEP's status page), which would change how the log files and exported list are written (P6).
