#### 9.5.2 Inconsistencies across files (flagged)

1. **Three guard idioms** for the same need: platform check + `ImportError` (`core/excel_handler.py:21-28`, `utils/helpers.py:583-585`); `ImportError` only (`power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:20-36`); `except Exception` around the import of a module that is already guarded (`gui/tabs/extract_tab.py:24-30`) — whose "needs pywin32" card can therefore never show for a missing pywin32 and would blame pywin32 for any other failure (A-R129).
2. **Two platform tests:** `platform.system() == 'Windows'` (`core/excel_handler.py:21`, `utils/helpers.py:583`, `gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:507`) and `sys.platform == 'win32'` (`utils/requirements_check.py:17`). Equal on normal Windows CPython; different only on unusual builds (LOW).
3. **The start-up check and the import guards can disagree:** the check only looks for the FILE `pythoncom` with `find_spec` (`utils/requirements_check.py:64-70`), while Step 3 needs `win32com.client` AND `pythoncom` to IMPORT (`core/excel_handler.py:22-25`). RAN (XL E2, simulated): a present-but-broken pywin32 passes the gate and Step 3 silently falls back to openpyxl (A-G7).
4. **Three texts still call pywin32 optional** after be6418c made it essential on Windows: `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:11-13` ("genuinely optional: the main organizer works without it"), `gui/tabs/extract_tab.py:21-23` and `:101-105` ("Steps 1-3 are unaffected: organising files and creating the reports works without pywin32") versus `utils/requirements_check.py:49-57` (HIGH, H3).
5. **`os.startfile`:** platform-checked in one place (`gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:507`), unchecked in two (`gui/handlers/client_handler.py:255`; `power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:973`).
6. **The standalone extractor runs no requirements check at all** (`launch_extractor.py:12-27`); without pywin32 it opens and refuses each client (H3). And since ba2a753 it depends on the main app's `utils` package (`power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:39`), found only because `launch_extractor.py:10` APPENDS the program folder to the search path (Python also puts the script's folder first when run normally); under a portable Python that does not add the script folder, a different `utils` earlier on the path would win (LOW; EXT 5.1).
7. **Console handling:** `main.py:17` assumes a console; B guards the same line (`main.py:12-13` in project B, HS O10) — for the later comparison.

### 9.6 File-system assumptions

**Folder layout read and written (READ; EXT 2-3; details in Sections 3-4).**
- **Input:** ONE flat source folder holding every client's files together; sub-folders are ignored silently (`utils/helpers.py:328`; A-R8). Names must follow the six patterns [GST RULE] ⚠ (A-R1 to A-R6).
- **Output tree** under the chosen target folder: `Annual Statement-<DDMMYY HHMM>` / `<client>-<STATE CODE>` / `Version-<DDMMYY HHMM>` / `GSTR3B`, `ITC`, `Sales` (+ " (<client>)" when chosen), with the reports, the Annual Report and the text report in the Version folder, and the summary and consolidated workbooks in the run folder (`utils/constants.py:81-96`; `core/file_organizer.py:71-148`; A-R32 to A-R42). The target is created if missing (`core/file_organizer.py:65-69`).
- **Step 4 expects** the parent of the `Annual Statement-*` folders, takes the newest by date modified, and inside each client folder the newest `Version-*` by date modified (`power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:611-668`; A-R42, A-G45).

**Network drives (READ).** The program is designed for source and target folders on an office SMB share reached over a VPN (4f84ba9 "11 min -> 41s on the real share" ⚠; `utils/helpers.py:267-270`; `gui/tabs/setup_tab.py:135`). Assumptions: every PC that later refreshes a report must reach the share by the SAME path that was written into the report's `Links` sheet, because folder values are absolute — drive letter or UNC exactly as picked (`utils/helpers.py:418-422`; `core/excel_handler.py:143-146`; A-R56, A-G46); "newest" folders are decided by the server's date-modified values (A-R42); a dropped connection mid-copy leaves partial files (A-G11, A-G12). OneDrive is named in a603c02's message as one of the places the source folder may live (H1; MEDIUM that it is used).

**Path lengths ⚠ (READ).** The code treats ~218 characters as Excel/Power Query's practical limit (`utils/constants.py:85-90`; `core/excel_handler.py:356`; `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:720, 795`; help `gui/tabs/setup_tab.py:116, 122`); Windows' classic 260-character limit (`README.md:317`) applies to Python's own copies unless long paths are enabled in Windows (MEDIUM, general knowledge). Nothing measures a path before folders and files are created (A-G41). Worst case with defaults (EXT 3.7): `len(target) + 90 + len(file name)` for a copied ITC file; the refreshed copy adds about 22 more characters (EXT 3.6).

**Local folders that must be writable (READ; RAN where marked).**

| Folder | Why | If not writable | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|

**Other file-system assumptions:** the template files are readable and not locked; a read-only template makes read-only copies (`shutil.copy2`), so Excel's `Save` fails (A-G43, MEDIUM); files of at least 1,024 bytes with a real Excel signature (A-R9, A-R10); Excel's `~$` lock files ignored by the size check; no other program writes into the run folders between Step 3 and Step 4 (dates decide "newest").

### 9.8 Setting the program up on a fresh machine (as the code needs it today)

**What the code actually needs, in order (READ; Windows):**

1. **A full python.org Python with tkinter** — the version is not pinned anywhere; 3.14 is what these runs used and (MEDIUM, 9.4) what the author used ⚠, and 3.8 or newer is needed for today's openpyxl (9.4). One interpreter only: the author's PC had `py` and `python` pointing at different Pythons (c463256), and the start-up check tests only the one that runs the program (`utils/requirements_check.py:87-90` prints which).
2. **Copy the WHOLE program folder.** README's folder tree (`README.md:68-95`) names the files of `utils/` one by one (`__init__.py`, `constants.py`, `helpers.py`) and so omits `utils/excel_com.py`, `utils/requirements_check.py` and `utils/dependency_installer.py`; without them the program stops with "❌ Could not start" (`main.py:68, 82, 114-127`; `core/excel_handler.py:41`). (`utils/dependency_installer.py` is imported only when a package is missing, `main.py:78-82`: on a Windows PC with everything installed its absence goes unnoticed; off Windows pywin32 always counts as missing, so it is always needed there — READ.) The tree also shows no file directly inside `gui/` (`gui/__init__.py`, `gui/main_window.py`) or `power_query_extractor/` (`__init__.py`, `extractor_main.py`), only their sub-folders — harmless when the folders are copied whole, but a reader checking the tree item by item would not see that they are needed (`main.py:39-43` recreates a missing `gui/__init__.py` as a placeholder, but not `gui/main_window.py`) (READ `README.md:82-94`). The `gui/` sub-folders are listed only as folders, so copying them whole also brings `gui/tabs/extract_tab.py` (READ `README.md:83-87`; the older-documents notes also counted `extract_tab.py` as omitted, but the tree lists the whole `tabs/` folder).
3. **Install the packages:** `python -m pip install -r requirements.txt` from the program folder — this installs openpyxl, pywin32 (Windows only), lxml AND pytest: any that is missing at the newest version pip finds for that Python; one already installed at or above the minimum is kept as it is (`requirements.txt:5-15`; pip's normal behaviour, general knowledge). Or start the program and accept the offer, which runs the same command with the running Python (`main.py:78-95`). README and the March 2026 audit also say to run `python Scripts/pywin32_postinstall.py -install` as administrator (`README.md:275`; `PROJECT_AUDIT_ANNUALSTATEMENT.md:760`); the code assumes a restart is enough ("pywin32 only becomes importable in a freshly started interpreter", `main.py:79-81`) — whether the post-install step is still needed is NOT SURE (how to check: on a clean Windows PC, `pip install pywin32`, restart, and run Step 3 for one client).
4. **Microsoft Excel** installed and activated on every PC that runs Step 3 or Step 4, with the user logged in; for Step 4 an unlocked desktop that nobody uses during the refresh, and (by the key tips) an English Excel ⚠.
5. **The two templates** (ITC and Sales) with a `Links` sheet and the Power Query queries, and an `Info` sheet whose `BB2` the queries fill (A-R54, A-R55, A-R73) [GST RULE] ⚠ — not in the repository; they must come from the author.
6. **Access to the share** by the same drive letter or UNC path on every PC that will refresh reports (9.6).
7. **Start it from a console in the program folder:** `python main.py` (the log then lands in the program folder; started from elsewhere it lands there instead). The extractor alone: `python launch_extractor.py`. A double-click on `main.py` uses the console Python on Windows (START) — fine; a shortcut to `pythonw.exe` is not (9.5.1).
8. **Tests (developers only):** `python -m pytest` from the program folder (`pytest.ini:1-6`; `tests/conftest.py:9` adds the folder to the search path). Results (TEST): on Linux with a virtual display 287 of 288 pass (the one failure needs Windows path splitting); without any display 14 fail and 33 are skipped; on the author's Windows PC all 288 are expected to pass with the interpreter that has pywin32 (MEDIUM-HIGH, cannot run here). One test builds the real main window and so reads, and can rewrite, the developer's real settings file (A-G60). (Added during self-review, from Appendix X3.6:) three tests start a second Python without `-B`, so a test run writes compiled files into the program folder even when pytest itself was started with `-B`; setting `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1` prevents it (RAN, Appendix X3).

### 9.9 How the app is started, compared with the author's Standard 13

Standard 13 (`rebuild_pipeline_FINAL.md:900-1061`): users double-click a desktop shortcut to `Run [App Name].bat`, which starts the shared portable `_runtime\python\pythonw.exe -B -s main.py` with no console; `main.py` first installs error hooks that write a log under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\[App Name]\` and show a message box; nothing is installed on users' PCs. Facts only — every difference below is a decision for the author.

Started with `python main.py` / `py main.py` in a console, or by double-clicking `main.py` (console Python). A second entry point `launch_extractor.py` | `main.py:136-137`; `launch_extractor.py:29-30`; START |

| One shared portable Python (910-916, 924) | `_runtime\python` (embeddable package + packages); "Nothing is installed on users' PCs" | Uses whatever Python runs it; offers to `pip install -r requirements.txt` into that Python and restart | `main.py:78-95`; `utils/dependency_installer.py:26-74, 88-158`; A-G59 |

**Summary (facts).** A is built to be started by someone who has a console and their own Python with pip, on a PC where the program folder and the current folder are writable — a developer-style installation. It matches Standard 13 only in finding its own program files from the script's folder and in keeping settings per user.

### 9.10 Open questions for the author (Sections 8 and 9)

1. **Refresh method (D4).** Was Excel's own `RefreshAll` through COM ever tried before the Alt+A, R, A key presses, and what went wrong? Is the key-press method still wanted in the merged app? (8.4.1)
2. **Attaching to your open Excel (D5).** Should the program ever use an Excel you already have open? Today Step 3 attaches to it, hides it and closes it. (8.4.2; A-G54)
3. **Python version.** Which Python will every PC run: the normal build (`python.exe` — which version is it on your PC?) or the free-threaded `python3.14t`? Should `requirements.txt` say 3.14 instead of "3.7 or higher"? (9.4)
4. **Exact versions.** Should the package versions be pinned exactly (Standard 13) and pytest left out of the users' list? (9.1, 9.9)
5. **Install offer.** Should the program keep offering to `pip install` on a user's PC, or should packages only ever be added to a shared runtime by you? (8.4.11, 9.9)
6. **How users start it.** Will users get a no-console launcher (Standard 13)? If so, the start-up code must change: today it dies silently without a console. (9.5.1, 9.9)
7. **Where logs and settings go.** `%LOCALAPPDATA%\[App Name]\` (Standard 13), the home folder (today), or the current folder (today's logs)? Are the unused `logs/` and `temp/` program-folder folders wanted? (8.6, 9.6)
8. **Excel language and version.** Do all PCs run English Excel (key tips, dialog words)? Which Excel version is the minimum? (9.5.3, 9.7)
9. **Drive letters.** Do all PCs reach the share by the same drive letter or by UNC? Reports carry absolute paths. (9.6)
10. **pywin32 post-install step.** Is `pywin32_postinstall.py -install` still part of your set-up on a new PC? (9.8)
11. **Re-export lists.** Keep the package `__init__.py` re-export lists (four are out of date and nobody uses them) or drop them in the merged app? (8.8)
12. **Unfinished features.** Are the never-wired items (`EXCEL_SAFETY`, calculated columns, "critical files" check, clean-up after a failed client, the extra extraction options) planned work to keep, or safe to drop? [GST RULE] for the calculated columns and the critical-file list. (8.6)
13. **Window toolkit.** Tkinter (A) or Standard 12's PySide6 for the merged app? (8.2.1, 8.2.8)

## SECTION 10: UI/INTERFACE DOCUMENTATION

Project A = `goyal-sidhant/AnnualStatement_oldv1`, branch `main`, snapshot `bf2f1dd` (27-07-2026). This section describes every window, tab, dialog and message box the user can meet, every control on them, how they look, what turns them on and off, and the order in which a user normally clicks through them. Feature and rule IDs are those of the registry (`/root/merge-scratch/audit/A_registry.md`), for example "A-F4" (feature 4) and "A-R133" (rule 133).

### 10.0 How to read this section

**Evidence marks.**

- **READ** = established by reading the code at `bf2f1dd` (file:line given, repository-relative).
- **RAN** = I opened the real window off-screen and looked at it. Positions, sizes, colours, which widgets exist and which are visible are reliable (RAN); exact font look and emoji are not. Whether Tk on the author's Windows PC draws the emoji in tab titles and buttons is **not sure - here is how to check**: start the app on that PC and look at the tab titles ("📁 Step 1: Setup") and the "🌙 Dark Mode" tick; Tk 8.6 has had trouble with characters outside the basic character range on some systems (LOW).

**Plain-English terms used in this section** (first use explained here once):

- **window / dialog / message box** - a window is a framed area on screen; a dialog is a small window that asks something; a message box is a standard small dialog with an icon, a text and buttons such as OK or Yes/No. **Modal** = it blocks the rest of the program until answered.
- **Tk / Tkinter** (Python's built-in window toolkit) and **ttk** (Tk's "themed" widgets, whose colours come from a shared style table rather than from each widget). **widget** = any single on-screen element (button, label, text box, table). **theme 'clam'** = one of Tk's built-in looks (flat grey-beige).
- **tab / notebook** - a notebook is the container with clickable tab titles ("Step 1" … "Step 4"); a **sub-tab** is a tab inside a tab.
- **Treeview** - Tk's table widget (the Step 2 client table).
- **Entry** (one-line text box), **Spinbox** (number box with small up/down arrows), **Checkbutton** (tick box), **Radiobutton** (round option button, one of a group), **Text / ScrolledText** (multi-line text box, with a scroll bar), **Label** (fixed text), **LabelFrame** (a box with a title written into its border), **Canvas** (a drawing area, used here to make a page scroll), **progress bar**.
- **pack / grid / place** - three Tk ways to position widgets: *pack* stacks them top-to-bottom or side-by-side, *grid* puts them in rows and columns, *place* puts them at fixed pixel coordinates.
- **`command=` vs `.bind('<Button-1>')`** - two ways to connect a button to a function. `command=` runs on a normal click (press and release), is ignored when the button is disabled (greyed out), and can be triggered from the keyboard. `.bind('<Button-1>')` reacts to the raw left-mouse press: it still fires on a greyed-out button and cannot be reached from the keyboard.
- **tooltip** - a small yellow pop-up text that appears when the mouse rests on something.
- **status bar** - the strip at the bottom of a window that shows a one-line message.
- **worker thread** - a second line of work running beside the window so the window stays usable; **UI thread / main thread** - the one that draws the window.
- **debounce** - wait until typing pauses before re-checking.
- **hex colour** - a colour written as `#RRGGBB`, e.g. `#0078D4` (blue).
- **COM / pywin32** - Windows' way for Python to drive Microsoft Excel, and the Python package that provides it.
- **settings file** - `~/.gst_organizer_cache.json` in the user's home folder, where the program remembers paths and choices (A-F27). `~` means the user's home folder (on Windows `C:\Users\<user>`).
- **pip** - Python's own tool that downloads and installs extra packages; **openpyxl** - the Python package that reads and writes Excel files without Excel; **pywin32** - see COM above.
- **UTF-8** - a way of storing text that can hold every character, including emoji; **exit code** - the number a program hands back to Windows when it stops (0 = fine, 1 = failed).
- **ImportError / AttributeError / traceback** - Python's names for "a module could not be loaded" and "a thing has no such part"; a traceback is Python's technical listing of where an error happened.
- **late binding (closure) mistake** - a programming slip where a function written inside a loop uses the loop's LAST value instead of the value at the time it was written; the "default-argument form" `lambda e, cmd=command: cmd()` avoids it.
- **tag (of a table row)** - a named style a Treeview row carries ("complete" / "incomplete"); changing the tag's colours recolours every row that carries it. **style map** - ttk's per-state colour list (e.g. "when selected, use this colour").
- **dictionary order** - Python remembers the order in which items were first added to a collection; the client list follows that order. **NTFS** - Windows' usual disk format. **regex (regular expression)** - a text pattern the program matches file names against.

**GST rules on screen.** Several things the screens show are decided by GST rules (which return files are expected, how file names identify the return and period, the state code in a client key, which report each client gets). They are tagged **[GST RULE]**, described only, never judged; values that can change over time carry ⚠.

### 10.3 Start-up: the console window and the install offer (A-F1)

The user starts the program with `python main.py` (or `py main.py`, or by double-clicking `main.py`, which Windows opens with the console Python). There is no `.bat` launcher, no shortcut and no `pythonw.exe` use in A (READ; START notes). The program **needs** a console: its first line re-wraps the console output as UTF-8 (`main.py:17`), which fails when there is no console (RAN START: with `sys.stdout = None`, as `pythonw.exe` gives, the program dies with `AttributeError` before any window or log exists). (A-R127.)

#### 10.3.1 What the console shows (W1)

Printed by `main.py:62-73` and `utils/requirements_check.py:93-133` (READ; RAN on this machine for the report part, python path replaced):

```text
============================================================
🚀 GST File Organizer v3.0 - Production Ready
============================================================
Checking requirements...
   [OK     ] openpyxl   - Reading and writing Excel files
   [not found] pywin32    - Excel automation: preserves Power Query when creating reports, and powers the refresh in Step 4

⚠️  pywin32 is not installed for this Python.
   Without it: Excel automation: preserves Power Query when creating reports, and powers the refresh in Step 4.
   Reports would be created WITHOUT their Power Query connections, and Step 4 could not refresh them.
   Install with:  pip install pywin32

   Running: Python 3.14.6 at <python.exe path>
   Note 'py' and 'python' can be different interpreters - install
   for the one you start the app with.
============================================================
```

- `[OK     ]` / `[MISSING]` / `[not found]`: "MISSING" is used for an essential package, "not found" for an optional one; "not found" is 9 characters while "OK     " and "MISSING" are 7 (`utils/requirements_check.py:97-98`), so its line is two columns wider than the others (RAN START; re-RAN VERIFY-A-S10 `v_pure.py`: the " - " separator sits at column 25 on the "not found" line and at column 23 on the "OK" line). [Corrected during verification - originally stated "one column wider".] On Windows pywin32 is essential, so the second block reads "❌ pywin32 is REQUIRED and is not installed.", "   Needed for: …", the consequence line, "   The app stops here rather than produce damaged output." and "   Install with:  pip install pywin32" (`utils/requirements_check.py:114-123`, READ). (A-R124.)
- After this, the console stays open behind the main window and receives every log line at INFO level (`main.py:20-27`, A-R120), so it fills with technical messages while the user works (READ).
- The text printed before the install offer may not appear in the console until later, because the UTF-8 wrapper buffers output (RAN START on Linux; HIGH that Windows behaves the same).

#### 10.3.2 The install offer (W2, W3, W4)

Shown only when openpyxl or pywin32 is missing (`main.py:78-95`; A-R125). READ; RAN START (dialogs replaced by recorders):

- **W2 - message box "Install missing packages?" (Yes / No)**, text (exact, `utils/dependency_installer.py:110-115`):

  ```text
  The app needs these packages:

  • pywin32 - Excel automation: preserves Power Query when creating reports, and powers the refresh in Step 4
      Reports would be created WITHOUT their Power Query connections, and Step 4 could not refresh them.

  Install them now for:
  <full path of the running python.exe>

  The app will restart afterwards.
  ```

  It is shown over a hidden, empty Tk window (`:106-108`), so on Windows the box appears on its own without a parent window (READ).
- **"No"** → the program continues to the main window if only optional packages are missing; if an essential one is missing it logs "Required package missing: …", prints "Press Enter to exit..." and stops with exit code 1 (`main.py:97-102`, `:45-54`).
- **"Yes"** → pip is asked to install everything listed in `requirements.txt` (openpyxl, pywin32 on Windows, lxml and pytest), not only the missing package, whenever that file exists (`utils/dependency_installer.py:133-134`; `requirements.txt:5, 9, 12, 15`; A-R125) (READ) - and **W3, window "Installing…"**, 760×380, a scrolling text box in Consolas 9 that shows "Installing into: <python.exe>" then "Running: <pip command>" and, only after pip has finished, pip's whole output (`utils/dependency_installer.py:121-134`, `:41-60`). pip runs on the window's own thread, so the window cannot repaint or respond during the install (up to 600 seconds); on Windows it will probably show "Not Responding" (READ HIGH for the blocking, MEDIUM for how Windows shows it; START). The commit message of a5ad487 (A only (after the split)) says the window "streams pip's output" - it does not; output arrives at the end (READ). RAN (tour 5, shot 37; pip replaced by a stand-in that only writes one line and fails, so nothing was installed): the window is titled "Installing…", 760×380, a plain white text area with a scroll bar filling the window with a 10-pixel grey margin, showing "Installing into: <python path>", an empty line and "Running: <python path> -m pip install -r <app folder>/requirements.txt"; there is no button, no progress bar and no "please wait" text. The window is a child of the hidden window of W2, not of the main window (which does not exist yet).
  - Success → "✅ Installed successfully. Restarting the app…" is added, the window closes almost at once, the console prints "✅ Packages installed - restarting…", a new copy of the program starts and this one exits (`utils/dependency_installer.py:136-139`; `main.py:89-95`). If the restart fails: "Could not restart automatically. Please start the app again." and "Press Enter to exit...".
  - Failure → "❌ Installation failed." is added and **W4, error box "Installation failed"**: "The packages could not be installed automatically.\n\nPlease run this yourself:\n\n<command>\n\n" plus "The app cannot start without them." when an essential package is missing (`:141-148`). RAN (tour 5, optional pywin32 on Linux): the box read "…Please run this yourself:\n\n<python path> -m pip install -r <app folder>/requirements.txt pywin32\n\n" with nothing after it (the "cannot start" sentence appears only when the missing package is essential, i.e. pywin32 on Windows). The suggested command contains both `-r <requirements.txt>` and the package names and does not quote paths with spaces (READ; START).
- Off Windows pip skips pywin32 (its requirement line is Windows-only), reports success and restarts; pywin32 is still missing, so the offer returns at every start (RAN START). On the author's Windows PCs this loop does not happen (READ).

#### 10.3.3 Other console messages

| When | Text (exact) | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| An `ImportError` while starting | "❌ Could not start: <error>", "This usually means a required package is missing for THIS Python,", "or a source file has been moved.", "   Running: Python X.Y.Z at <exe>", "   Try:  pip install -r requirements.txt", "   Note 'py' and 'python' can be different interpreters.", then "Press Enter to exit..." | `main.py:114-127` |
| Any other error while starting | "💥 Critical error: <error>", then "Press Enter to exit..." | `main.py:130-134` |
| Errors after the window is open (in a button's code or in a worker thread) | Not caught by the program; Tk prints a traceback (the technical error listing) to the console only | READ: no `sys.excepthook` / `threading.excepthook` anywhere; RAN GUI exp2/exp4 |

> **Standard 13 comparison (facts only).** Standard 13 says users start apps with a `.bat` launcher using `pythonw.exe` and see no console window, that `print()` shows nothing, that problems are reported in the window and logged to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\[App Name]\`, and that nothing is installed on users' PCs (`rebuild_pipeline_FINAL.md:900-1061`, especially `:1035-1040`). Project A needs a console, reports start-up problems only as console text, sends errors that happen after start-up to the console only, and offers to pip-install packages into the user's Python. Which behaviour the merged program should have is the author's decision.

The Fresh / Re-Run / Resume decision and the folder-name rules are not GST rules (they decide folder names, not where a figure goes). The client key "<client>-<STATE CODE>" used behind the Step 2 table is a **[GST RULE]** (state-code logic, A-R21 ⚠, A-R23).

#### 10.5.8 What the user sees during and after a scan

- **During:** nothing moves. The scan runs inside the button's click, on the window's own thread, and nothing asks the window to repaint (`gui/handlers/file_handler.py:62-72`), so the window does not respond until the scan ends; on a slow network share Windows may mark it "Not Responding" (READ HIGH; the message of commit 4f84ba9 (A only (after the split)) reports a scan of 2,508 files on the real share taking about 41 seconds after a speed-up, down from a projected 11 minutes). The status texts set during the scan are never painted (10.4.2).
- **After, ≥ 1 client found:** Step 2 opens with the summary and the table filled (RAN shot 06).
- **After, no client found:** the user stays on Step 1; only the status bar says "No valid GST files found"; the warning line "⚠️ No valid GST files found" goes to the Step 3 log, which is not on screen (`gui/handlers/file_handler.py:89-91`). A folder that exists but cannot be listed (for example a share that drops between the existence check and the listing, or a folder the user may not list) also ends here, because a listing error is turned into an empty list (`utils/helpers.py:321-365`) (READ HIGH). A folder that does not exist at all is stopped earlier by the box "Source folder does not exist" (`gui/handlers/file_handler.py:126-128`). [Corrected during verification - originally "an unreachable folder", which for a path that no longer exists gives the box instead.]
- **Error boxes:** "Error" / "Please select a source folder containing GST files" (source empty) and "Error" / "Source folder does not exist" (`gui/handlers/file_handler.py:120-130`) - Scan and Re-scan are greyed under the same condition (`gui/tabs/setup_tab.py:585-591`), so these two boxes are reachable only when the checklist is behind the box: during the 350 ms before it re-checks a just-changed path, or when its remembered "exists" answer is out of date (READ HIGH; the tour called the scan function directly to see the wording) [Corrected during verification - originally said "or via Re-scan", but Re-scan is greyed exactly like Scan]; any other failure → "❌ Scan error: <error>" in the Step 3 log and box "Scan Error" with the error text (`:93-95`). A file path in the source box passes the checklist and fails here with "Not a directory: <path>" (`core/file_parser.py:154-155`).
- Files that are not recognised are only COUNTED on Step 2 (A-F9); there is no on-screen list of them (A-F9; DOCS RM20).

#### 10.5.9 Scrolling the Setup page (A-F31, A-R146)

- Scroll bar on the right of the page; mouse wheel scrolls 3 units of 22 pixels per wheel notch, collecting small touch-pad movements until they add up to a whole unit (`gui/tabs/setup_tab.py:137-138, 191, 220-248`).
- The wheel works only while the pointer is over this page and only when the page is taller than the window; elsewhere the wheel event is left for other widgets (`:230-238`). One application-wide binding added with `add='+'` so other wheel handlers survive (`:193-201`) - the result of two fixes, d64d3a9 and bf2f1dd (A only (after the split)); `tests/test_scroll_bindings.py` guards the pattern.
- Only the Windows/macOS wheel event (`<MouseWheel>`) is handled; with Tk 8.6 on Linux the wheel sends a different event (Button-4/5) that nothing handles (LOW; the app targets Windows).
- RAN: at 1200×800 the page is 1,521 px tall in a 640-px view, so roughly the top 40% is visible at first (checklist and workflow card fully, the top of "📂 FOLDERS & TEMPLATES"); the Scan button is only reachable by scrolling down (shots 01, 03, 04). Font sizes on Windows differ, so the exact heights may differ (MEDIUM).

#### 10.5.10 "📝  EXPECTED FILE NAMES" card (A-F31) [GST RULE] ⚠

Purple card (`#7B1FA2` stripe and title) with "Files in the source folder must follow these patterns to be recognised." and one row per pattern, alternate rows tinted `#FAF5FC`; type in purple Segoe UI 8 bold, pattern in Consolas 8 (`gui/tabs/setup_tab.py:477-503`). The rows come from the `description` fields of `FILE_PATTERNS` (`utils/constants.py:13-62`), RAN (shot 04):

| Type shown | Pattern shown (exact) | Registry rule |
|---|---|---|
| GSTR-2B Reco | `GSTR-2B-Reco-ClientName-State-Period.xlsx` | A-R1 ⚠ |
| IMS Reco | `ImsReco-ClientName-State-DDMMYYYY.xlsx` | A-R2 ⚠ |
| GSTR-3B Export | `GSTR3B-ClientName-State-Month.xlsx` | A-R3 ⚠ |
| Sales | `Sales-ClientName-State-StartMonth-EndMonth.xlsx` | A-R4 ⚠ |
| Sales Reco | `SalesReco-ClientName-State-Period.xlsx` | A-R5 ⚠ |
| Annual Report | `AnnualReport-ClientName-State-Year.xlsx` | A-R6 ⚠ |

These are the return files the program expects and how the period is written in each name - a **[GST RULE]**, and time-varying ⚠ (the list of returns and naming conventions can change). Described only. Technical note: the docstring says this card "can never drift from the regexes the parser actually uses" (`:478-479`), but the shown texts are separate description strings, not generated from the patterns; they leave out that `.xls` and any letter case are accepted, that a "(N) " prefix (GSTR3B) and a " (N)" suffix (IMS) are accepted, and that the IMS date must be exactly 8 digits (`utils/constants.py:15, 23, 31, 39, 47, 55`) (READ; A-F31).

#### 10.5.11 Tooltip texts on Step 1 (exact) (A-R147)

Tooltips appear 450 ms after the pointer rests, wrap at 520 px, pale yellow `#FFFFE0` with dark text `#333333`, Segoe UI 9, 12 px right of and 6 px below the widget; they disappear when the pointer leaves or on a click; they are not kept inside the screen edge (`gui/widgets/tooltip.py:12-69`). RAN (shot 05: the Scan tooltip). Only Step 1 has tooltips.

| Attached to | Text (exact; "\n" = new line) | Agrees with the code? |
|---|---|---|
| Source row (all 4 widgets of the checklist row) | "The folder holding the GST files you received.\nThey are read from here and copied into the target folder - nothing here is moved, renamed or deleted." | Yes (copies are made; the COPIES get cleaned names) - READ `utils/helpers.py:199` |
| ITC row | "Your ITC report template (.xlsx / .xltx).\nA copy is made per client and its Links sheet is filled in, so the template itself is never modified." | Yes on the template; the checklist also accepts .xltm/.xlsm |
| Sales row | "Your Sales report template (.xlsx / .xltx).\nUsed the same way as the ITC template - copied per client, never modified." | Yes (same note) |
| Target row | "Where the organised folders and generated reports are created.\nEach run adds a new timestamped folder, so previous runs are left untouched." | **No** for Re-Run / Resume (they write into the newest existing run folder) and for two Fresh runs in the same minute (RAN GUI exp7) |
| Workflow 'organize' | "Sort the files into folders and build the ITC/Sales reports, then stop.\nFast - no Excel automation involved." | **No** on Windows with pywin32 (reports are built through Excel) |
| Workflow 'full' | "Everything above, and then open each report in Excel to refresh its Power Query and pull the figures out.\nMuch slower - Excel is driven for a while per report." | **No** - the refresh is not started automatically (10.5.4) |
| Fresh | "Create a brand new timestamped folder for this run.\nUse this normally - previous runs are left alone." | Yes, except two runs in the same minute share one folder (A-R33/A-F13) |
| Re-Run | "Add a new version inside the most recent run's folder instead of starting a new one.\nUse when redoing work for the same batch." | Yes ("most recent" = newest date modified) |
| Resume | "Continue a run that was interrupted, skipping files that are already in place." | **No** (RAN GUI exp7) |
| Include-name tick | "Adds the client's name to the folders inside each version folder, e.g.\n'ITC (<generic example name> Pvt Ltd)' instead of just 'ITC'.\n\nLeave off if paths are getting long - Excel stops opening files beyond about 218 characters." (the code uses a three-letter placeholder company name, `gui/tabs/setup_tab.py:114`; the example is written with spaces, while real folder names use underscores, e.g. "ITC (GenericLongClientNamePlaceholder_Pvt_Ltd)", RAN GUI exp7) | Yes about which folders; example spelling differs |
| Length spinbox | "Longest client name allowed in a folder name before it is shortened.\n\nLower values keep paths shorter, which matters on a network share: Excel cannot open files whose full path exceeds roughly 218 characters." | **No** (only the Level-2 folder is shortened; the limit includes "-<STATE>") |
| Scan / Re-scan | quoted in 10.5.7 | Yes ("Results appear on Step 2" only if a client was found) |
| Browse buttons | quoted in 10.5.5 | Yes |
| Path boxes | the full path currently in the box | Yes |

The "218 characters" figure is a technical threshold of Excel paths used by the code (A-R104), not a GST rule.

### 10.6 Step 2 - Validation tab (A-F8, A-F9 count, A-F10 per-client, A-F11, A-F12, Start of A-F13)

Unchanged since the first commit edac6a3 (shared - before the split on 30-10-2025) (READ: `git log` of `gui/tabs/validation_tab.py` lists only edac6a3); the behaviour behind it changed in 1c48722 (shared) and 33d0baf (A only (after the split)) in `gui/handlers/client_handler.py`.

#### 10.6.1 Layout

Background `#F8F9FA`, 20 px margins. Left column fixed 450 px wide: instructions box, scan summary, action card. Right column fills the rest: client selection (`gui/tabs/validation_tab.py:18-42`). RAN (shots 06, 31).

#### 10.6.2 Left column

**Collapsible instructions box** (`gui/tabs/validation_tab.py:44-66`; widget `gui/widgets/collapsible_frame.py:7-41`):

- Outer box pale orange `#FFF3E0` with a 2-px solid border. Its title row - a small flat button "▼" (expanded) / "▶" (collapsed) and the bold title "📋 VALIDATION INSTRUCTIONS" (Arial 11 bold) - keeps the default system grey, because the colour passed in only colours the outer frame (READ; RAN shot 06: grey title strip on an orange box).
- Content (Arial 10, dark orange `#E65100`), exact:
  - "• Review the scan summary below"
  - "• Check client list - ✅ = complete, ⚠️ = missing files"
  - "• Select clients using click or keyboard (↑↓ + SPACE)"
  - "• Try 'Dry Run' to preview without processing"
  - "• Click 'Start Processing' when ready"
- Clicking ▼ hides the content and shows ▶; clicking ▶ shows it again (RAN shot 08; RAN START). The state is not remembered.
- Text vs program: the button on this tab is labelled "🚀 START", not "Start Processing"; "⚠️" also marks clients that only have duplicates; the per-client "📁 Name" column is not mentioned anywhere on screen (READ).

**"📊 SCAN SUMMARY"** - blue 40-px header band, then a read-only text box 200 px high (Consolas 9, background `#f8f9fa`, word wrap, own scroll bar) (`gui/tabs/validation_tab.py:68-92`). Filled after every scan by `gui/main_window.py:294-328` (A-R31), emptied by Re-scan (`gui/handlers/file_handler.py:108-111`). Template (exact; RAN with invented data):

```text
📊 SCAN RESULTS SUMMARY:
════════════════════════════════════════════
📁 FILES ANALYSIS:
   Total Excel Files Found: 18
   ✅ Successfully Parsed: 17
   ❌ Unparsed/Variations: 1
   📊 Parsing Success Rate: 94.4%

👥 CLIENTS ANALYSIS:
   Total Clients Identified: 3
   ✅ Clients with All Files: 1
   ⚠️ Clients with Missing Files: 2
   📈 Completeness Rate: 33.3%

📋 FILE TYPE DISTRIBUTION:
   • Annual Report: 2 files
   • GSTR-2B Reco: 3 files
   • GSTR-3B Export: 4 files
   • IMS Reco: 2 files
   • Sales: 4 files
   • Sales Reco: 2 files

🔍 FILE VARIATIONS: 1 files

💾 TOTAL DATA SIZE: 88.9 KB
```

- "🔍 FILE VARIATIONS" appears only when at least one file name was not recognised; the names themselves are never shown on screen (A-F9). "Clients with Missing Files" also counts a client that has every file but a duplicate (in the run above "ClientC" had all six types plus two GSTR-2B Reco files and was counted there) (RAN; A-R31).
- Only the first 13 lines fit in the 200-px box; the rest needs scrolling (RAN shot 06).

**Action card** (`gui/tabs/validation_tab.py:94-142`): the heading "🎯 READY TO PROCESS?" (Arial 14 bold, green) and three flat coloured buttons with white Arial 10 bold text and a hand cursor:

| Button (exact) | Colour | What it does | Enabled? | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| "🧪 DRY RUN" | orange `#FF8C00` | Checks that both templates are set and exist and a target is set (A-R51, A-R134 - although a dry run uses none of them), then that at least one client is ticked; switches to Step 3 and writes the preview (10.6.5) into the Step 3 log. Touches no file | Never disabled; reacts on mouse press; can run during a real run (no "running" check) | `gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:38-67` |
| "📋 EXPORT LIST" | teal `#0099BC` | Saves the ticked clients to a text file (10.6.6) | Never disabled | `gui/handlers/client_handler.py:225-257` |
| "🚀 START" | green `#107C10` | Same as "🚀 START PROCESSING" on Step 3 (10.7.3) | Never disabled; a second press during a run is ignored by a check in the code (`gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:75-76`) | `gui/tabs/validation_tab.py:142` |

#### 10.6.3 Right column: client selection

- Green 40-px header "👥 CLIENT SELECTION".
- Hint box (Arial 9, blue text on pale blue `#E3F2FD`, thin border): "⌨️ Use ↑↓ arrows + SPACE to select, or click with mouse".

Wired with `.bind('<Button-1>', lambda e, cmd=command: cmd())` - the default-argument form, so each button calls its own function (no late-binding mistake) (`gui/tabs/validation_tab.py:174-190`).
- The client table (Treeview, 20 rows high, both scroll bars) (`:192-247`):

| Column heading (exact) | Width (px) | Content of each row | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|

| "🏢 Client Name" | 250 | client name as read from the file names | `:37` |
| "🌏 State" | 100 | state as written in the file names (e.g. "Delhi"), not the code | `:38`; A-R23 |
| "📊 Status" | 150 | "✅ Complete", "⚠️ Missing <N> files" or "⚠️ Has duplicates" **[GST RULE]** (which returns a complete client must have, A-R26 ⚠, A-R27 ⚠, A-R29) | `:39`; `core/file_parser.py:277-286` |
| "📁 Files" | 60 | number of recognised files of the client | `:40` |
| "❌ Missing" | 180 | missing file types joined by ", " (sorted), or "None" **[GST RULE]** ⚠ | `:31, 41` |
| "➕ Extra" | 80 | number of file TYPES that appear more than once (GSTR-3B Export never counts), "0" if none - not the number of extra files **[GST RULE]** ⚠ (which return may have several files, A-R27) | `:32, 42`; `core/file_parser.py:262-271`; A-R27 |

The highlighted row is drawn with the theme's selection colour (slate blue `#4a6984` with white text at start; bright blue `#0078D4` with BLACK text after the first dark-mode round trip, RAN - see 10.10).
- Row order: the order in which the scan first met each client in a name-sorted list of files (`utils/helpers.py:361`; dictionary order) - not alphabetical by client. RAN: invented files gave the order ClientA, ClientC, ClientB, because "AnnualReport-ClientC-…" sorts before "GSTR3B-ClientB-…". **UNREGISTERED: client list order** (Step 2 rows here, Step 4 rows in 10.8.3; no registry rule states it - A-R60 only says the run follows "table order"). (Added during self-review:) this is the same unregistered decision that Section 5.18 describes as "5.18 U3 — UNREGISTERED: Order of clients in each step"; Section 11 lists the two together.
- After a scan: all rows unticked, every "📁 Name" cell "☐ No" (even when the global tick on Step 1 is on - the run will still add the names, RAN GUI exp1 "globalname"), first row highlighted and focused (`gui/handlers/client_handler.py:27, 43, 46-49, 61-65`).
- Column headings cannot be clicked to sort (no heading command, READ).

> **Finding (RAN, shots 06 and 25): the "📁 Name" column is off-screen at the default window size.** The columns add up to 970 px, but at 1200×800 the table shows only 597 px (397 px at 1000×700). The visible part ends inside "📁 Files"; "❌ Missing", "➕ Extra" and "📁 Name" are reached only with the horizontal scroll bar. Together with the instructions not mentioning the Name column, the per-client folder-name toggle (A-F10) is hard to discover. Technical observation; whether the column is wanted is the author's call.

#### 10.6.4 Mouse and keyboard on the table

| User action | Effect | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Click in the "✓" column of a row | Ticks / unticks that client; status bar "Selected <n> clients" | `gui/handlers/client_handler.py:67-75, 118-131` |
| Click in the "📁 Name" column (data column 7) | Flips that client's name flag. Turning ON: cell "☑ Yes"; if the client name is longer than **10** characters (fixed number, not the Step 1 setting): box "Long Client Name Warning" - "Client name '<name>' has <n> characters.\n\nThis will create long folder names. Continue?" (Yes/No); No reverts to "☐ No". Turning OFF: cell "☐ No"; if the Step 1 global tick is on, it is switched off with box "Global Setting Disabled" - "Global folder name setting has been turned off\nsince you unchecked an individual client." (not saved to the settings file). | `:76-79, 175-209`; RAN tour 2 (both boxes recorded, texts as quoted); A-R136, A-R137 |
| Click anywhere else on a row | Highlights it (Tk's normal behaviour) | READ |
| Space | Ticks / unticks the first highlighted row only | `:81-86` |
| ↑ / ↓ | Moves the highlight one row (replacing Tk's own handling); ↓ with nothing highlighted highlights the first row | `:88-116` |
| "☑️ Select All" | Ticks every row; status "Selected all <n> clients" | `:133-138` |
| "☐ Clear All" | Unticks every row; status "Cleared all selections" | `:140-145` |
| "✅ Complete Only" | REPLACES the ticks: ticks rows whose status contains "Complete", unticks all others; status "Selected <n> complete clients" | `:147-159` |

- Digit-only names: Tk hands back a cell that looks like a whole number as a number, so a client written "0042" becomes "42" when the program rebuilds the client key from the row, and a state written as digits crashes the rebuild; Dry Run, Start, Export and the Name toggle then fail or crash, with the error visible only in the console (RAN GUI exp2; A-F8).
- The table rows show the state NAME, and the program converts it back to the code to find the client - **[GST RULE]** state-code logic (A-R21 ⚠, A-R22, A-R23) (`gui/handlers/client_handler.py:168-170, 181, 218`).

#### 10.6.5 Dry Run preview text (A-F11, A-R139)

Written into the Step 3 log (each line prefixed "[HH:MM:SS] "), exact (RAN, shot 09; `gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:51-67`):

```text
🧪 ════════ DRY RUN PREVIEW ════════
🎯 Mode: fresh
👥 Selected: 3 clients

🏢 ClientA - Delhi
  📄 Would organize: AnnualReport-ClientA-Delhi-FY.xlsx
  … one line per file …
  📊 Would create: ITC Report
  💰 Would create: Sales Report
… one block per ticked client …

🧪 ════════ DRY RUN COMPLETE ════════
💡 No files were actually moved or created
```

- "Mode" shows the internal word (`fresh` / `rerun` / `resume`), not the on-screen radio label.
- Every client is shown with "Would create: ITC Report" and "Would create: Sales Report", whatever files it has - the program always attempts both reports for every client **[GST RULE]** (which report each client gets, A-R60).
- The preview shows no destination folders, no report names, no workflow and no folder-name effect (READ).

#### 10.6.6 Export list (A-F12, A-R142)

1. Nothing ticked → box "No Selection" / "Please select clients to export".
2. Save dialog: default ending ".txt", file types "Text files (*.txt)" and "All files (*.*)", suggested name `selected_clients_<YYYYmmdd_HHMMSS>.txt`, no starting folder (`gui/handlers/client_handler.py:233-237`).
3. File content (exact): "Selected Clients List", "Generated: <YYYY-mm-dd HH:MM:SS>", "Total: <n> clients", 50 "=" signs, an empty line, then one "<client> - <state name>" line per ticked client (`:241-249`).
4. Box "Export Complete" / "Exported <n> clients to:\n<file name only>"; then the file is opened with Windows' default program for `.txt` (`os.startfile`, `:251-255`).
5. Any error → box "Export Error" / "Failed to export: <error>". On Linux both "Export Complete" and then "Export Error" appear, because `os.startfile` exists only on Windows (RAN GUI exp8).

A message that starts with a line break (e.g. "\n🏢 Processing …") is shown as a time stamp alone on one line and the text, without time stamp, on the next line (RAN, shots 09 and 12).

#### 10.7.2 The log at start-up

Three lines are written when the window opens (`gui/main_window.py:394-396`; RAN shot 32):

```text
[hh:mm:ss] 🎉 Application started                                                   (blue)
[hh:mm:ss] 💡 Ready to organize your GST files!                                     (green)
[hh:mm:ss] ⚠️ IMPORTANT: Templates must have 'Links' sheet for reports to work!     (orange)
```

The Links-sheet warning is shown to everyone at every start; nothing checks a template's Links sheet before a run (A-R51).

#### 10.7.3 What happens when the user presses Start (Step 2 "🚀 START" or Step 3 "🚀 START PROCESSING")

In this order (`gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:69-134`; RAN tours 1 and 2):

1. If a run is already active: nothing (no message).
2. Template / target checks - boxes titled "Error": "Please select both ITC and Sales template files", "Please select a target folder for organized files", "ITC template file not found", "Sales template file not found" (`gui/handlers/file_handler.py:132-151`; A-R51).
3. Nothing ticked → box "Warning" / "Please select at least one client to process".
4. Only when Step 1's "Include client name in Level 4 folder names" is ticked: client names longer than the Step 1 maximum length (fallback 10 if that is 0 or unreadable) are listed (at most 5) in a Yes/No box "Warning" - exact (RAN tour 2, limit 20): "Long client names detected (exceeding 20 chars):\n\n• GenericLongClientNamePlaceholder (32 chars)\n\nIf you continue, these client names will be used in folder names.\n\nContinue anyway?" - No stops here (A-R136).
5. The app switches to Step 3, greys out START, enables STOP, writes "🚀 ════════ PROCESSING STARTED ════════" and starts the background worker (a daemon thread, killed without clean-up if the program exits).
6. Per ticked client, in table order: folders → copies → ITC report → Sales report → organisation text file, with the log lines of 10.7.4 and the progress texts of 10.7.1 (A-R60).
7. Summary workbook, completion lines, then the box **"Processing Complete"** - "Successfully processed <p>/<t> clients\n\nFiles organized in:\n<target folder>" (RAN; called from the worker thread, RAN thread name "Thread-1 (process_files_thread)"). The same wording appears after a Stop or when clients failed (RAN tour 2: "Successfully processed 1/3 clients" after Stop). It names the target folder, not the new `Annual Statement-…` folder.
8. After OK: the new `Annual Statement-…` folder is opened in Windows File Explorer (`os.startfile`) and "📂 Opened output folder" is logged (on Linux/macOS through `xdg-open` / `open`; the success line is logged even when that fails - RAN: "sh: 1: xdg-open: not found" yet "📂 Opened output folder" appeared).
9. Workflow 'organize': "ℹ️ Workflow is 'organise only'. Open Step 4 if you also want to refresh Power Query." Workflow 'full': "🔄 Full pipeline: moving to Step 4 to extract…", the app switches to Step 4, fills its folder box, scans, and logs "✅ Step 4 ready - review the client list and press Process to refresh." (RAN shot 11). If Step 4 could not be built, the log shows the technical "Could not open Step 4 automatically: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'folder_path'" (RAN tour 3).
10. START normal again, STOP greyed out - set directly from the worker thread in its `finally` block (`gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:527-530`) (RAN VERIFY-A-S10: during the run START "disabled" / STOP "normal", afterwards START "normal" / STOP "disabled").

**What the screens still let the user do during a run** (READ; RAN by the GUI reader, `A_code_gui_tabs_handlers.md` exp8): nothing is locked. Step 1's Browse, the path boxes, Scan and Re-scan, every Step 2 button (including Dry Run and Export) and all of Step 4 stay usable. The worker reads the two template paths afresh for every client (`gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:301, 310, 332`), so changing a template on Step 1 mid-run changes it for the next client (RAN exp8: the log showed the other template's name for client 2). Re-scan mid-run empties the scan results in place (`gui/handlers/file_handler.py:102-105`); because the running job holds the same unrecognised-files list (`gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:224`), its summary workbook's Variations sheet then reported no variations although the scan had found one (RAN exp8). The processing mode and the global include-name tick are read once at the start (`:191-192`); the per-client "📁 Name" flags are handed over as the live collection (`:193`), so a Step 2 Name click mid-run can still affect later clients (READ, MEDIUM - not run). A-R135.

Any error that escapes the per-client protection ends the whole run: "💥 Fatal error: <error>" in the log and a box "Processing Error" with the bare error text (`:522-525`; e.g. a client key rebuilt wrongly from a digit-only name, RAN GUI exp2).

Step 4 was added in bfcb24a (26-07-2026) and guarded in c463256 (A only (after the split)). It wraps the extractor panel (`ExtractorPanel`, split out of the old standalone window in a677670, A only (after the split)); the panel's two-column Setup layout, wait-time box, suffix box, separate ITC / Sales ticks per client and "Last Refresh Status" date from bd176bf (shared - before the split on 30-10-2025); the Skip Refresh tick is older - it was already in edac6a3 (shared - before the split on 30-10-2025) as one line "Skip Refresh (Use existing refreshed files)" (`git show edac6a3:power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py` lines 189-198), and bd176bf moved it into the left column and split its text over two lines (READ: `git log -S` per label; `git blame` counts in the PQ notes). 5. "Waiting for file to be released..." and a 3-second pause (`:184-185`, added).
6. Extraction (`:527-636`): "Creating new Excel instance for data extraction...", "✓ Excel instance created (hidden mode)", "Opening file in read-only mode: <name>" - the file is in fact opened read-write, A-F23 - then the opening helper's lines again (as in step 2), "✓ File opened in read-only mode" (added; equally untrue), "Starting data extraction for <ITC/Sales> report", "Number of sheets to process: <n>" (added); per configured sheet "Processing sheet: '<sheet>'", "  Cells to extract: <n>", "  Looking for sheet '<sheet>'...", "  ✓ Sheet found", "  Reading cell values..." and per cell "    Reading <cell>..." then "    ✓ <field> (<cell>) = <value>" (added: all but "Processing sheet" and the value line; a cell that cannot be read gets no second line on screen, only "⚠️ Could not read <cell>" in the log file, `:591-594`); when the sheet is missing, one "    <field> = None (sheet not found)" per field, and on a sheet error one "  <field> = None (sheet error)" per field (added); then "✅ Extraction complete. Total values extracted: <n>", "Extraction summary:", "  ✓ <field>: <value>" / "  ✗ <field>: None", and the clean-up lines "Cleaning up extraction Excel instance...", "  ✓ Workbook closed", "  ✓ Excel quit", "  ✓ COM uninitialized" (added).

Technical note (READ, HIGH): each value read is stored twice - under its field name and under its cell address (`:585, 588`) - so the "Total values extracted" count and the "Extraction summary" list each value twice (once as "<field>: <value>", once as "<cell>: <value>"). **These lines show extracted figures on screen** (and in the log file, A-R122). Without pywin32 each client shows, once, "❌ pywin32 is not installed for this Python, so Power Query cannot be refreshed. Install it with: pip install pywin32" (`:66-77`) (RAN, shot 14).

#### 10.8.5 What happens when the user presses "🚀 Start Processing" (A-F21 to A-F24)

1. Clients with at least one tick are collected; none → box "No Selection" / "Please select at least one report to process" (`power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:845-861`).
2. The wait time and suffix are copied to the refresher (`:864-865`); the Processing sub-tab is selected; Start is greyed; the log is cleared; a background worker (daemon thread) starts (`:867-883`).
3. **Outside the program (Windows, pywin32, READ only):** for each ticked report Excel opens **visible and maximised**, the program brings it to the front and **types Alt+A, R, A** (Data → Refresh All in English Excel, A-R71 ⚠), waits at least about 36 seconds per report at the default 10 seconds (A-R72), closes error dialogs it finds - on ANY program's visible dialog-type window (window classes `#32770`, `NUIDialog`, `bosa_sdm_msword`) whose title contains "microsoft excel" or one of the words error, problem, cannot, failed, unable, could not, exception, invalid, missing, by clicking a button labelled OK / Close / Yes / Continue or else asking the window to close (`report_processor.py:417-525`; A-F26) - then saves and closes; then opens the copy again in a second, hidden Excel to read the cells (A-F23). If Excel could not be brought to the front, the keystrokes go to whatever window has the focus (`report_processor.py:259-276`). Inference (HIGH): the user must not type or click while a refresh runs.
4. At the end: the consolidated workbook is written into the chosen `Annual Statement-…` folder; the box **"Complete"** - "Processing complete!\n\nOpen the consolidated report?" (Yes / No) (RAN text); Yes opens it with Windows' default program (Excel) (`:968-975`). Any failure in the run → log "❌ Error: …" and box "Error" / "Processing failed: <error>" (`:957-960`).
5. Start is enabled again, the progress resets to "Ready", and the "Last Refresh Status" texts are recomputed (`:977-986`).

There is **no Stop button** in Step 4, and closing the main window during a Step 4 run gives no warning (A-R143; `gui/main_window.py:344-355`). Nothing stops Step 3 and Step 4 from running at the same time (A-R135).

#### 10.8.6 What is invisible when the panel is embedded

The panel's status messages ("Scanning folder...", "No processed folders found", "Found <n> clients", "Error scanning folder", "Processing <client>", "Creating consolidated report", "Processing complete", "Ready") go only to the panel's own status bar, which is switched off in the main window (`gui/tabs/extract_tab.py:78`; `power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:573-585, 617, 627, 663, 667, 952, 1019`). RAN (tour 4): Scan on a folder that holds no `Annual Statement-*` folder → the panel's status became "No processed folders found", the main status bar still said "💡 Step 4: Extract", the Setup sub-tab showed nothing new, and the only trace was a log line on the Processing sub-tab - **the user gets no visible feedback**. Also RAN (shot 13): after a successful scan the Setup sub-tab shows the list, while "Found 3 clients" appears only on the Processing sub-tab. A-F18, A-F19.

#### 10.8.8 Fallback card when the extractor cannot be loaded (W5.4b, A-R129)

RAN (tour 3, import blocked on purpose; shot 28). Under the explanation strip, a pale-orange card `#FFF4E5` with a thin border (`gui/tabs/extract_tab.py:84-105`):

```text
⚠️  Power Query refresh is unavailable                      (bold, brown #8A5300)

This step needs pywin32 (Excel automation), which is not installed for the Python running this app.

Install it with:    pip install pywin32

Note that 'py' and 'python' can be different interpreters - install it for the one you launch the app with.

Details: <the import error>
```

and below the card, in grey italic: "Steps 1-3 are unaffected: organising files and creating the reports works without pywin32."

> **This card blames pywin32 for any loading failure, but a missing pywin32 can no longer cause it.** Since c463256 (A only (after the split)) pywin32 is imported inside a guard in the refresher (`power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:20-36`), so without pywin32 the panel loads normally and each report fails at run time with "pywin32 is not installed…" (RAN: my main tours ran without pywin32 and showed the normal panel). The card can now appear only for other errors, for which its explanation is wrong (RAN tour 3: "Details: import of power_query_extractor.gui.extractor_window halted; None in sys.modules" under the pywin32 text). Also, since be6418c (A only (after the split)) the program refuses to start on Windows without pywin32 (10.3), so "Steps 1-3 are unaffected … without pywin32" no longer describes Windows (READ; DOCS). With the card shown, a 'full' Step 3 run ends with the log line "Could not open Step 4 automatically: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'folder_path'" (RAN tour 3).

### 10.11 Every message box and every file or folder picker

#### 10.11.1 How message boxes look and behave

- They are Tk message boxes (`tkinter.messagebox`). On Windows Tk shows the standard Windows box: `showerror` with the red ✕ icon and an OK button, `showwarning` with the yellow triangle and OK, `showinfo` with the blue "i" and OK, `askyesno` with a question-mark icon and Yes / No buttons (READ; how each looks on the author's PC not seen, LOW for exact look).
- Each box is **modal**: the program waits until it is answered. Two boxes are raised by the Step 3 worker thread ("Processing Complete", "Processing Error"); the worker then waits for OK, so until then the Start button stays greyed, the output folder is not opened and the Step 4 hand-over does not happen (READ `gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:498-519`; RAN: the recorder saw the thread "Thread-1 (process_files_thread)"). Raising a box from a worker thread relies on Tk passing the call to the window's own thread; it worked here (Linux, Tk 9); on the author's Windows Python not checked (MEDIUM).
- Every Step 4 box is raised on the window's own thread (`power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:952-960, 989-1010`; RAN "MainThread").
- None of the boxes names the window it belongs to, except the two install boxes (M1: the hidden start-up window; M2: the "Installing…" window); for the others Tk uses the main window and Windows decides where they appear (READ `utils/dependency_installer.py:116-117, 141-148`).
- Wording: the exact text of all 25 was seen in runs - 23 in this section's tours (recorders replaced the boxes and wrote down title, text and thread) and M17 / M18 in an earlier reader's run (GUI exp8). Their Windows look is READ only.

- **Technical texts reach the user.** M6, M18, M20 and M25 show Python's raw error text, in English programmer's terms (RAN examples above: "Not a directory: …", `expected floating-point number but got ""`, "[Errno 2] No such file or directory: …"). M20 in particular does not say which client or which step failed.
- **The same title "Error" is used for eight different boxes** (M3, M4, M5, M7, M8, M9, M10, M25 - four kinds of situation: launch failure, scan inputs, processing inputs, Step 4 failure) [Corrected during verification - originally "six different situations"; READ: 8 `showerror("Error", …)` calls, `launch_extractor.py:26`, `gui/handlers/file_handler.py:123, 127, 135, 139, 144, 148`, `power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:960`] and "Warning" for three (M11-M13); "No Selection" is used both in Step 2 (M16) and Step 4 (M23).
- **M19 always says "Successfully"** and names the Step 1 target folder rather than the new `Annual Statement-…` folder (RAN; 10.7.3).
- **No box asks before overwriting or before the long Excel phase.** Nothing warns the user, before Step 4 starts, that Excel will open visibly and that keystrokes will be typed into it (10.8.5); the only warning texts about long names are M13 and M14, which use different limits (configured vs fixed 10, A-R136).
- **Closing during Step 4** gives no box at all (M21 checks only Step 3) (READ; A-R143).
- Step 4 failures inside a single report never produce a box; they appear only as "⚠️ …" lines in the Step 4 log (10.8.4).

### 10.13 The typical user workflow, click by click

The order below is what the code expects (READ), confirmed on screen where marked (RAN tours 1-6). Variants follow.

#### 10.13.1 Main path: organise files and create reports ('organize' workflow)

1. **Start the program** from a console window in the program folder: `python main.py` (or `py main.py`, or double-click `main.py`). A black console window shows the banner and the requirements report (10.3). If a package is missing, answer the "Install missing packages?" box (M1); "Yes" installs and restarts, "No" continues only if nothing essential is missing.
2. **The main window opens on "📁 Step 1: Setup"** (1200×800, centred). If the program was used before, the four paths, the workflow, the processing mode, the include-name tick, the length and dark mode come back from the settings file, and the checklist shows ✓ / ✕ for each path (RAN: tour 4 restored every value; shot 34 shows a restored checklist, there in dark mode). Scan results are NOT remembered - Step 2 is empty at every start (RAN shot 31).
3. **Check the CHECKLIST card.** All four rows "✓" (pill "Ready - all 4 items set") is the intended state before Step 3; only the source row is needed to scan. The checklist does not itself block Step 3: Step 3's own check is weaker - both template files must exist and a target must be typed, but a target folder that does not exist yet is simply created by the run (A-R51; `gui/handlers/file_handler.py:132-151`; `core/file_organizer.py:65-69`) (READ HIGH). [Corrected during verification - originally said every row "must show ✓ … before Step 3 can succeed".]
4. **In "WHAT SHOULD THIS RUN DO?" leave "📁 Organise files & create reports" selected** (the default; the choice is saved at once).
5. **Scroll down** (wheel or scroll bar - at 1200×800 only the top 40 % of the page is visible, RAN) **to "📂 FOLDERS & TEMPLATES" and click the four "Browse…" buttons** in turn: source folder (P1), ITC template (P2), Sales template (P3), target folder (P4). Each choice is saved; typing a path instead also works but is not saved until something else saves (A-R116).
6. **In "⚙️ PROCESSING MODE" pick "🆕 Fresh Run"** (default) for a new batch - or "🔄 Re-Run" to add a new version to the latest batch (this choice is not saved). Optionally tick "Include client name in Level 4 folder names" and adjust "Max client folder name length" with the arrows.
7. **Scroll further and click "🔍  Scan Files".** The window freezes while the top level of the source folder is read (seconds; longer on a network share). When at least one client is recognised, the program jumps to **"✅ Step 2: Validation"** by itself (RAN shot 06). If nothing is recognised the user stays on Step 1 and only the status bar says "No valid GST files found".
8. **Read the "📊 SCAN SUMMARY"** (files found, recognised, unrecognised count, clients complete / with missing files).
9. **Tick the clients to process** in the table: click the "✓" column of a row, or use ↑ / ↓ and Space, or the buttons "☑️ Select All" / "☐ Clear All" / "✅ Complete Only". All rows start unticked (A-R138).
10. Optional: **scroll the table to the right** (horizontal scroll bar) to reach the "📁 Name" column and click a client's cell to add its name to its folder names (M14 / M15 may appear) (10.6.3, A-F10).
11. Optional: **click "🧪 DRY RUN"** - the program jumps to Step 3 and writes a text preview into the log (no file touched); click the "✅ Step 2: Validation" tab to come back.
12. Optional: **click "📋 EXPORT LIST"** to save the ticked clients to a `.txt` file (P5, M17).
13. **Click "🚀 START"** (Step 2) - or "🚀 START PROCESSING" on Step 3. Possible stops: M7-M10 (templates / target), M12 (nothing ticked), M13 (long names, only with the include-name tick on). Then the program jumps to **"🚀 Step 3: Processing"**: Start greys out, Stop becomes active, the bar and the "Client i of n: … | ETA: …" line move, the dark log fills (RAN shots 26, 12).
14. **Wait** (do not close the window - the box M21 appears if you try, and closing kills the run in the middle of a client). "⏹ STOP" stops after the current client.
15. **Click OK on "Processing Complete"** (M19). Windows Explorer then opens the new `Annual Statement-<DDMMYY HHMM>` folder, and the log ends with "ℹ️ Workflow is 'organise only'. Open Step 4 if you also want to refresh Power Query." (RAN tour 2).

#### 10.13.2 Continuing to Step 4 (refresh Power Query and extract)

16. **Click the "🔄 Step 4: Extract" tab.** The "Folder Path" box already holds the Step 1 target folder (unless the user typed another one there); the client list is empty and "🚀 Start Processing" is greyed (RAN shot 33).
17. **Click "🔍 Scan"** (or "📁 Browse" to pick another folder, P6, which scans at once). The newest `Annual Statement-*` folder inside that folder is used; one row per client folder appears with ITC and Sales ticks pre-ticked where the report exists, and "Last Refresh Status" (RAN shot 11). Nothing visible confirms the scan except the list itself; "Found <n> clients" is written only on the "Processing" sub-tab (10.8.6).
18. Optional: untick reports, or use "✓ Select All" / "✗ Deselect All" / "ITC Only" / "Sales Only"; change "Power Query Wait Time" (arrows, 5-60 s), "Refreshed File Suffix", or tick "Skip Refresh".
19. **Click "🚀 Start Processing".** The panel switches to its "Processing" sub-tab and the log starts. On Windows, Excel opens visibly and maximised for each report and the program types Alt+A, then R, then A into it (10.8.5; `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:282-292`). [Corrected during verification - originally said "Alt, R, A"; the first keystroke is Alt+A.] **Inference (HIGH): the user must not use the mouse or keyboard until the run ends** - keystrokes go to whatever window is in front. There is no Stop button.
20. **Answer "Complete" / "Open the consolidated report?" (M24)** - "Yes" opens `PQ_Extraction_Report_<YYYYMMDD_HHMM>.xlsx` (saved inside the `Annual Statement-…` folder) in Excel. The "Last Refresh Status" texts update.

#### 10.13.3 Variants

| Variant | What changes in the clicks | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **'full' workflow** (step 4 = "🔄 Full pipeline") | After step 15 the program itself switches to Step 4, fills the folder and scans (steps 16-17 happen automatically; the log ends "✅ Step 4 ready - review the client list and press Process to refresh."). The user still does steps 18-20 | RAN (shot 11); A-R154 |
| **Re-processing a batch** | Step 6: choose "🔄 Re-Run" (or "▶️ Resume") - a new `Version-<DDMMYY HHMM>` folder is added inside the newest `Annual Statement-…` folder (newest by date modified). Resume differs from Re-Run only when a file of the same name is already in that Version folder, which happens only if the run is repeated within the same minute: Resume then skips it, Re-Run overwrites it, and Fresh first makes a back-up copy (T4) | RAN (GUI exp7); READ `core/file_organizer.py:163-196` (which Level-1 folder), `:276-287` (existing file: Fresh → back-up, Resume → skip, Re-Run → overwrite) |
| **Only Step 4** (reports made earlier) | Start the program, click the Step 4 tab, Browse / Scan, then steps 18-20; Steps 1-3 are not needed | READ |
| **Standalone extractor** | `python launch_extractor.py`: its own window opens, takes the target folder from the settings file and scans at once; then steps 18-20; no start-up checks, no close warning | RAN (shots 29-30) |
| **A later day** | Settings come back, but Step 2 is empty: the user must Scan again before ticking clients | RAN (tour 4) |
| **Something not recognised** | Rename the files to the patterns on the "📝  EXPECTED FILE NAMES" card, then "🔄  Re-scan". The names of unrecognised files are not shown anywhere on screen; after a run they are listed on the "Variations" sheet of the summary workbook (A-F9) | READ |

> **What the user is never told on screen** (READ): which files were not recognised (only their count, A-F9); which copies failed (only successful copies are logged, A-F17); that Excel is about to be driven and must not be touched (Step 4); that a Stop happened (T12); where the Step 4 log goes when the Setup sub-tab is showing (10.8.6).

### 10.14 Keyboard, mouse and accessibility

The program defines no keyboard shortcuts of its own (no Ctrl/Alt combinations, no Enter or Escape handling; READ: the only key bindings in the GUI code are the four Step 2 table keys, `gui/tabs/validation_tab.py:241-244`). Everything else is Tk's built-in behaviour (READ; exact Windows behaviour MEDIUM).

| Where | Key / mouse | Effect | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Anywhere | Tab / Shift+Tab | Moves the keyboard focus between controls (Tk default) | READ (no override) |
| Step 1, Step 4 (and the title-strip tick) | Space on a focused button, tick box or radio button | Presses it (these use `command=`) | READ `gui/tabs/setup_tab.py:383-384`; `power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:229-397` |
| Step 2 "🧪 DRY RUN", "📋 EXPORT LIST", "🚀 START", "☑️ Select All", "☐ Clear All", "✅ Complete Only"; Step 3 "🚀 START PROCESSING", "⏹ STOP" | Space / keyboard | **Nothing**: the buttons have no command; they react only to a mouse press | RAN (tour 5: "🧪 DRY RUN" has an empty command, and pressing it the keyboard way added nothing to the log) |
| Step 2 table (has the focus when the tab is built, `gui/tabs/validation_tab.py:247`) | ↑ / ↓ | Move the highlight one row (↓ with nothing highlighted highlights the first row) | 10.6.4 |
| Step 2 table | Space | Ticks / unticks the first highlighted row | 10.6.4 |
| Step 2 table | Mouse click in "✓" / in "📁 Name" | Tick / name toggle | 10.6.4 |
| Main tab strip, Step 4 sub-tabs | Mouse click | Switch tab (keyboard switching is Tk's default only when the tab strip itself has the focus; `enable_traversal` - Ctrl+Tab - is not switched on) | READ (grep: no `enable_traversal`) |
| Step 1 page | Mouse wheel | Scrolls the page (only over the page, only if it overflows) | 10.5.9 |
| Step 4 client list / Step 4 log | Mouse wheel | Scrolls (log: small touch-pad movements are ignored) | 10.8.3, 10.8.4 |
| Step 2 summary, Step 2 table, Step 3 log | Mouse wheel | Scroll (Tk default) | READ (MEDIUM - no program binding; relies on Tk's own wheel handling) |
| Step 1 | Mouse resting 450 ms | Tooltip (no keyboard way to see it) | 10.5.11 |

Accessibility observations (READ unless marked; technical, for the author to weigh): text sizes are small (Segoe UI 8-9 for most Step 1 detail and hint texts, Consolas 8-9 in logs and the patterns card) and fixed - they do not follow Windows' text-size setting (MEDIUM); status is often shown by colour, but the Step 1 checklist and the Step 2 status column also carry symbols / words (✓ ○ ✕, "✅ Complete", "⚠️ Missing …"), so they do not depend on colour alone; the Step 3 log uses colour only to separate success / warning / error lines, while most lines also start with a symbol (✅ ❌ ⚠️); the light-mode progress bar is pale grey on grey (10.7.1); in dark mode colour coding of buttons disappears and several texts become hard to read (10.10.3).
