## SECTION 11: RECONSTRUCTION BLUEPRINT

This section is the plan for rebuilding project A (`goyal-sidhant/AnnualStatement_oldv1`, branch `main`, snapshot `bf2f1dd` of 27-07-2026, the Tkinter program that calls itself "GST File Organizer v3.0") from scratch. It follows the six items of the author's audit method (`/home/user/Annual_Statement_2.0/.build-docs/toolkit/Project_Audit_FINAL.md`, Section 11): 11.1 Foundation, 11.2 Core logic build order, 11.3 Feature priority, 11.4 Known improvements, 11.5 Estimated complexity, 11.6 Suggested skills. 11.7 collects the decisions the rebuild needs from the author, and 11.8 lists the runs made for this section.

### 11.0 How to read this section

**What "rebuild" means here.** A rebuild that does everything A does today (the 31 features A-F1 to A-F31 and the 157 rules A-R1 to A-R157 of the registry, `/root/merge-scratch/audit/A_registry.md`), without A's known defects (the 79 gaps A-G1 to A-G79 of Section 7). Whether the merged program is built from A, from project B or from both is decided later (the comparison); nothing here chooses between A and B.

**What this section does and does not do.**
- It gives technical recommendations only: how to structure, order, test and harden the code.
- It never decides a GST rule. Anything that decides a tax figure, which return / table / sheet / cell a figure or file belongs to, a rate, limit or threshold, rounding, the financial year or tax period, GSTIN / PAN / state-code logic, ITC eligibility or reversal, or a due date is tagged **[GST RULE]**: the rebuild copies such rules exactly as the author approves them, and every improvement that touches one is limited to making the code do what the author's rule says (for example "make the cell wiring match the mapping table the author approves"). Nothing here says whether any GST rule is right.
- Values that change over time (package and Python versions, Excel behaviour and keyboard shortcuts, the ~218-character path figure, template cell positions, table numbers, file-name conventions, the state list) carry **⚠** so the author can check them.
- Where the author's own Standards 12 and 13 (`/home/user/Annual_Statement_2.0/.build-docs/toolkit/rebuild_pipeline_FINAL.md:817-898` and `:900-1061`) say something, this section states the fact and what each choice means for the rebuild; adopting a standard is the author's decision.

**The IMPORTANT CONSTRAINT of the audit method (item 4), and how it was applied.** Before any improvement was written, Section 8 (Design decisions D1 to D20, iterations I1 to I23, patterns P1 to P9) was checked for that topic. Every row of 11.4 has a "Section 8 check" column. Where Section 8 explains why A's approach was chosen over the alternative that would otherwise be obvious, the row does NOT recommend that alternative: it gives a third option that keeps the original reason, or states the trade-off honestly. These cases are collected in 11.4.3 (T1 to T10).

**Evidence markers.**
- Every statement about the code cites `file:line` at `bf2f1dd` (repository-relative; the copy `/root/merge-scratch/A-copy` has the same line numbers). Older code is written `path:line@commit`.
- **READ** = established by reading the code. **RAN** = executed on made-up inputs in a scratch copy. "RAN (me)" = run for this section in `/root/merge-scratch/run/A-S11/` (scripts `s1` to `s6`, listed in 11.8); every run used `python -B` (no compiled files written), a redirected home and temporary folder, and the copy was checked identical to A-copy afterwards. Other RAN marks name the section whose run is cited (for example "RAN, Section 7 r2").
- Anything that needs Excel through COM or Windows could not run here (Linux, no Excel, no pywin32) and is READ only.
- Inferences carry **HIGH** (clear from the code, a comment or a commit message), **MEDIUM** (a reasonable inference) or **LOW** (speculation). "NOT SURE" always comes with a way to check.

**IDs.** Features `A-F…`, rules `A-R…` (registry), gaps `A-G…` (Section 7), design decisions `D…`, iterations `I…` and patterns `P…` (Section 8), Standard 12's "Excel through COM" rules `C1` to `C18` (as numbered in Appendix X1, `/root/merge-scratch/audit/A/X12.md`, X1.3.1). New labels in this section: foundation decisions `FD1`-`FD9` (11.1.1), structural rules `SR1`-`SR8` (11.1.5), contracts `K1`-`K8` (11.2.3), trade-offs `T1`-`T10` (11.4.3) and skills `SK1`-`SK13` (11.6). No feature, rule or gap ID was invented; findings of Sections 3, 5 and 10 that Section 7 did not number are cited by their place there (11.4.4).

**Commit labels.** The 12 commits shared by A and B (`edac6a3` … `47a1492`) are "shared - before the split on 30-10-2025"; A's 34 later commits are "A only (after the split)". A has one branch, `main`. Every shared commit is labelled where it is named. Every other commit hash in this section is one of A's 34 later commits — A only (after the split): `fc279af`, `f7eb8f1` (March 2026) and `a603c02` … `bf2f1dd` (23-07-2026 to 27-07-2026) — and the label is written out wherever the timing matters (RAN `git -C /root/merge-scratch/combined log A/main`: 46 commits) [Corrected during verification — several shared commits were named without their label; they are now labelled].

**Confidentiality.** No client name, GSTIN, PAN, real file name or figure appears here; made-up names such as `<Client A>`, `ClientA Traders` and `0042` are used.

**Plain-English terms used in this section** (each is also explained where it first matters).

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| rebuild / reconstruction | Writing the program again from a clean start, using this audit as the specification |
| feature dependency | Feature X "needs" feature Y when X cannot work, or cannot be tested, until Y exists (for example the refresh needs the reports) |
| build order, phase | The order in which parts are written; a *phase* is a group of parts finished and checked together before the next group starts |
| module, package | A *module* is one `.py` file; a *package* is a folder of modules with an `__init__.py` file |
| pure logic | Code that only calculates (names, rules, decisions) and touches no window, no Excel and no network, so it can be tested anywhere in seconds |
| unit test, characterization test, guard test | A *unit test* checks one small piece; a *characterization test* records what the code does today so a change cannot alter it unnoticed; a *guard test* reads the source code and fails if a known bad pattern comes back (A has one: `tests/test_scroll_bindings.py`) |
| acceptance test | A check run by a person on a real office PC with Excel (needed for everything that drives Excel, which cannot run on Linux) |
| contract | The agreed shape of data that one part hands to another (names, keys, folder patterns); a *contract test* checks that the writer and every reader agree |
| run plan | A frozen copy of everything a run needs (clients, files, templates, options), taken when Start is pressed, so later clicks cannot change a run in progress |
| manifest | A small file, written during a run, that lists what has been done (for example each file copied and its size), so a stopped run can be resumed exactly |
| atomic save | Writing a file under a temporary name and then renaming it over the final name in one step, so a crash never leaves a half-written file under the real name |
| run lock, single-instance lock | A marker (in memory or a small file) that says "a run is in progress", so a second run, or a second copy of the program, cannot start on top of it |
| COM, pywin32 | *COM* is Windows' way for one program to drive another (here Python drives Excel); *pywin32* is the Python package that provides it |
| GetActiveObject / Dispatch / DispatchEx | Three ways to get an Excel through COM: take the one already running; start one, which may still attach to a running one; always start a separate, private one (Standard 12 asks for `DispatchEx`) |
| context manager | A Python `with` block that always runs its clean-up (closing a workbook, quitting Excel), even after an error |
| openpyxl, Power Query, DataMashup | *openpyxl* reads and writes `.xlsx` files without Excel, but drops Power Query when it SAVES; *Power Query* is Excel's data-import tool in the ITC/Sales templates; its queries live in a hidden part of the file called *DataMashup* |
| Links sheet, Info!BB2 | The template sheet into which Step 3 writes folder paths and file names; the cell whose value Step 4 treats as proof of a refresh [GST RULE] ⚠ |
| key presses (SendKeys), key tips | Pressing keyboard keys by program into whatever window has the focus; Excel's *key tips* are the Alt shortcuts (Alt, A, R, A = Data → Refresh All in English Excel) ⚠ |
| foreground window, process | The window that receives key presses; a *process* is one running program (each Excel is one process) |
| Tk / Tkinter, PySide6 | *Tkinter* is Python's built-in window toolkit (used by A); *PySide6* is the Qt window toolkit Standard 12 names |
| worker thread, daemon thread, bridge | A *worker thread* is a second line of work beside the window; a *daemon* thread is killed instantly when the program ends; a *bridge* (queue + `after`) is the one safe road from the worker to the window |
| row id (iid) | The hidden identifier Tk's table widget (Treeview) gives each row; it can hold any text and is returned unchanged |
| schema | The expected shape of a settings file (which keys, which value types) |
| pre-flight check | A check of inputs (templates, folders, path lengths, name clashes) made before a run creates or changes anything |
| launcher, `pythonw.exe`, `_runtime`, embeddable Python | Standard 13's start-up: a `.bat` file starts `pythonw.exe` (Python without a console window) from one shared, portable Python folder `_runtime` (python.org's *embeddable* package plus packages) |
| `%LOCALAPPDATA%` | The per-user, per-PC settings folder of Windows (`C:\Users\<name>\AppData\Local`), where Standard 13 keeps settings and logs |
| SKILL.md | A Claude Code *skill* file: written instructions, checks and examples that Claude loads whenever it does a certain kind of task, so a pattern learnt once is reused in later projects |
| pip, `requirements.txt` | *pip* is Python's package installer; `requirements.txt` is the list of packages (and minimum or exact versions) it installs from |
| console, `sys.stdout` | The black text window a program started from a command prompt writes to; `sys.stdout` is Python's channel to it, which does not exist under `pythonw.exe` |
| `excepthook`, callback-error hook | Python's (and Tk's `report_callback_exception`) "last resort" for an error nothing else caught; Standard 13 sets it to write an error file and show a message box |
| `find_spec` | A Python check that a package's files exist, without loading it — so it cannot see a package that is present but broken |
| log levels (DEBUG, INFO, WARNING), rotating log | A log line's level says how important it is; DEBUG lines are normally switched off. A *rotating* log starts a new file at a size limit and keeps only a few old files, so it never grows without end |
| UTF-8, code page (cp1252) | Two ways of storing text as bytes; UTF-8 can store every character (including ₹ and emoji), the older Windows code page cannot, so such lines are lost or garbled |
| mapped drive, UNC path, network share | A *network share* is a folder on the office server; it can be reached by a *mapped drive* letter (for example `Z:`) or by its *UNC path* `\\server\share\…`; the two forms name the same place only where the letter is mapped the same way |
| VPN | A secure link from outside the office to the office network; every file-system call over it is a slow round-trip |
| free-threaded Python | A special build of Python 3.14 (`python3.14t`) that runs threads in parallel; on the author's PC it was the interpreter without pywin32 |
| `.xltx`, `.xltm`, `.xlsm`, content type | Excel template (`.xltx`), macro template (`.xltm`) and macro workbook (`.xlsm`); a workbook's *content type* (inside `[Content_Types].xml`) tells Excel whether the file is a template or a normal workbook |
| debounce | Waiting until typing has paused (A: 350 ms) before re-checking, so a check does not run on every key press |
| ETA | The estimated time left, shown in the progress bar |
| fake COM, virtual display (Xvfb) | A *fake COM* object records the calls the code would make to Excel, so the call order can be tested on Linux; a *virtual display* lets window tests run on a computer without a screen |
| mutation check, vacuous test | A *mutation check* deliberately changes one thing in a scratch copy (usually re-introducing an old bug) and runs the tests to see whether one fails; a *vacuous* test is one that can never fail |
| callback, lambda | A *callback* is a function the window calls when something happens (a click, a timer); a *lambda* is a one-line unnamed function, often used as a callback |
| git pickaxe (`git log -S`) | A search of the whole history for every commit that added or removed a given text |

### The blueprint in brief (for the author)

1. **Decide nine things before writing code** (11.1.1): the window toolkit, how users start the app, the Python version, where packages come from, the refresh method, which Excel to use, whether the standalone extractor stays, where settings and logs live, and the GST data (templates, patterns, cells) the rebuild copies.
2. **Build from the inside out** (11.2): first the author-owned data and the start-up gate, then the pure rules (file names, clients, completeness, names), then file work without Excel, then one Excel layer, then the refresh, then the windows. Every phase ends with tests; everything that drives Excel ends with an acceptance test on an office PC.
3. **Essential features** (11.3, Tier 1): the start-up check, the main window, choosing the source, target and templates, scanning and recognising files, choosing clients, organising files, the two reports, run control, one home for Step 4 (the Step 4 tab or the standalone window), finding the reports in Step 4, the refresh, the naming of refreshed copies, extraction, the consolidated workbook and an error log. Nice-to-have (Tier 3): the workflow mode, the include-client-name option, the dry run, the client-list export, dark mode, the standalone launcher (unless it is the only Step 4 home) and the help texts and tooltips. [Corrected during verification — the brief originally left out A-F3, A-F18/A-F29 and A-F22 (naming) from Tier 1 and named only four of the seven Tier 3 features]
4. **Fix what Section 7 found, without undoing what Section 8 explains** (11.4): for example the 9 columns of the consolidated workbook that today show another cell's value are made to follow the mapping table the author approves, by looking values up by their exact name (RAN me: 22 of 22 columns hold the cell their configuration names, instead of 13 of 22) — which cell is right stays the author's call [GST RULE] ⚠ — while the editable cell-mapping file the author relies on (D20) stays. Ten places where Section 8 records a reason for A's way are handled as trade-offs (11.4.3).
5. **Size of the work** (11.5): 7 features rated COMPLEX (3+ hours each), 12 MODERATE, 12 SIMPLE. The COMPLEX ones are the start-up and runtime set-up (A-F1), the file recognition (A-F7), the organiser (A-F13), the ITC report mechanism (A-F14, which the Sales report then reuses), run control (A-F17), the refresh (A-F21) and the consolidated workbook (A-F24). A rough total of 39-90 hours of AI-assisted work plus cross-cutting work and the office-PC acceptance sessions (an inference, LOW-MEDIUM confidence).
6. **Reusable skills** (11.6): 13 skill ideas, from "Excel through COM session" to "characterization tests first".
7. **What the author must decide or supply** (11.7): 39 items, from the window toolkit to blank copies of the two templates; 12 of them are [GST RULE] matters or touch one, and the rebuild decides none of them.

| pytest | Test suite (288 tests) | Standard 13: not in the app's own `requirements.txt` (`:937-940`) | 8.2.6, HIGH | Keep, in a separate developer list. |
| GST portal | Not automated | "Do not automate" (`:836`) | 8.2.7, HIGH | Keep: the program works on files a person downloads. |
| Small helper scripts | None outside Python | Python, no `.ps1` (`:842`) | — | Keep (the Standard 13 launcher is a `.bat`, `:951-963`). |

No library is needed for the improvements of 11.4 beyond the ones above: atomic saves (`os.replace`), rotating logs (`logging.handlers`), the worker bridge (`queue`), JSON schema checks and lock files are all in Python's standard library; window ownership (`win32process`) and UNC resolution (`win32wnet`) are part of pywin32 (READ, general knowledge; their exact behaviour on the office PCs is NOT SURE and belongs to the acceptance tests of 11.1.6).

#### 11.1.5 Project structure

A's layering (`core/` · `utils/` · `gui/` · `power_query_extractor/`, Section 8.3.2) is sound in outline; its weak points are values typed in several places (P4), package files that load the whole window (8.8), one object that holds all shared state (8.3.4), and Excel code mixed into the same files as pure rules (`core/excel_handler.py` holds both the COM session and `prepare_template_data`). The structure below keeps the layering, fixes those points, and matches the `config\ core\ gui\` layout Standard 13 shows (`rebuild_pipeline_FINAL.md:919-921`).

```text

├── pytest.ini                    ← [pytest] / pythonpath = . / testpaths = tests
├── config\                       ← AUTHOR-OWNED DATA, one place per value
│   ├── file_patterns.py          ← A-R1..A-R12 (A-R1..A-R7, A-R12 [GST RULE] ⚠), A-R26, A-R27 [GST RULE] ⚠
│   ├── states.py                 ← A-R21, A-R22 [GST RULE] ⚠
```

#### 11.1.6 The test foundation

1. **Set up first:** `pytest.ini` as Standard 13 shows it; a shared test fixture that points the home folder, the temporary folder and `%LOCALAPPDATA%` at a temporary directory for every test (A's `tests/test_main_window_tabs.py:36-38` can rewrite the developer's real settings file, RAN Section 7 A-G60); the same fixture sets `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1` for every child Python a test starts, because A's three probe tests otherwise write 38 compiled files into the program folder despite `-B` (added during self-review, from Appendix X3.6 item 4).
2. **Carry A's rule tests over as the specification.** Of A's 288 tests (RAN, Section 2.1), these files check rules and build no window (RAN me: an import listing of every test file): `tests/test_file_patterns.py` (21), `tests/test_helpers.py` (47), `tests/test_file_ops.py` (22), `tests/test_scan.py` (5), `tests/test_excel_com.py` (3), `tests/test_requirements_check.py` (15), plus the logic of `tests/test_refresh_naming.py` (19; three of them import `power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py` for `_latest_refresh_times`), `tests/test_setup_validation.py` (19; imports through the `gui` package, which loads the window, SR3) and `tests/test_workflow_mode.py` (7; uses fakes but imports `gui/handlers/processing_handler.py`) — 158 tests in 9 files. The window tests (`test_setup_tab_smoke.py` 13, `test_dark_mode.py` 11, `test_extractor_panel.py` 10, `test_extractor_standalone.py` 6, `test_main_window_tabs.py` 7, `test_scroll_bindings.py` 64) depend on FD1; `test_optional_pywin32.py` (4), `test_dependency_installer.py` (13) and `test_processing_handler.py` (2) depend on FD2/FD4 and the run-control design. Where an A test pins a GST rule (for example `tests/test_helpers.py:96-97` pins `Unknown Place` → `UP`, A-R22), it pins the author's rule as it is; it does not judge it.
3. **Write the tests A never had, first** (coverage measured in the test notes, `/root/merge-scratch/notes2/A_tests.md` §7, RAN): `core/file_organizer.py` 0 of 12 functions ever run by a test; `power_query_extractor/core/data_consolidator.py` 0 of 6; `core/excel_handler.py` 1 of 15; `gui/handlers/client_handler.py` 1 of 14; the Step 3 worker, the settings writer/reader agreement, and every Excel session. The contract tests of 11.2.3 come first.
4. **Turn the surviving mutations into tests.** A mutation check (deliberately putting one change into a scratch copy — mostly an old bug that a later commit fixed — and running the suite to see whether any test notices; RAN, test notes §6, 30 mutations M01-M28 with M12 in three variants) found 14 changes that no test notices (plus M12b, a spacing variant of a pattern the guard test looks for, and M22, which goes unnoticed only on Linux):
   - **11 fixes that no test protects:** M08 (the Setup checklist recompute after a theme switch, `c89c1d4`), M13-M15 (dark-mode details, `725fbaf`, `169c7b5`), M16 (the per-client folder-setting key by state code, `33d0baf`), M17 (the short category folder names, `7347383`), M18 (newest Version folder by date modified, `c1583d6`), M19 (worker log lines scheduled, `c1f425e`), M20 (refresh status re-read after a run, `2acffed`), M21 (Skip Refresh with the configured suffix, `2aaa2b1`), M28 (Step 4 not overwriting the folder the user chose there, `bfcb24a`) — each becomes a test.
   - **2 rules present since `edac6a3` (shared - before the split on 30-10-2025) that no test pins:** M23 (one entry of the state table changed) [GST RULE] ⚠ and M24 (GSTR-3B duplicates flagged like the other types) [GST RULE]. The new test pins the author's table or rule as approved; it does not judge it.
   - **1 vacuous test:** M27 replaced the dependency check's `find_spec` (a check that a package's files exist, without loading it) by a real import, and all 15 tests still passed, because `tests/test_requirements_check.py:27-32` can never fail. This is NOT a fix to protect: 11.4.2 A-G7 recommends exactly that real import. The rebuild replaces the vacuous test with one that a present-but-broken package is reported as missing.

### 11.2 Core logic build order

The rule of the order: **build what other features need before the features that need it, and build what can be tested anywhere before what can only be tested on an office PC.** A's own history followed the opposite route for Step 4 (a separate program first, merged in July 2026, I12) and paid for it with a start-up crash chain on one evening (I13); the order below avoids such late joins by fixing the contracts (11.2.3) first.

### 11.3 Feature priority

**Tiers.** *Tier 1 — essential*: without it the program cannot do its job (sort the clients' GST files, build the ITC and Sales reports, refresh them and bring the figures into one workbook) or cannot be run safely. *Tier 2 — important*: protects correctness, saves a lot of time or is used in every run, but the job can be done without it for a first release. *Tier 3 — nice-to-have*: convenience or appearance. The tiers are a technical view of the evidence; which features the merged program keeps is the author's decision, and "essential" says nothing about whether any GST rule inside a feature is right.

| ID | Feature | Tier | Reason (from the evidence) | Other features that need it |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A-F1 | Start-up and dependency checks | 1 (the check); the install offer: the author's decision (T6) | "Producing damaged reports is worse than refusing to start" (`utils/requirements_check.py:52-53`; D14, HIGH): without pywin32 the reports silently lose Power Query (RAN, Appendix X1 R1) | all |
| A-F2 | Main window, tabs, status bar, close confirmation | 1 | The container of every screen (`gui/main_window.py:131-149`); its close handler is what protects a running job (A-G27) | all screens |
| A-F3 | Choose source, target and templates | 1 | Every run starts from these four paths (`gui/handlers/file_handler.py:19-55`) | A-F4, A-F7, A-F13, A-F14, A-F15, A-F18 |
| A-F4 | Live setup checklist | 2 | Catches wrong inputs before a run; added in `322717f` (A only (after the split)) after the older pop-up checks; can be replaced by a check at Start, but the network-friendly design (D7) is worth keeping | — |

### 11.4 Known improvements (from the gaps of Section 7)

#### 11.4.1 How each improvement was checked

For every gap A-G1 to A-G79 (Section 7, all 79 are covered below, in Section 7's order):
1. The gap's evidence was taken from Section 7 (severity as Section 7.10 gives it) and its key lines re-opened in the code where this section relies on them (READ).
2. Section 8 was checked for a decision (D1-D20), an iteration (I1-I23) or a pattern (P1-P9) on the same topic. The column "Section 8 check" names it and says what it records; "none" means Section 8 records no reason for A's way on this point.
3. Where Section 8 explains why A's approach was chosen over the obvious alternative, the improvement keeps that reason: it gives a third option or states the trade-off (marked **T#**, collected in 11.4.3).
4. Where a gap touches a [GST RULE], the improvement is limited to making the program show, check or follow the author's rule; the column "The author decides" names what only the author can settle, with the question number where one exists (7.11 Q#, 9.10 #, 5.23 #).

#### 11.4.3 Trade-offs where Section 8 records a reason for A's way (T1 to T10)

The audit method's IMPORTANT CONSTRAINT: where Section 8 explains why A's approach was chosen over the alternative that looks obvious, that alternative is not recommended. Each row names A's approach and its recorded reason, the obvious alternative and what it would bring back, and a third option (or, where none exists, the trade-off stated honestly). Which way to go is the author's decision in every row; the facts for it are here.

D4: kept on purpose (HIGH — design note `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-25-merge-extractor-design.md:125-126`); WHY keys instead of Excel's own command is not recorded (LOW). 8.4.1 names two possible reasons: (a) a `RefreshAll` sent through COM returned at once and the save stored old data; (b) prompts that appear only in a visible Excel. The texts `RefreshAll`, `CalculateUntilAsyncQueriesDone` and `DispatchEx` occur in no `.py` file at any of A's 46 commits (RAN, Section 12 pickaxe), so if it was tried, it was before git. | Standard 12's sequence: `BackgroundQuery = False` on each connection, `RefreshAll()`, `CalculateUntilAsyncQueriesDone()`, no connection still `Refreshing`, then save (C10-C13, `rebuild_pipeline_FINAL.md:860-867`). ### 11.5 Estimated complexity

#### 11.5.1 How the ratings were made

**Scale (the audit method's):** SIMPLE = under 1 hour, MODERATE = 1 to 3 hours, COMPLEX = 3 hours or more, for AI-assisted rebuilding (Claude Code working from this audit as the specification).

**What one rating covers:** writing the feature in the structure of 11.1.5, its tests that can run anywhere (unit, contract and guard tests, 11.1.6), and the technical fixes 11.4 lists for it. **Not covered:** the author's decisions (11.7), preparing the shared runtime on the office share, and the time of the office-PC acceptance sessions for everything that drives Excel (they depend on the PCs and cannot be estimated from the code); the column "Office-PC test" says which features need one.

**Evidence used for each rating:**
- the size of the feature in A, counted from the registry's "Where it lives" ranges (RAN me, `s1_feature_size.py`: physical lines, and "code lines" = not blank and not a pure comment line, overlapping ranges counted once; A-F14 and A-F15 share one mechanism and are counted together). The script holds the registry's MAIN ranges, typed into it by hand: some are widened to the span between two nearby ranges of one file (for example A-F1's `utils/dependency_installer.py:23-158` for the registry's `:26-38, 41-60, 63-74, 88-158`), and single-line mentions in other files are left out (for example A-F6's `gui/main_window.py:93, 369, 386-387`, `core/file_organizer.py:30, 42, 83-87` and `gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:194`), so the "files" figure counts the files with a main range, not every file the registry names, and the sizes are approximate (READ `/root/merge-scratch/run/A-S11/scripts/s1_feature_size.py:13-78`; re-run by verification with identical output) [Corrected during verification — the approximation was not stated];
- the rules the feature carries (registry);
- the gaps the rebuild must fix in it (11.4.2's "Features" column; HIGH and MEDIUM-HIGH gaps named);
- whether it drives Excel through COM (then it can be finished only with an office-PC test);
- how often A itself had to rework it (Section 8.5, iterations I1 to I23).

**Confidence:** every rating is an inference (MEDIUM for the order between features; LOW-MEDIUM for the hours themselves). The size of a feature in A is a weak guide: A's code carries dead and duplicated parts (SR8, P4), while the rebuild adds the checks of 11.4.

#### 11.5.3 Totals, and the older audit's ratings against today's evidence

**A rough total (inference, LOW-MEDIUM confidence):** 12 SIMPLE features × ½-1 hour + 12 MODERATE × 1-3 hours + 7 COMPLEX × 3-6 hours (6 is an assumption for the range, not a measurement) ≈ 39-90 hours of AI-assisted work, plus the cross-cutting work above (about 4½-13 hours on the same scale: four MODERATE items and one SIMPLE) and the office-PC acceptance sessions, which cannot be estimated from the code. The answers of 11.7 move the total: keeping key presses (T1) adds A-F26 and the foreground check; PySide6 (FD1) changes A-F2, A-F28 and A-F31 but not the rules; dropping Tier 3 features (11.3) removes up to seven SIMPLE or MODERATE items.

### 11.6 Suggested skills (SKILL.md ideas)

A Claude Code skill is a `SKILL.md` file (a short header with a name and a one-line description, then instructions, checklists and examples) that Claude loads whenever it does that kind of task. The ideas below turn what A's history taught — often the hard way — into reusable patterns for this and later projects. Each idea says what the skill would encode, which checks it would carry, the evidence from A behind it, and what it must NOT contain: GST rules (patterns, cells, state codes, success markers, thresholds) belong to each project's configuration and to the author, never to a skill.

#### 11.6.3 Example: the outline of SK1's SKILL.md

```markdown
---
name: excel-com-session
description: Drive Microsoft Excel from Python through COM (pywin32) safely - use whenever code opens, writes, refreshes or reads an Excel workbook through win32com.
---
# Excel through COM session

## Rules (the author's Standard 12, C1-C18)
1. COM only for workbooks with Power Query that the app writes into or refreshes (C1).
2. Before an openpyxl save of a workbook the app did not create: check for DataMashup (C2) - see skill SK3.
3. One private Excel per run: DispatchEx, never GetActiveObject, never the user's Excel (C3, C6).
4. Visible = False unless the step needs a window; DisplayAlerts = False until after Quit() (C4, C5).
5. Open with IgnoreReadOnlyRecommended=True; if workbook.ReadOnly: close and tell the user (C8, C9).
6. Quit() in finally; protect every clean-up step on its own; CoUninitialize() after the
   function that held Excel objects has returned (C7, C16, C17).
7. Compare COM objects with `is None`, never by truthiness.

## Template: excel_session() context manager
(code)

## Testing
- On any computer: a fake-COM object that records calls; assert the order of calls.
- On an office PC: the acceptance checklist below, one line per rule.

## Acceptance checklist
(table: rule | how to check | result)

## Never put here
Workbook names, sheet names, cell positions, success markers: they belong to the project.
```

## SECTION 12: CHANGELOG ARCHAEOLOGY (FROM GIT HISTORY)

> **About this section.** It is built from reading the full diff (the exact lines a commit added and removed) of every commit (one saved change in the project's history) of project A, `goyal-sidhant/AnnualStatement_oldv1`, up to the snapshot `bf2f1dd` (27-07-2026): 46 commits in all. The first 12 commits (`edac6a3` … `47a1492`, 31-08-2025 to 30-10-2025) are shared with project B and are labelled "shared - before the split on 30-10-2025"; their entries are written once for both audits and are inserted at the marker in 12A below. The other 34 commits belong to A alone and are labelled "A only (after the split)"; their entries follow the marker. Sub-sections 12B to 12F (file evolution, rule evolution, edge cases, abandoned approaches, dependencies) follow in a separate part.

**How to read the evidence in this part**

- Code is cited as `path:line` for the line at the snapshot `bf2f1dd` (identical to `/root/merge-scratch/A-copy`), and as `path:line@commit` for that line in an older commit's version of the file. Paths are repository-relative.
- **READ** = established by reading the code or the diff (`git -C /root/merge-scratch/combined show <hash>`; every one of the 34 own diffs was opened in full and saved under `/root/merge-scratch/run/A-S12own/diffs/`). **RAN (me)** = I executed something for this part on made-up inputs, always on extracted copies of the commit (`git archive`) under `/root/merge-scratch/run/A-S12own/trees/`, with `python -B` and `pytest -p no:cacheprovider`, a fake home folder (`/root/merge-scratch/run/A-S12own/home`) so no real settings file was read or written, and nothing written into the repositories or into `/root/merge-scratch/A-copy`. My scripts: `runtests.sh` (runs the test suite of one commit), `scripts/cmp_names.py` (name cleaning across commits), `scripts/misc_checks.py` (file-name pattern, day-first folder names, refreshed-file recognition), `scripts/dryrun_binding.py` (dry-run messages before and after `0890022`), `scripts/folders_count.py` (the "Folders Created" count before and after `275d9a4`), plus one-line checks quoted where used. Where pywin32 (the Windows-only package that lets Python drive Excel) had to be importable for a test run, I used empty stand-in modules (`/root/merge-scratch/run/A-S12own/stubs/`) and say so. **RAN (H-A1 / H-A2 / H-A3)** = run by the history reader whose working notes (`/root/merge-scratch/notes2/A_history_part1.md`, `…part2.md`, `…part3.md`) are named; I re-checked those runs against the code wherever I rely on them. Anything that needs Windows or Excel was traced by reading only.
- Inferences carry **HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW** confidence. "Not sure — here is how to check" is used where the history cannot settle a question.
- **[GST RULE]** marks code that decides a tax figure, which return, table, sheet or cell a figure or file belongs to, a state code, a period, rounding or similar. For these I only say what the code does; whether it is right is the author's call. **⚠** marks values that can change over time (return and table names, file-naming conventions, template cell positions, state lists, financial-year labels, package versions, Excel's path limit) so the author can check them.
- Feature and rule IDs (A-F…, A-R…) are those of the project registry; features are described in Section 3, rules in Section 5, gaps (A-G…) in Section 7.
- Times are the commit times git recorded, India Standard Time (+05:30). For every own commit the author date equals the committer date (RAN (me): `git log --format='%h %cd %ad' --date=iso 47a1492..A/main` shows no difference).
- **Confidentiality.** No client name, GSTIN, PAN, real file name or figure appears in this part. Example names are made up (`ClientA`, `ClientB`, `<Client A>`) or are the generic examples the code and tests themselves use (`ABC`, `XYZ`). Three things in the history are not repeated here: the office server share path named in the messages of `4f84ba9` and `7347383`, the author's own project folder path in the header of `PROJECT_AUDIT_ANNUALSTATEMENT.md`, and the company-like name used in that document's worked examples (lines 130-232).

**Words used in this part** (plain meanings of the technical terms; each is also explained the first time it matters below)

| Term | Plain meaning |
|---|---|
| commit / diff / parent | one saved change in git / the exact lines it added (+) and removed (−) / the commit just before it |
| trailer | a closing line in a commit message, here naming the AI assistant as co-author |
| regex (regular expression) / pattern | a text-matching rule, here for recognising file names; `[^-]+` means "one or more characters that are not a hyphen" |
| glob / directory listing (`os.scandir`) | a wildcard file search such as `ITC_Report_*.xlsx` / reading a folder's whole list of entries in one request |
| stat / date modified (mtime) | asking the file system for a file's size, dates and type / the time a file or folder was last changed |
| network share / UNC path / round-trip | a folder on another computer or server / a path such as `\\server\share\…` / one request to that computer and its answer (slow over a network or VPN) |
| VPN | a secure connection to the office network from outside (here the product Tailscale) |
| COM / pywin32 | Windows' way for one program to drive another (here Python drives Excel) / the Python package that provides it (`pythoncom`, `win32com`, `win32api`, `win32con`, `win32gui`) |
| `Dispatch` / `GetActiveObject` / `DispatchEx` | three ways to get an Excel through COM: may attach to an Excel already running / attaches to the user's open Excel / always starts a separate one (the one Standard 12 asks for) |
| openpyxl | a Python library that reads and writes `.xlsx` files without Excel; when it saves a workbook it drops Power Query |
| Power Query / Links sheet | Excel's data-import tool inside the ITC and Sales templates / the template sheet into which the program writes folder paths and file names that those queries read |
| staging file | a temporary local copy that is worked on and then copied to its final place |
| Tk / Tkinter / ttk / widget | Python's built-in window toolkit / its themed widgets, coloured through shared styles / one on-screen element |
| binding / `bind_all` / `unbind_all` / `add='+'` | telling Tk to call a function when an event happens / a binding for the whole application / removing every application-wide binding for that event / "add my handler next to the existing ones" instead of replacing them |
| worker thread / marshalling | a second line of work beside the window / handing a screen update from the worker to the window's own thread with `after(0, …)`, because Tk is not safe to use from two threads |
| lambda / late binding | a small one-line function / such a function reads its variables when it finally runs, not when it is made, so inside a loop it can show a later value |
| debounce / cache | waiting a short time after the last keystroke before doing slow work / remembering an answer so it is not asked again |
| tooltip | a small pop-up text shown while the pointer rests on a widget |
| panel / shell / `__getattr__` | a reusable block of screen elements that can sit inside any window / a small window whose only job is to host a panel / a Python hook that answers requests for names an object does not have (here: passes them on to the panel) |
| pytest / fixture / characterization test / mutation check | Python's testing tool / shared set-up handed to tests / a test that pins down what the code does today / deliberately breaking the code to prove a test then fails |
| `find_spec` | a Python check that a module can be found, without running it |
| pip / free-threaded build / `pythonw` | Python's package installer / a special Python 3.14 build (`python3.14t`) without the usual global lock, which some packages do not support / the Windows Python that runs with no console window |
| interpreter / `sys.executable` / `sys.argv` / `Popen` | the installed Python program that runs the code (one PC can have several) / the path of the Python program that is running right now / the words the program was started with (script name and arguments, without Python's own switches such as `-B -s`) / Python's way to start another program without waiting for it |
| guarded import / `ImportError` | loading a module inside `try … except` so that a missing module does not stop the program / the error Python raises when a module cannot be loaded |
| weak reference | a reference that does not keep a destroyed widget alive |
| style map | the part of a ttk style that says which colour to use when a widget is selected, disabled and so on |
| regression / patch / proper fix | something that worked and was broken by a later change / a fix that removes the symptom / a fix that removes the cause |
| 8.3 short path / extended path (`\\?\…`) | the old DOS-style short form of a Windows path / a Windows path prefix that lifts the usual length limit |
| DataMashup | the hidden part of a workbook (inside a `customXml` file) where Power Query keeps its queries |

### 12A. Complete Development Timeline

This sub-section lists every commit of A's single branch `main` in date order, with what the diff actually changed (files touched and lines added and removed, then the code changes in plain English), why it most likely changed (an inference, with a confidence), what it reveals about the project's rules, data flow, edge cases and design philosophy, and where the commit message disagrees with the diff. The twelve shared commits form Phases 1 to 3 and are inserted at the marker below. A's own 34 commits follow as Phases 4 to 12: two documentation commits in March 2026, then 32 commits made with an AI assistant in five days, 23-07-2026 to 27-07-2026, in short bursts that each have a clear theme (network speed, a test safety net, the new Setup screen, merging the separate Power Query Extractor into the main window, dark mode, start-up checks). For each own commit the entry ends with what is still true at the snapshot `bf2f1dd`, because later commits often revisited the same code.

> **About this part.** It covers the twelve commits that project A (goyal-sidhant/AnnualStatement_oldv1) and project B (goyal-sidhant/AnnualStatement_oldv2) have in common, from the first upload on 31-08-2025 to the split point 47a1492 on 30-10-2025. The same text appears unchanged in both audits. All twelve commits are on branch `main` in both repositories and every one is labelled "shared - before the split on 30-10-2025". Each audit continues with its own Phase 4.

**How to read the evidence in this part**

- Code is cited as `path:line@commit`, meaning "that line number in that commit's version of the file", for example `core/file_parser.py:254@edac6a3`. Files that did not change between edac6a3 and 47a1492 have the same line numbers at both. A citation without `@commit` means: inside the description of the first commit (sub-sections A to Y under edac6a3) the line at edac6a3; inside a later commit's entry the line at that commit (for bd176bf the files at bd176bf and 47a1492 are identical); in "Where the two projects started" the line at 47a1492. `:N` alone means "line N of the file named just before".
- Feature and rule IDs (A-F…, A-R…, B-F…, B-R…) are not used in this part: the same text serves both audits, and those IDs describe each project's latest snapshot, while this part describes code from before the split. Sub-sections of the first commit are referred to by their letters (A to Y).
- **READ** = I read the code or the diff (`git show <hash>`, and `git show -m --first-parent 9c56a1c` for the merge). **RAN** = I executed the code on made-up data, always on my own extracted copies under `/root/merge-scratch/run/SHARED-12A/` (Linux, Python 3.14, Tk under a virtual display, run with `python -B` so nothing is written into the copies). Anything that needs Excel or Windows was traced by reading only. Inferences carry **HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW** confidence.
- **[GST RULE]** marks code that decides a tax figure, which return, sheet or cell a figure belongs to, a state code, a period, rounding or display of figures. For these I only say what the code does; whether it is right is the author's call. **⚠** marks values that can change over time (state lists, return table numbers, template sheet names and cell positions) so the author can check them.
- Times are the commit times git recorded, in India Standard Time (+05:30). Times taken from compiled-file headers are in UTC and are labelled "UTC".
- No client name, GSTIN, PAN, real file name, folder path from the author's computer or figure appears in this part. Names such as `<Client A>`, "Alpha Traders" or "Beta Stores" are made up for the test runs.

**Words used in this part** (plain meanings of the technical terms used below)

| Term | Plain meaning |
|---|---|
| commit | one saved change in the git history |
| diff | the exact lines a commit added and removed |
| merge commit | a commit that joins two lines of work into one |
| split point | 47a1492, the last commit both projects share |
| regex (regular expression) | a text pattern used to recognise file names, for example "starts with `GSTR3B-`" |
| GUI | the program's windows, buttons and lists |
| Tkinter (Tk) | the window toolkit that comes with Python; every shared commit uses it |
| thread / worker thread | a second line of work running at the same time, so the window stays responsive; Tk windows should only be changed from the main thread |
| callback | a small piece of code handed to another part of the program to be run later |
| lambda / late binding | a lambda is a tiny inline function; "late binding" means it reads its variables when it finally runs, not when it was created, so inside a loop it can show the last value for every line |
| COM / pywin32 | COM is the Windows mechanism that lets a program drive Microsoft Excel; pywin32 is the Python package that provides it (`win32com`, `pythoncom`, `win32gui` ...) |
| openpyxl | a Python package that reads and writes .xlsx files without Excel |
| Power Query | Excel's built-in data-import engine; the ITC and Sales templates use it to pull data from the organised files |
| SendKeys | simulating key presses into whatever window is in front |
| cache file / JSON | a small settings file that remembers last-used folders; JSON is the text format it is written in |
| glob | a wildcard file search such as `ITC_Report_*.xlsx` |
| modification time (mtime) | a file's "last changed" date and time |
| `.pyc` / `__pycache__` | compiled copies of Python files that Python writes automatically into `__pycache__` folders |
| CRLF | Windows line endings (two characters per line end); git shows LF (one character) |
| Treeview | the table-like client list on the Validation screen |
| dead code | code that is never called |
| UTF-8 | the standard way of storing text that can hold any character, including emoji |
| 8.3 short path | the old Windows short form of a path (each folder or file name shortened to 8 characters plus a 3-character extension, such as `PROGRA~1`), used to get around path-length limits |
| NTFS | the file system Windows uses on its disks; it lists the names in a folder in sorted order |
| IST / UTC | India Standard Time / Coordinated Universal Time (IST = UTC + 5 h 30 min) |
| `.xltx` | an Excel template file; double-clicking it in Windows starts a new, unsaved workbook based on it |

**The original program in detail - where both projects started**

**A. Two separate programs**

- **The organiser** is started with `python main.py`. In order (READ):
  1. `main.py:18@edac6a3` replaces the console output (`sys.stdout`) with a UTF-8 version of it, so emoji in messages can be printed.
  2. `main.py:21-28` sends all log messages of level INFO and above both to a file `gst_organizer.log` and to the console. The file name has no folder, so the file is created in whatever folder the program is started from, and it is appended to on every start.
  3. `setup_environment()` (`main.py:30-44`) puts the program folder on Python's search path, creates the folders `core`, `utils`, `gui`, `logs` and `temp` inside the program folder if missing, and writes a one-line `__init__.py` into `core`, `utils` and `gui` if missing. `logs` and `temp` are never used afterwards.
  4. `main()` (`main.py:46-80`) imports the main window, prints a banner and runs the window. On a missing module it prints the list of expected files - which still includes **`gui/app.py`** (`main.py:72`), a file that is not in the commit (see Y) - and waits for Enter (`main.py:73`). On any other error it logs the details, prints them and waits for Enter.
  5. The first line `# !/usr/bin/env python3` (`main.py:1`) has a space after `#`, so it was never a working "shebang" (the line that tells Linux/macOS which interpreter to use) (READ, HIGH).
  6. The header says "Author: Advanced AI Assistant" and "Version: 3.0 (Production Ready)" (`main.py:6-7`).
  - RAN (`test_window.py`, `t_edac6a3`): the main window builds with title "GST File Organizer v3.0" and the tabs "📁 Step 1: Setup", "✅ Step 2: Validation", "🚀 Step 3: Processing".
  - Console dependence (READ, HIGH): the program prints banners and waits for Enter on errors (`main.py:54-56,63-79`), and step 1 assumes a console exists. Started without a console (for example with `pythonw.exe` on Windows, where `sys.stdout` is empty), line 18 fails with an AttributeError before anything is logged. RAN (re-check 21-10-2026, `main.py` of edac6a3 and of 47a1492 started with its output stream closed, from an empty scratch folder): both stop at once with `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'buffer'`, exit code 1, and no `gst_organizer.log` is created. Under `pythonw.exe` the error output is missing too, so the user would see nothing at all - the program simply does not open (READ of Python's documented behaviour, MEDIUM; not run on Windows) (added in re-check 21-10-2026).
- **The Power Query Extractor** is a second, separate program started with `python launch_extractor.py` "after GST Organizer processing" (`launch_extractor.py:2-3`). The launcher puts its own folder on the search path (`:10`), imports and runs `PowerQueryExtractor` (`:14-18`), and on any error shows a Tk error box and re-raises it (`:20-27`). Importing `power_query_extractor/extractor_main.py` sets up its own log file `pq_extractor.log` (again relative to the start folder) plus console output (`extractor_main.py:12-19`), but only if no logging was set up before. The extractor's window class is `PowerQueryExtractorApp` (`power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:18`), title "Power Query Extractor", 1000×700 (`:43-45`).
  - The extractor is **Windows-only with pywin32 installed**: `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:11-15` imports `pythoncom`, `win32com.client`, `win32api`, `win32con` and `win32gui` at the top with no fallback, so without them the program cannot even start. RAN: importing `power_query_extractor.extractor_main` from my copy stops with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pythoncom'`. The organiser, by contrast, imports pywin32 only on Windows and falls back to openpyxl (`core/excel_handler.py:19-33`). The two programs handle the same missing package in opposite ways (READ, HIGH).
- The two programs never call each other. They communicate only through the folders and file names the organiser creates (HIGH, READ of both).

- Almost every action button (Browse, Scan, Re-scan, Dry Run, Export, Start, Stop, Select All, Clear All, Complete Only) is wired with a mouse-click binding `bind('<Button-1>', ...)` instead of Tk's normal `command=` option (for example `setup_tab.py:115,161,199,306,318`, `validation_tab.py:118,130,142,190`, `processing_tab.py:74,87`). Comments call this "working mouse events" and "proper event binding" (`setup_tab.py:20,103`), which hints that `command=` had given trouble in an earlier version (LOW). Consequence: a button that is "disabled" still reacts to a click (RAN, `test_misc.py`: a disabled Tk button with such a binding still ran its handler), and pressing Space on a focused button does nothing, because there is no `command` to run (READ, MEDIUM). The extractor, written separately, uses `command=` throughout (`extractor_window.py:133,143,168,178,223`) - an inconsistency between the two programs (READ, HIGH).

**C. What SCAN FILES does** (READ; `gui/handlers/file_handler.py:57-95` → `core/file_parser.py:128-179`)

1. Checks that a source folder is entered and exists (`file_handler.py:120-130`).
2. `find_excel_files()` (`utils/helpers.py:249-266`) lists only the top level of the folder (no sub-folders) with the wildcards `*.xlsx`, `*.xls`, `*.xlsm`, and **silently drops** every file that fails `validate_excel_file()` (`helpers.py:210-247`): smaller than 1,024 bytes, or extension not one of .xlsx/.xls/.xlsm/.xltx/.xltm, or first bytes not the ZIP signature `PK\x03\x04` or the old-Excel signature `\xd0\xcf\x11\xe0`. Such files appear nowhere - not in the client list and not in "variations" (the "Invalid or corrupted Excel file" branch at `file_parser.py:188-195` can only be reached if a file changes between the two checks) (READ, HIGH; RAN in re-check 21-10-2026 with `v_scan.py`: a 104-byte file and a file with a wrong signature, both named like Sales files, appear neither among the clients nor among the variations). The list is sorted by name (`helpers.py:262`).
3. Each file name is tried against six patterns in a fixed order (D below). A match that yields a client and a state goes into the client data under the key `<client as written>-<state code>` (`file_parser.py:228-252`); everything else becomes a "variation" with a suggested pattern (`file_parser.py:212-222,290-308`).
4. Completeness is computed per client (E below), the summary text (`gui/main_window.py:267-301`) and the client list are refreshed, and the window switches to the Validation screen (`file_handler.py:78-88`).
- The scan runs in the main thread, so the window does not respond while a large folder is scanned; the per-file status messages it sets are not repainted until the scan ends (READ, MEDIUM).

**D. File-name patterns the scanner recognises** - `utils/constants.py:13-62@edac6a3`, unchanged up to the split point. [GST RULE] ⚠ (they decide which return or report each file is treated as)

All patterns ignore upper/lower case, must match the whole name, and accept only `.xls` or `.xlsx` (`\.xlsx?$`), so an `.xlsm` file is found by the scan but always ends up as a variation. `[^-]+` means "one or more characters that are not a hyphen", so **a client name or a state name containing a hyphen is never read correctly** (READ, HIGH). [Corrected during re-check 21-10-2026 - originally stated "can never be read"; a RAN scan (`v_scan.py`, edac6a3 parser, made-up files) showed two different outcomes:]
- In the three patterns that end in `(.+)` (GSTR-2B Reco, Sales Reco, Annual Report) the name is **silently mis-read**: for a client "Alpha-Beta Traders" in Maharashtra the parser takes client "Alpha", state "Beta Traders" (state code by the fallback "BT") and puts the rest into the period, so these files form a separate, wrongly named client "Alpha-BT" with no warning shown.
- In the other three patterns (GSTR-3B, IMS Reco, Sales) the name matches nothing and the file becomes a variation ("No matching pattern found").

| Order | Key | Pattern (quoted exactly) | Treated as | Copied to | Parts captured |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `GSTR-2B-Reco` | `^GSTR-2B-Reco-([^-]+)-([^-]+)-(.+)\.xlsx?$` | "GSTR-2B Reco", category ITC | ITC folder | client, state, period (the period may contain hyphens) |
| 2 | `ImsReco` | `^ImsReco-([^-]+)-([^-]+)-(\d{8})\.xlsx?$` | "IMS Reco", category ITC | ITC folder | client, state, date (exactly 8 digits; described as DDMMYYYY) |
| 3 | `GSTR3B` | `^(?:\(\d+\)\s*)?GSTR3B-([^-]+)-([^-]+)-([^-]+)\.xlsx?$` | "GSTR-3B Export", category GSTR3B | GSTR-3B folder | client, state, month; an optional prefix such as `(2) ` (probably a duplicate-download number) is allowed only here |
| 4 | `Sales` | `^Sales-([^-]+)-([^-]+)-([^-]+)-([^-]+)\.xlsx?$` | "Sales", category Sales | Sales folder | client, state, start month, end month |
| 5 | `SalesReco` | `^SalesReco-([^-]+)-([^-]+)-(.+)\.xlsx?$` | "Sales Reco", category Sales | Sales folder | client, state, period |
| 6 | `AnnualReport` | `^AnnualReport-([^-]+)-([^-]+)-(.+)\.xlsx?$` | "Annual Report", category Annual | the Version folder itself | client, state, year |

- [GST RULE] The period, date, month and year parts are stored (`file_parser.py:97-98`) and **never used anywhere** (READ, HIGH: no reader in any file). The code does not check a tax period or financial year at all; apart from the IMS date being 8 digits, these parts are free text.
- Client and state parts are checked by `validate_client_name()` (`helpers.py:321-342`: 2-100 characters, none of `< > : " / \ | ? *`); problems are stored as "warnings" (`file_parser.py:100-111`) that are **never shown** (READ, HIGH).
- Suggestions for unrecognised names (`file_parser.py:290-308`) are chosen by keywords in this order: "gstr" and "2b" → GSTR-2B pattern; "ims" → IMS; "gstr" and "3b" → GSTR-3B; "sales" and "reco" → Sales Reco; "sales" → Sales; "annual" → Annual Report; otherwise "Check file naming convention".

**E. When a client counts as "Complete"** - `core/file_parser.py:254-288@edac6a3`, list `utils/constants.py:68-75`. [GST RULE] ⚠ (it decides which returns and files a client must have)

- Six file types are expected: GSTR-2B Reco, IMS Reco, GSTR-3B Export, Sales, Sales Reco, Annual Report.
- "Missing" = expected types with no file. "Extra" = any type other than GSTR-3B Export with two or more files ("GSTR-3B can have multiple files (monthly filings - unlimited)", `:268-270`).
- Status: "Complete" ✅ when nothing is missing and nothing is extra; "Missing N files" ⚠️ when anything is missing; otherwise "Has duplicates" ⚠️. Completeness % = types found ÷ 6 × 100, rounded to one decimal (`:276-277`).
- A never-called method `validate_results()` (`:340-373`) would have flagged "Annual Report" and "GSTR-3B Export" as "critical" files - an unfinished idea.

**F. Client identity and state codes** (READ; RAN where marked)

- [GST RULE] ⚠ **State name → state code** (`utils/helpers.py:485-511`, list `utils/constants.py:234-275`): the state part of the file name is trimmed, lower-cased and looked up in a fixed list of 39 entries that map full state and union-territory names to two-letter **alphabetic** abbreviations (for example 'maharashtra' → MH, 'telangana' → TS, 'odisha' and 'orissa' → OD, 'uttarakhand' → UK, 'chhattisgarh' → CG, 'dadra and nagar haveli and daman and diu' → DD, 'delhi' and 'national capital territory of delhi' → DL, 'ladakh' → LA, 'puducherry' and 'pondicherry' → PY). If the name is not in the list, the code logs a warning and builds a fallback: with two or more words, the first letters of the first two words; with one word, the first three characters in capitals. The code never uses numeric state codes, and it does not read, build or check a GSTIN or PAN anywhere (READ, HIGH).
  - RAN (`test_tree_values.py`, the helper is identical at edac6a3 and 47a1492 apart from its import line): 'Maharashtra' → MH; ' tamil nadu ' → TN; 'MH' → MH (through the fallback, with a warning); 'NCT of Delhi' → NO; 'Jammu & Kashmir' → J&; 'Gujrat' (misspelt) → GUJ; '' → ''. So a misspelt state name produces a different client key and a different folder from the correctly spelt one.
- **Client key** = `<client exactly as written>-<state code>` (`core/file_parser.py:231-232`). It is case-sensitive: "Alpha" and "alpha" are two clients, and so are "X Private Limited" and "X Pvt Ltd" - although both later get the same output folder name (G below), so the second one's reports can overwrite the first one's (READ, MEDIUM).
- **Client-state folder name** `create_client_state_key()` (`helpers.py:513-537`): whole words "Private" → "Pvt" and "Limited" → "Ltd" (any case), then `<client>-<state code>`; if longer than the maximum (default 35, `core/file_organizer.py:42`; setting `gui/main_window.py:89`), the client part is cut to fit; if that would leave 5 characters or fewer the whole key is cut, which can cut off the state code. RAN: "Alpha Beta" with maximum 8 → "Alpha Be"; a long name can end with a space before the hyphen.
- **File-name cleaning** `sanitize_filename()` (`helpers.py:66-112`): replaces the text "Private" → "Pvt" and "Limited" → "Ltd" anywhere and case-sensitively (RAN: "Privately Limitedness" → "Pvtly_Ltdness"), replaces control characters and `` <>:"/\|?*[]{}+=!@#$%^,;'"`~ `` (`:82`) with `_`, turns runs of spaces/underscores into one `_`, trims `_`, `.` and spaces at the ends, uses "unnamed" if nothing is left, and cuts the name to `200 - len(extension) - 10` characters (RAN: a 300-character name → 190 characters; with an `.xlsx` extension → 185 + `.xlsx` = 190). Hyphens are kept on purpose (comment `:81`).

**G. Output folders and names** (READ; `core/file_organizer.py`, `gui/handlers/processing_handler.py`, `power_query_extractor/...`)

```
<Target folder>/
  Annual Statement-<DDMMYY HHMM>/                  Fresh Run: new each run. Re-Run/Resume: the newest existing one by modification time
    GST_Processing_Summary_<DDMMYY_HHMM>.xlsx      summary workbook (K below)
    PQ_Extraction_Report_<YYYYMMDD_HHMM>.xlsx      written later by the extractor (Q below)
    <client-state key>/                            for example "Alpha Traders-MH" (spaces kept)
      Version-<DDMMYY HHMM>/                       always a new time stamp per run
        GSTR-3B Exports[ (<cleaned client>)]/
        Other ITC related files[ (<cleaned client>)]/
        Sales related files[ (<cleaned client>)]/
        <Annual Report file, cleaned name>
        ITC_Report_<cleaned client>_<state code>_<DDMMYY_HHMM>.xlsx
        Sales_Report_<cleaned client>_<state code>_<DDMMYY_HHMM>.xlsx
        ITC_Report_..._Refreshed_<DDMMYY_HHMM>.xlsx  written later by the extractor
        _Organization_Report_<client as written>_<state as written>.txt
```

- Time stamps: `get_timestamp()` = day, month, two-digit year, space, hours, minutes (`helpers.py:23-25`); report names replace the space with `_` (`processing_handler.py:215,383`). With minute precision, two runs in the same minute share the same folders.
- The bracketed client name in the three category folders ("Level 4" in the screen text) is added when the global checkbox is on, or when the per-client "📁 Name" setting for key `<client>-<state code>` is on (`file_organizer.py:113-135`). The bracket uses the cleaned client (spaces → `_`), the client-state folder keeps spaces.
- Which file goes where (`file_organizer.py:285-298`): GSTR-3B Export → GSTR-3B folder; GSTR-2B Reco and IMS Reco → ITC folder; Sales and Sales Reco → Sales folder; Annual Report → the Version folder itself.

**H. Copying the files and the three processing modes** (READ)

- Processing (`processing_handler.py:54-447@edac6a3`) runs in a background thread. Per selected client: create the folders → copy the files under cleaned names → ITC report → Sales report → per-client text report; after all clients the summary workbook; then an information box and the output folder is opened (`os.startfile` on Windows, `open` on macOS, `xdg-open` on Linux, `:425-437`). STOP is checked only between clients (`:149-151`).
- Each file is copied with `shutil.copy2` and the copy's size compared with the original; a size difference deletes the copy (`helpers.py:142-185`). After a successful copy the in-memory record gets the cleaned name, so the template is given the copied name (`file_organizer.py:216-229`).
- If the destination already exists (`file_organizer.py:259-270`): **Fresh Run** first makes a backup `<name>_backup_<DDMMYY_HHMM><ext>` (`helpers.py:187-204`); **Resume** skips the file; **Re-Run** overwrites it silently.
- Because the Version folder always gets the current time stamp (`file_organizer.py:43,98-104`), a destination can only already exist within the same minute or when two different source files clean to the same name. In practice **Resume behaves like Re-Run** (READ, HIGH). When two source files clean to the same name (for example names that differ only in "Private" versus "Pvt" or in a space versus an underscore), Re-Run keeps only the last one copied (READ, MEDIUM).
- Optional warning before processing: if "include client name" is on and any selected client name has **more than 10 characters**, a list of up to five names is shown with "Continue anyway?" (`processing_handler.py:64-75@edac6a3`); the per-client "📁 Name" toggle has its own >10 warning (`client_handler.py:193-202@edac6a3`).
- A client counts as "Success" whenever no exception was raised, even if both its reports failed (`processing_handler.py:337-350`) (READ, HIGH).

**I. Writing paths into the templates - the "Links" sheet** - `utils/constants.py:96-120@edac6a3`, values from `core/excel_handler.py:551-661`. [GST RULE] ⚠ (it decides which file feeds which input of the ITC and Sales reports; the cell positions depend on the templates)

| Report | Cell | What is written |
|---|---|---|
| ITC | B2 | path of the GSTR-3B folder (the whole folder, so all monthly GSTR-3B files are available) |
| ITC | B4 / B5 | path of the Version folder / Annual Report file name without extension |
| ITC | B7 / B8 | path of the ITC folder / GSTR-2B Reco file name without extension |
| ITC | B10 / B11 | path of the ITC folder / IMS Reco file name without extension |
| Sales | B2 / B3 | path of the Sales folder / Sales file name without extension |
| Sales | B5 / B6 | path of the Version folder / Annual Report file name without extension |
| Sales | B8 / B9 | path of the Sales folder / Sales Reco file name without extension |

- Paths are written with backslashes (`helpers.py:311-315`); file names lose their extension (`helpers.py:446-448`), so the template must add it itself (MEDIUM). Only the **first** file of each type is used (`annual_files[0]` and so on, `excel_handler.py:577,588,599,615,631,647`) - the alphabetically first name, because the scan sorts. Further files of the same type are copied but not linked.
- Empty values are not written (`if value:`, `excel_handler.py:173,260`), so when a file type is missing the template's existing cell content stays as it was (READ, HIGH; whether the template then shows stale data depends on the template - MEDIUM).
- Through Excel the sheet is found by the exact name "Links" (any case), else any sheet with "link" in its name, else a new sheet "Links" is added (`excel_handler.py:146-164`). The openpyxl route accepts only the exact name "Links" (any case, `:249-253`) and writes nothing when there is no such sheet (`:255`) [Corrected during re-check 21-10-2026 - originally the "link"-in-the-name fallback read as if it applied to both routes; it exists only in the Excel route]. The organiser never reads any figure from any workbook (READ, HIGH).
- Report file names: `ITC_Report_<cleaned client>_<state code>_<DDMMYY_HHMM>.xlsx` and `Sales_Report_...` in the Version folder (`processing_handler.py:212-219,276-277@edac6a3`). The template is copied to that name whether it is an .xlsx or an .xltx template (`excel_handler.py:135,239`). Whether Excel opens an .xltx template copied under an .xlsx name without complaint was not testable here - not sure; how to check: run one client with an .xltx template on Windows and open the produced report.

**J. Excel through COM in the organiser** (`core/excel_handler.py:103-228@edac6a3`; READ only - cannot run here)

- `pythoncom.CoInitialize()` (start COM for this thread); then **`GetActiveObject("Excel.Application")` first** - this attaches to the user's own Excel if one is open - and only otherwise `Dispatch(...)` (`:121-126`). It sets `Visible=False`, `DisplayAlerts=False`, `ScreenUpdating=False` on that Excel (`:129-131`), so a user's own open Excel would be hidden.
- It copies the template to the output name, waits 0.5 s (`:133-136`), opens the copy (`_safe_open_workbook`, `:275-317`: reuses an already open workbook with the same path; on error -2147352567, an error mentioning "path", or a path longer than 218 characters, retries with the Windows 8.3 short path), writes the Links cells, saves, closes, checks the file exists.
- In the clean-up (`:206-228`) it sets `ScreenUpdating=True` and `DisplayAlerts=True` and calls `excel.Quit()` if `self.excel_app is None`. `self.excel_app` is set to None in `__init__` (`:55`) and never assigned anywhere, so **Quit is always called - also on a user's Excel attached through GetActiveObject**, although the comment says "Don't quit if Excel was already open" (`:217`) (READ, HIGH that Quit is always called). What Excel then does with the user's unsaved workbooks while hidden and with alerts switched back on is not sure (MEDIUM); how to check: on Windows, open Excel with an unsaved workbook, run one client, and watch whether that Excel closes or asks to save. The run log (X below) records only newly started Excel instances, never an attached one, so in the logged runs no open Excel was attached.
- Without pywin32 or off Windows, `_create_report_openpyxl` (`:230-273`) copies the template and saves it through openpyxl with `keep_links=True`, after logging "Power Query content may be lost!" (`:235`). The file header explains why the Excel route exists: "WINDOWS VERSION - Uses Excel COM to preserve Power Query and all Excel features" (`:2-3`).
- `warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')` (`:17`) silences every Python warning in the whole program, not only Excel ones (READ, HIGH).
- `ExcelHandler()` creates `<system temp>/gst_excel_temp` at every start (`:52-53`) and never uses it.

**K. Summary workbook, per-client text report, exported client list** (READ)

- Summary workbook `GST_Processing_Summary_<DDMMYY_HHMM>.xlsx` in the Annual Statement folder, always written with openpyxl (`excel_handler.py:319-357`; name `processing_handler.py:383-385`): sheets "Summary" (date, totals, reports created, errors, mode, target folder, include-name Yes/No, `:380-410`), "Client Status" (Client, State, Status, Files, Missing count, Complete %, `:412-439`), "File Mapping" (original file, client key, type, destination, status, `:441-467`), "Errors" (`:469-500`), "Variations" (file name, issue, expected pattern, size, "Rename file", `:502-533`).
- Per-client text report `_Organization_Report_<client>_<state>.txt` in the Version folder (`file_organizer.py:300-362`), using the client and state exactly as written in the file names. Its "Successfully Copied" and "Folders Created" figures count **everything done so far in the whole run**, not just this client, because one FileOrganizer object is used for all clients (`processing_handler.py:110-116`, `file_organizer.py:346-351`) (READ, HIGH).
- EXPORT LIST (`client_handler.py:227-259`) writes the selected clients as "client - state" into a .txt file the user chooses (default name `selected_clients_<YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS>.txt`), with the system's default text encoding (`:243`), then opens it with `os.startfile` (`:257`), which exists only on Windows; elsewhere the file is written, the "Export Complete" box (`:253-254`) appears, and then "Failed to export" is shown as well (READ).

This file did not change in the shared range, so the defect is present at the split point.

Because the typing check runs on every key press and rejects any single digit (1-9 is below 10) but allows an empty box, a user who clears the box cannot type a new number into it key by key; only the arrows, pasting a whole number, or editing inside the existing digits work (READ, HIGH; RAN in re-check 21-10-2026 with `v_spin.py` on the real Setup screen at 47a1492: after clearing the box, the key presses "2" and "5" leave it empty, while inserting "25" in one step is accepted); in addition the arrow handler resets 0 or less to 35 (`:262-267`) and the cache loader does the same (`main_window.py:353-354`) (READ, HIGH) [Corrected during re-check 21-10-2026 - originally "three different limits"; the three places hold two different ranges].

**M. The Power Query Extractor - screens and flow** (READ; `power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py@edac6a3`)

- Heading "🔄 Power Query Report Extractor" and two tabs. **Setup**: Target Folder (entry, 📁 Browse, 🔍 Scan); "Select Clients" with ✓ Select All, ✗ Deselect All and a checkbox "Skip Refresh (Use existing refreshed files)"; a scrollable list with one checkbox per client (all ticked) and "ITC ✓" / "Sales ✓" labels where a report exists; "🚀 Start Processing" (`:95-232,408-468`). **Processing**: progress bar and a log (`:245-313`).
- At start it tries to load the target folder from a cache (S below), then scans.
- **Finding the processed clients** (`:353-406`): in the target folder, the newest `Annual Statement-*` folder by modification time; inside it every sub-folder whose name does not start with `_`; inside each, the `Version-*` folder with the **largest name** (`:385`). Names are `Version-DDMMYY HHMM`, so day-first text order is not date order - RAN (`test_misc.py`): of "Version-310825 2211", "Version-151025 0900" and "Version-291025 2146" the code picks the 31-08-2025 one. The client name shown and used in the consolidated workbook is the client-state folder name.
- **Per client, per report type** (`core/report_processor.py:37-141`): take the first file matching `<ITC|Sales>_Report_*.xlsx` in that Version folder (`:54-67`; the wildcard also matches the extractor's own refreshed copies, and the order of the list depends on the operating system - on Windows NTFS the original usually comes first because "." sorts before "_" - LOW-MEDIUM); copy it to `<name>_Refreshed_<DDMMYY_HHMM>.xlsx` (`:69-71,96-98`); refresh the copy in Excel (N); wait 3 s (`:117-119`); read the configured cells from the copy in a second, hidden Excel (`:462-571`). "Extract data regardless of refresh status" (`:121-122`).
- **Skip Refresh** already exists here: the checkbox writes into the shared `EXTRACTION_OPTIONS` dictionary at run time (`extractor_window.py:234-243`); the processor then uses the newest `<name>_Refreshed_*.xlsx` by modification time, or refreshes if there is none (`report_processor.py:73-93`). It does not check whether that earlier refresh had passed validation (READ, HIGH).
- After all clients, the consolidated workbook is written (Q) and the user is asked whether to open it (`os.startfile`, `extractor_window.py:570-573`). The worker thread writes to the log, the progress bar and message boxes directly (`:516-601`), although Tk widgets should only be changed from the main thread (READ, HIGH).

**N. Refreshing Power Query by key presses** (`report_processor.py:143-350@edac6a3`; READ only)

- `print(f"PROCESSING: ...")` sits before the docstring (`:144-146`, "TEST: Add this line to check if logging works"), so the description is not a docstring and the line writes to the console.
- `Dispatch("Excel.Application")` (`:154`; this may return an Excel that is already running - MEDIUM), then up to five tries, 2 s apart, to set **`Visible=True`**, `DisplayAlerts=False` and `WindowState=-4137` (maximised) ("Keep it visible to avoid issues", `:156-170`); open the workbook with three tries on "Call was rejected by callee" (`:174-185`); wait 5 × 1 s ("Increased from 3 to 5", `:187-191`); bring the window to the front with `WScript.Shell.AppActivate` (three tries, `:193-212`); then **send the keys Alt+A, R, A** one second apart ("Increased from 0.5", `:214-229`) - Excel's ribbon shortcut for Data → Refresh All.
- Wait 10 × 1 s - the comment says "WAIT 7 SECONDS AS REQUESTED" (`:233-238`), so comment and code disagree. Check five times, one second apart, for an error dialog (`_find_error_window`, `:352-388`: any visible, enabled top-level window whose title contains 'microsoft excel', 'error', 'problem', 'cannot', 'failed', 'unable', 'could not', 'exception', 'invalid' or 'missing', and whose window class is `#32770`, `NUIDialog` or `bosa_sdm_msword`); read its text (`:390-425`) and press a button labelled ok/close/yes/continue, otherwise send it a close message (`:427-460`). Wait 10 s more "for complex queries" (`:260-265`), check once more, validate (O), save, close.
- There is no `RefreshAll()` call, no wait for asynchronous queries to finish and no check of whether a query is still refreshing; the refresh is assumed finished after the fixed waits (READ, HIGH). Because the keys go to whatever window is in front, the user must not use the computer while a refresh is running, and the program needs an interactive, logged-in desktop. Each report spends roughly 40 seconds in fixed waits alone (adding up the waits in the code; MEDIUM).
- The refreshed copy is saved even when validation fails (`:279-296`), and a later Skip Refresh run can reuse it (M above) (READ, HIGH).
- Clean-up closes without saving, quits Excel and stops COM (`:329-350`). A final `return {'success': True ...}` (`:318-321`) can never run, and the `except` in `_process_report` that looks for "Open method of Workbooks class failed" (`:101-115`) can never trigger, because `_refresh_power_query_simple` catches every error itself (READ, HIGH). Comments such as "ADD THE NEW CODE HERE (notice the indentation - 3 levels)" (`:73`) and "Rest of your code remains same..." (`:231`) are left-overs of code pasted from chat answers.
- Opening (`_safe_open_workbook`, `:622-731`): an already open workbook with the same full path is reused (`:641-644`); paths over 218 characters are converted to the Windows long-path form (`:652-664`); after the first `Open` fails there are at most three further attempts: (2) close any open workbook with the same name, wait 3 s and retry (`:675-685`); (3) the 8.3 short path (`:692-700`); (4) **either** - if the long-path prefix was added - the path without it (`:702-706`), **or** - otherwise - `Open(..., UpdateLinks=0, ReadOnly=False, IgnoreReadOnlyRecommended=True, Notify=False)` (`:708-715`); when the last attempt fails and the error contains -2147352567, advice is written to the log (file open elsewhere, damaged, path too long, OneDrive/SharePoint sync, `:719-729`) (READ) [Corrected during re-check 21-10-2026 - originally "up to four further attempts" listing the last two as separate steps; they are alternatives, so a long path never gets the `UpdateLinks=0` call].

**O. When a refresh counts as successful** - `report_processor.py:573-620@edac6a3`. [GST RULE] ⚠ (a rule about the template; the sheet and cell depend on the template)

- A sheet named "Info" (any case) must exist and its cell **BB2** must be not empty, not blank, not "0" or "0.0", and not one of `#REF! #VALUE! #NAME? #NULL! #DIV/0! #N/A #NUM! #ERROR!`. The success message calls BB2 "Client Name" (`:616`).

| Output sheet | Report | Template sheet!cell → output column | Lines |
|---|---|---|---|
| GSTR-3B Difference | ITC | `Diff GSTR-3B`!J15 → "Diff IGST"; !K15 → "Diff CGST"; !L15 → "Diff SGST" | `:35-58` |
| GSTR-1 Difference | Sales | `Diff - GSTR-1`!N1 → "Diff Taxable Value"; !O1 → "Diff IGST"; !P1 → "Diff CGST"; !Q1 → "Diff SGST" | `:61-89` |
| Turnover GSTR-1 | Sales | `Diff - GSTR-1`!I1 → "Taxable Value" | `:92-102` |

- The file is written to be edited by hand ("MASTER VERSION ... HOW TO EDIT THIS FILE", `:1-27`); every entry can also name a calculation (subtract, add, multiply, divide; divide by zero gives the text "Div/0", non-numbers "Error", `data_consolidator.py:188-218`). No entry uses one.
- `EXTRACTION_OPTIONS` (`:122-127`): skip_refresh False (changed by the checkbox), auto_refresh_if_missing True (never read), show_timestamp False (never read), missing_data_text "Missing".

If two output sheets ever named the same template sheet and cell, the later one would silently replace the earlier one (READ, HIGH; no such pair exists in the shared range).

Bare references from different template sheets of the same report would overwrite each other (READ, MEDIUM; no calculation uses them here).
