#### 12F.10 Limits of the evidence in 12B–12F

- Everything that needs Windows, Excel or pywin32 (COM sessions, key presses, pip installing pywin32, the restart making it importable, `pythonw` beyond the simulated missing console) was traced by reading only; where another reader simulated it, that is marked RAN (H-A3).
- Claims in commit messages that rest on measurements outside the repository — "11 min -> 41s", "3030 files", "220 widgets … no drift", "byte-identical characterization snapshot", "mutation-checked" — could not be verified here and are reported as the messages' claims.
- `gst_organizer.log` was not opened (described by kind only, from H-S's counts of message shapes); the compiled `.pyc` files were analysed only through their header fields and identifier strings by other readers, never decompiled.
- Blame and pickaxe identify the commits that touched a line or a text; that a change was "substantive" or "cosmetic" was decided by reading each diff.

## APPENDIX X1: EXCEL AND POWER QUERY SAFETY (STANDARD 12)

This appendix is a merge-specific addition the author asked for. It covers project A only (`goyal-sidhant/AnnualStatement_oldv1`, branch `main`, snapshot `bf2f1dd`, 27-07-2026), including the 12 commits it shares with project B. It answers four questions, in this order: (a) where does A open, create, save, refresh, read, close or quit a workbook; (b) how does each Excel session measure up against the author's Standard 12 "Excel through COM" (`/home/user/Annual_Statement_2.0/.build-docs/toolkit/rebuild_pipeline_FINAL.md:844-877`); (c) where can openpyxl strip Power Query, is there any DataMashup check, and what happens without pywin32; (d) what actually happens, call by call, in realistic runs.

### X1.0 How to read this appendix

**Evidence labels.**

- **READ** = established by reading the code at `bf2f1dd` (repository-relative `file:line`; an old version is written `path:line@commit`).
- **RAN** = executed on this Linux computer on invented data, in my scratch copy `/root/merge-scratch/run/A-X12/A` (never in the repository and never in `/root/merge-scratch/A-copy`, whose checksums were taken before and compared after the runs: unchanged). Runs used `python -B`, `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1`, and `HOME` / `TMPDIR` pointed into the scratch folder.
- **RAN (fake COM)** = this computer has no Excel and no pywin32, so I drove A's real Excel functions with *recording fakes* (small stand-in objects that only write down which call A makes, in which order, and can be told to fail where a real Excel could). These runs prove the **order of A's own calls and which clean-up steps run**; they prove **nothing about what a real Excel does** with those calls. Every statement about real Excel behaviour is marked READ with a confidence level.
- **HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW** = my confidence in an inference.
- **[GST RULE]** = the code decides a figure, a return/table/sheet/cell, a period, a state code or similar. I only say what the code does; whether it is right is the author's call. **⚠** marks values that can change over time (cell positions, sheet names, table numbers, Excel key tips, package versions, limits).

**Scripts and outputs** (all under `/root/merge-scratch/run/A-X12/`): `scripts/common.py` (builds invented workbooks; injects a Power-Query-like `customXml/item1.xml` DataMashup part and an `xl/connections.xml` connection; checks for DataMashup the way Standard 12 describes), `scripts/fakecom.py` (the recording fakes), `scripts/r1_step3_openpyxl.py` → `out/r1_output.txt`, `scripts/r2_step3_com_fake.py` → `out/r2_output.txt`, `scripts/r3_step4_com_fake.py` → `out/r3_output.txt`, `scripts/r4_no_pywin32.py` → `out/r4_output.txt`, `scripts/r5_settings_logs.py` → `out/r5_output.txt`, `scripts/r6_step4_scan.py` → `out/r6_output.txt`, `scripts/r7_patterns.py` → `out/r7_output.txt`. All client names are invented (`ClientA`, `ClientB` ...); in prose I write `<Client A>` etc.

**Verification re-run (21-10-2026).** An independent checker copied these scripts (paths changed only) and re-ran R1 to R7 against a fresh scratch copy of A in `/root/merge-scratch/run/VERIFY-A-X12/` (outputs in `out/`; `/root/merge-scratch/A-copy` checksums compared before and after: unchanged). Every RAN result quoted below was reproduced. R3 was extended to print all seven consolidated sheets, and one extra fake-COM scenario was added (`scripts/v1_rejected_open.py` → `out/v1_output.txt`, see the X1.5.3 branch table). The five Excel-related pytest files were also re-run there (54 passed).

**Plain-English terms used in this appendix.**

- **Workbook / template**: `.xlsx` is a normal Excel workbook, `.xltx` an Excel template, `.xlsm` / `.xltm` their macro versions. All four are ZIP files holding XML "parts".
- **Power Query** (Excel's data-import tool). Its queries live inside the workbook in a hidden part `customXml/item*.xml` that contains an element called **DataMashup**, plus connection records in `xl/connections.xml`. **Refresh** = re-running the queries so they read the source files again.
- **openpyxl** (a Python library that reads and writes `.xlsx` files without Excel). When it **saves**, it rebuilds the file from what it understands and drops the Power Query parts; reading is harmless.
- **COM** (Windows' way for one program to drive another; here Python drives Microsoft Excel). **pywin32** is the Python package that provides COM (`win32com`, `pythoncom`) and window functions (`win32gui`, `win32api`, `win32con`).
- **GetActiveObject / Dispatch / DispatchEx** (three ways for Python to get an Excel): `GetActiveObject` grabs the Excel that is already running (normally the user's own); `Dispatch` starts one but, for Excel, commonly connects to one already running; `DispatchEx` always starts a separate Excel. Standard 12 requires `DispatchEx`.
- **Visible / DisplayAlerts / ScreenUpdating** (Excel settings: is its window shown, does it show prompts such as "Save changes?", does it repaint the screen). **Quit()** closes that whole Excel with all its workbooks.
- **RefreshAll / BackgroundQuery / CalculateUntilAsyncQueriesDone / Refreshing / RefreshDate** (the COM calls and properties Standard 12 names for a safe refresh: switch off background refresh on each connection, refresh, wait until every query has finished, check none is still refreshing, never trust the refresh date).
- **SendKeys** (pressing keyboard keys by program; the keys go to whichever window has keyboard focus). **Ribbon key tips** (Excel's Alt-key shortcuts: Alt, A = Data tab; then R, A = Refresh All).
- **Thread / worker thread** (a second line of work beside the window). **Daemon thread** (a worker that is killed instantly, without its clean-up, when the program ends).
- **CoInitialize / CoUninitialize** (calls a worker thread must make before and after using COM).
- **Staging file** (a temporary local copy that is worked on and then copied to its final place). **UNC path** (a network path `\\server\share\...`). **8.3 short path** (an old DOS-style short alias of a long path). **`\\?\` prefix** (a Windows prefix that lifts the 260-character path limit for programs that support it).
- **pip** (Python's package installer; `pip install pywin32` downloads and installs a package into one particular Python). **ImportError** (the error Python raises when a package cannot be loaded).
- **find_spec** (a Python check that a module file exists, without loading it). **glob** (a wildcard file search such as `ITC_Report_*.xlsx`). **mtime** (a file's or folder's "date modified").

### X1.1 The findings that matter most (author's top priority)

> **1. Step 3 takes over the user's own open Excel, hides it, and then closes it.** `core/excel_handler.py:123-125` first calls `GetActiveObject("Excel.Application")` (the user's running Excel), and only if that fails `Dispatch` (`:126-128`). It then sets `Visible = False` (`:131`) and never sets it back (the clean-up at `:238-246` restores only `ScreenUpdating` and `DisplayAlerts`). The comment "Don't quit if Excel was already open" (`:241`) is not what happens: the test is `if self.excel_app is None` (`:242`) and `self.excel_app` is only ever `None` (`:56`; no other assignment anywhere, READ by search), so `excel.Quit()` (`:244`) is called **every time**. Just before it, `:240` switches `DisplayAlerts` back to `True`. RAN (fake COM, R2 scenario a): the call order is `GetActiveObject` → `Visible=False` → ... → `DisplayAlerts=True` → `Quit()` with the user's unsaved workbook still open. What a real Excel then does (the user's windows vanish; Excel either closes or waits on an invisible "Save changes?" prompt, which would also block the Step 3 worker) is READ, MEDIUM-HIGH, untestable here. Present since the first commit `edac6a3` (shared - before the split on 30-10-2025) and unchanged by A. See A-R97, A-F14, A-F15.

> **2. Step 4 does not use `RefreshAll` at all: it presses keys in a visible Excel and then always saves.** `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:278-293` sends `SendKeys("%a")`, `"r"`, `"a"` (Alt+A, R, A ⚠) to whichever window has focus, after trying to bring Excel to the front (`:260-276`, and it carries on even if that failed, `:273-274`). It then waits fixed times and saves (`:349`) whether or not an error dialog appeared or the success check failed. No `BackgroundQuery`, `RefreshAll`, `CalculateUntilAsyncQueriesDone` or `Refreshing` exists anywhere in A (RAN search). The design note keeps this on purpose ("the SendKeys approach and its fixed `time.sleep` waits stay as they are", `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-25-merge-extractor-design.md:125-126`). RAN (fake COM, R3): 39 seconds of fixed waiting per report at the default 10-second wait (added during self-review, to match Sections 3, 7, 8 and 11, which quote "about 36 s": 36 s inside the refresh routine plus the 3-second wait before extraction, `report_processor.py:184-185`, which also runs when the refresh is skipped; Section 3 `A-F21`). See A-R71, A-R72, A-F21.

> **3. Step 4 uses `Dispatch` (not `DispatchEx`) twice per report and quits whatever it got.** `report_processor.py:218` (refresh, made visible and maximised `:225-227`) and `:536` (extraction, hidden `:537`), each ending with `Quit()` (`:406`, `:628`). If `Dispatch` attaches to the user's running Excel (MEDIUM-HIGH, general pywin32/Excel behaviour and the premise of Standard 12; cannot be tested here), that Excel is maximised, driven by keystrokes and then quit with `DisplayAlerts = False`, which by Microsoft's documented behaviour closes without asking about unsaved work. RAN (fake COM, R3 scenario b): `Quit()` is called on the attached Excel while its unsaved workbook is still open. See A-R103.

> **4. A failed refresh is saved under the "_Refreshed_" name and later trusted.** If the refreshed copy cannot be opened, the copy made at `report_processor.py:164` stays in the Version folder under the refreshed name; "Skip Refresh" (`:137-155`) then reuses the newest such file and reports `success: True` ("Skipped - Using existing refreshed file"). RAN (fake COM, R3 scenarios f and f2): the second run marks the never-refreshed copy ✓ and its values reach the consolidated workbook. See A-R69, A-F22.

> **5. The only proof of a successful refresh is "`Info!BB2` is not empty, not 0, not an error"** (`report_processor.py:638-685`) [GST RULE] ⚠ — it cannot tell a new value from one already in the file. `RefreshDate` is never used (MET). See A-R73.

> **6. The openpyxl fallback silently strips Power Query and still reports success.** RAN (R1): on Linux, A's own `create_report_from_template` returned `True` for both reports while the output had lost `customXml/item1.xml` (DataMashup), `customXml/itemProps1.xml`, `customXml/_rels/item1.xml.rels` and `xl/connections.xml`. No DataMashup check exists anywhere in A (RAN search). On Windows the start-up check (added in `f363946` and made blocking in `be6418c`, both A only (after the split)) blocks a *missing* pywin32, but it checks only that a `pythoncom` file exists (`utils/requirements_check.py:64-70`), while Step 3 needs `import win32com.client` **and** `import pythoncom` to succeed (`core/excel_handler.py:21-28`). RAN (R4, simulated broken pywin32 on "Windows"): start-up check passes, Step 3 falls back to openpyxl. See A-R96, A-R124.

> **7. Nine columns of the consolidated workbook show a different cell's value from the one the configuration names** — a technical mismatch between configuration and code; which cell is right is the author's call [GST RULE] ⚠. RAN (R3): in `PQ_Extraction_Report_*.xlsx` the IGST/CGST/SGST columns of "IMS Reco", "Extra In Purchase" and "Extra In GSTR2B" received the markers placed in `Diff GSTR-3B!J15/K15/L15`, not those in `IMS_Reco!AA1/AD1/AG1`, `ExtraInPurchase!O1/P1/Q1`, `ExtraInGSTR2B!S1/T1/U1` (the original R3 printout showed only the first two sheets; the verification re-run printed all three and confirmed "Extra In GSTR2B" too). Cause: `power_query_extractor/core/data_consolidator.py:141-145` takes the first stored key that *contains* the column title. See A-R88, A-R80 to A-R82, A-F24.

> **8. Nothing stops Step 3 and Step 4 driving Excel at the same time, and closing the window during Step 4 kills the worker without its clean-up.** Step 3's flag `app.is_processing` (`gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:71-76, 124, 528`) and Step 4's own `ExtractorPanel.is_processing` (`power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:119, 872, 962`) never check each other; both workers are daemon threads (`processing_handler.py:129-133`, `extractor_window.py:878-883`); the close handler asks only about Step 3 (`gui/main_window.py:344-355`). READ, HIGH for the code; what a real Excel is left doing is MEDIUM.

> **9. Originals are never modified.** Client input files are only read (8 bytes) and copied (`utils/helpers.py:282-283, 199`); templates are only copied (`core/excel_handler.py:154, 279`); Step 3 reports are copied before Step 4 touches them (`report_processor.py:164`). READ (search for remove/unlink/rename/move/rmtree: every hit is on a copy, a staging file or something the app made) and RAN (R1: templates and inputs unchanged). HIGH. No code anywhere kills an Excel process (no `taskkill`, `psutil`, `os.kill`, `TerminateProcess`; RAN search).

#### X1.2.6 What A never does (RAN: search of every non-test `.py` file)

- No `DispatchEx`; no `RefreshAll`, `BackgroundQuery`, `CalculateUntilAsyncQueriesDone`, `Refreshing`, `RefreshDate`, `Queries`, `Connections` or `ListObjects`; no `workbook.ReadOnly` check (the only `ReadOnly` is the keyword `ReadOnly=False` at `report_processor.py:780`, next to the keyword `IgnoreReadOnlyRecommended=True` at `:781`). None of these words appears anywhere else in the repository, tests and documents included — the only other hit is the ordinary English word "Refreshing" in a test docstring (`tests/test_workflow_mode.py:86`) (RAN search, verification).
- No DataMashup / `customXml` check; the only `load_workbook` is `core/excel_handler.py:282`.
- No code kills, lists or waits for `EXCEL.EXE` (no `taskkill`, `psutil`, `os.kill`, `TerminateProcess`, `subprocess` outside the pip installer). The only other program launches are `os.system('open …')` / `os.system('xdg-open …')` to show the output folder off Windows (`gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:510, 512`), unrelated to Excel.
- No check that Microsoft Excel is installed, nor of its version or interface language.
- Existence-only checks of templates (not reads): `gui/handlers/file_handler.py:143-149` (processing gate), `gui/utils/setup_validation.py:56-64` (Setup checklist, suffixes `.xlsx .xltx .xltm .xlsm` at `:21`).

### X1.3 (b) Each Excel session checked against Standard 12 "Excel through COM"

#### X1.3.1 The rules, numbered for this appendix

The rules are those of `rebuild_pipeline_FINAL.md:844-877`, split so that each can be marked on its own. Line numbers refer to that file.

| Rule | What Standard 12 asks | Standard line |
|---|---|---|
| C1 | Use COM only for a workbook with Power Query that the app writes into or refreshes | 846-847 |
| C2 | Before saving with openpyxl into a workbook the app did not create, check it for a `customXml/item*.xml` part containing `DataMashup`; if found use COM or stop and tell the user; never let openpyxl save over such a workbook | 847-850 |
| C3 | Start a separate Excel with `DispatchEx("Excel.Application")` | 851-852 |
| C4 | `excel.Visible = False` | 853 |
| C5 | `excel.DisplayAlerts = False` (without it, `Quit()` can wait forever on an invisible "save changes?" prompt) | 853-855 |
| C6 | Never take over the user's own open Excel | 853-854 |
| C7 | Always call `excel.Quit()` in a `finally` block, even after an error | 856 |
| C8 | Open the workbook with `IgnoreReadOnlyRecommended=True` | 857 |
| C9 | If `workbook.ReadOnly` is then true: close it and ask the user to close the workbook in Excel first | 857-859 |
| C10 | Set `BackgroundQuery = False` on each of the workbook's connections | 860-861 |
| C11 | Call `workbook.RefreshAll()` | 861 |
| C12 | Then `excel.CalculateUntilAsyncQueriesDone()`, and only then save | 861-865 |
| C13 | Before saving, check that no connection's `Refreshing` is still true | 865-866 |
| C14 | Never use a connection's `RefreshDate` as proof of a refresh | 866-867 |
| C15 | Adding a query through COM works, loading it into a new table failed: ask first if an app needs that | 868-871 |
| C16 | In a worker thread, call `pythoncom.CoInitialize()` first | 872-873 |
| C17 | Do the Excel work in a separate function and call `pythoncom.CoUninitialize()` after that function returns, so no Excel object is still held | 873-875 |
| C18 | Excel installed on every PC that runs the app; a logged-in user; never a scheduled job | 876-877 |

The Excel sessions in A (places where Excel is started or attached):

- **S1** — Step 3 report creation, `core/excel_handler.py:104-260` (`_create_report_win32com`). Once per report (two per client), on the S3 worker. Features A-F14, A-F15; rules A-R96 to A-R101.
- **S2** — Step 4 refresh, `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:209-415` (`_refresh_power_query_simple`). Once per ticked report, on the S4 worker. Features A-F21, A-F26; rules A-R71 to A-R73, A-R102, A-R103, A-R105.
- **S3** — Step 4 value extraction, `report_processor.py:527-636` (`_extract_data`). Once per ticked report, right after S2 (also after a failed S2 and in Skip mode), on the S4 worker. Feature A-F23; rules A-R83, A-R102, A-R103.
- Not Excel sessions: the `WScript.Shell` COM object inside S2 (`report_processor.py:260`) and the `win32gui` window scan (`:417-525`). Dead: `ExcelHandler.__del__` (`core/excel_handler.py:58-64`) never has an Excel to quit.
- The openpyxl path **F** (`core/excel_handler.py:262-322`) is not COM, but rule C2 is about exactly that path, so it is marked too.

So each client costs up to two Excel start/attach-and-quit cycles in Step 3 and four in Step 4 (RAN fake COM: R2, R3 a).

#### X1.3.2 S1 — Step 3 report creation (`core/excel_handler.py:_create_report_win32com`)

| Rule | Verdict | Evidence (file:line, READ/RAN) |
|---|---|---|
| C1 | MET | S1 writes the Links cells of a copy of the author's template (`:189-197`) and lets Excel save it (`:203`), which is how the queries survive. READ. (It is also used for a template without queries; nothing checks.) |
| C2 | NOT APPLICABLE to S1 | S1 saves through Excel, not openpyxl. For the openpyxl path see F below. |
| C3 | NOT MET | `GetActiveObject` first (`:124`), else `Dispatch` (`:127`); never `DispatchEx` (RAN search). Present since `edac6a3` (shared - before the split on 30-10-2025: `core/excel_handler.py:122, 125@edac6a3`). |
| C4 | MET as written, with a harmful side effect | `Visible = False` (`:131`). When `:124` attached to the user's Excel, the user's own Excel is hidden and never shown again — the clean-up restores only `ScreenUpdating` and `DisplayAlerts` (`:238-240`). READ HIGH; RAN (fake COM R2 a): at `Quit()` the attached Excel still has `Visible=False`. |
| C5 | NOT MET at the moment it matters | `DisplayAlerts = False` at `:132`, but set back to `True` at `:240`, immediately before `Quit()` at `:244`. The standard's reason (an invisible "save changes?" prompt can block `Quit()`) applies exactly: the Excel is invisible (`:131`) and, if it is the user's, may hold unsaved work. RAN (fake COM R2 a): `Quit()` is called with `DisplayAlerts=True`, `Visible=False` and an unsaved user workbook open. Real outcome (hang or prompt) READ, MEDIUM. |
| C6 | NOT MET (deliberately attaches) | `GetActiveObject("Excel.Application")` (`:124`) is the call that takes over the running Excel; the log even says "Using existing Excel instance" (`:125`). RAN (fake COM R2 a). |
| C7 | NOT MET (not reliable, and quits the wrong Excel) | `Quit()` is inside `finally` and its own `try` (`:243-246`), but the two property sets before it (`:239-240`) are unprotected. RAN (fake COM R2 c — Excel rejects calls; R2 g — Excel crashes during `Save`): the exception escapes the `finally`, so `Quit()`, `CoUninitialize()` (`:250`) and the staging-file delete (`:255-260`) never run; in R2 g the staging file was left behind; the exception reaches `processing_handler.py:324-326` ("❌ ITC Report Error: Call was rejected by callee"; for the Sales report `:400-406`, "❌ Sales Report Error: …") and the original error is only in the log (`:227`). And when it does run, `Quit()` closes the user's own Excel, because the "already open" test uses `self.excel_app`, which is never set (`:56`, `:242`). |
| C8 | NOT MET | `excel.Workbooks.Open(file_str)` (`:349`) and `excel.Workbooks.Open(short_path)` (`:364`) pass no other argument. READ; RAN (fake COM: recorded calls carry no keyword). |
| C9 | NOT MET | `ReadOnly` is never read (RAN search). Note: `shutil.copy2` (`:154`) copies the template's file attributes; on Windows that includes the read-only flag (Python's documented `copystat` behaviour, MEDIUM-HIGH), so a template marked read-only on the share gives a read-only staging copy that Excel would open read-only, and `wb.Save()` (`:203`) would fail → report "Failed". RAN (fake COM R2 f, a failing `Save`): returns `False`, clean-up runs. |
| C10 | NOT APPLICABLE | S1 does not refresh. Caveat: if a template query is set to "Refresh data when opening the file", opening it (`:349`) could start a refresh that S1 then saves part-way (`:203`). LOW; how to check: the template's query properties. |
| C11 | NOT APPLICABLE | No refresh (same caveat). |
| C12 | NOT APPLICABLE | No refresh (same caveat). |
| C13 | NOT APPLICABLE | No refresh (same caveat). |
| C14 | MET | `RefreshDate` is not used anywhere in A (RAN search). |
| C15 | NOT APPLICABLE | No query is added (RAN search: no `Queries`, no `ListObjects`). |
| C16 | MET | `pythoncom.CoInitialize()` at `:120`, on the S3 worker (`processing_handler.py:129-134` → `:309` / `:376`). RAN (fake COM: first call recorded). |
| C17 | NOT MET | `CoUninitialize()` is called inside the same function (`:250`) while `excel`, `ws` and the loop variable `sheet` still refer to Excel objects (`wb` is set to `None` only on the success path, `:207`). READ HIGH; possible effect (Excel lingering in the background, COM errors when Python later frees those objects) MEDIUM-LOW. |
| C18 | MET (with a note) | Never a scheduled job (interactive window only; no scheduler code), so the rule as written is met. Note: Excel's presence is not checked: the start-up check looks only for pywin32 (`utils/requirements_check.py:37-61`). Without Excel, `Dispatch` fails inside the `try` → `False` (`:226-228`) → the window says "Check if template has 'Links' sheet" (`processing_handler.py:322-323`, `:396-398`), a misleading cause. READ HIGH. |
| (extra) | – | A template with no sheet named `Links` (and none containing "link") gets a NEW sheet called `Links`, filled and saved, and the report counts as a success (`:180-183`, A-R58) — the template's queries would not read that new sheet. RAN (fake COM R2 d). A sheet such as "Hyperlinks" would be written into instead (R2 e). |

#### X1.3.3 S2 — Step 4 refresh (`report_processor.py:_refresh_power_query_simple`)

| Rule | Verdict | Evidence (file:line, READ/RAN) |

#### X1.3.7 Pattern consistency across the three sessions (audit method step 8)

- How Excel is obtained differs: S1 `GetActiveObject` then `Dispatch`; S2 and S3 `Dispatch` only; none uses `DispatchEx` (READ).
- Visibility differs: S1 hides, S2 shows and maximises, S3 hides (READ).
- Clean-up differs: S1's `finally` has two unprotected calls (`core/excel_handler.py:239-240`); S2 and S3 protect every Excel clean-up call (`report_processor.py:397-415`, `:618-636`) — only their window-log lines (`self._log(…)` at `:396` and `:619`) sit outside a `try` (READ; RAN fake COM).
- The two `_safe_open_workbook` methods are deliberately different and share only the "already open" check (`utils/excel_com.py:1-15` comment, commit `ba2a753`, A only (after the split)). Neither passes `IgnoreReadOnlyRecommended` on its normal path (READ).
- Logging differs: `ReportProcessor._log` always writes INFO and always sends level "info" to the window (`report_processor.py:53-60`), so even "❌" lines appear in the plain info colour (RAN fake COM R3: every processor line had level `info`; also R4: the pywin32 refusal); `ExcelHandler` uses `logger.error/warning`, which never reach the window.
- All three sessions were written in the first commit `edac6a3` (shared - before the split on 30-10-2025); A after the split changed only: local staging for S1 (`12d505f`), the shared already-open check (`ba2a753`), log levels and a stray print (`064c634`), the guarded pywin32 imports (`c463256`) and the configured-suffix lookup (`2aaa2b1`) (READ: `git diff 47a1492 A/main` for both files). So project B very probably carries the same three sessions — whoever audits B should confirm (MEDIUM, from history only).

#### X1.4.1 Every openpyxl save in A

| 1 | `core/excel_handler.py:306` `wb.save(str(local_temp))` | the local staging copy of the ITC or Sales TEMPLATE, then copied to the report path (`:308`) | YES | NONE | Reached only when `USE_WIN32COM` is False (`:90-102`): not Windows, or pywin32 cannot be imported. RAN (R1, both an `.xltx` ITC template and an `.xlsx` Sales template carrying an injected DataMashup part and a connection): four parts lost — `customXml/_rels/item1.xml.rels`, `customXml/item1.xml`, `customXml/itemProps1.xml`, `xl/connections.xml`; "DataMashup present after save = False"; the function returned `True` for every report; the only warnings were two log lines ("Not on Windows - Power Query may not be preserved!", `:98`; "Using openpyxl - Power Query content may be lost!", `:267`). Limitation: my template is synthetic, not made by Excel; Standard 12 records the loss as tested on real files. |
| 2 | `core/excel_handler.py:402` `wb.save(str(output_path))` | `GST_Processing_Summary_<DDMMYY_HHMM>.xlsx`, created by `Workbook()` (`:381`) | NO | not needed | Written straight into the Level-1 folder on the share (no staging). RAN (R1). |
| 3 | `power_query_extractor/core/data_consolidator.py:179` `wb.save(report_path)` | `PQ_Extraction_Report_<YYYYMMDD_HHMM>.xlsx`, created by `Workbook()` (`:27`) | NO | not needed | Written straight into the Level-1 folder on the share. RAN (R3). |

Further points:

- A never loads and saves a refreshed report or a client input file with openpyxl; the only `load_workbook` is `core/excel_handler.py:282` (RAN search). HIGH.
- openpyxl 3.1.5 (the version in this computer's environment) writes the ZIP straight onto the target path (`openpyxl/writer/excel.py:291`, `ZipFile(filename, 'w', …)`, READ of the library). So for saves 2 and 3, a network drop mid-save leaves a broken workbook under the final name (no write-to-temporary-then-rename). MEDIUM-HIGH.
- **Template type.** RAN (R1): the ITC report made from an `.xltx` template is named `.xlsx` but its main content type (the label inside the file's `[Content_Types].xml` part that tells Excel what kind of file it is) is still "template" (`spreadsheetml.template.main+xml`), because openpyxl remembers that it loaded a template (`openpyxl/reader/excel.py:158`). The Sales report made from an `.xlsx` template is a normal workbook. Whether Excel opens such a mislabelled file without complaint: NOT SURE — check by opening one Step 3 report built from an `.xltx` on Windows. The same question exists on the COM path: S1 copies the `.xltx` bytes into a file named `.xlsx` (`core/excel_handler.py:147, 154`) and opens and saves it through Excel (`:349`, `:203`); what Excel then writes is NOT SURE (LOW either way); how to check: run Step 3 once with an `.xltx` template and look for `template.main` in the report's `[Content_Types].xml`. The tool has evidently been used with templates (Browse filter `*.xltx *.xlsx`, `gui/handlers/file_handler.py:31, 42`; help text `gui/tabs/setup_tab.py:77-82`), which suggests it works, but no test or commit message confirms the `.xltx` case.
- **Macro templates.** The Setup checklist accepts `.xltm` / `.xlsm` (`gui/utils/setup_validation.py:21`) but the report is always named `.xlsx` (`gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:298, 356`). On the openpyxl path `keep_vba` is not passed, so macros are dropped (`core/excel_handler.py:282`). On the COM path, Excel generally refuses to save macro content under `.xlsx` (MEDIUM-LOW, untested).
- **Links sheet missing on the openpyxl path.** RAN (R1, template with only a sheet "MyLinks"): `create_report_from_template` returned `True`, nothing was written, `MyLinks!B2` kept its old value. (The COM path adds a new `Links` sheet instead — X1.3.2.)
- **Template placeholders survive.** RAN (R1): `<Client B>` has no Annual Report and no IMS file, so the empty values for B4, B5, B10, B11 are not written (`if value:` `core/excel_handler.py:192, 300`) and the report keeps whatever the template held there (`PLACEHOLDER-B4` … in my template). [GST RULE] (A-R56).

### X1.5 (d) Realistic runs traced call by call

Each run below lists A's calls in order. Steps marked "RAN (fake COM)" were executed with the recording fakes, which proves the order of A's calls and which clean-up steps run, but not real Excel behaviour. Steps marked RAN without "fake" were executed with real code and real files (openpyxl, file system).

#### X1.5.1 Run 1 — Step 3 on Windows with pywin32: ITC and Sales reports for `<Client A>` (READ; call order RAN with fake COM, R2)

Set-up: Setup tab has an ITC and a Sales template, a source folder and a target folder; processing mode "fresh"; `<Client A>` has one file of each of the six types (two GSTR-3B months). The user presses Start.

1. `gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:69-134` — "already running?" guard (`:71-76`), input checks (`gui/handlers/file_handler.py:132-151`: both templates set and existing, target set), Start greyed, worker started as a daemon thread (`:129-134`).
2. `processing_handler.py:189-195` — `FileOrganizer(...)`; the target folder is created if missing (`core/file_organizer.py:65-69`); the run's time stamp is taken once (`:43`).
3. `processing_handler.py:253` → `core/file_organizer.py:71-148` — creates `Annual Statement-<DDMMYY HHMM>\<client>-<STATE>\Version-<DDMMYY HHMM>\GSTR3B\`, `ITC\`, `Sales\` (RAN R1 shows the tree; X2.4).
4. `processing_handler.py:271-273` → `core/file_organizer.py:198-300` — each input file copied with `shutil.copy2` and a size check (`utils/helpers.py:172-215`) under a cleaned name; the client's file records renamed to the cleaned names (`core/file_organizer.py:233-246`). Originals untouched (RAN R1).
5. ITC report name `ITC_Report_<cleaned client>_<state code>_<DDMMYY_HHMM>.xlsx` in the Version folder (`processing_handler.py:292-298`); values for B2, B4, B5, B7, B8, B10, B11 from `prepare_template_data` (`core/excel_handler.py:603-656`) [GST RULE] ⚠.
6. `core/excel_handler.py:82-87` template exists, folder ensured; `USE_WIN32COM` True → `_create_report_win32com`.
7. Calls to Excel, in order (RAN fake COM, R2 a and b, matches the code line by line):
   1. `pythoncom.CoInitialize()` (`:120`).
   2. `win32com.client.GetActiveObject("Excel.Application")` (`:124`) → **if the user has Excel open, S1 now holds the user's Excel**; otherwise it raises and `win32com.client.Dispatch("Excel.Application")` (`:127`) starts one.
   3. `excel.Visible = False`, `excel.DisplayAlerts = False`, `excel.ScreenUpdating = False` (`:131-133`) → with the user's Excel, all its windows disappear now (READ, MEDIUM-HIGH).
   4. Delete an old staging file (`:147-152`); `shutil.copy2(template, %TEMP%\gst_excel_temp\ITC_Report_….xlsx)` (`:154`); wait 0.5 s.
   5. `_safe_open_workbook`: exists check; loop over `excel.Workbooks` comparing each `FullName` (`utils/excel_com.py:26-28`); `excel.Workbooks.Open(<staging path>)` (`:349`).
   6. Loop over `wb.Sheets` reading `.Name` until `Links` is found (`:166-170`).
   7. `ws.Range("B2").Value = "<folder>"`, B7, B8 … (`:193`) — only non-empty values.

## APPENDIX X2: WHAT THE CODE NEEDS FROM OUTSIDE THE REPOSITORY

This appendix lists everything project A (`bf2f1dd`) expects to find, or creates, outside its own source files: the two Excel templates, the client input files and their exact file-name patterns, the folders it reads and the folders it builds, every settings, cache, log and history file, the environment it assumes, how each storage place compares with the author's Standard 13 (`rebuild_pipeline_FINAL.md:900-1061`), and a checklist of what the author would have to hand over for a build. Evidence labels, scripts and terms are those of X1.0. Two more terms: **CWD / current folder** (the folder a program was started from; a file name with no folder part is created there, so it depends on *how* the program was started), and **home folder** (`C:\Users\<name>` on Windows, what Python's `Path.home()` returns).

> **Nothing outside the code is in the repository.** No template, sample input file or settings file exists at `bf2f1dd`, and none ever did: a search of the whole history for added `.xlsx`, `.xltx`, `.xls`, `.xlsm`, `.json` (JSON = a plain-text format for settings) and `.log` files finds only `.claude/settings.local.json` (`bd176bf`) and a run log `gst_organizer.log` committed in `edac6a3` (RAN `git log --diff-filter=A`). The log is history only (present in `edac6a3` and `6237597`, deleted by `cbfa4a5`, absent after the merge `9c56a1c`); it is a log of an earlier run and was not opened for this audit. Everything below about template content is therefore inferred from the code that reads and writes it.

#### X2.1.2 What must be INSIDE each template — Step 3 writes these cells [GST RULE] ⚠

The code writes **text** into sheet `Links` of each copy (`utils/constants.py:102-126`; values `core/excel_handler.py:603-713`; written `:189-197` (COM) and `:297-303` (openpyxl)). Which source file feeds which cell is the author's template design; this table only records what the code writes (A-R54, A-R55).

| Template | Cell ⚠ | Key | What is written | When it is written |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ITC | B2 | `gstr3b_folder` | full path of the client's `GSTR3B` category folder (backslashes) | always — even when the client has no GSTR-3B file (the folder always exists) (`:622`) |
| ITC | B4 | `annual_folder` | full path of the Version folder (where the Annual Report is copied) | only if the client has an Annual Report (`:625-633`) |
| ITC | B5 | `annual_filename` | stem (name without extension) of the FIRST Annual Report file, cleaned name | same (`:628-630`) |
| ITC | B7 | `gstr2b_folder` | full path of the `ITC` category folder | only if a GSTR-2B Reco file exists (`:636-644`) |
| ITC | B8 | `gstr2b_filename` | stem of the FIRST GSTR-2B Reco file | same |
| ITC | B10 | `ims_folder` | full path of the `ITC` category folder | only if an IMS Reco file exists (`:647-655`) |
| ITC | B11 | `ims_filename` | stem of the FIRST IMS Reco file | same |
| Sales | B2 | `sales_folder` | full path of the `Sales` category folder | only if a Sales file exists (`:661-674`) |
| Sales | B3 | `sales_filename` | stem of the FIRST Sales file | same |
| Sales | B5 | `annual_folder` | full path of the Version folder | only if an Annual Report exists (`:677-690`) |
| Sales | B6 | `annual_filename` | stem of the FIRST Annual Report file | same |
| Sales | B8 | `sales_reco_folder` | full path of the `Sales` category folder | only if a Sales Reco file exists (`:693-706`) |
| Sales | B9 | `sales_reco_filename` | stem of the FIRST Sales Reco file | same |

Cells B3, B6, B9 of the ITC template and B4, B7 of the Sales template are never touched (READ). RAN (R1): `<Client A>` got all seven ITC and all six Sales cells; `<Client B>` (only GSTR-3B and Sales files) got ITC B2 only and Sales B2, B3 only.

Rules that follow, each READ and where marked RAN:

- **No extension is written**, only the stem (`utils/helpers.py:553-555`); the template's queries must add it. An `.xls` input is linked the same way (MEDIUM: whether the template then finds it depends on its queries — question for the author).
- **Empty values are skipped**, so the template's own content of that cell stays (`if value:` `core/excel_handler.py:192, 300`). RAN (R1): placeholders I put in B4, B5, B10, B11 of the ITC template stayed in `<Client B>`'s report. So whatever the author left in those cells when building the template is what a client without that file will query [GST RULE] (A-R56).
- **"FIRST" = first in sorted full-path order** (`utils/helpers.py:361`; `[0]` at `core/excel_handler.py:629, 640, 651, 667, 683, 699`). A space sorts before a dot, so a Windows duplicate download `… (1).xlsx` beats the plain file; a day-first date `01042025` beats `31032025` (A-R57; TRACE notes T3 (b), RAN). The other files of that type are copied but not linked, without any message [GST RULE].
- **Paths are absolute** and use whatever the user picked as target (a mapped drive letter or a `\\server\share` path), `/` turned into `\` (`utils/helpers.py:418-422`). A report built on one PC through `Z:` refreshes on another PC only if that PC maps the same letter (MEDIUM). Commit `12d505f` relies on these absolute paths for "Power Query is preserved".
- **Finding the sheet**: COM path — `Links` ignoring case, else the first sheet whose name contains "link", else a NEW `Links` sheet is added and the report still counts as success (`core/excel_handler.py:162-183`; RAN fake COM R2 d, e). openpyxl path — `Links` ignoring case only; otherwise nothing is written and the report still counts as success (`:285-310`; RAN R1). The only hint for the user is the start-up log line "⚠️ IMPORTANT: Templates must have 'Links' sheet for reports to work!" (`gui/main_window.py:396`) and "Check if template has 'Links' sheet" after a FAILED report (`gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:323, 397`) (A-R58).

The first three groups date from `edac6a3`; "Reco Diff" to "Extra In GSTR2B" were added in `47a1492` (both shared - before the split on 30-10-2025). So, as the code stands, the ITC template must contain (after refresh) the sheets `Info`, `Diff GSTR-3B`, `Reco`, `T6 of R9`, `T8 of R9`, `IMS_Reco`, `ExtraInPurchase`, `ExtraInGSTR2B` and `Links`; the Sales template `Info`, `Diff - GSTR-1` and `Links` (READ).

#### X2.1.4 The queries themselves

The code never reads, adds, edits or checks a query (RAN search: no `Queries`, `Connections`, `DataMashup`). It only assumes, in comments, that the templates contain Power Query queries that take their folder and file locations from the Links cells (`core/excel_handler.py:3, 66-72, 143-146`; message of `12d505f`). How the queries read the cells (named ranges, `Excel.CurrentWorkbook()`, …), whether the GSTR-3B folder query (B2) reads every file in the folder or filters by name, and which extension they add, cannot be seen from the repository. HIGH that the code is silent; the rest is a question for the author.

#### X2.1.5 Template file-format pitfalls

| Pitfall | What happens | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `.xltx` template, openpyxl path | Report named `.xlsx` but marked "template" inside | RAN R1 |
| `.xltx` template, COM path | Template bytes copied under an `.xlsx` name and opened and saved by Excel; result not sure | READ, LOW (X1.4.1) |
| `.xlsm` / `.xltm` template | Accepted by the checklist, report still named `.xlsx`; openpyxl drops macros; Excel generally refuses macro content under `.xlsx` | READ; MEDIUM-LOW |
| Template marked read-only on the share | `shutil.copy2` copies the flag to the staging copy (Excel opens it read-only → `Save` fails → report "Failed"); a stale read-only staging file cannot be deleted by the next run (`core/excel_handler.py:148-152`, error ignored) and the following `copy2` fails; the finished report (`:215`) and Step 4's copy (`report_processor.py:164`) carry the flag on | READ (Python's documented `copystat` behaviour on Windows, MEDIUM-HIGH); RAN (fake COM R2 f, a failing `Save`) |
| Two copies of A run by the same Windows user for the same client in the same minute | Same staging file name `%TEMP%\gst_excel_temp\<report name>` | READ, LOW |

### X2.2 Input files and file-name patterns

#### X2.2.1 Which files are looked at at all (A-R8 to A-R10)

| Filter | Rule | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Where | Only the TOP level of the chosen source folder; sub-folders are ignored without any message | `utils/helpers.py:328` (`os.scandir`, not recursive). RAN R1 (a GSTR-3B file in `sub/` never appeared) |
| Extension, listing step | Name ends with `.xlsx`, `.xls` or `.xlsm`, any case; `.xltx`, `.xltm`, `.csv`, `.pdf`, `.xlsb` are never looked at and never reported | `utils/helpers.py:327, 330`. RAN R1 (`notes.csv` absent everywhere) |
| Extension, second check | `.xlsx .xls .xlsm .xltx .xltm` (redundant after the first) | `utils/helpers.py:299` |
| Regular file | Folders named like workbooks are skipped | `utils/helpers.py:296` |
| Size | At least 1024 bytes; smaller files (incl. Excel's `~$` lock files) dropped silently; no upper limit (`MAX_FILE_SIZE_MB = 100` is unused, `utils/constants.py:198`) | `utils/helpers.py:302-303` |
| Signature | First bytes `PK\x03\x04` (ZIP-based) or `\xd0\xcf\x11\xe0` (old `.xls`); others dropped silently | `utils/helpers.py:264-265, 275-287` |
| Order | Sorted by full path (on Windows Python sorts paths ignoring case) — decides "which file wins" | `utils/helpers.py:361` |

Files that pass are matched against the six patterns below; a name that matches none — or matches with an empty client or state — becomes a "variation" (shown only as a count on Step 2 and listed on the "Variations" sheet of the Step 3 summary workbook; never copied) (`core/file_parser.py:209-220`; A-R11). RAN R1: `Purchase Register ClientB.xlsx` → variation "No matching pattern found".

#### X2.2.2 The six patterns, exactly as coded [GST RULE] ⚠

All six live in `utils/constants.py:13-62` as regexes (regular expressions: text patterns the code matches each file name against), compiled with `re.IGNORECASE` (letter case ignored), tried in this order, first match wins (`core/file_parser.py:82-128`, `break` at `:128`). Every captured part is trimmed of surrounding spaces (`:102-106`). "Category" and "folder" labels are copied into each result and never read (A-R16); the real destination is decided in `core/file_organizer.py:302-315`.

| # | Key | Regex (verbatim) ⚠ | type | groups captured | shown to the user as ⚠ (`constants.py` description; Setup card `gui/tabs/setup_tab.py:477-503`) | copied into | feeds | duplicates | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `GSTR-2B-Reco` | `^GSTR-2B-Reco-([^-]+)-([^-]+)-(.+)\.xlsx?$` | `GSTR-2B Reco` | client, state, period | `GSTR-2B-Reco-ClientName-State-Period.xlsx` | `ITC` category folder | ITC template B7 (folder), B8 (stem of the first) | "Multiple GSTR-2B Reco (n files)" | A-R1 |
| 2 | `ImsReco` | `^ImsReco-([^-]+)-([^-]+)-(\d{8})(?:\s*\(\d+\))?\.xlsx?$` | `IMS Reco` | client, state, date (exactly 8 digits) | `ImsReco-ClientName-State-DDMMYYYY.xlsx` | `ITC` category folder | ITC B10, B11 | "Multiple IMS Reco (n files)" | A-R2 |
| 3 | `GSTR3B` | `^(?:\(\d+\)\s*)?GSTR3B-([^-]+)-([^-]+)-([^-]+)\.xlsx?$` | `GSTR-3B Export` | client, state, month | `GSTR3B-ClientName-State-Month.xlsx` | `GSTR3B` category folder | ITC B2 (the whole folder) | any number allowed ("monthly filings - unlimited", `core/file_parser.py:266-268`) ⚠ | A-R3, A-R27 |
| 4 | `Sales` | `^Sales-([^-]+)-([^-]+)-([^-]+)-([^-]+)\.xlsx?$` | `Sales` | client, state, start_month, end_month | `Sales-ClientName-State-StartMonth-EndMonth.xlsx` | `Sales` category folder | Sales B2, B3 | "Multiple Sales (n files)" | A-R4 |
| 5 | `SalesReco` | `^SalesReco-([^-]+)-([^-]+)-(.+)\.xlsx?$` | `Sales Reco` | client, state, period | `SalesReco-ClientName-State-Period.xlsx` | `Sales` category folder | Sales B8, B9 | "Multiple Sales Reco (n files)" | A-R5 |
| 6 | `AnnualReport` | `^AnnualReport-([^-]+)-([^-]+)-(.+)\.xlsx?$` | `Annual Report` | client, state, year | `AnnualReport-ClientName-State-Year.xlsx` | the Version folder itself | ITC B4, B5 and Sales B5, B6 | "Multiple Annual Report (n files)" | A-R6 |

Unrecognised names get a hint (`core/file_parser.py:288-306`, first hit wins on the lower-cased name): contains "gstr" and "2b" → pattern 1's text; "ims" → 2; "gstr" and "3b" → 3; "sales" and "reco" → 5; "sales" → 4; "annual" → 6; otherwise "Check file naming convention" (A-R12) ⚠.

|---|---|
| `GSTR-2B-Reco-ClientA-Maharashtra-Apr25-Mar26.xlsx` | GSTR-2B Reco, client `ClientA`, state `Maharashtra` → code `MH`, period `Apr25-Mar26` |
| `gstr-2b-reco-ClientA-Maharashtra-Q1.XLSX` | recognised (any letter case) |
| `GSTR-2B-Reco-Client-A-Delhi-Apr25.xlsx` | **parts shifted**: read as client `Client`, state `A` (code `A`), period `Delhi-Apr25` — a hyphen inside a client name moves every later part |
| `GSTR-2B-Reco-ClientA-Delhi-Apr25 (1).xlsx` | recognised; period `Apr25 (1)` |
| `GSTR2B-Reco-…`, `GSTR-3B-…`, `Sales Reco-…`, `Annual Report-…` | not recognised (variation with the matching hint) |
| `ImsReco-ClientA-Delhi-31032026.xlsx`, `… (1).xlsx`, `…(2).xlsx` | recognised; date `31032026` |
| `ImsReco-ClientA-Delhi-31032026 (1) (2).xlsx`, `ImsReco-ClientA-Delhi-31-03-2026.xlsx` | not recognised |
| `(1) GSTR3B-ClientA-Delhi-Apr25.xlsx` | recognised (leading "(N)" allowed for GSTR-3B only) |

Other facts about the patterns (READ; RAN in TRACE notes T1-T3 and R7):

- The period / date / month / year parts are captured but **never used** (`core/file_parser.py:106` writes `metadata`, nothing reads it): there is no financial-year or tax-period logic anywhere in A, so files of different periods or years for one client are grouped together [GST RULE] (A-R25).
- The state part is turned into a two-letter code through a 39-entry table of state and union-territory names (`utils/constants.py:251-292`; lookup `utils/helpers.py:592-606`) ⚠; a name not in the table becomes the initials of its first two words, or the first three characters of a one-word name (`utils/helpers.py:608-618`) [GST RULE] (A-R21, A-R22). No GSTIN or PAN is read anywhere (A-R24).
- The client key is `"<client as written>-<state code>"` (`core/file_parser.py:229-230`), case- and space-sensitive: `<Client A> Private Limited` and `<Client A> Pvt Ltd` are two clients (A-R17).
- Expected per client: all six types (`utils/constants.py:68-75`); completeness = types found ÷ 6 (`core/file_parser.py:273-275`) [GST RULE] ⚠ (A-R26, A-R28).
- Client and state warnings ("too short", "invalid characters") are computed and never shown (`core/file_parser.py:108-119`; A-R18).

#### X2.2.3 What the author's files must look like inside

Nothing in A reads the CONTENT of an input file: it copies it byte for byte (`utils/helpers.py:199`) and reads its first 8 bytes (`:282-283`). The content matters only to the template's queries, which are not in the repository (X2.1.4). So the inside of each input type is whatever the template queries expect — a question for the author (HIGH that the code is silent).

```text
    │       └── _Organization_Report_ClientA Private Limited_Maharashtra.txt   (core/file_organizer.py:330; client and state as written)
    └── ClientB-DL/
        └── Version-211026 1818/
            ├── GSTR3B/   GSTR3B-ClientB-Delhi-Apr25.xlsx
            ├── ITC/      (empty, still created)
            ├── Sales/    Sales-ClientB-Delhi-Apr25-Mar26.xlsx
            ├── ITC_Report_ClientB_DL_211026_1818.xlsx
            ├── Sales_Report_ClientB_DL_211026_1818.xlsx
            └── _Organization_Report_ClientB_Delhi.txt
```

Rules behind the names (READ; registry IDs):

- Copied input files get `sanitize_filename` names (`core/file_organizer.py:271`; `utils/helpers.py:68-126`; A-R20): Private→Pvt, Limited→Ltd, unsafe characters → `_`, runs of spaces → `_`.
- The Level-2 name is NOT cleaned the same way (spaces kept, no character replacement) and is shortened to the "maximum client folder name length" (default 35; A-R35, A-R36); the Level-4 folders, the copied files and the report names keep the FULL cleaned client name.
- In "fresh" mode an existing destination file (same-minute re-run) is first copied to `<stem>_backup_<DDMMYY_HHMM><ext>` **in the same folder** (`utils/helpers.py:217-234`; A-R45, A-R46) — inside the `GSTR3B` folder that B2 links as a whole.
- Two clients whose Level-2 names come out equal (Pvt/Private variants, the same first characters up to the limit, letter case on Windows) share one Level-2 folder and one Version folder (TRACE notes T6 §7, T8; A-F13).
- Time stamps have minute resolution, so a second run in the same minute reuses the Level-1 and Version folders and overwrites reports and the summary without backup (A-R33; report names A-R59, summary A-R61; the consolidated workbook likewise, A-R86).

Other things created outside the target (READ; RAN R1, R5):

| Created | Where | By | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Staging folder | `%TEMP%\gst_excel_temp\` (per user, per PC, local) | `core/excel_handler.py:53-54`, when the main window starts | RAN R1 |
| Staging files | `%TEMP%\gst_excel_temp\<report file name>` — named like the report, so they carry the client name and state code | `core/excel_handler.py:147-155, 273-279`; deleted after each report (best effort) | RAN R1 (empty after); RAN (fake COM R2 g: left behind after a crash) |
| `logs\` and `temp\` | the PROGRAM folder | `main.py:35-37`, created if missing (checked at every start); never used | RAN R5 |
| `__init__.py` placeholders | program folder `core\`, `utils\`, `gui\` (only if missing) | `main.py:39-43` | READ |
| Settings file | home folder | X2.5 item 1 | RAN R5 |
| Log files | the CWD | X2.5 items 3-4 | RAN R5 |
| Exported client list | wherever the user saves it | `gui/handlers/client_handler.py:233-255` | READ |

Path length (READ; registry A-R39, A-R104): the full path of a copied ITC file is at most `len(target) + 90 + len(cleaned file name)` characters with the defaults (28 for `Annual Statement-DDMMYY HHMM`, up to 35 for Level 2, 19 for `Version-DDMMYY HHMM`, 3 for `ITC`, plus separators; notes `A_outside_files_state.md` §3.7, re-counted from `utils/constants.py:82-95`). The client name appears twice (shortened at Level 2, full in the file name) and a third time when include-client-name is on. Nothing measures a path before creating it; the 218-character figure ⚠ appears only in open fallbacks, error hints and help texts (`core/excel_handler.py:356`; `report_processor.py:720, 795`; `gui/tabs/setup_tab.py:115-116, 122`). A refreshed copy is about 22 characters longer than its original (`_Refreshed_DDMMYY_HHMM`).

> **The 215-character margin depends on a shorter share root.** The code comment says the short category names "bring the worst case to 215 with none over" (`utils/constants.py:85-90`). The commit that made the change (`7347383`, 26-07-2026, A only (after the split)) says more: the real run of 3030 files had a worst path of 270 characters with 1094 files (36%) over the limit; 235 characters with 27 files over was the figure for the *old* names on a *planned shorter share root* (a financial-year folder on the office server); 215 with none over combines the short names *and* that shorter root; and "the margin is thin (215 vs 218) and the copied filename still carries the full untruncated client name". So the target root the author uses is an input the build needs (X2.8).

## APPENDIX X3: TEST SUITE

### X3.0 How to read this appendix

**Scope.** Project A = `goyal-sidhant/AnnualStatement_oldv1`, branch `main`, snapshot `bf2f1dd` (27-07-2026). Everything below is about A's own test suite: `pytest.ini`, `tests/conftest.py`, the 18 files `tests/test_*.py` and `tests/README.md`. All 18 test files and `pytest.ini` were added by A's own commits (A only (after the split)); none of the 12 shared commits (`edac6a3` ... `47a1492`, shared - before the split on 30-10-2025) contains a test. Project B has no tests at all (READ: `git ls-tree -r --name-only B/main` lists no test file and no `pytest.ini`).

**Labels.**
- **RAN (me)** = I executed it for this appendix, in `/root/merge-scratch/run/A-X3/` (a fresh copy of the snapshot) or in `/root/merge-scratch/run/A-X345/` (my other scratch work). Outputs are saved there: `pytest_xvfb.txt`, `pytest_noxvfb.txt`, `pytest_isolated.txt`, `hist/` (old commits), `mut/` (mutation copies), `consol/` (consolidator check).
- **RAN (TEST notes)** = executed by the reader who wrote `/root/merge-scratch/notes2/A_tests.md`; I did not repeat it unless I say so.
- **READ** = established by reading the code or the git history.
- **HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW** = how sure an inference is.
- **[GST RULE]** = the tested code decides which return, table, sheet, cell, state code or period a file or figure belongs to. I only describe what is pinned; I never say whether it is right. **⚠** = a value that can change over time (return names, file-naming conventions, state lists, template cells, package versions).

**Plain-English terms used in this appendix.**
- **test** (a small program that runs one part of the app with known inputs and checks the result); **test suite** (all of them together); **pytest** (the tool that finds and runs them).
- **collected** (how many individual tests pytest found); **passed / failed / skipped / error** (the check held / did not hold or crashed / the test chose not to run, e.g. because there is no screen / something broke while preparing or loading the test).
- **fixture** (a helper that prepares something before a test, e.g. a temporary folder or a fake Excel file); **parametrize** (one test function run several times with different inputs; each input counts as one collected test).
- **tmp_path** (a fresh throw-away folder that pytest makes for each test, under the computer's temp area).
- **monkeypatch** (temporarily replacing a real function by a fake, e.g. a fake `pip`).
- **subprocess / probe** (a test that starts a second, separate Python program, which runs a short script and reports back as text).
- **Tk root** (the main window object of Tkinter, the window toolkit A uses); **display / xvfb** (Linux needs a display server to open windows; `xvfb-run` supplies an invisible one; a Windows PC always has one).
- **COM / pywin32** (Windows' way for Python to drive Microsoft Excel / the package that provides it); none of it exists on Linux.
- **mutation check** (deliberately putting an old bug back into a scratch copy and running the tests to see whether they notice: CAUGHT = a test failed, SURVIVED = nothing noticed).
- **characterization test** (a test that records what the code does today so that later changes cannot alter it silently; it does not claim the behaviour is right).
- **bytecode / `__pycache__`** (compiled copies of Python files that Python writes into a `__pycache__` folder next to the source unless told not to, with `-B` or `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1`).
- **coverage** (which parts of the program a test run actually executes).

> **Correction to a working file.** `/root/merge-scratch/audit/A_files.txt` gives line counts from `wc -l`, which misses the last line of files that do not end with a newline (37 tracked files of A; for example `power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py` really has 1063 lines, not 1062). None of the test files is affected (RAN (TEST notes); confirmed for the files I cite).

### X3.2 Every failure and every skip, explained

#### X3.2.1 The one failure in both runs

**`tests/test_setup_validation.py::TestEvaluateSetup::test_ok_template_shows_filename_only`** (test at `tests/test_setup_validation.py:65-66`).

- What it expects: for the Windows-style template path `C:\gst\itc.xltx` (sample paths at `tests/test_setup_validation.py:12-17`) the Setup checklist row should show only `itc.xltx`.
- What happened (RAN (me)): `AssertionError: assert 'C:\\gst\\itc.xltx' == 'itc.xltx'`.
- Why it fails here (READ + RAN (me)): the message is `Path(value).name` (`gui/utils/setup_validation.py:64`). On Linux a backslash is an ordinary character, not a folder separator, so the "name" is the whole text. I checked: `PurePosixPath(r'C:\gst\itc.xltx').name` gives `C:\gst\itc.xltx`, `PureWindowsPath(...)` gives `itc.xltx`.
- On the author's Windows PC: **would pass** (HIGH).
- Side note: the suffix check one line earlier (`gui/utils/setup_validation.py:62`) works on Linux only by coincidence, because the text after the last dot is still `.xltx` (RAN (TEST notes)).

In the real program the tab is never destroyed while the window is open, so there the effect is only a redundant second refresh (MEDIUM).

(`core/file_parser.py:131`); "Unknown state ..., using fallback" (`utils/helpers.py:612, 617`); "Error finding Excel files in .../nope" (`utils/helpers.py:364`); "No Excel files found" (`core/file_parser.py:160`); "Could not open the extraction tab: scan exploded" (`gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:174`).

### X3.8 Test-suite hygiene issues (technical, no GST content)

1. **Dark-mode tests leave the shared window dark** (RAN (TEST notes)): `tests/test_dark_mode.py:112-121` and `:123-127` switch dark mode on and do not switch it back; `:129-141` does switch back (`restore_original_colors()` at `:138`), but each test builds a new manager (`tests/test_dark_mode.py:42-44`) whose `initialize()` records the CURRENT ttk values as the originals (`gui/utils/dark_mode_manager.py:81-101`), so after the two earlier tests it "restores" to the already-dark state (READ, HIGH) [Corrected during verification - originally `:129-141` was listed among the tests that do not switch back]; the manager themes the shared Tk root and the global ttk styles (`gui/utils/dark_mode_manager.py:105-115`). Later tests do not check colours, so nothing fails.
2. **Delayed Setup refreshes fire after their widgets are gone** (X3.2.5, RAN (me)).
3. **Each Setup tab or extractor panel built in a test adds one more application-wide wheel binding** to the shared root (`gui/tabs/setup_tab.py:201`; `power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:478`; never removed); the handlers cope with destroyed canvases (`gui/tabs/setup_tab.py:224-228`; `extractor_window.py:459-463`) (READ).
4. **Loading almost any `gui.*` module loads the whole program** (`gui/__init__.py:7` imports the main window, which imports every tab and the extractor) - this is how the pywin32 import problem broke test loading from `a677670` to `aeb83cf` (X3.7.2) (READ + RAN (me)).
5. **Weak or vacuous tests**: `tests/test_requirements_check.py:27-32` can never fail; `tests/test_dark_mode.py:182-188` does not test what its name says; `tests/test_dark_mode.py:190-198` checks source text and is defeated by M08; `tests/test_workflow_mode.py:85-90` checks a log string only; `tests/test_scroll_bindings.py` is text-based (M12b).
6. **Stale comments**: `tests/test_helpers.py:110-111` ("sanitize_filename's underscore/substring behaviour"); `tests/README.md:28-30` (X3.7.1).
7. **Misleading failure message**: `tests/test_requirements_check.py:71` says "openpyxl is needed" although the assertion covers every essential package, pywin32 on Windows included.
8. **No `pythonpath = .` in `pytest.ini`** (Standard 13, `rebuild_pipeline_FINAL.md:944-947`); the suite relies on `tests/conftest.py:9` instead. Whether it works unchanged under the author's portable `_runtime` Python: probably yes because of that line (MEDIUM; not run).

Before doing so, copy `%USERPROFILE%\.gst_organizer_cache.json` aside (X3.6 item 3).

### X4.2 `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-25-merge-extractor-design.md` (the design note, `b276542`, 25-07-2026) - plan versus what was built

### X4.6 In-code docstrings, comments, help texts and version strings versus the code

A **docstring** is the explanation text at the top of a Python file, class or function; a **comment** is a `#` note inside the code; **help texts** are the hover texts the user sees. They were written at different times by AI-assisted sessions, so some describe an earlier state of the code. Every row below was READ by me in the file named; "Verdict" uses the labels of X4.0.

### X4.7 High-value discrepancies (most important first)

Each item says what the documents claim, what the code does, and where the full gap entry is in Section 7 (A-G numbers).

1. **The consolidated Step 4 workbook puts another cell's value into 9 columns** [GST RULE] ⚠ - mentioned by no document. RAN (me) with the real configuration and made-up numbers (`/root/merge-scratch/run/A-X345/consol/check_consol.py`): 13 columns OK, 9 MISMATCH - the IGST/CGST/SGST columns of the sheets "IMS Reco", "Extra In Purchase" and "Extra In GSTR2B" (configured `IMS_Reco!AA1/AD1/AG1`, `ExtraInPurchase!O1/P1/Q1`, `ExtraInGSTR2B!S1/T1/U1`) received the values of `Diff GSTR-3B!J15/K15/L15` (re-run independently in verification with a separate script, `/root/merge-scratch/run/VERIFY-A-X345/consol/check.py`: the same 13 OK / 9 MISMATCH, the same nine columns, each receiving J15, K15 or L15 respectively). Cause: `power_query_extractor/core/data_consolidator.py:139-145` takes the first extracted field whose name CONTAINS the column title, and only then the exact field (`:147-150`). A technical mismatch between configuration and code; which cell is right is the author's call. Since `47a1492` (shared - before the split on 30-10-2025). Also: when a refresh is not marked successful, every column of that report shows "Missing" (`:128-129`) although values were read and the log says "(Data extracted despite error)" (`power_query_extractor/gui/extractor_window.py:924-925, 935-936`). → A-G1, A-G17.
2. **Creating a report quits the user's own running Excel.** The comment says "Don't quit if Excel was already open" (`core/excel_handler.py:241`); the code always quits, because `self.excel_app` is never set (`:56, 242`); it also hides that Excel (`:131`). The March audit (G12) noted only the reuse; the README advises "close all Excel files" without saying why. READ (me), HIGH on the logic; behaviour on Windows CANNOT VERIFY. → A-G54.
3. **A template without a "Links" sheet produces no error.** The README says templates "must" have one (119-122) and the March audit says the error "surfaces during report creation" (G14); the COM path adds an empty sheet and reports success (`core/excel_handler.py:180-183, 218-221`), the openpyxl path writes nothing and returns True (`:295-310`). → A-G4.
4. **"Resume" does not resume.** README (145), the March audit (R17, E7) and the hover help (`gui/tabs/setup_tab.py:108-109`) describe continuing interrupted work; every run makes a new `Version-<minute>` folder (`core/file_organizer.py:102-108`), so a later Resume copies everything again (RAN (DOCS notes), RAN (TRACE)). → A-G10.
5. **Texts that call pywin32 optional, while the program requires it on Windows.** `power_query_extractor/core/report_processor.py:11-13` ("genuinely optional"), `gui/tabs/extract_tab.py:20-22` and the user-visible notice `:101-105` ("Steps 1-3 are unaffected ... works without pywin32") versus `utils/requirements_check.py:44-60` and `main.py:97-102` (`be6418c`, the same evening as `c463256`). → related A-G7, A-G66.
6. **The Step 3 worker thread still touches the window directly**, although the March audit says all updates are scheduled (F8.4, PC3): 45 direct `log_message` calls, two `update_progress`, two message boxes and button changes from the worker (`gui/handlers/processing_handler.py:182-530`, RAN (me) count). The July thread-safety work (`c1f425e`) was done for the extractor only; the design note itself calls this pattern "a genuine cause of freezes and crashes" for the extractor (note lines 60-64). → A-G70.
7. **The design note and the build differ in four places**: "full" mode does not start the refresh (P15); there is no "Continue to extraction" button (P17); the extractor's logging set-up was not moved, only avoided (P12); pointing Step 4 at an older `Annual Statement-...` folder finds nothing (P19). Its claimed existing test coverage did not exist (P26, P31). → A-G45, A-G66.
8. **Help texts that promise behaviour the code does not have**: "Fast - no Excel automation involved", "Each run adds a new timestamped folder, so previous runs are left untouched", the Resume text, the length text, "press Process" (X4.6.4). → A-G66, A-G69.
9. **Invalid or too-small Excel files vanish silently.** The March audit says they are "added to variations" (E4) - that branch could not run even at `47a1492` and was removed in `a603c02`; `tests/test_scan.py:52` pins the silent drop. → A-G37.
10. **README instructions that are wrong for A today** - nine items, X4.4.1 (folder layout that will not start, wrong requirements, no variations tab, Dry Run location, button name, output names, Links advice, undocumented Step 4 and workflow, Resume).
11. **Widgets built while dark mode is on stay light** - the design note listed it as a defect (P41); still present; `c89c1d4`'s message says otherwise (RAN (DOCS notes)). → A-G64.
12. **`tests/README.md` says "No GUI ... runs fast (<1s) and anywhere"** - no longer true: 46 GUI tests, 14 failures and 33 skips without a display, 1 failure on Linux (RAN (me), X3). → see X3.2.

## SELF-CONSISTENCY REVIEW

> **How this record was made.** The review below was carried out on 22-10-2026 by an independent
> reviewer agent, after the twelve sections and six appendices had been assembled into this one
> document. It read the whole document in 44 chunks and made every correction directly in the text.
> Each correction is marked there as `[Corrected during self-review - ...]` or "(added during
> self-review)". The computer running the session was restarted just after the reviewer's last check,
> before it could write this record. The record was therefore compiled from the reviewer's own working
> log (`/root/merge-scratch/run/A-ASSEMBLE-AND-REVIEW/review_log.md`). Nothing in the audit text was
> changed while compiling it. The completeness check that follows it was run afterwards, separately.

### What was checked, and how

| Check (the audit method's list) | How it was done | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Assembly | A script (`assemble.py`) joined the section files in order and inserted the shared-commit entries at the 12A marker. A second script (`check_headings.py`) confirmed every section and appendix heading appears once, in order. It was run again after all edits. | 24 headings, each once, in order. Code fences balanced. No placeholder left. |
| 1. No cross-section contradictions | The whole document was read in 44 chunks, against the writers' 123 cross-section flags (`A_cross_flags.md`). Particular attention went to Section 3 vs Section 7, Section 8 vs Section 11, Section 12B "never changed" claims vs imports, Section 2 dead code vs dead code named elsewhere, and the appendices vs the sections. | Contradictions found and corrected: see the table below. |
| 2. Every feature has a concrete trace | Script check over Section 3. | All 31 features (A-F1 to A-F31) have a "Concrete trace" subsection, each marked ran or read. |
| 3. Shared state: write path vs read path | Section 4.4.1 and 4.5 and Appendix X2.5 were read against each other. | Every settings, cache and log file has its write path and read path compared. One correction was made to X2.5 (EDIT 4). |
| 4. Every Section 8 pattern checked across the codebase | Section 8 P1-P9 were read with their search evidence. | Each pattern lists the files that follow it and the files that break it, with the searches that found them. |
| 5. IDs consistent; every registry item appears | Script checks. | A-F1 to A-F31 each have one heading in Section 3. A-R1 to A-R157 all appear in Section 5 with a definition line. A-G1 to A-G79 are all referenced. No out-of-range F/R/G IDs, and no B- IDs. |
| Section 8 vs Section 11 constraint | Every HIGH-confidence decision in Section 8 (D2, D3, D6-D8, D11, D12, D14-D20, 8.2.5, 8.3.7) was checked in Section 11.4. | Each one is either kept, or given a third option (T1-T10). Nothing justified with HIGH confidence is recommended for replacement. |
| Confidentiality | Searches across the whole document. | 0 hits for the company-like name in the March 2026 audit, the author's local paths, share-root paths, GSTIN-like or PAN-like strings, and `Users\<name>` paths. 0 hits for 100 candidate client-name tokens taken from the old run log's message shapes (matched by script; nothing printed). |
| Counts re-run | `pytest --collect-only` on a fresh copy (`python -B`, `-p no:cacheprovider`, home and temp folders redirected). Plus `git log` per file, and a module count for Section 9. | 288 tests collected; the per-file counts match Section 11.1.6 (158 rule tests in 9 files). There are 36 `.py` files that have never changed since they were added (24 program and 12 test files), which matches 12B.7. The module count is given as dependent on the build and the counting method (222 / 334 / 339); every place in the document says so. |

### Handling of the writers' cross-section flags

The writers raised 123 flags (`/root/merge-scratch/audit/A_cross_flags.md`). Many had already been
dealt with by the section checkers before assembly. The reviewer read the rest alongside the
document. The flags that still needed work are EDITs 1, 5-8, 10-25, 27-36, 48, 49 and 51-58 above.
The flags the reviewer found already reflected are listed under "Checked and found consistent".
One flag was stale and was not applied: README does not omit `gui/tabs/extract_tab.py` (EDIT 58).
The ten UNREGISTERED items are kept in the text under that label. Section 5.18 (U1-U3) and Section
10.16 (U1-U17) collect them, with cross-references between the two lists where an item appears in
both (EDITs 38-40).
